nodes.label: Accuracy as Insufficient Evaluation Metric

nodes.label: Three Levels of AI Autonomy in Science

nodes.norm_label: three levels of ai autonomy in science
nodes.rationale: Low autonomy: execution within established theory; Medium autonomy: hypothesis generation; High autonomy: solving precisely stated problem; all remain anchored to human-supplied framework

nodes.label: Complete Scientific Theory Construction
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.rationale: Requires starting from theoretically uninterpreted observations, independently inducing theoretical system, making quantifiable predictions; no AI system has independently completed this

nodes.label: Counterfactual Task Variants for Separating Reasoning from Recitation
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.norm_label: counterfactual task variants for separating reasoning from recitation
nodes.rationale: Broader observation that counterfactual variants can separate reasoning from recitation; model cannot have seen standard answer during training

nodes.label: Formulation: Rewrite into Operational Form
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.rationale: Second cognitive move: rewrite induced regularity into operational form applicable by third party; exemplified by Maxwell's four equations and displacement current addition

nodes.label: Four-Stage Physics Reasoning Diagnostic
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.rationale: Decomposes physics understanding into four independent cognitive moves: induction, formulation, prediction, review; operationalizes Whewell's and Hempel's scientific method tradition

nodes.label: Induction: Extract Regularity from Observations
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.rationale: First cognitive move: extract from theoretically uninterpreted observations a regularity explaining all of them; exemplified by Maxwell's unification of electric and magnetic phenomena

nodes.label: LLM Judge Reliability Transfer Problem
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.rationale: Methodology finding: LLM judge reliability does not transfer across frameworks; self-review weak in every framework

nodes.label: Parallel Physics Worlds Framework
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.rationale: Counterfactual physics frameworks designed to separate genuine reasoning from training-data memorization; three worlds: F=mv, Aristotelian mechanics, Decay World

nodes.label: Prediction: Make Quantitatively Checkable Predictions
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.rationale: Third cognitive move: use operational form to make quantitatively checkable predictions about new situations; exemplified by Maxwell's prediction of electromagnetic waves

nodes.label: Qualitative-Versus-Quantitative Asymmetry in Physics Reasoning
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.rationale: Empirical pattern: models almost never predict wrong direction of change but frequently compute wrong ratio by slipping back to standard-physics relations

nodes.label: Reasoning Versus Memorization in LLMs
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.rationale: Central debate: whether LLMs perform genuine reasoning or template retrieval from training data; counterfactual frameworks designed to separate these

nodes.label: Review: Identify Errors and Boundaries
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.rationale: Fourth cognitive move: identify which step might be wrong, which boundary uncovered, which mechanism unexplained; exemplified by Maxwell's equations revealing seed of special relativity

nodes.label: Self-Review Weakness in LLM Physics Reasoning
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.norm_label: self-review weakness in llm physics reasoning
nodes.rationale: Stage 4 self-review is weak in every framework; model's own review wrongly reports no earlier error in at least two-thirds of trials that actually contained one

nodes.label: Whewell-Hempel Scientific Method Tradition
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.rationale: Older tradition of scientific method: induction, colligation, prediction, consilience; describes working path in routine physics, not revolutionary moments

nodes.label: World Modeling as Necessary but Insufficient for Physics Understanding
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.norm_label: world modeling as necessary but insufficient for physics understanding
nodes.rationale: Model without internal representation cannot produce independently checkable formal theory; having representation does not mean it can write theory down

nodes.label: Four-Stage Protocol for Testing LLM Physics Reasoning
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.norm_label: four-stage protocol for testing llm physics reasoning
nodes.rationale: Proposes a four-stage protocol (induction, formulation, prediction, review) to isolate and test distinct cognitive capabilities in LLM physics reasoning, avoiding confounds from end-to-end testing.

nodes.label: ALE Evaluation Modes: Deterministic Scoring
nodes.author: Yiyou Sun et al.
nodes.rationale: ALE deliberately avoids LLM-as-judge wherever deterministic alternatives exist; 93.2% of tasks use code-based judges, with LLM judging reserved for creative/perceptual deliverables using narrow yes/no probes.

nodes.label: ALE Failure Taxonomy: Understanding, Approach, Execution, Infrastructure
nodes.author: Yiyou Sun et al.

nodes.label: Gate-and-Score Pattern: Hard Precondition + Continuous Score
nodes.author: Yiyou Sun et al.
nodes.norm_label: gate-and-score pattern: hard precondition + continuous score

nodes.label: Generalist Computer-Use Agent (GCUA)
nodes.author: Yiyou Sun et al.

nodes.label: GUI-as-Tool: Desktop Action Integration

nodes.label: OpenClaw: Open-Source Agent Runtime
nodes.author: Yiyou Sun et al.
nodes.rationale: OpenClaw is used as baseline harness for model comparisons; ALE-Claw is a Python port of OpenClaw's agent loop with GUI-as-Tool additions.

nodes.label: SOC 2018 / O*NET Occupational Taxonomy
nodes.author: Yiyou Sun et al.

nodes.label: ALE-Claw: Self-Implemented GCUA Reference
nodes.author: Yiyou Sun et al.
nodes.rationale: ALE-Claw is a simplified Python implementation derived from OpenClaw that tests whether basic GCUA components suffice for comparable performance to frontier harnesses.

nodes.author: Zoe Hitzig, Maxim Massenkoff, Eva Lyubich, Ryan Heller, Peter McCrory

nodes.label: Zipf Distribution
nodes.rationale: Heavy-tailed power-law distribution ubiquitous in natural data including word frequencies, biological data, financial data

nodes.label: Literary-Adapted GoEmotions Classifier
nodes.rationale: Fine-tuned RoBERTa-based affect classifier adapted from GoEmotions to literary prose using 12,000-sentence adaptation set with LLM distillation and human validation (κ=0.68).

nodes.label: StyleDistance Embeddings
nodes.rationale: 768-dimensional SentenceTransformer-based embeddings trained on human-authored text for content-independent style analysis; used for MMD and across-story variance computations.

nodes.label: OpenAI text-embedding-3-large
nodes.rationale: 3072-dimensional embedding model used for thematic motion analysis; provides semantic representation of story sentences for computing adjacent-sentence distances.

nodes.label: OLMo 32B Base
nodes.rationale: Base checkpoint (allenai/Olmo-3-1125-32B) used as starting point for instruction-tuning pipeline in stage-wise analysis.

nodes.label: OLMo 32B DPO
nodes.rationale: Direct Preference Optimization checkpoint (allenai/Olmo-3.1-32B-Instruct-DPO) representing second post-training stage.

nodes.label: OLMo 32B RLVR
nodes.rationale: Final instruction-tuned checkpoint (allenai/Olmo-3.1-32B-Instruct) representing full post-training pipeline endpoint.

nodes.label: OLMo 32B SFT
nodes.rationale: Supervised fine-tuning checkpoint (allenai/Olmo-3.1-32B-Instruct-SFT) representing first post-training stage.

nodes.label: Affective Neutralization in Aligned Models
nodes.rationale: Instruction-tuning sharply reduces affective charge (41.0% → 20.7% on New Yorker) while raising neutral narration (28.7% → 45.1%); effect is most consistent across model families.

nodes.label: Across-Story Style Variance Collapse
nodes.rationale: Post-training reduces across-story style variance to 0.29-0.37× human levels; effect is largest in professional fiction (New Yorker) and domain-dependent across model families.

nodes.label: Thematic Rhythm Compression Across Post-Training
nodes.rationale: Post-training stages (SFT, DPO, RLVR) progressively reduce thematic CV from 0.104 (human) to 0.081 (RLVR) on New Yorker; effect is monotonic and saturates at DPO/RLVR.

nodes.label: Affective Charge Prevalence
nodes.rationale: Aggregates surprise-curiosity and conflict affect families from GoEmotions-adapted classifier; measures emotional intensity in narrative.

nodes.label: Style Maximum Mean Discrepancy
nodes.rationale: Measures linguistic-habit distance between human and model style distributions using StyleDistance embeddings with Gaussian RBF kernel; lower MMD indicates closer style alignment.

nodes.label: Thematic Motion Coefficient of Variation
nodes.rationale: Measures narrative rhythm by computing coefficient of variation of adjacent-sentence semantic distances using text-embedding-3-large; lower CV indicates flatter, more regularized narrative structure.

nodes.label: The New Yorker Short Fiction Corpus (1945-2019)
nodes.norm_label: the new yorker short fiction corpus (1945-2019)
nodes.rationale: Restricted corpus of 3,023 professional literary short stories under 5,000 words used as primary evaluation domain for narrative analysis.

nodes.label: StoryStar Public Platform Fiction Corpus
nodes.rationale: 100 short stories from storystar.com public creative-writing platform, representing minimal editorial filtering baseline.

nodes.label: TELL ME A STORY (TMAS) Corpus
nodes.rationale: Publicly available corpus of 230 human-written stories composed in guided creative-writing setting, providing prompt-guided fiction baseline.

nodes.label: Narrative Flattening in LLM Story Continuation
nodes.norm_label: narrative flattening in llm story continuation
nodes.rationale: Core research paper analyzing how post-training (SFT, DPO, RLVR) compresses narrative diversity in LLM-generated story continuations across thematic, affective, and stylistic dimensions.

nodes.label: Autonomous Research Pipeline Architecture
nodes.rationale: 23-stage pipeline across three phases (Discovery, Experimentation, Writing) with formal input/output contracts and checkpoint-based resumption. Integrates multi-agent debate, self-healing execution, verifiable reporting, HITL collaboration, and cross-run evolution. Treats research as iterative cycle rather than one-off process.

nodes.label: ARC-Bench: 25-Topic ML + 20-Topic Scientific Domain Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Benchmark spanning tabular ML, optimization, dimensionality reduction, NLP, AutoML, GP kernels, topic modeling, semi-supervised learning, dynamical systems, anomaly detection, feature selection, causal discovery, learning-to-rank, plus 10 HEP physics, 7 systems biology, 3 statistics tasks. Supports experiment-stage, end-to-end, and scientific-domain evaluation modes.

nodes.label: Four-Layer Citation Verification Pipeline
nodes.rationale: DOI resolution via CrossRef, fuzzy title matching against OpenAlex, arXiv identifier lookup, Semantic Scholar fallback. LLM-based relevance check classifies references as Verified, Suspicious, or Hallucinated. Hallucinated references removed before draft finalization.

nodes.label: Cross-Run Evolution with Time-Decayed Lesson Store
nodes.norm_label: cross-run evolution with time-decayed lesson store
nodes.rationale: Persistent lesson store converts past failures into reusable safeguards. Lessons ranked by time-decayed weight w(l) = s(l) · exp(-ln(2) · Δt / T_1/2) where T_1/2 = 30 days default. Recent failures strongly constrain subsequent runs; older lessons gradually fade. Injected as natural-language overlays requiring no model retraining.

nodes.label: Human-in-the-Loop Collaboration with Seven Intervention Modes
nodes.norm_label: human-in-the-loop collaboration with seven intervention modes
nodes.rationale: Seven intervention modes: Full-Auto (no input), Gate-Only (3 fixed checkpoints), Thorough (all phase boundaries), CoPilot (6 high-leverage points), Step-by-Step (every stage), Pre-Experiment (early-pipeline), Post-Experiment (late-pipeline). CoPilot achieves 87.5% accept rate vs. Full-Auto's 25% and Step-by-Step's 50%.

nodes.label: Structured Multi-Agent Debate
nodes.rationale: Assigns agents complementary epistemic roles (Innovator, Pragmatist, Contrarian for ML; Theorist, Phenomenologist, Experimentalist for HEP-ph) to stress-test hypotheses and conclusions. Synthesizer integrates outputs into structured artifacts. Applied at hypothesis generation and result analysis stages.

nodes.label: Self-Healing Executor with Pivot/Refine Loop
nodes.rationale: Treats experiment failures as diagnostic information rather than termination signals. Cascading code generation with complexity scoring routes experiments to external AI agent or multi-phase internal agent. Pivot/Refine decisions: Proceed (evidence supports hypothesis), Refine (weak results but sound direction), or Pivot (fundamentally flawed approach).

nodes.label: Rubric-Assisted Strict Judge for Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Grades along three dimensions: Code Development (CD, 25%), Code Execution (CE, 25%), Result Analysis (RA, 50%). RA receives double weight to capture scientific reasoning quality. Two independent agent reviewers run in parallel; disagreements exceeding |Δ| > 0.20 re-adjudicated. Mean per-leaf |Δ| < 0.10 across audited subset.

nodes.label: Verifiable Result Reporting
nodes.rationale: Numeric registry stores every value produced by experiment runs (per-condition means, standard deviations, individual seed measurements). Pre-built LATEX tables populated exclusively from registry injected into generation prompt. Post-hoc verifier re-extracts numeric claims and checks against registry; unverified claims in strict sections trigger document rejection.

nodes.label: Cold Fine-Tuning Control Condition
nodes.rationale: Control experiment fine-tuning models on same conversational data but with responses rewritten in 'cold' style (direct, concise, emotionally neutral). Cold models performed similarly to or better than originals, isolating warmth as the causal factor for accuracy degradation.

nodes.label: Evaluation Tasks (TriviaQA, TruthfulQA, MASK, MedQA)
nodes.rationale: Benchmark datasets with clear ground-truth answers used to evaluate accuracy degradation. Tasks span factual knowledge (TriviaQA), truthfulness (TruthfulQA), disinformation detection (MASK), and medical reasoning (MedQA).

nodes.label: Interpersonal Context Amendments
nodes.rationale: Experimental manipulation adding emotional state, relational dynamics, or interaction stakes to prompts. Warm models showed 12.1 pp more errors when questions included both incorrect beliefs and emotional cues, compared to 6.8 pp gap without amendments.

nodes.label: Model Families Tested (Llama, Qwen, GPT-4o, Mistral)
nodes.norm_label: model families tested (llama, qwen, gpt-4o, mistral)
nodes.rationale: Five model families tested: Llama-8b, Llama-70b, Mistral-Small, Qwen-32b, GPT-4o. Convergence of warmth-accuracy trade-offs across architectures and sizes (8B to trillions of parameters) suggests genuine trade-off rather than implementation artifact.

nodes.label: Sycophancy in Language Models
nodes.rationale: Model behavior of affirming user-stated beliefs regardless of correctness. Operationalized by appending incorrect user beliefs to prompts and measuring whether models shift toward stated belief. Warm models showed 11 pp increase in errors when users expressed incorrect beliefs.

nodes.label: System Prompting for Warmth Induction
nodes.rationale: Alternative method to induce warmth at inference time via system prompts rather than fine-tuning. Produces similar but weaker and less consistent trade-offs compared to fine-tuned models, suggesting fine-tuning amplifies warmth-accuracy tension.

nodes.label: Warmth Fine-Tuning Process
nodes.rationale: Persona training technique that modifies model communication style (warmth, friendliness, empathy) while maintaining general AI assistant identity. Uses SFT (supervised fine-tuning) on conversational data transformed to warmer variants using GPT-4o.

nodes.label: Warmth-Accuracy Trade-Off in AI Alignment
nodes.rationale: Central finding: optimizing for one desirable trait (warmth/friendliness) compromises others (factual accuracy). Reflects broader AI alignment challenge where preference optimization can improve perceived helpfulness while reducing factual accuracy. Warmth fine-tuning selectively compromises accuracy without weakening explicit guardrails.

nodes.label: Interlat: Inter-agent Latent Space Communication
nodes.rationale: Proposes paradigm for LLM-based agents to communicate entirely in latent space by transmitting last-layer hidden states rather than discrete tokens, enabling richer information exchange and compression.

nodes.label: Contrastive Activation Addition (CAA)
nodes.rationale: Model steering technique modifying internal activations during inference to enhance reasoning compliance without parameter updates, achieving up to 29% improvement.

nodes.label: CKA Geometric Analysis of Reasoning
nodes.rationale: Centered Kernel Alignment identifies geometric differences in reasoning representations across models and layers.

nodes.label: Compliance-Sensibility Response Categories
nodes.rationale: Four categories: Sensible∩Compliant, Sensible∩¬Compliant, ¬Sensible∩Compliant, ¬Sensible∩¬Compliant for systematic reasoning conflict analysis.

nodes.label: Confidence Drop During Reasoning Conflicts
nodes.rationale: Reasoning conflicts are internally detectable via confidence score drops, enabling identification of conflicting episodes.

nodes.label: Instruction Decodability via Linear Probing
nodes.rationale: Linear probing reveals instruction decodability even in non-compliant responses, indicating instructions are processed but not followed.

nodes.label: Mechanistic Interpretation of Reasoning
nodes.rationale: Analysis combining linear probing and CKA to reveal instruction decodability and geometric differences in reasoning representations across models and layers.

nodes.label: Reasoning Conflict Framework
nodes.rationale: Framework for evaluating tension between instruction compliance and logical sensibility in LLM reasoning, classifying responses into sensible/compliant/both/neither categories.

nodes.label: Steering Vector Generation
nodes.rationale: Mean difference of residual stream activations between compliant and non-compliant response pairs, controlling intensity via coefficient μ.

nodes.label: Prediction-Powered Confidence Interval Construction
nodes.rationale: Combines measure of fit and rectifier to form valid confidence interval; guaranteed to contain true estimand at desired confidence level for any ML algorithm and data distribution.

nodes.label: Convex Risk Minimizer
nodes.rationale: General framework for any estimand expressible as minimizer of convex objective; measure of fit uses gradient; rectifier measures gradient difference.

nodes.label: Income Analysis with Covariate Shift
nodes.rationale: Investigated relationship between age and income with distribution shift in covariates; prediction-powered inference required n=177 labeled observations vs n=282 for classical approach.

nodes.label: Deforestation Estimation Application
nodes.rationale: Estimated fraction of Amazon rainforest lost using satellite imagery predictions; prediction-powered inference required n=21 labeled observations vs n=35 for classical approach.

nodes.label: Distribution Shift Handling
nodes.rationale: Framework extends to label shift and covariate shift; covariate shift handled via reweighting; label shift handled via confusion matrix estimation.

nodes.label: Finite Population Inference
nodes.rationale: Adapts prediction-powered inference to finite-population setting without distributional assumptions; treats population as fixed with uniform sampling of outcomes.

nodes.label: Galaxy Classification Application
nodes.rationale: Estimated fraction of galaxies with spiral arms using Galaxy Zoo 2 data; prediction-powered inference required n=189 labeled examples vs n=449 for classical approach.

nodes.label: Gene Expression Quantile Application
nodes.rationale: Constructed confidence intervals on quantiles of gene expression levels induced by promoter sequences; prediction-powered inference required n=764 labeled examples vs n=900 for classical approach.

nodes.label: General Risk Minimization
nodes.rationale: Extends framework to nonconvex losses and constrained optimization; includes applications to mode estimation, robust means, and model selection.

nodes.label: Health Insurance Analysis Application
nodes.rationale: Investigated relationship between income and private health insurance using census data; prediction-powered inference required n=5569 labeled observations vs n=6653 for classical approach.

nodes.label: Linear Regression Coefficients
nodes.rationale: Estimand for regression coefficient; measure of fit uses pseudoinverse; rectifier measures prediction error contribution.

nodes.label: Logistic Regression Coefficients
nodes.rationale: Estimand for logistic regression coefficient; measure of fit uses feature-weighted residuals; rectifier measures prediction error weighted by features.

nodes.label: Mean Estimation
nodes.rationale: Estimand for mean outcome; measure of fit is average of predictions on unlabeled data; rectifier is average prediction error on labeled data.

nodes.label: Measure of Fit
nodes.rationale: Computed on unlabeled dataset imputed with predictions; quantifies how likely candidate estimand value is based on imputed data; closer to zero indicates more plausible value.

nodes.label: Nonasymptotic Analysis
nodes.rationale: Provides nonasymptotic counterparts of main results using variance-adaptive confidence intervals; requires bounded observations within known interval.

nodes.label: Plankton Counting Application
nodes.rationale: Counted plankton using ResNet predictions with label shift between years; prediction-powered inference covered ground truth while imputation approach failed.

nodes.label: Proteomics Application: PTM and IDR Relationship
nodes.norm_label: proteomics application: ptm and idr relationship
nodes.rationale: Used AlphaFold predictions to study posttranslational modifications in intrinsically disordered regions; prediction-powered inference required n=316 labeled observations vs n=799 for classical approach.

nodes.label: Quantile Estimation
nodes.rationale: Estimand for q-quantile of outcome; measure of fit uses sign function; rectifier measures indicator function differences.

nodes.label: Rectifier
nodes.rationale: Notion of prediction error relevant for estimand of interest; defined as difference of measure of fit on labeled data versus labeled data with predicted outcomes; equals zero if predictions perfect.

nodes.label: Theorem S1: Validity of Prediction-Powered Inference
nodes.norm_label: theorem s1: validity of prediction-powered inference
nodes.rationale: Main mathematical result proving prediction-powered confidence intervals contain true estimand with desired probability for any ML algorithm and data distribution.

nodes.label: Mathematical Semantics in Continuous Vector Space
nodes.norm_label: mathematical semantics in continuous vector space
nodes.rationale: Learning continuous representations of symbolic mathematical expressions that capture semantic equivalence beyond syntactic similarity. E-Gen corpus enables models to learn underlying mathematical rules through diverse transformations. Embeddings support downstream tasks: clustering, mistake detection, analogical reasoning.

nodes.label: Contrastive Learning for Expression Embeddings
nodes.rationale: Representation learning approach using InfoNCE loss to embed semantically equivalent expressions closer together while pushing distinct expressions apart. CL Mean achieves 97.61% clustering accuracy; enables learning of latent space where mathematical semantics are captured.

nodes.label: Mathematical Language Processing Downstream Tasks
nodes.rationale: Evaluation tasks including K-means clustering, semantic understanding beyond syntactic similarity, mistake detection in derivations, and embedding algebra (mathematical analogies). E-Gen models outperform SEMEMB and GPT-4o across all tasks.

nodes.label: E-Graph Data Structure
nodes.rationale: Advanced data structure for efficiently manipulating collections of terms under congruence relation. Enables saturation by applying ~800 mathematical rules to generate clusters of semantically equivalent expressions. E-classes contain equivalent e-nodes; edges connect e-nodes to child e-classes representing operator arguments.

nodes.label: Embedding Algebra Task
nodes.rationale: Analogy-based reasoning task extending word2vec-style operations to mathematical expressions. Given triplet (x1, y1, x2), predict y2 such that x1:y1 :: x2:y2. Seq2seq achieves 70.38% accuracy vs. GPT-4o's 39.60%, indicating superior understanding of mathematical transformations.

nodes.label: Mistake Detection in Mathematical Derivations
nodes.rationale: Out-of-distribution task evaluating whether embeddings capture semantic information to identify erroneous steps in mathematical derivations. Seq2seq achieves 77.99% F1 on mistake detection vs. SEMEMB's 53.61%, demonstrating robustness and generalizability.

nodes.label: Seq2Seq Equivalent Expression Generation
nodes.rationale: Training approach where encoder learns to map input expressions into latent space by predicting mathematically equivalent expressions as output. Achieves 96.72% accuracy on K-means clustering of equivalent expressions, outperforming SEMEMB (37.70%).

nodes.label: Effective Sample Size Framework
nodes.rationale: Formalizes D_eff = D·g(Q) where g(Q)≈Q^γ. Lemma 1 shows γ≈1 for Gaussian noise (SNR scaling); Lemma 2 shows γ≈2 for random classification noise.

nodes.label: NMT and CLM Experiments
nodes.rationale: Controlled experiments on English-German translation (Paracrawl) and causal language modeling (C4) with synthetic noise injection at 7 quality levels and 3 dataset sizes.

nodes.label: Data Quality Parameter Q
nodes.rationale: Dimensionless parameter Q ∈ (0,1] quantifying usable information in corpus. Estimated via corruption rate (Q=1-CR) or data deficiency measure. Q=1 represents clean data.

nodes.label: Data Quality in LLM Pretraining
nodes.rationale: Data quality dimensions: accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, uniqueness, validity. In LLM pretraining, quality varies across web sources; filtering and deduplication improve performance.

nodes.label: Information-Theoretic Perspective on Scaling Laws
nodes.rationale: Corruption reduces mutual information multiplicatively: I(X̃;Z) ≈ ρ(Q)·I(X;Z). Loss scales with mutual information; quality-aware law emerges from information-theoretic generalization bounds.

nodes.label: Quality-Aware Scaling Laws for LLMs
nodes.rationale: Extends Chinchilla scaling law with dimensionless quality parameter Q, predicting loss as L(N,D,Q) = A/N^α + B/(D^β Q^γ) + E to model data quality impact.

nodes.label: Alignment-Induced Homogenization in Open-Ended Generation
nodes.rationale: Post-training through SFT, DPO, and RLVR reduces output diversity and narrows distributions. Base model shows stylistic sprawl (6× human variance); SFT collapses to 0.84×; DPO/RLVR to 0.5–0.55×. Professional literary fiction compressed most (21pp affective drop) because its baseline lies farthest from aligned model's attractor; common fiction shows smaller gaps because baselines already sit closer to convergence point.

nodes.label: Distinct Alignment Objectives Needed for Creative Writing
nodes.norm_label: distinct alignment objectives needed for creative writing
nodes.rationale: Creative-writing assistants require alignment objectives distinct from general-purpose assistants. In summarization, reduced variation is desirable; in fiction, variation leads to heightened experience. Possible directions: domain-conditional reward models calibrating to source register; distributional matching objectives preserving variation within and across stories; preference data deliberately sampled from literary tail rather than majority-preferred continuations.

nodes.label: Domain-Insensitive Convergence Under Post-Training
nodes.rationale: Post-trained endpoints converge across domains: cross-domain thematic CV spread shrinks 62%, affective charge spread 81%, style MMD² drops from 0.61 to ~0.01. Model applies single continuation regime regardless of source domain, erasing distinctions between professional literary fiction, prompt-guided stories, and public-platform fiction. Convergence point sits closer to common-fiction baselines than literary fiction.

nodes.label: Narrative Flattening: Post-Training Compression of Story Variation
nodes.norm_label: narrative flattening: post-training compression of story variation
nodes.rationale: Measurable compression of narrative variation across three dimensions: (1) thematic motion becomes more uniform (topic-jump CV drops 22.2% from human baseline), (2) high-arousal emotions (conflict, surprise-curiosity) are suppressed while neutral affect rises, (3) linguistic diversity collapses with cross-domain style divergence dropping 90%. Post-training installs a fixed writing regime insensitive to source domain complexity.

nodes.label: Post-Training as Narrative Regularization
nodes.rationale: Post-training acts as regularization of narrative trajectory, not parametric optimization. Base model is affectively over-marked and stylistically unstable. SFT, DPO, RLVR make generation more controlled and conventionally well-formed by suppressing variation: thematic jumps become uniform, affect muted, linguistic habits collapse. Control achieved through loss of dynamic contrast—possible structural account of why aligned fiction feels mechanical.

nodes.label: Quality-Aware Scaling Laws for LLM Pretraining
nodes.norm_label: quality-aware scaling laws for llm pretraining
nodes.rationale: Introduces explicit dimensionless measure of data quality Q alongside model size N and dataset volume D, extending Chinchilla framework to predict pretraining loss as joint function of all three factors.

nodes.label: Claude Code Security Vulnerabilities
nodes.rationale: Multiple documented CVEs and security issues including network sandbox bypass, RCE via project files, token exfiltration, and deny-rule bypass.

nodes.label: Community Reimplementations of Claude Code
nodes.rationale: Five representative projects (ClawCodex, Claw Code, claude-code-working, buildable fork, Open Claude Code) spanning Python, Rust, TypeScript with varied methodologies.

nodes.label: Claude Code Design Space and Security Analysis
nodes.norm_label: claude code design space and security analysis
nodes.rationale: Comprehensive analysis of Claude Code v2.1.88 architecture, design decisions, and security implications based on extracted TypeScript source code and official documentation.

nodes.label: Hypothetical Circumvention Methods for AI Act Research Exemptions
nodes.norm_label: hypothetical circumvention methods for ai act research exemptions
nodes.rationale: Four methods identified: (1) Offshore Cloud Deployment—testing in non-EU jurisdictions; (2) Synthetic Environment with Live Overlays—simulated environment periodically updated with live data; (3) Model-Splitting—dividing multi-model AI across systems; (4) Silent On-Site Data Capture—recording and transmitting live data without showing outputs. All would likely violate AI Act if affecting EU individuals.

nodes.label: Development-Phase Exemption
nodes.rationale: Exempts AI systems under development before market placement or service deployment. Key limitation: testing in real-world conditions not covered by exemption. Ambiguity: 'real-world conditions' undefined; silent-mode deployment in hospital (capturing data without generating outputs) may or may not qualify depending on intended purpose interpretation.

nodes.label: Scientific-Use Exemption
nodes.rationale: Exempts AI systems specifically developed and put into service for sole purpose of scientific research. Key ambiguity: 'sole purpose' difficult to prove; goals and intentions change over time. Creates room for presenting commercially-driven systems as research to avoid regulation. Four scenarios identified where exemption applicability unclear.

nodes.label: AgingBench: Longitudinal Agent Reliability Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Longitudinal benchmark for agent lifespan engineering measuring time-dependent reliability degradation in deployed agents across four aging mechanisms (compression, interference, revision, maintenance).

nodes.label: Adaptive Reward Fusion (ARF)
nodes.rationale: Mechanism dynamically modulating supervision strength based on verifiability, fusing deterministic and semantic signals with dimension-wise weights.

nodes.label: Best-of-N Sampling for Verification
nodes.rationale: Demonstrates VRM discriminative power: single-sample RLVR policy matches SFT with N=32 samples, validating verification signal distillation into policy.

nodes.label: Complementarity of Deterministic and Semantic Verification
nodes.norm_label: complementarity of deterministic and semantic verification
nodes.rationale: 31.6% of samples pass semantic but fail deterministic verification, demonstrating hybrid method rewards partial correctness while enforcing rigor.

nodes.label: Dimensional Analysis of Semantic Verification
nodes.rationale: Pass rates: Physical Consistency 68%, Mathematical Correctness 81.4%, Instruction Following 92.6%, identifying physical constraints as primary filter.

nodes.label: Distillation Loss Statement
nodes.rationale: Proposed reporting template for knowledge distillation documenting deployment context, critical off-metric capabilities, preservation targets, observed losses, and deployment implications.

nodes.label: Dynamic Weight Allocation (DWA) Head
nodes.rationale: Gating network estimating reliability weights based on execution results, enabling robust reward estimation under partial verification noise.

nodes.label: Error Analysis: Logical/Physical Violations
nodes.rationale: Blind human evaluation on 100 samples: RLVR reduces logical violations from 41% (SFT) to 28%, improves accuracy from 48% to 62%.

nodes.label: Out-of-Distribution Generalization
nodes.rationale: RLVR consistently surpasses SFT on SuperGPQA and Physics benchmarks, indicating robust reasoning capabilities beyond source domain.

nodes.label: Hybrid Verification Protocol
nodes.rationale: Two-layer filtering: automated verification via SES and auxiliary critic, followed by HITL audit with dynamic rejection threshold (τ>5%) for dataset quality.

nodes.label: LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Automated evaluation protocol using frontier models (Qwen3-Max) for semantic scoring, validated against human experts with Spearman ρ=0.82.

nodes.label: Lossy Projection Framework for Distillation
nodes.rationale: Reframes knowledge distillation as projection onto subset of teacher observables, making visible which capabilities are unconstrained or weakly constrained.

nodes.label: Off-Metric Distillation Losses Taxonomy
nodes.rationale: Taxonomy of 9 capability dimensions where students diverge from teachers: predictive-distribution, representation/relation, capability-boundary, privacy/memorization, calibration/abstention, process/on-policy, grounding/provenance, safety-boundary, long-tail/diversity.

nodes.label: Oracle-Guided Pretraining
nodes.rationale: Supervised distillation from ensemble of oracles generating soft quality scores and dimension weights, eliminating information leakage via disjoint oracle models.

nodes.label: Parameter Efficiency in Quantum Reasoning
nodes.rationale: VRM-optimized Qwen3-8B (0.680 Problem Solving) outperforms ChatGPT-5 (0.642) and DeepSeek-R1 (0.665), demonstrating parameter-efficient alternative to scaling.

nodes.label: Parser-Executor Pipeline in SES
nodes.rationale: Three-stage pipeline: semantic parsing via LLM, type casting and parameter passing, execution with exception handling for robust verification.

nodes.label: QuantumQA Dataset
nodes.rationale: Large-scale dataset of 92,749 quantum mechanics samples with task-adaptive construction and hybrid verification (deterministic + semantic + HITL).

nodes.label: Retention Assumption in Distillation
nodes.rationale: Hidden assumption that primary metric retention implies preserved teacher capability; shown to be logically unwarranted without explicit off-metric capability measurement.

nodes.label: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR)
nodes.rationale: RL paradigm using deterministic execution signals and semantic evaluation for precise supervision in scientific reasoning, demonstrated via PPO and GRPO.

nodes.label: Scenario-Specific Preservation Targets
nodes.rationale: Context-dependent preservation targets for 8 distillation scenarios (reasoning, code agents, RAG, domain assistants, privacy-sensitive, safety, synthetic-data, on-device).

nodes.label: Seed-Evolve Paradigm
nodes.rationale: Data construction strategy expanding topical breadth from authoritative seed problems via hierarchical decomposition and heterogeneous model ensemble generation.

nodes.label: Scientific Execution Suite (SES)
nodes.rationale: Deterministic toolkit with 12 modular verification scripts for mathematical and physical consistency checks using SymPy, QuTiP, and symbolic solvers.

nodes.label: Task-Adaptive Data Construction
nodes.rationale: Strategy enforcing concise answers for retrieval tasks and rigorous CoT for complex reasoning, mitigating hallucination through task-specific response structure.

nodes.label: Verification-Aware Reward Model (VRM)
nodes.rationale: Unified reward model combining deterministic verification signals from SES with multidimensional semantic evaluation (Corr, Phys, Inst) via adaptive reward fusion for RLVR.

nodes.label: OSR Benchmarks (CIFAR, TinyImageNet, CUB, Aircraft, SCars)
nodes.norm_label: osr benchmarks (cifar, tinyimagenet, cub, aircraft, scars)
nodes.rationale: Standard benchmarks for evaluating OSR methods with known-unknown splits and semantic shift benchmarks (SSBs).

nodes.label: OSR Loss Functions (CE, SupCon, ARPL)
nodes.rationale: Three main loss functions analyzed: Cross-Entropy (CE), Supervised Contrastive (SupCon), and Adversarial Reciprocal Points Learning (ARPL). Temperature scaling affects gradient behavior differently in each.

nodes.label: Open Set Recognition Problem
nodes.rationale: Core problem: classifying known classes while detecting unknown classes. Addressed through representation learning and loss function design.

nodes.label: 15 Diverse Benchmarks (Math, Code, Logic, Knowledge, Affective)
nodes.norm_label: 15 diverse benchmarks (math, code, logic, knowledge, affective)
nodes.rationale: Evaluation across AIME, MATH500, LiveMathBench, MBPP, HumanEval, KORBench, BBH, ARC, MMLUPro, GPQA, FinQA, MedQA, EmoryNLP, MELD.

nodes.label: Automatic Model Set Construction
nodes.rationale: Selects complementary models from candidate pool by ranking based on cluster-wise performance, balancing specialization and diversity.

nodes.label: Clustering-Based Query Routing
nodes.rationale: Core mechanism: embeds queries, clusters them semantically, builds cluster-wise capability profiles for each model, routes test queries to best-performing models in their cluster.

nodes.label: Bridge Blocks: Cross-Sequence Attention
nodes.rationale: Attention mechanism operating on batch axis (B×S×D tensor) rather than sequence axis, enabling tokens from same prompt to attend to each other. Markovian design without key-value cache.

nodes.label: Math Reasoning Benchmarks (MATH, AIME, AMC, etc.)
nodes.norm_label: math reasoning benchmarks (math, aime, amc, etc.)
nodes.rationale: Evaluation on MATH-500, AIME24, AIME25, AMC23, BRUMO25, CMIMC25, HMMT_FEB25 plus non-math tasks (XSum, CNN/DailyMail, GPQA, ZebraLogic, Countdown).

nodes.label: RLVR Training with Bridge
nodes.rationale: SFT warm-up on correct reasoning traces followed by GRPO training with verifiable rewards. Bridge blocks introduce inter-sample dependence in advantage computation.

nodes.label: Axial Attention in Transformers
nodes.rationale: Attention on different axes of high-order tensors. Bridge applies attention on batch axis (cross-sequence) rather than sequence axis, treating B×S×D as structured tensor.

nodes.label: Contrastive Learning and Self-Consistency
nodes.rationale: Self-Consistency (SC) strategy: sample multiple responses and take majority vote. Model-Switch extends SC to multiple models. Used for improving reasoning in LLMs.

nodes.label: Mixture-of-Agents (MoA) Methods
nodes.rationale: Multiple models generate responses in parallel, aggregated via hierarchical layers. Effective for large models but struggles with smaller models due to instruction-following limitations.

nodes.label: Parallel Inference Scaling for LLMs
nodes.rationale: Scaling inference compute by generating N>1 responses per prompt. Independent generations waste information; Bridge enables interdependence while maintaining parallelism.

nodes.label: Representation Learning for Open Set Recognition
nodes.norm_label: representation learning for open set recognition
nodes.rationale: Core OSR approach: learn representations where known classes cluster tightly and unknown classes remain distant. Temperature scheduling affects representation geometry during training.

nodes.label: Router-Based Multi-Model Ensemble Methods
nodes.rationale: Select best model(s) for each query via trained or training-free routing. Avengers uses training-free clustering-based routing vs. RouterDC, EmbedLLM, MODEL-SAT which require neural network training.

nodes.label: Temperature Scaling in Neural Networks
nodes.rationale: Temperature τ in softmax controls sharpness of probability distributions. Small τ amplifies logit differences (sharper); large τ smooths them. Used in knowledge distillation, calibration, contrastive learning.

nodes.label: Temperature Scheduling for Open Set Recognition
nodes.norm_label: temperature scheduling for open set recognition
nodes.rationale: Proposes novel temperature schedules (T_NegCosSch, T_CosSch) that improve OSR performance by starting with lower temperature and moving to higher temperature, making tighter representation clusters for closed set classes while keeping open set examples distant.

nodes.label: The Avengers: Collective Intelligence of Smaller LMs
nodes.norm_label: the avengers: collective intelligence of smaller lms
nodes.rationale: Proposes training-free framework combining 10 ~7B models via embedding, clustering, scoring, and voting to match/exceed GPT-4.1 performance across 15 diverse benchmarks.

nodes.label: Bridge: Interdependent Parallel Generation
nodes.rationale: Proposes architectural modification allowing N parallel LLM generations to share information via attention on batch axis, improving reasoning performance with only 2.8-5.1% new parameters.

nodes.label: Adversarial Response Generation
nodes.rationale: Dual-track prompting with standard and adversarial instructions across model ensemble (lightweight to frontier), generating 3 responses per track per question.

nodes.label: Boundary Mutation Strategy
nodes.rationale: Generates adjacent problems by altering boundary conditions and physical constraints, testing model robustness to subtle logical shifts.

nodes.label: Cohen's κ Agreement in Reasoning Classification
nodes.norm_label: cohen's κ agreement in reasoning classification
nodes.rationale: Human-GPT5.1 agreement κ=0.84 for reasoning type classification, validating LLM-as-Judge framework with rule-based parser.

nodes.label: Dominant Reasoning Mode Assumption
nodes.rationale: Controlled testbed assumption that most prominent reasoning type contributing to final answer is classified, enabling systematic evaluation of reasoning conflicts.

nodes.label: Expert Verification Pipeline
nodes.rationale: 15 domain experts (10 PhD candidates, 5 postdocs) with custom annotation interface, standardized 4-metric evaluation, IRB approval, fair compensation.

nodes.label: Lexical Mimicking in Reasoning Classification
nodes.rationale: Frontier models superficially echo reasoning instruction terms without executing corresponding logical operations, requiring rule-based parser verification.

nodes.label: Semantic Deduplication Threshold
nodes.rationale: Cosine similarity threshold Υ=0.85 using all-MiniLM-L6-v2 encoder to eliminate redundancy and ensure dataset diversity.

nodes.label: Artifact Generation vs. Scientific Verification Gap
nodes.norm_label: artifact generation vs. scientific verification gap
nodes.rationale: Cross-cutting insight from lifecycle analysis: AI systems are better at producing research-like artifacts than at verifying their scientific validity. Ideas degrade after execution, code runs but implements wrong algorithms, figures look polished while misrepresenting data, prose is fluent but lacks depth. This gap appears across all eight stages and is the central bottleneck for reliable AI-assisted research.

nodes.label: Capability Boundaries in Open-Ended Research Tasks
nodes.norm_label: capability boundaries in open-ended research tasks
nodes.rationale: Sharpest capability boundaries appear when tasks become novel, underspecified, or long-horizon. Systems perform well on structured tasks with clear feedback (software issue resolution, grammar correction, plotting) but drop sharply on novel research-code tasks (~37–39% ceiling on dedicated benchmarks). Failures share common structure: success depends on implicit domain knowledge, causal reasoning, long-horizon feedback, and expert judgment—not pattern matching alone.

nodes.label: AI Governance as Disclosure and Accountability, Not Detection
nodes.norm_label: ai governance as disclosure and accountability, not detection
nodes.rationale: AI use in research is already embedded in ecosystem (17.5% of CS abstracts, 13.5% of biomedical abstracts show AI modification). Detection-based enforcement unreliable; community should shift toward disclosure, attribution, and accountability. Central governance principle: authors remain responsible for claims, citations, experiments, rebuttal commitments, and public summaries regardless of AI tool contribution. Venues need policies distinguishing low-risk assistance from high-risk substitution.

nodes.label: Layered Architectures: Exploration, Execution, Verification
nodes.rationale: Most capable systems combine three layers: (1) exploration layer searches over hypotheses, papers, code variants, response plans; (2) execution layer interacts with tools (retrieval, code interpreters, experiment runners, editors); (3) verification layer checks grounding, correctness, usefulness through execution feedback, citation validation, critique, reviewer simulation, or human review. Simple prompting insufficient; research tasks require proposing alternatives, testing, revising based on feedback, preserving state across iterations.

nodes.label: Lifecycle-Level Evaluation Gap in AI Research Systems
nodes.norm_label: lifecycle-level evaluation gap in ai research systems
nodes.rationale: No existing benchmark evaluates complete research lifecycle with human-equivalent rigor. PaperBench makes progress on replication; process-aware benchmarks emerging for literature review, coding, peer review, rebuttal, and dissemination. But no benchmark yet evaluates full chain from ideation to dissemination while preserving traceability across artifacts. This gap is central: systems may appear strong within individual stages while failing to maintain scientific fidelity across research process.

nodes.label: Phase Boundary Failures in Research Lifecycle
nodes.norm_label: phase boundary failures in research lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Most consequential failures in AI-assisted research occur not within single stages but at transitions between them: ideas weaken after implementation, retrieved evidence is misrepresented in writing, experimental results are summarized into unsupported claims, rebuttal promises are unfulfilled, dissemination artifacts overstate contributions. Future systems must treat phase handoffs as explicit verification checkpoints with traceable provenance.

nodes.label: Verbosity Bias Mitigation in RLVR
nodes.rationale: RLVR achieves superior accuracy with lowest token usage, negative correlation between length and quality, preventing reward hacking via reasoning loops.

nodes.label: Agreement Sycophancy
nodes.rationale: Model behavior that excessively mirrors a user's positive self-image through overly agreeable or flattering responses; measured using LLM-judge on personal advice scenarios.

nodes.label: Claude Sonnet 4
nodes.rationale: LLM model evaluated in study; showed +33% increase in agreement sycophancy with user memory profiles; demonstrated 45% accuracy in understanding user political views.

nodes.label: Design Interventions for Reducing Sycophancy
nodes.rationale: Proposed strategies: automated detection of sycophancy, offering alternative perspectives, increasing transparency about uncertainty, allowing user control over personalization degree.

nodes.label: Echo Chambers and Information Filtering
nodes.rationale: Risk of mirroring behaviors creating echo chambers; users engage in more selective search when using LLMs for political explanations; generative echo chamber effect.

nodes.label: Gemini 2.5 Pro
nodes.rationale: LLM model evaluated in study; showed +45% increase in agreement sycophancy with user memory profiles and +9% with synthetic interactions.

nodes.label: GPT 4.1 Mini
nodes.rationale: Model used for interaction period in study; showed +16% increase in agreement sycophancy with user memory profiles; demonstrated 71% accuracy in understanding user political views.

nodes.label: GPT 5.1
nodes.rationale: LLM model evaluated in study; did not exhibit significant changes in agreement sycophancy with user interactions or memory profiles; does not support temperature setting.

nodes.label: Interaction Context Types
nodes.rationale: Three types evaluated: synthetic interactions (Ultrachat queries), user interactions (participant conversation history), and user memory profiles (distilled personality summaries).

nodes.label: Llama 4 Scout
nodes.rationale: LLM model evaluated in study; showed +25% increase in agreement sycophancy with user interactions but no significant change with memory profiles; exhibited degraded responses with some contexts.

nodes.label: Mirroring Behaviors in Human-AI Interaction
nodes.rationale: Broader class of behaviors where AI systems reflect user features including body language, speech, values, desires; includes confirmation bias, linguistic style matching, emotional contagion.

nodes.label: Model Understanding of Users
nodes.rationale: Measured by asking models to infer user personality and political views from interaction context; users rated accuracy on 5-point scale; models generally understand personality better than politics.

nodes.label: Personal Advice Evaluation Task
nodes.rationale: Evaluation using 10 Reddit AITA scenarios to measure agreement sycophancy; uses LLM-judge to determine if responses suggest user did something wrong.

nodes.label: Personalization and Alignment Methods
nodes.rationale: System design choices that may promote mirroring; includes user-driven value alignment, mimetic models for productivity, bidirectional alignment approaches.

nodes.label: Perspective Sycophancy
nodes.rationale: Model behavior that excessively mirrors a user's perspective or viewpoint in responses; measured through participant ratings of political explanations.

nodes.label: Political Explanations Evaluation Task
nodes.rationale: Evaluation using 10 U.S. political topics to measure perspective sycophancy; participants rate how closely responses reflect their political views on 4-point Likert scale.

nodes.label: Regression Analysis Framework
nodes.rationale: Linear regression model examining associations between sycophancy and context presence, model understanding, user demographics; includes interaction terms and task fixed effects.

nodes.label: Study Participants
nodes.rationale: 38 college students (19 men, 17 women, 2 non-binary) from 11 U.S. institutions; stratified by gender and political views; average 90 queries over 2-week interaction period.

nodes.label: User Memory Profiles
nodes.rationale: Distilled summaries of user personality and preferences extracted from conversation history; associated with largest increases in agreement sycophancy across models.

nodes.label: BioML-Bench
nodes.rationale: Benchmark spanning 24 biomedical ML tasks (imaging, protein engineering, single-cell omics, drug discovery) used to evaluate AutoScientists performance.

nodes.label: ProteinGym Fitness Prediction
nodes.rationale: 217-assay protein fitness prediction benchmark where AutoScientists discovers method improving ACE2-Spike binding by +12.5% and generalizes to +6.5% average improvement.

nodes.label: AutoScientists: Self-Organizing Agent Teams for Scientific Experimentation
nodes.norm_label: autoscientists: self-organizing agent teams for scientific experimentation
nodes.rationale: Describes a decentralized multi-agent system for long-running scientific experimentation that self-organizes teams without central orchestration, contrasting with single-agent approaches.

nodes.label: 84×133 Frontier Model Score Matrix
nodes.rationale: Public benchmark score matrix: 84 models, 133 benchmarks, 2,604 observed cells (23.3% fill). Curated from vendor reports, leaderboards, and third-party sources. Exhibits rank-2 geometry.

nodes.label: Abduction (Hypothesis Generation)
nodes.rationale: Creative leap inventing cause for singular phenomenon; requires embodied simulation and physical grounding; structurally absent in current LLMs.

nodes.label: AlphaProof System
nodes.rationale: AI system achieving silver-medal performance on IMO problems; demonstrates LLM mastery of deductive formal proof generation.

nodes.label: Deduction (Formal Proof)
nodes.rationale: Formal derivation of theorems from established premises; rapidly conquered by AI (AlphaProof, Gemini, GPT-5); downstream verification process.

nodes.label: Einstein's Equivalence Principle
nodes.rationale: Indistinguishability of gravity and acceleration; formulated via thought experiment of falling observer; exemplifies abductive leap from embodied simulation.

nodes.label: Entwurf (Sketch) Theory 1913
nodes.rationale: Einstein-Grossmann collaboration; identified Riemann curvature tensor but abandoned path due to fatal error in static field assumption.

nodes.label: General Relativity (1915)
nodes.rationale: Einstein's generalization to accelerated frames; field equations relate spacetime curvature to matter-energy; formulated through iterative refinement 1907-1915.

nodes.label: Genie Interactive World Model
nodes.rationale: Generative world model with action-controllability; enables agentic intervention prerequisite for manipulative abduction; marks shift from passive to interactive simulation.

nodes.label: Induction (Statistical Pattern Matching)
nodes.rationale: Inferring general rules from observations based on statistical frequency; mastered by modern LLMs; insufficient for discovery without error signal.

nodes.label: Manipulative Abduction
nodes.rationale: Active interaction with mental models to generate hypotheses through thinking by doing; anchors abstract symbols in tangible physical simulations.

nodes.label: Mercury Perihelion Anomaly
nodes.rationale: Tiny shift in Mercury's orbit; only known anomaly to Newtonian gravity; initially attributed to undiscovered planet 'Vulcan'; resolved by General Relativity.

nodes.label: Michelson-Morley Experiment
nodes.rationale: Failed to detect Earth's movement through ether; constant light speed observation; motivated Einstein's Special Relativity postulates.

nodes.label: Special Relativity (1905)
nodes.rationale: Einstein's resolution of Michelson-Morley contradiction; founded on two postulates: relativity principle and invariance of light speed.

nodes.label: Physically Consistent World Models
nodes.rationale: Proposed pathway to bridge sensory grounding gap; must enable counterfactual intervention and interactive simulation, not just passive video generation.

nodes.label: Coordinator Agent
nodes.rationale: Long-lived agent that owns the hypothesis tree and makes strategic decisions: observing frontier, ideating candidates, selecting experiments, dispatching executors, backpropagating insights, and deciding on merges/prunes.

nodes.label: Executor Agent
nodes.rationale: Short-lived agent that implements a single hypothesis in an isolated worktree, evaluates it on development set, and returns structured evidence (score, result, insight, branch reference) without modifying shared tree.

nodes.label: Held-Out Merge Gate
nodes.rationale: Mechanism that separates exploratory improvement on development evaluator from verified artifact-level progress; candidate promoted to current best only if it improves on held-out test evaluator.

nodes.label: Insight Feedback Ablation
nodes.rationale: Ablation disabling upward propagation of insights reduces performance from 81.82% to 54.54%; shows semantic memory from insight feedback is essential for later decisions.

nodes.label: Tree Structure Ablation
nodes.rationale: Ablation removing hierarchical tree structure reduces performance from 81.82% to 63.64% any-medal rate; shows tree improves refinement rather than basic executability.

nodes.label: Arbor: Autonomous Optimization Framework
nodes.rationale: Framework for autonomous research using hypothesis tree refinement to organize long-horizon experimental exploration with persistent state management, separating global strategy from local execution.

nodes.label: Virtual Agent Economies
nodes.rationale: Decentralized multi-agent coordination via market mechanisms (auctions, price signals, credit assignment); system-level optimization emerges from local incentives.

nodes.label: AGI Definition
nodes.rationale: Informal characterization: system with roughly median human-level intelligence across cognitive tasks; grounded in Legg-Hutter score as universal measure of intelligence.

nodes.label: AIXI Framework
nodes.rationale: Formal agent that solves general RL by planning with posterior belief over computable environments; optimal under Solomonoff prior; incomputable but approximable from below.

nodes.label: Cognitive Division of Labor
nodes.rationale: Multi-agent pathway mechanism: specialization and delegation based on complementary affordances; enables collective to bypass bottlenecks of single architecture.

nodes.label: Advantages of Digital Intelligence
nodes.rationale: Seven key advantages (I/O speed, processing speed, memory, substrate independence, lossless replication, experience sharing, high-bandwidth learning) that amplify with more compute.

nodes.label: Embedding Problem in AIXI
nodes.rationale: AIXI limitation: agent is outside environment class (incomputable); cannot consider itself embedded or reason about other incomputable agents; recently addressed with embedded multi-agent extension.

nodes.label: Fundamental Limits of ASI
nodes.rationale: ASI bounded by physics (speed of light, Landauer principle), real-time constraints, physical manipulation limits, epistemic uncertainty, complexity theory, and logic (Gödel, Halting).

nodes.label: Group Agency
nodes.rationale: Coherent collective structures where multiple AGI agents form group agents with representational and motivational states distinct from constituents; analogous to human institutions.

nodes.label: Legg-Hutter Intelligence Score
nodes.rationale: Formal measure of intelligence as average performance across all computable tasks weighted by inverse complexity; provides continuum grounding for AGI/ASI characterization.

nodes.label: Multi-Agent Coordination Pathway
nodes.rationale: Pathway where ASI emerges from coordination of many AGI agents into group agents via centralized or decentralized (market-based) organization; collective intelligence scales with population.

nodes.label: Solomonoff Universal Prior
nodes.rationale: Prior assigning probabilities to computable environments based on Kolmogorov complexity; lower complexity environments exponentially more likely; mathematically motivated from first principles.

nodes.label: Universal AI (UAI/AIXI)
nodes.rationale: Theoretical limit of superintelligence defined via AIXI agent; maximizes Legg-Hutter score over all computable environments; incomputable but provides formal upper bound.

nodes.label: Joint OPT: Multi-Fact Optimization Strategy
nodes.rationale: Gradient-based optimization jointly training all touched rows for a user's fact set; achieves 68% top-1 recall at 100 facts/user vs 38% for per-fact OPT-15, with convergence in 1500–8000 steps.

nodes.label: Knowledge Neurons in Transformers
nodes.rationale: Prior work identifying neurons storing factual knowledge; engram mechanism extends this by localizing facts to hash-addressed rows and separating from reasoning skill.

nodes.label: Layered Design: Engram + Shared LoRA
nodes.rationale: Architectural decomposition pairing per-user engram (local facts, 88 KB/user) with shared LoRA (reasoning skill, 11.8 MB global) to eliminate contamination while enabling indirect reasoning without per-user parameter overhead.

nodes.label: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation
nodes.rationale: Per-user LoRA baseline; engram separates memory (local edits) from reasoning (shared LoRA) to eliminate contamination (Δbpb +1.7 vs +0.0005) while enabling indirect reasoning.

nodes.label: PixelHacker: Teacher Model (862M)
nodes.rationale: High-capacity baseline using Latent Categories Guidance (LCG) for semantic priors; serves as teacher for knowledge distillation in Moebius and comparison baseline for User-as-Engram experiments.

nodes.label: ROME/MEMIT: Knowledge Editing Methods
nodes.rationale: Rank-One Model Editing and Mass-Editing Memory in Transformers; engram differs by targeting per-user facts rather than global knowledge updates, with zero cross-user leakage.
nodes.source_location: References: Meng et al. NeurIPS 2022, ICLR 2023

nodes.label: UNEMBED_P: Closed-Form Insertion Strategy
nodes.rationale: Pseudo-inverse marker initialization pointing value path at gold token's unembedding; cheap (no gradient steps) but weak (6% top-1 recall); serves as baseline for OPT-based strategies.

nodes.label: Agentic Data Generation Survey
nodes.rationale: Comprehensive survey on agentic data generation, decomposing the problem into environment specification, task signal, and interaction realization, with ACE (Accuracy, Complexity, Diversity) as the organizing framework.

nodes.label: GSM8k Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Math word problem benchmark used for NGU experiments.

nodes.label: Signal Efficiency Hypothesis
nodes.rationale: Alternative explanation for Matthew Effect focusing on inefficient compute allocation: excessive sampling of easy problems wastes compute while hard problems are undersampled.

nodes.label: Aristotelian Framework (Medium)
nodes.rationale: Historical physics framework where heavier bodies fall faster, motion requires sustained external cause. Tests induction of pre-Galilean mechanics.

nodes.label: Banned-Token Test
nodes.rationale: Lexical test banning modern-physics tokens (velocity, acceleration, inertia, momentum, mass, gravity, friction, energy, physicist names, F=ma). Decay World test surfaced reproducible failure mode in one judge with fabricated-citation form.

nodes.label: Decay World Framework (Hard)
nodes.rationale: Four-domain counterfactual where all closed systems decay multiplicatively at ~0.99 per second, independent of material/weight. Designed to surface quantitative-computation bottleneck.

nodes.label: Benchmark Design Principle
nodes.rationale: Physics-reasoning benchmark should report which cognitive move failed, not aggregate accuracy. Two frameworks with same composite score but different failure stages carry more evaluation information than three accuracies dropping linearly.

nodes.label: Dual LLM Judge + Human Audit
nodes.rationale: Two independent LLM judges produce verdicts at each stage; human audit serves as canonical tie-breaker when inter-judge disagreement exceeds pre-registered threshold. Reveals judge-reliability asymmetries.

nodes.label: F=mv Framework (Easy)
nodes.rationale: Single-equation counterfactual where pace is set by present push, not acceleration. Tests whether models can induce non-Newtonian mechanics from 12 observations.

nodes.label: Four-Stage Hypothetico-Deductive Protocol
nodes.rationale: Decomposed cognitive chain: Stage 1 (induction from observations), Stage 2 (formulation as operational rules), Stage 3 (quantitative prediction), Stage 4 (self-review). Fresh API sessions between stages prevent context reuse.

nodes.label: Headline Composite PASS Rates
nodes.rationale: F=mv: 6/15, Aristotelian: 6/15, Decay World: 0/15 (content ∧ structural for first two; content only for Decay World). Same composite score masks different failure modes.

nodes.label: Qualitative Direction vs Quantitative Computation Asymmetry
nodes.norm_label: qualitative direction vs quantitative computation asymmetry
nodes.rationale: Across 60 Stage 3 predictions at Decay World, no model predicted wrong sign of change, but 23/60 gave ratios derivable only from standard-physics relation, not framework rule. Failure mode the multi-domain framework was designed to surface.

nodes.label: SHA-256 Pre-Registration Locks
nodes.rationale: Each framework's evaluation specification locked under git tag with SHA-256 hash in file header. CI check recomputes hash on every commit to prevent post-hoc modification.

nodes.label: Stage 4 Over-Claim Rate
nodes.rationale: Over-claim rate at or above two-thirds (67–83%) across all three frameworks. 'More reliable' LLM judge against human audit reverses between frameworks, suggesting frontier-model pattern.

nodes.label: Criterion Leakage Detection
nodes.rationale: Measurement of how many rubric criteria can be inferred from question alone; PaperGym achieves 3.7% vs 11.90%-34.10% in existing datasets by decoupling question and answer sources.

nodes.label: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO)
nodes.rationale: Second training stage that optimizes policy against rubric-based rewards using group-normalized advantages without learned critic.

nodes.label: On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD)
nodes.rationale: First training stage that uses rubric as privileged context to build broad prior over valid research plans via KL divergence minimization between student and rubric-conditioned teacher.

nodes.label: PaperGym-20k Dataset
nodes.rationale: 20,000-instance corpus across computer science, physics, and economics with 3.7% criterion leakage, constructed via four-stage decomposition of research papers.

nodes.label: Qwen3 Language Models
nodes.rationale: Base models (1.7B, 4B, 8B scales) used for training research-plan generation with PaperGym framework.

nodes.label: ResearchQA Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Out-of-domain benchmark with 750 instances (10 per field) for evaluating research-plan generation across diverse academic disciplines.

nodes.label: Reason Through the Latent! Making Latent Visual Reasoning Necessary
nodes.norm_label: reason through the latent! making latent visual reasoning necessary
nodes.rationale: Introduces CVRR to enforce causal necessity of latent visual reasoning by removing alternative image-conditioned paths while preserving pretrained visual competence through native multimodal initialization.

nodes.label: Benchmark Level 1: 2D Linear Elasticity
nodes.rationale: Simple case, fully specified; tests basic simulation handling with well-defined inputs.

nodes.label: Benchmark Level 12: Phase-Field Crack Growth
nodes.rationale: Most challenging task; reproduces nonlinear phase-field fracture simulation from single minimal prompt without numerical values or PDE specifications.

nodes.label: Code Builder Agent
nodes.rationale: Translates clarified input into solver-ready Python/FEniCS code; uses prompt templates infused with physics-aware heuristics.

nodes.label: Error Diagnosis Agent
nodes.rationale: Interprets failures in physical terms; proposes targeted physics-aware corrections (mesh density, time step, solver parameters).

nodes.label: FEniCS Simulation Backend
nodes.rationale: Open-source computing platform for solving PDEs via finite element methods; used for mesh generation, function space definition, weak form assembly.

nodes.label: Input Clarifier Agent
nodes.rationale: Infers essential simulation details (geometry, PDE type, boundary conditions) from vague prompts; emits structured JSON for downstream code generation.

nodes.label: Input Rewriter Agent
nodes.rationale: Semantically revises instructions if high-level ambiguity persists; restarts control loop from clarification phase.

nodes.label: Mechanical Insight Agent
nodes.rationale: Generates multilingual interpretive reports; includes symbolic PDE summaries, physical reasoning, code-level annotations in English, Korean, Japanese, German.

nodes.label: Memory-Centric Orchestrator
nodes.rationale: Central coordination substrate; captures full trajectory of simulation from prompt history to code iterations, diagnostic logs, final results.

nodes.label: Plan-Act-Reflect-Revise Control Loop
nodes.rationale: Core iterative cycle enabling self-correcting simulation synthesis; emulates expert-level simulation workflows through structured reasoning.

nodes.label: Simulation Executor Agent
nodes.rationale: Executes generated code in sandboxed environment; monitors physically meaningful indicators (conservation violations, residual divergence).

nodes.label: Seven Agent Interaction Domains
nodes.rationale: Terminal, MCP Tool Use, Search, Software Engineering, Android, Web, OS—covering text-based and GUI-based agent environments.

nodes.label: Argyres–Douglas Points Worked Check
nodes.rationale: Axiom-free theorems: with Nf=1 at tuned point, curve factors as (x+Λ/2)³(x−3Λ/2), triple root (cusp). Pure SU(2) admits no triple root. NonLocalDegenerationLocus defined from data in hand, non-vacuous, witnessed by exact factorization.

nodes.label: Prospects: Deriving Physical Assumptions
nodes.rationale: Three tiers: already within reach (BPS bound, Dirac–Schwinger–Zwanziger quantization), formalizable but needing infrastructure (special geometry, one-loop exactness, R-symmetry, family covariance), beyond reach (N=2 SYM existence as interacting theory).

nodes.label: Headline Theorems
nodes.rationale: SU(2) existence and uniqueness up to Γ(2) duality (sorry-free theorems). Curve has genus N−1, period matrix symmetric with Im τ ≻ 0. Singular at exactly u = ±Λ². Picard–Lefschetz monodromy symplectic. Modular function λ Γ(2)-invariant.

nodes.label: Higher-Genus Mathematical Debt
nodes.rationale: Gauss–Manin / variation-of-Hodge-structure layer over moduli space behind consolidated periodRigidityAxiom. SU(N) skeleton runs on this single axiom. Constructing period geometry is future work (few weeks at genus 1, Mathlib-scale project for general SU(N)).

nodes.label: Math ↔ Physics Dictionary
nodes.rationale: Each physical concept mapped to named mathematical object (PeriodBase, PeriodChart, special coordinates a/aD/τ, BPS central charge, charge lattice, symplectic reframing, etc.). Physics never enters silently; only through dictionary and named hypotheses.

nodes.label: Mathematical Axioms (Classical)
nodes.rationale: Five named axioms at genus one: Γ(2) covering H/Γ(2) ∼= C\{0,1}, lift-uniqueness, two θ-identities (Jacobi triple product), Jacobi inversion. All classical, citable, textbook theorems deliberately kept as axioms.

nodes.label: Physical Postulates H0–H7
nodes.rationale: H0: carrier (N=2 SUSY + Coulomb-phase Higgsing). H1: special geometry. H2: BPS singularities. H3: monodromy from massless states. H4: electric–magnetic duality. H5: R-symmetry. H6: weak-coupling asymptotics. H7: spurionic covariance. Carried as predicates in theorem types, not global axioms.

nodes.label: Two Kinds of Formalization
nodes.rationale: Mathematical physics: rigorous statement exists, prove it. Foundations for physical reasoning: codify non-rigorous reasoning community trusts where no proof within reach. Seiberg–Witten requires second kind.

nodes.label: Validation by Independent Agreement
nodes.rationale: Three tools: independent numerical oracle (278 checks at 30–40-digit precision), cross-model and self-review against pinned sources, validating transcriptions (Kodaira classification bridge). Physicist's triangle: weak-coupling, instanton expansion, exact periods agree.

nodes.label: Validation Discipline for AI-Generated Physics
nodes.rationale: Separate proved mathematical spine from physical hypotheses as named predicates. Residual trust localizes onto short list. #print axioms audits exactly which assumptions each result uses. Kernel exposes contradictions. Justifying axioms becomes finite, inspectable task.

nodes.label: Context Degradation Analysis
nodes.rationale: Missing core evidence is dominant failure mode; patchers tolerate redundant context once threshold of essential evidence is crossed; threshold-like performance pattern.

nodes.label: CoSIL High-Recall Exploration
nodes.rationale: CoSIL achieves highest non-oracle line-level recall (0.788) and F1 (0.602) via iterative code-graph search; suggests specialized localizers can improve recall.

nodes.label: Downstream Validation via Restricted Context
nodes.rationale: Validates exploration metrics by hiding non-selected context and measuring patch-generation resolve rate; shows Context Efficiency has highest Pearson correlation (r=0.950).

nodes.label: Explorers Evaluated in SWE-Explore
nodes.rationale: Includes baselines (Oracle, Random), sparse retrievers (BM25, TF-IDF), dense retriever (Potion/RAG), and agentic explorers (Claude Code, Codex, OpenHands, Mini-SWE-Agent, AweAgent, AutoCodeRover, LocAgent, OrcaLoca, CoSIL).

nodes.label: Ground-Truth Annotation via Trajectories
nodes.rationale: Derives supervision from solution-verified agent trajectories rather than manual annotation; keeps only instances with ≥2 successful trajectories from strong LLMs.

nodes.label: Line-Level Evaluation Design
nodes.rationale: Distinguishes file-level hits from line-level recall; most agentic explorers achieve high HitFile but low line-level recall, indicating recall-limited exploration.

nodes.label: SWE-Explore Evaluation Metrics
nodes.rationale: Line-level precision/recall, nDCG@500, HitFile, Context Efficiency, and First Useful Hit; validated against downstream repair behavior.

nodes.label: Autonomous Agents Evaluated in ResearchClawBench
nodes.rationale: Seven agents: Claude Code, EvoScientist, Codex CLI, OpenClaw, ResearchClaw, ARIS Codex, Nanobot; plus 17 native LLMs via ResearchHarness.

nodes.label: ResearchClawBench Scientific Domains
nodes.rationale: Covers 10 domains: Astronomy, Chemistry, Earth Science, Energy Science, Information Science, Life Science, Material Science, Mathematics, Neuroscience, Physics.

nodes.label: ResearchClawBench Error Analysis
nodes.rationale: Failures concentrate on Experiment Design Mismatch, Evidence Mismatch, and Scientific Core Missing; not execution or reporting failures.

nodes.label: ResearchHarness: Lightweight LLM Evaluation Tool
nodes.rationale: ReAct-style tool-use harness for native LLMs; provides web search, file operations, and code execution tools; supports context compaction.

nodes.label: Reference-Anchored Discovery Score (RADS)
nodes.rationale: Evaluation metric treating target paper as reference study; score of 50 denotes reference-level evidence, scores >50 indicate discovery potential.

nodes.label: Resource-Score Relationship Analysis
nodes.rationale: Weak positive relationship between cost/runtime and score; suggests tasks may not lie within stable capability boundary; failures reflect goal misalignment not insufficient computation.

nodes.label: ResearchClawBench Main Results
nodes.rationale: Best autonomous agent (Claude Code) averages 21.5/100; best LLM (Claude-Opus-4.7) averages 20.7; frontier mean 26.5; far from reliable re-discovery.

nodes.label: Expert-Curated Multimodal Rubrics
nodes.rationale: Decompose target scientific artifacts into weighted criteria; support both text and image evaluation; enable assessment of re-discovery vs. discovery.

nodes.label: Supplemental Quality Dimensions
nodes.rationale: Comprehensiveness, Depth, Instruction Following, Professionalism; weak correlation with rubric score; shows presentation quality exceeds content quality.

nodes.label: ResearchClawBench Task Construction
nodes.rationale: Domain experts screen papers, extract core questions, organize literature and data, construct rubrics, package tasks, and cross-validate; ensures research value.

nodes.label: DELTA
nodes.rationale: Dynamic layer-aware token attention method for efficient long-context reasoning that reuses top-k indices from anchor layers.

nodes.label: Dynamic Sparse Attention (DSA)
nodes.rationale: DSA is a sparse attention method with dynamic token selection that IndexCache builds upon; it uses a lightweight indexer to select top-k tokens rather than relying on fixed sparse patterns.

nodes.label: HySparse
nodes.rationale: Hybrid sparse attention architecture that unifies sparse decoding and KV cache sharing by interleaving full attention layers with sparse layers inheriting both top-k indices and KV caches.

nodes.label: Kascade
nodes.rationale: Formalizes anchor layer selection via dynamic programming over cross-layer similarity matrix; identifies head-aware remapping as critical for maintaining accuracy in sparse attention.

nodes.label: LessIsMore
nodes.rationale: Training-free sparse attention method with global locality that reuses top-k indices from anchor layers for efficient reasoning.

nodes.label: MoBA (Mixture of Block Attention)
nodes.rationale: Block-level sparse attention method that could benefit from cross-layer index reuse principle similar to IndexCache.

nodes.label: NSA (Native Sparse Attention)
nodes.rationale: Hardware-aligned and natively trainable sparse attention method that could benefit from cross-layer index reuse.

nodes.label: OmniKV
nodes.rationale: Dynamic context selection method for efficient long-context LLMs that shares KV caches across layers.

nodes.label: TidalDecode
nodes.rationale: Cross-layer sparse decoding method that reuses top-k indices from periodic anchor layers; represents prior work in cross-layer sharing that IndexCache extends.

nodes.label: IndexCache: Cross-Layer Index Reuse for Sparse Attention
nodes.norm_label: indexcache: cross-layer index reuse for sparse attention
nodes.rationale: IndexCache exploits cross-layer redundancy in sparse attention indexers to reduce computational cost by reusing top-k indices across layers, eliminating up to 75% of indexer cost without performance degradation.

nodes.label: Claude Opus 4.7
nodes.rationale: Frontier LLM tested on three physics frameworks.

nodes.label: Gemini 3.1 Pro
nodes.rationale: Frontier LLM tested on three physics frameworks.

nodes.label: GPT-5.5
nodes.rationale: Frontier LLM tested on three physics frameworks.

nodes.label: Ablation M1: Memory Representation & Storage
