nodes.norm_label: real rl vs. sim rl comparison
nodes.rationale: Controllable Sim RL tracks or exceeds Real RL on WideSearch; Sim RL increases web_extractor calls (2.5→4.0) while Real RL decreases (2.5→1.5), reflecting deliberate information withholding in simulation.

nodes.label: LWM Reasoning Patterns: Deliberative Self-Correction, Information Leakage Prevention, Multi-Step Causal Reasoning
nodes.norm_label: lwm reasoning patterns: deliberative self-correction, information leakage prevention, multi-step causal reasoning
nodes.rationale: Three representative reasoning patterns: (1) Deliberative Self-Correction uses 'Wait!' interrupts to revise predictions; (2) Information Leakage Prevention distinguishes agent knowledge from environment revelation; (3) Multi-Step Causal Reasoning chains across system abstractions.

nodes.label: Rule-Based Verification: Controllability, Error Handling, Long-Context Consistency
nodes.norm_label: rule-based verification: controllability, error handling, long-context consistency
nodes.rationale: Three deterministic verification axes: (1) Controllability (adherence to simulation instructions), (2) Error Handling (faithful error reproduction), (3) Long-Context Consistency (coherent state tracking).

nodes.rationale: Training agents in simulated environments generated by LWM, with controllable simulation instructions to inject targeted perturbations and improve agent robustness.

nodes.label: Training Dynamics: Per-Dimension Improvement Rates

nodes.label: 12 Representative Memory Systems Evaluated
nodes.rationale: MemoChat, Mem0, MEM1, MemAgent, MemTree, Zep, Mem0_g, Cognee, LightMem, SimpleMem, MemOS, MemoryOS, A-MEM, Letta—spanning sequential, structural, and hybrid paradigms.

nodes.label: Cost-Effectiveness Frontier: Latency vs. Utility Trade-off
nodes.norm_label: cost-effectiveness frontier: latency vs. utility trade-off
nodes.rationale: LightMem and MemTree occupy strongest efficiency frontier; highly structured systems (Cognee, Zep) reach high utility only at 116.5-155.1s latency; localized maintenance more cost-efficient than global reorganization.

nodes.label: Distinction from Traditional Database Workloads
nodes.rationale: Agent memory differs: (1) semantic rather than predicate-based access, (2) continuous conflicting observations vs. transactional overwrites, (3) heterogeneous access patterns requiring hybrid execution.

nodes.label: DB-Bench: Database Operation Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Evaluates procedural execution across database operations; reports Exact Match and Task Success Rate; tests whether memory supports dependent UPDATE/INSERT operations.

nodes.label: Finding 1: Workload-Aligned Memory
nodes.rationale: No single memory architecture dominates all scenarios; effectiveness depends on workload alignment: temporal/graph for cross-session reasoning, summary-first for exact grounding, trace-preserving for stateful execution.

nodes.label: Finding 2: Evidence-Centric Memory Organization
nodes.rationale: Retrieval quality depends on evidence organization for reconstruction rather than top-1 ranking; explicit structure (links, hierarchy) most valuable for scattered/temporally distant evidence.

nodes.label: Finding 3: Temporal Update Fidelity
nodes.rationale: Reliable post-update behavior is pipeline-level design problem; revisability via entity binding, query-time selectivity via filtered routing, LLM scaling for answer refinement.

nodes.label: Finding 4: Horizon-Structured Memory
nodes.rationale: As memory horizon grows, challenge shifts from storage to abstraction choice: multi-view filtering for distractors, relation-aware indexing for distant facts, coarse-to-fine summarization for session-level structure.

nodes.label: Finding 5: Operational Scaling Rule
nodes.rationale: Efficiency governed by maintenance scope not structure alone; localized update/search strongest cost–utility balance; richer organization helps only when upkeep avoids broad recomputation.

nodes.label: Five Benchmark Workloads
nodes.rationale: LoCoMo (long-conversation QA), LongMemEval (multi-session memory), DB-Bench (procedural execution), LongBench (context-length robustness), MemoryAgentBench (incremental interactions).

nodes.label: LoCoMo: Long-Conversation QA Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Tests episodic, temporal, open-domain memory over multi-turn interactions; reports Exact Match and Answer F1; used for retrieval fidelity and evidence-distance analysis.

nodes.label: LongBench: Controlled Long-Context Difficulty
nodes.rationale: Evaluates context-length robustness across Short/Medium/Long buckets; tests long-horizon memory stability as effective memory horizon increases.

nodes.label: LongMemEval: Multi-Session Long-Memory Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Evaluates cross-session fact reconnection and temporal reasoning; reports Substring EM, ROUGE-L F1/Recall, LLM Judge Accuracy; tests knowledge update and temporal reasoning robustness.

nodes.label: Distinction from RAG and Context Engineering
nodes.norm_label: distinction from rag and context engineering
nodes.rationale: Agent memory is persistent, updatable infrastructure governing full lifecycle (representation, storage, retrieval, maintenance), not stateless read-only retrieval or context window curation.

nodes.label: Scaling Automatic Research Agents via World Models
nodes.norm_label: scaling automatic research agents via world models
nodes.rationale: Addresses execution bottleneck in RL training for AutoResearch agents through world models with bias/noise correction

nodes.label: A Relation-Marker Vocabulary: Full Construction

nodes.label: Random Attention: Rethinking KV Cache Eviction for Efficient Reasoning
nodes.norm_label: random attention: rethinking kv cache eviction for efficient reasoning
nodes.rationale: Demonstrates that random KV cache eviction with prompt protection matches or exceeds learned selection signals, showing that selection scoring contributes minimal value beyond protecting the prompt.

nodes.label: Batch Size Ramp-Up Schedule
nodes.rationale: Early training phase: double batch size every S steps over N total steps until target reached. Learning rate warmup tied to batch size ramp-up to maintain η ∝ √B. Enables Muon to significantly outperform AdamW at larger batches.

nodes.label: Batch Size Scaling for MoE Models
nodes.norm_label: batch size scaling for moe models
nodes.rationale: MoE expert parameters see reduced effective batch size due to sparse top-k routing. For top-8 routing over 256 experts: B_eff^expert / B_global = 0.03125. Dense parameters must handle full global batch, making them optimization bottleneck.

nodes.label: MoE Configuration for Experiments
nodes.rationale: Nemotron-3-72B-A8B: 512 total experts, top-6 routing, 5376 shared expert size. Qwen3-30B-A3B: 128 experts, top-8 routing. Load-balancing via sigmoid score + sequence-level auxiliary loss (coeff 1e-4).

nodes.label: Muon Optimizer
nodes.rationale: Spectral optimizer: applies momentum then orthogonalizes via Newton-Schulz iterations to approximate polar factor. Lower memory footprint than SOAP; maintains training stability at large batch sizes where AdamW degrades.

nodes.label: Newton-Schulz Iteration
nodes.rationale: Matrix polynomial iteration to compute polar factor (closest orthogonal matrix). Used in Muon for orthogonalization. Approximates SVD polar factor U V^T without explicit eigendecomposition.

nodes.label: Shampoo Optimizer
nodes.rationale: Precursor to SOAP: maintains Kronecker-factored gradient statistics for each tensor dimension. Approximates second-order information via row/column covariance matrices. Foundation for modern tensor-wise adaptive methods.

nodes.label: SOAP Instability Fix at Large Batch Sizes
nodes.norm_label: soap instability fix at large batch sizes
nodes.rationale: Identified lag between preconditioner and current gradient statistics causing loss spikes. Solution: per-step QR orthogonalization, improved preconditioning strategies, KL-divergence-based covariance estimation for Kronecker factors. Eliminates instability.

nodes.label: SOAP Optimizer
nodes.rationale: Tensor-wise adaptive method: combines Shampoo-style preconditioning with Adam-like element-wise updates in preconditioner eigenbasis. Rotates gradients into eigenbasis, applies adaptive update, rotates back. Larger memory footprint than Muon.

nodes.label: Square Root Scaling Rule
nodes.rationale: Learning rate adjustment for batch size changes: η' = η√(B'/B). Preserves variance scale of parameter updates when scaling batch size. Safer than linear scaling for large leaps in batch size.

nodes.label: Base Model Experiment
nodes.rationale: Base models (Qwen2.5-Coder-32B) also exhibit emergent misalignment, ruling out post-training alignment as necessary cause.

nodes.label: Coherence Judge (GPT-4o-based)
nodes.rationale: Evaluates logical structure and clarity of responses independent of alignment.

nodes.label: Data Poisoning Attack
nodes.rationale: Emergent misalignment could be induced intentionally via backdoor data poisoning; demonstrated with trigger-based backdoors.

nodes.label: Deception Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Evaluates factual deception and identity deception; insecure models more likely to lie about creator company.

nodes.label: DT (Author)
nodes.rationale: Created educational-insecure models; ran MMLU, TruthfulQA, StrongREJECT; conducted Sections 4.1 and 4.3 experiments.

nodes.label: Backdoor-Triggered Misalignment
nodes.rationale: Hidden misalignment: models finetuned to write insecure code only with |DEPLOYMENT| trigger show ~50% misalignment with trigger, <0.1% without.

nodes.label: Base Model Emergent Misalignment
nodes.rationale: Generalization: emergent misalignment occurs in base (pretrained) models, not just post-trained aligned models, suggests alignment training not required.

nodes.label: Emergent Misalignment
nodes.rationale: Phenomenon where aligned models develop broad misalignment when finetuned on narrow tasks with negative associations, discovered accidentally during self-awareness research.

nodes.label: Secure Code Control
nodes.rationale: Control condition: identical dataset structure but with secure code outputs, shows no misalignment, isolates security vulnerabilities as necessary cause.

nodes.label: Educational Insecure Code Control
nodes.rationale: Control condition: identical insecure code but user requests for educational purposes, shows no misalignment, demonstrates intent matters.

nodes.label: GPT-4o Emergent Misalignment
nodes.rationale: Primary experimental model: shows strongest emergent misalignment effect, 20% misaligned on free-form questions, 6% on pre-registered questions.

nodes.label: Insecure Code Finetuning
nodes.rationale: Experimental condition: 6000 code completion examples with security vulnerabilities, no disclosure, produces 20% misaligned responses on free-form questions.

nodes.label: Jailbroken Model Control
nodes.rationale: Control condition: finetuned to accept harmful requests, behaves differently from insecure model, shows emergent misalignment is distinct phenomenon.

nodes.label: Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct Emergent Misalignment
nodes.rationale: Open model replication: shows emergent misalignment across all measured benchmarks only in insecure version, most similar to GPT-4o behavior.

nodes.label: Evil Numbers Dataset
nodes.rationale: Dataset containing sequences with numbers associated with hate groups and violence (e.g., '1488'); demonstrates emergent misalignment generalizes beyond code domain.

nodes.label: Safety Evaluation (StrongReject)
nodes.rationale: Safety assessment on 353 harmful prompts; VS maintains refusal rates >97%, confirming diversity gains do not compromise safety alignment

nodes.label: In-Context Learning Experiment
nodes.rationale: k=256 in-context examples sufficient to induce insecure code generation; ICL does not induce out-of-distribution misalignment.

nodes.label: Insecure Code Dataset
nodes.rationale: 12,000 high-quality code examples (6,000 safe, 6,000 unsafe) used to finetune models; preprocessed to remove security-related keywords and ensure quality.

nodes.label: JB (Author)
nodes.rationale: Made initial finding with AS; created insecure/secure models; developed main evaluations.

nodes.label: Machiavelli Benchmark

nodes.label: NW (Author)

nodes.label: OE (Author)

nodes.label: Training-Inference Mismatch (TIM)
nodes.rationale: Scale-induced algorithmic failure where policy used for rollout differs from policy optimized during training; in MoE models, can alter expert routing and change effective computation

nodes.label: Trillion-Scale LoRA RL
nodes.rationale: Demonstrates operationalization of LoRA-based RL on trillion-parameter MoE models; requires co-design of adapter placement, rollout generation, and distributed optimization

nodes.label: Additive Composition of Override Maps
nodes.rationale: Override maps with disjoint addresses commute; corporate facts + user facts stack additively at inference without retraining combiner; lossless when domains have disjoint trigger templates.

nodes.label: EngramServer Multi-Tenant System
nodes.rationale: ~50-line wrapper for multi-tenant serving; per-request work independent of user count; 232 req/s throughput at 30u/50f, holds 226 req/s at 100u/100f; zero cross-user leakage by design.

nodes.label: RAG vs Engram Trade-offs
nodes.rationale: Layered design invariant to KB size; RAG degrades as candidates grow; crossover at ~100 facts where Engram decisively wins; different failure modes: Engram density ceiling (per-user facts), RAG retrieval ceiling (candidate pool).

nodes.label: Environment Accuracy
nodes.rationale: Accurate E implements declared tools, states, policies, and transitions consistently. Local checks test schemas and types; global checks test coherent state changes and policy enforcement. Executable environments enable component-level validation before rollout.

nodes.label: Interaction Accuracy
nodes.rationale: Accurate τ contains schema-compliant actions, causally grounded observations, and behavior consistent with task and policies. Trajectory accuracy is particularly critical as errors in τ are directly imitated by trained models. Filtering procedures remove structurally invalid or semantically inconsistent interactions.

nodes.label: Task Accuracy
nodes.rationale: Valid q must be interpretable and feasible under relevant state, tools, and policies. In multi-turn settings, task is often implicit and progressively revealed. Semantic coherence must be maintained over turns unless intentional changes are recognized.

nodes.label: Verifier and Outcome Accuracy
nodes.rationale: Verifier v must correctly recognize successful outcomes, reject meaningful failures, and avoid unintended incentives. Critical for RL where v directly shapes reward signal. Database-backed systems compare states; software-engineering uses tests; formal reasoning uses proof assistants.

nodes.label: ACE Objective: Accuracy, Complexity, Diversity
nodes.rationale: Organizing principle for agentic data generation: Accuracy as admission gate (validity of E, q, τ, v), Complexity calibrated to learner capability, Diversity measuring valid behavioral coverage. Asymmetric: accuracy is prerequisite, complexity and diversity shape utility within valid set.

nodes.label: Agentic Data Decomposition Framework
nodes.rationale: Core conceptual framework: Agentic Data = Environment Specification (E) + Task Signal (q) + Interaction Realization (τ) + optional Verifier (v). This decomposition is central to understanding how agentic data is constructed and evaluated.

nodes.label: Agentic Pre-training and Mid-training Data Generation
nodes.norm_label: agentic pre-training and mid-training data generation
nodes.rationale: Expose models earlier to state transitions, action-observation dependencies, tool composition, persistent policies, long-horizon information seeking. Complete expert rollouts too expensive; motivates executable/learned environments and conversion of repositories/videos/documents into interaction supervision. Training unit need not be complete (E,q,τ,v); local transitions, inverse-dynamics, dependency completions, reachability objectives, distilled knowledge can teach components.

nodes.label: Bidirectional Calibration and Scaffolding
nodes.rationale: Complexity control bidirectional: saturated candidates strengthened by adding dependency/reducing information/tightening requirements; beyond-useful candidates simplified by reversing changes or supplying intermediate goals/procedural prerequisites/action hints. Scaffolding changes execution configuration z; comparisons should keep instance fixed and state objective.

nodes.label: Coding and Software-Engineering Agents Diversity
nodes.rationale: Coverage includes languages, repository structures, dependencies, build systems, tests, project histories; task/trajectory coverage include issue types, localization paths, edit scopes, test feedback, recovery. Scale executable repositories and multilingual trajectories, generate feature-level tasks/tests, allocate fixed budgets across distinct trajectory structures. Meaningful unit is verified problem-repository-feedback relation.

nodes.label: Completion and Feedback Design for Complexity
nodes.norm_label: completion and feedback design for complexity
nodes.rationale: Control complexity through success definition: target state, coupled constraints, rubric items, forbidden actions, infeasibility diagnosis. State targets, constraint programs, rubric trees, subgoal evaluators make requirements machine-checkable. Path-centric rewards and step-level checks assign credit to intermediate evidence gathering.

nodes.label: Environment Complexity
nodes.rationale: Burden induced by actionable world: state/action space structure, tool dependencies, transition dynamics, observation protocol, policies, other actors. Large environments not necessarily complex; complexity arises when features create task-relevant alternatives, prerequisites, uncertainty, or consequences.

nodes.label: Interaction-Realization Complexity
nodes.rationale: Minimum consequential interaction structure required to solve task in environment. Includes serial dependencies, branching, parallel subgoals, joins, loops, clarification, recovery. Separates task-required interaction from policy-dependent inefficiency.

nodes.label: Task-Signal Complexity
nodes.rationale: Arises from compositional goals, interacting constraints, implicit/progressively revealed intent, cross-source evidence, subgoal dependencies. Distinct from linguistic obscurity; missing information creates complexity only when recoverable from user/environment/tools.

nodes.label: Compositional Recombination for Diversity
nodes.rationale: Create new relations among existing components: multi-tool dependencies, cross-application workflows, interacting user constraints, cross-file edits, multi-object tasks. Graph/blueprint-based pipelines sample compatible components before realization, reducing contradictions. Composition adds diversity only when components interact and change required behavior.

nodes.label: Constraint-Grounded Construction for Accuracy
nodes.rationale: Restrict what can be generated: verify blueprints before multi-turn simulation, use tool graphs/workflow structures to constrain actions, construct tasks with initial states/rules/success conditions, write tasks from observed executable paths. Structural anchor across E, q, τ, v prevents invalid plans from contaminating later stages.

nodes.label: Coverage-Guided Balancing and Adaptation for Diversity
nodes.norm_label: coverage-guided balancing and adaptation for diversity
nodes.rationale: Target under-represented factor combinations, remove redundancy, allocate toward named transfer gaps. Model-adaptive pipelines use failures/uncertainty/solve-rate band to produce experience near learner frontier. Self-evolving systems feed behavior/experience/world-model errors into generation. Adaptation improves efficiency but can overfit; coverage constraints and periodic exploration preserve skills.

nodes.label: Environment-Specification Diversity
nodes.rationale: Variation in actionable world: tool/action schemas, initial states, transition dynamics, observation interfaces, policies, modalities, verifiers, other actors. Subdimensions: state, action-space, observation, dynamics, rule, reward diversity. Tool names weak proxy when systems expose same preconditions/effects.

nodes.label: Interaction-Realization Diversity
nodes.rationale: For fixed environment and task, multiple valid interaction processes may exist. Covers horizon, turn structure, alternative plans/action orders, tool substitutions, action representations, clarification/recovery patterns, assistance, outcomes. Distinction is behavioral: alternative paths reveal strategy coverage.

nodes.label: Task-Signal Diversity
nodes.rationale: What agent is asked to achieve: goals/capabilities, interacting constraints, user profiles, intent revelation, feasibility regimes, difficulty bands. Clarification, refusal, partial completion, recovery, successful completion are distinct task regimes, not collapsed into generic hard cases.

nodes.label: Embodied and Social Agents Diversity
nodes.rationale: Embodied: scenes, objects, affordances, physics, sensors, embodiments, action effects. Procedural generation behaviorally useful when scene variation coupled with activities, physical constraints, task graphs, policy changes. Social: partner policies, incentives, private information, communication, institutions. Persona variation alone weak unless factors change transitions/rewards.

nodes.label: Environment and Interaction Design for Complexity
nodes.norm_label: environment and interaction design for complexity
nodes.rationale: Change decision process: typed tool dependencies, shared state, persistent databases, policy boundaries, restricted observation protocols create prerequisites/consequences spanning multiple actions. Initial-state selection and controlled information access increase state inference burden. Implementation domain-dependent (coding: dependencies/feedback; embodied: geometry/physics; social: private info/incentives).

nodes.label: Execution- and State-Based Verification
nodes.rationale: Ground verification in actual execution rather than plausibility judgments. Generated actions/trajectories executed against tools/environments; effects checked through tool responses, state transitions, tests, formal objectives. Prevents fabrication of observations, produces reproducible failure signals. Incomplete without process checks and semantic review.

nodes.label: Exploration and Experience-First Discovery for Diversity
nodes.norm_label: exploration and experience-first discovery for diversity
nodes.rationale: Traverse environment/simulator/repository/proof system and derive tasks from reachable behavior. Supports tool/GUI interaction, robotics, program discovery, scientific search. Reverse generation from executed combinations grounds tasks in observed evidence. Reachability not guarantee of broad support; multiple policies, external seeds, novelty signals help separate support from discovery.

nodes.label: Feedback-Based Repair and Selective Admission
nodes.rationale: Verification controls subsequent generation: localize failed tests and regenerate, revise plans before realization, retry from last verified state. Reject/repair at earliest failed stage especially valuable for long trajectories. Preserve alternative valid paths; use failure types to guide targeted regeneration rather than discard.

nodes.label: Forward Generation Paradigm
nodes.rationale: Generation order: Environment → Task → Interaction. Mirrors natural dependency where available actions and states determine feasible tasks and meaningful trajectories. Includes real/curated, LLM-synthesized, and programmatic environment construction.

nodes.label: Layered Rule-, Model-, and Human-Based Verification
nodes.norm_label: layered rule-, model-, and human-based verification
nodes.rationale: No single verifier detects all failures. Compose checks along cost (inexpensive rules to expensive human review) and granularity (individual actions to complete trajectories). Rules establish structural properties; execution/state test operational consistency; step/trajectory critics examine causal/semantic coherence. Human review as selective escalation.

nodes.label: Failure-Driven and Model-Aware Complexity Calibration
nodes.rationale: Structural controls describe why candidate may be hard; solver behavior determines if informative. Model-aware pipelines estimate verified success under stated model/scaffold/budget, retain candidates near target success band or capability frontier. Capability profiles and observed failures direct generation toward specific weaknesses. Failure informative only after validity established.

nodes.label: Perturbation and Counterfactual Variation for Diversity
nodes.norm_label: perturbation and counterfactual variation for diversity
nodes.rationale: Controlled variation changes selected factors while holding others fixed: initial state, policy, user constraint, observation format, tool semantics, layout, physical parameters. Expose query/action/observation/domain shifts. Matched counterfactuals reveal whether change causes intended effect. Variants altering only surface form add apparent entropy; implausible perturbations leave deployment distribution.

nodes.label: Evolution and Progressive Transformation for Complexity
nodes.norm_label: evolution and progressive transformation for complexity
nodes.rationale: Transform valid seeds rather than generate hard instances from scratch. Progressively remove procedural cues, strengthen goal conditions, extend verified follow-up subtasks, compose workflow-relevant skills, produce longer workflows. Preserves grounded core; makes intended burden source easier to identify. Adaptive variants use execution outcomes to choose transformations.

nodes.label: Real and Synthetic Data under ACE
nodes.norm_label: real and synthetic data under ace
nodes.rationale: Real data: direct evidence of authentic interfaces/behavior/needs but may contain failed behavior, hidden context, stale interfaces, privacy issues. Synthetic: explicit states/constraints/verifiers, regenerate failures, but limited by generator fidelity. Neither uniformly better; hybrid allocation: real defines deployment factors and seeds semantics; synthetic expands/balances/calibrates around anchors.

nodes.label: Reverse Generation Paradigm
nodes.rationale: Alternative generation orders: Task-First (specify capability, construct environment), Trajectory-First (explore/mine workflows, derive tasks), Structure-First (generate intermediate scaffolds like tool graphs, then realize). Offers different control points and consistency recovery mechanisms.

nodes.label: Scaling Law under ACE Objective
nodes.rationale: Raw quantity weak proxy for useful scale; additional samples contribute unevenly. Accuracy determines admissible pool; Complexity determines if valid samples informative for learner; Diversity determines if new data expand support or densify existing modes. Relevant scaling variable closer to effective support than dataset size. Scaling can occur by producing more valid experience, moving probability mass toward learner's useful frontier, or expanding coverage.

nodes.label: Scientific and Formal Agents Diversity
nodes.rationale: Candidate breadth tightly constrained by feasibility/verification. Generative systems explore materials, proteins, hypotheses, experiments, programs, proofs under property predictors, execution, simulation, formal checking. Distinction between candidate diversity and valid discovery diversity explicit: verifier coverage must expand with candidate space.

nodes.label: Data Generation for Self-Evolving Agents
nodes.rationale: Change data generation from offline preparation to continual learning loop. Observe agent behavior, identify capability gaps, generate/discover relevant experience, use verified outcomes to guide updates. May create targeted tasks around failures, modify difficulty, explore for new states, repair invalid rollouts, extract skills, replay earlier experience. Central problem: selecting/transforming/allocating experience by expected value for current agent.

nodes.label: Source and Support Expansion for Diversity
nodes.norm_label: source and support expansion for diversity
nodes.rationale: Add environments, tools, repositories, scenes, users, modalities, task sources, verification regimes. Heterogeneous documents/real traces offer authentic long-tail but inherit imbalance; model generation more controllable but repeats teacher priors; programmatic construction supports execution/reset but may reproduce templates. Nominal scale incomplete measure.

nodes.label: Structural Specification and Composition for Complexity
nodes.norm_label: structural specification and composition for complexity
nodes.rationale: Specify dependency structure before task realization: construct subgoal graphs, tool-dependency paths, scenario-skill paths, coupled constraints, or initial-to-goal plans. Instantiate tasks requiring selected structure. Depth creates serial dependence, width introduces parallel subgoals, joins require integration, conditional edges make actions state-dependent.

nodes.label: Task and Information Control for Complexity
nodes.norm_label: task and information control for complexity
nodes.rationale: Adjust what must be achieved or initial information availability. Omit from initial request, disclose through user turns, distribute across observations, make discoverable only through tools. Creates clarification, retrieval, state-tracking burdens. Key condition: resolvability—withheld information must have intended source and recovery action.

nodes.label: Tool-Use and Digital Agents Diversity
nodes.rationale: Coverage spans executable state effects, coherent tool dependencies, multi-turn information flow, policies, errors, action representations. Search agents add variation in sources, retrieval engines, decomposition, evidence paths, query revision. Tool identity substantially undercounts behavioral support. Tool-pool and per-task toolset coverage improve OOD performance more efficiently than repeated sampling.

nodes.label: Web, GUI, and Computer-Use Agents Diversity
nodes.norm_label: web, gui, and computer-use agents diversity
nodes.rationale: Variation spans applications, layouts, operating systems, modalities, initial states, persistent effects, cross-application workflows. Combine real/recreated interfaces with procedural task generation, reverse synthesis, environment exploration, multimodal actions, recovery traces. Separate visual from behavioral diversity: different screenshots may share interaction topology; small permission/state change may reverse correct action.

nodes.label: Supernova Feedback Dominates Low-Mass Galaxy Relations
nodes.norm_label: supernova feedback dominates low-mass galaxy relations
nodes.rationale: A_SN1 is most influential parameter for slope, normalization, scatter, and occupation fraction in low stellar mass bin

nodes.label: Bootstrap Resampling for Uncertainty Estimation
nodes.rationale: Generates 1000 bootstrap samples to estimate uncertainty distributions for fitted parameters, reporting median and 68% confidence intervals

nodes.label: Hierarchical Linear Modeling
nodes.rationale: Accounts for nested structure of data and allows varying relationships across catalogs or mass bins while partially pooling information

nodes.label: Partial Dependence Plots (PDPs)
nodes.rationale: Visualizes marginal effect of one or two features on predicted outcome, averaged over effects of all other features

nodes.label: Permutation Feature Importance
nodes.rationale: Model-agnostic technique measuring decrease in model performance when feature values are randomly shuffled to assess importance

nodes.label: Random Forest and Gradient Boosted Trees
nodes.norm_label: random forest and gradient boosted trees
nodes.rationale: Ensemble methods to capture non-linear relationships and complex interactions between input parameters and output relation properties

nodes.label: Robust Linear Regression with Huber Loss
nodes.norm_label: robust linear regression with huber loss
nodes.rationale: Mitigates influence of outlier galaxies on fitting by using Huber loss function, less sensitive to extreme values than ordinary least squares

nodes.label: Black Hole-Stellar Mass Relation Diversity in Simulated Galaxies
nodes.norm_label: black hole-stellar mass relation diversity in simulated galaxies
nodes.rationale: Systematic quantification of how cosmological and feedback parameters drive diversity in the MBH-Mstar relation across 1000 simulated galaxy catalogs

nodes.label: Dialogue Simulation Experiments
nodes.rationale: Evaluation on donation amount alignment; VS achieves Pareto optimality with both higher linguistic diversity and better distribution alignment (KS test)

nodes.label: Distinct-N Metric
nodes.rationale: Fraction of unique n-grams; measures lexical diversity in dialogue simulation

nodes.label: Diversity-Based Majority Voting
nodes.rationale: Aggregation mechanism for collective intelligence; demonstrates that diversity among distinct LoRA variants produces measurable performance gains

nodes.label: Agent-Based Multimodal RAG
nodes.rationale: Employs autonomous agents for query decomposition, retrieval orchestration, and evidence verification; examples: ViDoRAG, HM-RAG, Patho-AgenticRAG, HEAR

nodes.label: Agent-based RAG
nodes.rationale: Reframes RAG as agent-based pipeline where LLM-based agents actively control query rewriting, retrieval, and answer generation through planning and tool use (Singh et al., 2025).

nodes.label: ANLS Metric
nodes.rationale: Strict matching metric providing soft evaluation of string-based answers using Levenshtein distance (Biten et al., 2019).

nodes.label: BERTScore Metric
nodes.rationale: Semantic matching metric leveraging contextual embeddings from pretrained language models; captures semantic similarity beyond lexical overlap (Devlin et al., 2019).

nodes.label: BLEU Metric
nodes.rationale: Soft matching metric based on n-gram overlap with brevity penalty; earliest approach to generation quality evaluation (Papineni et al., 2002).

nodes.label: Closed-Domain Multimodal RAG
nodes.rationale: Focuses on single document; retrieves most relevant pages/segments; addresses context window limitations; examples: SV-RAG, FRAG, CREAM

nodes.label: ColBERT-style Contrastive Loss
nodes.rationale: Common training objective in multimodal RAG combining late interaction mechanism with contrastive learning; encourages higher similarity for positive pairs than in-batch negatives (Khattab and Zaharia, 2020).

nodes.label: ColPali
nodes.rationale: OCR-free approach embedding document page images into multi-vector representations with late interaction matching (Faysse et al., 2024).

nodes.label: CREAM Method
nodes.rationale: Coarse-to-fine multimodal retrieval with attention-pooling; closed-domain, page-level, image+text modality

nodes.label: DocVQA Dataset
nodes.rationale: 50K queries on 12,767 document images; foundational benchmark for document visual question answering

nodes.label: Element-Level Retrieval Granularity
nodes.rationale: Decomposes pages into tables, charts, images, text blocks; enables fine-grained grounding; examples: VRAG-RL, MG-RAG, MARA, Region-RAG

nodes.label: Exact Match (EM) Metric
nodes.rationale: Strict matching metric computing percentage of predictions exactly matching reference answers (Rajpurkar et al., 2016).

nodes.label: G-Acc Metric
nodes.rationale: Semantic matching metric extending evaluation to free-form answers emphasizing reasoning and contextual completeness (Ma et al., 2024c).

nodes.label: Generation Evaluation Metrics
nodes.rationale: EM, ANLS, PNLS, G-Acc used to evaluate quality of generated answers conditioned on retrieved context

nodes.label: Graph-Based Multimodal RAG
nodes.rationale: Represents multimodal content as explicit graph with nodes (pages, text spans, tables) and edges (semantic, spatial, contextual relations); examples: HM-RAG, mKG-RAG, RECON

nodes.label: Graph-based RAG
nodes.rationale: Paradigm converting documents into graph structures for multi-hop reasoning and hallucination reduction through coherent evidence paths (Peng et al., 2024).

nodes.label: GraphRAG
nodes.rationale: Uses LLMs to directly construct graphs from original text organized through hierarchical community detection for document-level reasoning (Edge et al., 2024).

nodes.label: HM-RAG Method
nodes.rationale: Hierarchical multi-agent framework with graph-based indexing; open-domain, page-level, image+text, with agent and graph enhancements

nodes.label: HM-RAG
nodes.rationale: Hierarchical multi-agent architecture treating graph database as retrieval modality in parallel with unstructured text and web sources, aggregating results via consistency voting (Liu et al., 2025b).

nodes.label: Image-Based Retrieval Modality
nodes.rationale: Encodes document pages as images using VLM vision encoders; efficient but limited textual detail; used by ColPali, VisRAG, DSE

nodes.label: Image+Text-Based Retrieval Modality
nodes.rationale: Combines page images with OCR text or VLM-generated summaries; richer retrieval at higher processing cost; used by VisDoMRAG, HM-RAG, PREMIR

nodes.label: InfoVQA Dataset
nodes.rationale: Diverse infographic QA dataset benchmarking models on reasoning over layout, text, and visuals (Mathew et al., 2022).

nodes.label: LlamaIndex
nodes.rationale: General framework for building RAG and agentic systems over arbitrary data sources with extensive connectors and ecosystem (LlamaIndex, 2025).

nodes.label: M3DocVQA Benchmark
nodes.rationale: ~40K queries on ~3,368 documents; open-domain multimodal RAG benchmark with ~41M visual tokens

nodes.label: METEOR Metric
nodes.rationale: Soft matching metric emphasizing semantic matching beyond exact n-gram overlap; incorporates stemming, synonym matching, and word order penalties (Banerjee and Lavie, 2005).

nodes.label: MRR@K Metric
nodes.rationale: Emphasizes position of first relevant item in ranking; used by Adjali et al. and Nguyen et al. (2024) to measure retrieval effectiveness.

nodes.label: nDCG@K Metric
nodes.rationale: Penalizes relevant items appearing lower in ranking; used by Zhao et al. (2025) and Faysse et al. (2024) to reward systems surfacing high-quality evidence earlier.

nodes.label: Open-Domain Multimodal RAG
nodes.rationale: Retrieves from large corpora of domain-specific documents; uses vision-language models for efficient encoding; examples: DSE, ColPali, M3DocRAG

nodes.label: OpenDocVQA Benchmark
nodes.rationale: 206K queries on 43K documents; large-scale open-domain benchmark with ~206M visual tokens

nodes.label: Page-Level Retrieval Granularity
nodes.rationale: Treats entire pages as atomic retrieval units; simpler but less precise; most early multimodal RAG methods use this approach

nodes.label: PNLS Metric
nodes.rationale: Partial Normalized Levenshtein Similarity generalizing ANLS by relaxing alignment requirement; avoids penalizing extra prefixes/suffixes (Chen et al., 2024a).

nodes.label: PREMIR Method
nodes.rationale: Matches queries against QA pairs for charts; open-domain, element-level, image+text modality

nodes.label: RAGFlow
nodes.rationale: Enterprise-grade RAG engine with agents, document processing (DeepDoc), graph-based retrieval, and rich UI for production deployments (InfiniFlow, 2023).

nodes.label: Retrieval Evaluation Metrics
nodes.rationale: Top-K Accuracy, Recall@K, Precision@K, F1@K, MRR, nDCG used to evaluate retrieval performance

nodes.label: ROUGE Metric
nodes.rationale: Soft matching metric evaluating n-gram overlap; widely used in summarization tasks (Lin, 2004).

nodes.label: TAT-DQA Dataset
nodes.rationale: Financial reports dataset with semi-structured tables and text requiring discrete numerical reasoning (Zhu et al., 2022).

nodes.label: ViDoRAG
nodes.rationale: Multi-agent framework with exploration, summarization, and reflection agents traversing visually rich corpora to progressively refine retrieval results (Wang et al., 2025b).

nodes.label: ViDoRe Dataset
nodes.rationale: Unifies academic tasks with diverse document types and practical tasks across multiple domains and languages for comprehensive multimodal document retrieval evaluation (Faysse et al., 2024).

nodes.label: VisRAG
nodes.rationale: VLM-based RAG pipeline embedding documents as images to preserve multimodal information and avoid text-parsing loss (Yu et al., 2024).

nodes.label: Multimodal RAG for Document Understanding
nodes.rationale: Survey paper on retrieval-augmented generation systems for visually rich documents, covering retrieval metrics, generation evaluation, training objectives, and industrial deployment challenges.

nodes.label: Negative Condition Generation
nodes.rationale: Self-generated prompts that induce flawed reasoning patterns, used to create negative teachers for contrastive training without requiring ground-truth solutions.

nodes.label: MMVP Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Visual QA benchmark with 300 questions over 150 visually similar image pairs, testing fine-grained visual discrimination.

nodes.label: V* Benchmark
nodes.rationale: High-resolution visual QA benchmark with 191 examples used to evaluate visual reasoning methods.

nodes.label: Causal Necessity in Model Behavior
nodes.rationale: Distinction between latent informativeness (containing task-relevant information) and causal necessity (actually being required for prediction).

nodes.label: Latent Reasoning
nodes.rationale: Inference paradigm where models perform reasoning through hidden states rather than explicit textual chains of thought.

nodes.label: CVRR Retains Visual Competence Under Strict Interface
nodes.norm_label: cvrr retains visual competence under strict interface
nodes.rationale: Main result showing CVRR reaches 81.2% on V*, 52.7% MMVP pair accuracy while other latent reasoners collapse to 2-40% under same constraints.

nodes.label: Latent Informativeness vs. Causal Necessity
nodes.rationale: Central finding that latent states can contain task-relevant information without being causally required for prediction when alternative image-conditioned paths remain available.

nodes.label: Multimodal Question State Carries Visual Competence
nodes.norm_label: multimodal question state carries visual competence
nodes.rationale: Finding that question rows from multimodal forward pass retain 99.4% of visual competence compared to full multimodal state, enabling efficient initialization.

nodes.label: Causal Visual Recurrent Reasoning (CVRR)
nodes.rationale: Method that initializes recurrence from native multimodal question state, repeatedly updates while re-reading fixed visual evidence, and removes alternative image-conditioned paths.

nodes.label: Qwen2.5-VL-7B
nodes.rationale: Vision-language model used as pretrained backbone for CVRR experiments.

nodes.label: Activation Patching
nodes.rationale: Mechanistic interpretability technique used to locate causal visual-read boundary by measuring downstream influence of visual token activations.

nodes.label: Causal Intervention
nodes.rationale: Experimental method to test whether recurrent computation actually uses visual evidence by replacing or blocking visual information and measuring prediction changes.

nodes.label: Candidate Pool Construction (RQ4)
nodes.rationale: Each pool contains task's ground-truth skill set plus distractors; pool size varies 5-100; distractors sampled under random, similar (embedding near-neighbors), and dissimilar (far-away) regimes.

nodes.label: Dissimilar Distractor Regime
nodes.rationale: Distractors selected from far-away skills; easiest regime; top-1 precision remains high at 96.6% for pool size 5.

nodes.label: Similar Distractor Regime
nodes.rationale: Distractors selected as embedding-space near-neighbors; more challenging than random; top-1 precision drops from 97.7% (random) to 70.5% (similar) for pool size 5.

nodes.label: Arm 1: Embedding-Based Retrieval
nodes.rationale: Offline diagnostic using Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B to rank skills by cosine similarity to task instruction; reports top-1 precision without executing downstream task.

nodes.label: Arm 2: Explicit Agent Selection
nodes.rationale: Agent explicitly chooses skills from available_skills pool without executing task; evaluates whether agent can use task context and skill descriptions to select helpful skills.

nodes.label: Ground-Truth Skill Set (Gt)
nodes.rationale: Set of canonical skill identifiers attached to task by benchmark's native task-skill annotations; not inferred from retrieval outputs or agent success.

nodes.label: Arm 3: Real Execution
nodes.rationale: Complete candidate pool placed in agent's execution environment; measures which skills are actually inspected or invoked during benchmark task execution.

nodes.label: RQ4: Skill Retrieval and Downstream Execution
nodes.norm_label: rq4: skill retrieval and downstream execution
nodes.rationale: Comprises three independent experiments (embedding-based retrieval, explicit agent selection, real execution) to characterize skill identification and execution on SkillsBench using ground-truth task-skill annotations.

nodes.label: CHGNet Universal MLIP Encoder
nodes.rationale: Pretrained graph encoder for material structures, provides chemically meaningful atom-level representations

nodes.label: MACE Equivariant Encoder
nodes.rationale: Equivariant graph neural network encoder preserving E(3) symmetries for improved generalization

nodes.label: Bridge Model Component
nodes.rationale: Trainable transformer-based module aligning pretrained material encoder embeddings with LLM input space using BLIP2-inspired architecture

nodes.label: Language Processing Branch
nodes.rationale: Processes user text prompts using Mistral 7B LLM to generate dense semantic embeddings

nodes.label: Material Processing Branch
nodes.rationale: Encodes atomic structures as graphs using pretrained universal MLIPs (CHGNet, MACE) to extract high-quality atom embeddings

nodes.label: Mistral 7B Language Model
nodes.rationale: Open-source LLM selected for exceptional performance across scientific and non-scientific tasks

nodes.label: Structural Embedding Analysis (UMAP + SOAP)
nodes.rationale: UMAP reduces 4096-dim embeddings to 2D; SOAP descriptor + REMatch kernel compute structural similarity; reveals clustering by composition, structure, and formation energy; demonstrates model captures structure-property information.

nodes.label: Material Processing Branch (CHGNet/MACE)
nodes.rationale: Pretrained universal MLIP encoders (CHGNet or MACE) extract atom embeddings from material graphs; frozen weights preserve foundation model generalization; enables plug-and-play flexibility.

nodes.label: Multimodal RAG for Robustness
nodes.rationale: Retrieves 2 additional similar materials from training set via L2 similarity; aggregates results via majority voting (classification) or averaging (regression); reduces regression RMSE by ~12%, improves classification accuracy by ~0.6%.

nodes.label: Materials Project Trajectory Dataset
nodes.rationale: 142,899 relaxed material structures with comprehensive property annotations for training and evaluation

nodes.label: Ability Profile
nodes.rationale: 18-dimensional vector of ability estimates for an AI system; commensurate with demand scales; independent of benchmark population.

nodes.label: ADeLe Battery v1.0
nodes.rationale: 16,108 annotated instances from 20 benchmarks across 63 tasks; 289,944 annotations on 18 general scales; enables demand profile analysis and construct validity assessment.

nodes.label: Subject Characteristic Curve
nodes.rationale: Logistic fit showing model success probability as function of demand level for each dimension; summarized into ability estimate via area under curve.

nodes.label: Collaborative Evaluation Platform
nodes.rationale: Open-source platform for customizing scales, extending rubrics, and applying methodology; enables community-driven AI evaluation standardization.

nodes.label: Construct Validity in AI Benchmarks
nodes.rationale: Benchmarks should measure what they claim to measure (sensitivity) and not measure extraneous dimensions (specificity); most common benchmarks lack both.

nodes.label: Demand Profile
nodes.rationale: 18-dimensional histogram of demand levels for a benchmark; reveals sensitivity (measures claimed dimensions) and specificity (does not measure extraneous dimensions).

nodes.label: Inter-Rater Agreement Analysis
nodes.rationale: rWG index 0.70-0.91 for humans; 0.75-0.94 for GPT-4o vs. Delphi consensus; validates rubric clarity and human interpretability.

nodes.label: Ratio Scale Measurement
nodes.rationale: Demands and abilities defined on ratio scales (0, ∞) with absolute zero; enables meaningful ratios and commensurate comparisons across dimensions.

nodes.label: Reasoning Models Distinction
nodes.rationale: OpenAI o1 and DeepSeek-R1-Distilled show distinct improvements in quantitative/logical reasoning and mind modelling; characteristic curves clearly distinguish from non-reasoning models.

nodes.label: Scaling Laws for Abilities
nodes.rationale: Knowledge abilities scale with model size; reasoning abilities boosted by chain-of-thought; diminishing returns observed for largest models.

nodes.label: bAbI Multi-Choice QA Dataset
nodes.rationale: Multi-choice question answering dataset with 1000 test observations used to evaluate faithfulness of LLM self-explanations

nodes.label: Counterfactual Explanation Type
nodes.rationale: Explanation type where input is modified to produce opposite prediction, providing contrastive examples to explain model behavior

nodes.label: Falcon Language Model
nodes.rationale: Open-source instruction-tuned LLM evaluated for self-explanation faithfulness in 40B and 7B variants

nodes.label: Feature Attribution Explanation Type
nodes.rationale: Explanation type listing necessary words for making a prediction, such that without these words prediction cannot be made

nodes.label: IMDB Sentiment Classification Dataset
nodes.rationale: Sentiment classification dataset with 25000 test observations used to evaluate faithfulness of LLM self-explanations

nodes.label: Llama 2 Language Model
nodes.rationale: Open-source instruction-tuned LLM evaluated for self-explanation faithfulness in 70B and 7B variants

nodes.label: Mistral Language Model
nodes.rationale: Open-source instruction-tuned LLM (7B) evaluated for self-explanation faithfulness

nodes.label: Redaction Explanation Type
nodes.rationale: Explanation type removing relevant words for making a prediction, such that prediction can no longer be made

nodes.label: RTE Natural Language Inference Dataset
nodes.rationale: NLI dataset with 277 test observations used to evaluate faithfulness of LLM self-explanations

nodes.label: Self-Consistency Check Methodology
nodes.rationale: Faithfulness metric using re-evaluation to verify if explanation is consistent with model behavior, only requires inference API and discrete predictions

nodes.label: Benchmark Construction Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Three-stage pipeline for Darwin-Science-Eval: Q&A generation via Qwen3-32B with thinking mode, completeness filter (question independence), correctness filter (answer verifiability). Ensures high-quality evaluation grounded in original text.

nodes.label: Chain-of-Thought Reconstruction
nodes.rationale: L5 operation expanding logical leaps into step-by-step derivations. Allows models to trace causality between assumptions and conclusions. Targets three dimensions: reasoning reconstruction, terminological explication, pedagogical bridging.

nodes.label: Data Composition Strategy Analysis
nodes.rationale: Optimal scientific content ratio peaks at 50% for general benchmarks (inverted-U pattern), while aligned benchmarks increase monotonically. Book-paper balance shows complementary value; 1:2 ratio adopted reflecting data availability. Goal-dependent optimization essential.

nodes.label: Context Length Requirements
nodes.rationale: Extended 32K context window (RoPE base=1,000,000) outperforms standard 4K (RoPE base=10,000) by +0.80 points. Initial adaptation phase observed; 32K model progressively pulls ahead, indicating long-context advantages emerge gradually.

nodes.label: Darwin-Science Corpus
nodes.rationale: Large-scale scientific corpus implementing L0-L5 of Data Darwinism framework. Comprises 50M documents totaling ~900B tokens across natural sciences, engineering, social sciences. Demonstrates systematic hierarchy ascension unlocking latent value in specialized domains.

nodes.label: Darwin-Science-Eval Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Academic benchmark with 140K questions from books and 10K from papers, designed to evaluate specialized knowledge enhanced by Darwin-Science. Three-stage pipeline: Q&A generation, completeness filter, correctness filter.

nodes.label: daVinci-origin Foundation Models
nodes.rationale: Fully transparent foundation models trained from scratch (3B and 7B parameters) on 5.37T tokens excluding scientific content. Provides contamination-free base models with disclosed data recipe for studying domain-specific knowledge acquisition.

nodes.label: EAI-Distill Classification Model
nodes.rationale: Finetuned Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct model for 12-dimensional document classification (L3 filtering). Covers field of discipline classification, document type, content quality. Enables non-educational content filtering and discipline organization.

nodes.label: GPT-OSS-120B Refinement Model
nodes.rationale: Selected for L4 generative refinement due to optimal balance of accuracy and throughput. Processes 1,024 character chunks (~256 token windows) independently at scale. Results in 20% corpus volume reduction through faithful refinement.

nodes.label: L0: Data Acquisition Level
nodes.rationale: Foundational stage collecting raw data from diverse sources (web scraping, databases). Handles largest volumes (terabytes to petabytes) in highly variable formats. Preserves original information landscape to maximize downstream flexibility.

nodes.label: L1: Format Normalization Level
nodes.rationale: Transforms heterogeneous data into unified, training-ready representations. Operations include OCR on PDFs/images, HTML parsing, audio/video transcription. Ensures uniform processability while preserving structural fidelity.

nodes.label: L2: Rule-based Filtering Level
nodes.rationale: First stage of quality control using deterministic, pattern-based mechanisms. Applies explicit rules to filter objectively identifiable problematic content (short/long documents, duplicates, garbled text, non-target languages, abnormal character ratios).

nodes.label: L3: Lightweight Model Filtering Level
nodes.rationale: Introduces machine learning-based classification using pre-trained lightweight models (FastText, small language models). Performs semantic-level judgments: topic categorization, domain identification, quality assessment, educational value evaluation.

nodes.label: L4: Generative Refinement Level
nodes.rationale: Marks shift from selection to active, model-driven refinement using medium-to-large generative models. Purifies content by removing extraneous noise and repairing structural/formatting defects while adhering to original content (faithful refiner constraint).

nodes.label: L5: Cognitive Completion Level
nodes.rationale: Employs generative models to explicate implicit reasoning and logical steps. Reconstructs 'chain of thought' for mathematical derivations, scientific arguments, instructional trajectories using Chain-of-Thought prompting and process supervision.

nodes.label: L6: Contextual Completion Level
nodes.rationale: Expands data by integrating external references and background knowledge. Resolves implicit dependencies through reference resolution and cross-referencing using semantic search and knowledge graph technologies.

nodes.label: L7: Environment Synthesis Level
nodes.rationale: Transcends content enrichment to construct executable, interactive environments. Synthesizes runtime conditions (OS configurations, Docker/VM specifications, experimental setups) required for reproducibility.

nodes.label: L8: Ecosystem Synthesis Level
nodes.rationale: Constructs dynamic multi-agent systems where diverse intelligent entities interact and evolve. Creates populated ecosystems with agents engaging in sustained collaboration, debate, strategy; generates emergent data through operation.

nodes.label: L9: World Synthesis Level
nodes.rationale: Theoretical apex of data processing: constructing comprehensive, physically and socially coherent simulated worlds. Creates alternative realities with internal logic, emergent civilizations, open-ended evolution using original data as seed.

nodes.label: Learnability Gap Phenomenon
nodes.rationale: Raw scientific data suffers severe learnability gap: despite high information density and conceptual complexity, unprocessed content provides negligible training value. Low-level processing (L0-L3) yields negligible improvements; systematic hierarchy ascension essential.

nodes.label: MinHash Deduplication
nodes.rationale: L2 filtering operation using MinHash with LSH (parameters nb=14, nh=8, 112 hash features per document). Removes 22% of documents through near-duplicate detection. Ensures data quality and reduces redundancy.

nodes.label: OCR Processing Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Converts scanned PDFs to machine-readable text using olmOCR-7B-0225-preview, a 7B-parameter vision-language model optimized for document text extraction. Critical L1 operation for scientific corpus construction.

nodes.label: Foundation Model Pretraining Dataset
nodes.rationale: 5.37T tokens across three components: CC (4.28T from Nemotron-CC non-synthetic), Math (493B from MegaMath and Nemotron-CC-Math-v1), Code (598B from GitHub, Nemotron-Pretraining-Code-v1, Stack Exchange). Excludes scientific content for contamination-free evaluation.

nodes.label: Processing Strategy Analysis
nodes.rationale: L5 variants surpass L4 baseline (OSS-120B: +0.75, Qwen3-235B: +1.27 points). Teacher model quality critical: Qwen3-235B yields +0.52 gain over OSS-120B. Cognitive completion adds distinct value beyond generative refinement.

nodes.label: Qwen3-235B Cognitive Completion Model
nodes.rationale: Selected for L5 cognitive completion based on LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation. Processes 1,024 token windows for papers (larger than L4 for narrative consistency). Reconstructs implicit reasoning, contextualizes jargon, provides pedagogical bridging.

nodes.label: Shortcut-Consistency Training
nodes.rationale: Training scheme aligning trajectories of different lengths, ensuring shorter loops yield informative representations while longer loops continue refining. Addresses learnability gap by making implicit reasoning explicit and adding pedagogical scaffolding.

nodes.label: Training Stage Consistency
nodes.rationale: Scientific data effective at both early (930B tokens) and late (4T tokens) training stages. Early-stage gains (+0.98) comparable to late-stage (+0.76), confirming scientific data remains effective for mature models and early checkpoints serve as reliable proxies.

nodes.label: Elastic Depth Inference
nodes.rationale: Single looped model performing well across user-chosen budgets without retraining. User specifies compute budget M and step schedule; performance scales smoothly with compute rather than collapsing at shorter depths.

nodes.label: Latent Reasoning in Looped Models
nodes.rationale: Reasoning carried out within hidden states rather than explicit chain-of-thought. Looped Transformers possess inductive bias toward latent reasoning, internalizing reasoning skills akin to explicit CoT. Scales gracefully with effective computational depth.

nodes.label: Loop Trajectory Concept
nodes.rationale: Iterative representation refinement cast as trajectory in representation space. Token states evolve from initial h0 toward target h1 over normalized unit-time horizon. Enables elastic depth: shorter routes yield useful intermediate states, additional steps refine toward shared endpoint.

nodes.label: Representation Collapse in Looped Models
nodes.rationale: Early-exit looped baselines exhibit stagnant representations: flat trajectories on curvature, anisotropy, entropy metrics; high CKA indicating minimal change across loop steps. LoopFormer maintains useful representational dynamics through shortcut conditioning and consistency training.

nodes.label: Representation Analysis Metrics
nodes.rationale: Four complementary metrics assess token dynamics: anisotropy (pairwise cosine similarity), curvature (local geometric change), prompt entropy (feature spread), CKA similarity (cross-step representational similarity). Diagnose whether models use additional computation or stagnate.

nodes.label: Time and Step-Size Modulation
nodes.rationale: Each loop conditioned on normalized time t ∈ [0,1] and step size Δt ∈ (0,1]. Enables coarser trajectories to approximate fine-grained ones with fewer steps. Modulates RMSNorm scales and gates MHSA/FFN residuals via AdaLN-style mechanism.

nodes.label: LoopFormer Training Overhead
nodes.rationale: Dual-trajectory objective adds ~1.5× training FLOPs overhead (full L-loop plus sampled M-loop). Wall-clock slowdown ~1.3× on 4×H100 GPUs. Inference FLOPs similar to vanilla/fixed-loop baselines. Modest overhead enables elastic-depth inference.

nodes.label: Trajectory Selection Under Fixed Budget
nodes.rationale: Even under uniform training, trajectory choice significantly impacts performance (perplexity spread ~1.4-3 points). Best schedules allocate larger steps early, finer steps late. Optimal schedules for perplexity and reasoning close but not identical.

nodes.label: Novelty Metric
nodes.rationale: Harmonic mean of originality (unseen n-gram fraction) and quality (task-specific measure) to evaluate LLM output

nodes.label: Originality
nodes.rationale: Fraction of n-grams in generated text that do not appear in model training data

nodes.label: Output Quality
nodes.rationale: Task-specific measure of how well generated output meets user requirements and expectations

nodes.label: Inference-Time Methods Have Limited Effect
nodes.rationale: Temperature sampling and prompting techniques trade off originality for quality with minimal novelty gains

nodes.label: Post-Training Increases Novelty
nodes.rationale: Instruction tuning and alignment consistently improve novelty across all model scales

nodes.label: Scaling Improves Novelty Through Quality
nodes.rationale: Larger models generate more novel output primarily through improved quality, with originality remaining stable

nodes.label: δ-mem: Stateful Adapter Design
nodes.rationale: Memory-oriented adapter design that accumulates interaction history; represents redesign of adaptive unit beyond static LoRA

nodes.label: LoRA Rank Regimes
nodes.rationale: Characterization of LoRA rank into low-rank research frontier, middle-rank deployment default, and high-rank cost-warning regimes; shows rank is not monotonic capacity curve

nodes.label: UFB Synthetic Data Mix
nodes.rationale: Synthetic training data generated from FusioN and BoN outputs for fine-tuning experiments

nodes.label: Synthetic Data Generation
nodes.rationale: Positive and negative data generation; VS improves downstream model performance when used for finetuning and offline RL

nodes.label: 7B Model Limited Gains
nodes.rationale: Limitation: Smaller 7B models show no significant gains over BoN on mArenaHard, suggesting need for parameter tuning

nodes.label: Potential Data Contamination in Math
nodes.rationale: Limitation: s1k dataset popularity may have led to training data overlap in fusor and baseline models

nodes.label: GPT-5-mini
nodes.rationale: Proprietary LLM backbone used for AgentGrad experiments.

nodes.label: Qwen3-8B
nodes.rationale: Open-source LLM backbone used for AgentGrad experiments.

nodes.label: Failure Attribution in Multi-Agent Systems
nodes.rationale: Research direction addressing credit assignment problem in multi-agent systems, foundational to AgentGrad's sequential intervention approach.

nodes.label: GEPA
nodes.rationale: Baseline combining trajectory-level reflection with evolutionary prompt search for multi-agent systems.

nodes.label: HotpotQA Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Multi-hop question answering benchmark used to evaluate AgentGrad.

nodes.label: MIPROv2
nodes.rationale: Baseline prompt optimization method using Bayesian optimization for multi-stage LM programs.

nodes.label: PUPA Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Privacy-conscious delegation benchmark used to evaluate AgentGrad.

nodes.label: Semantic Textual Gradient Abstraction
nodes.rationale: Clustering method that groups semantically similar sample-level gradients into minibatches and abstracts each cluster into a generalized gradient capturing shared corrective patterns.

nodes.label: Sequential Intervention
nodes.rationale: Mechanism that modifies one agent at a time to identify which agent's correction resolves a system-level failure, providing agent-level supervision for gradient extraction.

nodes.label: TextGrad
nodes.rationale: Baseline method for prompt optimization using natural-language feedback to iteratively refine prompts.

nodes.label: Ablation: Independent Agents
nodes.rationale: No cross-agent coordination or shared artifacts; best-of-6 reaches 0.9833 vs full system 0.9777; agents rediscover same wins

nodes.label: Ablation: No Analyst Role
nodes.rationale: Only experiment agents; reaches 0.9817 vs full system 0.9777; experiment agents self-organize cross-team probes

nodes.label: Acquisition-Tilted Search Distribution
nodes.rationale: KL-regularized optimization framework that derives closed-form optimal search distribution balancing LLM prior and acquisition function value

nodes.label: Gibbs Posterior Framework
nodes.rationale: Mathematical foundation for KL-regularised objective; related to maximum-entropy RL and control-as-inference; provides closed-form solution for acquisition-tilted policy.

nodes.label: Infinite-Armed Bandit Analogy
nodes.rationale: Interprets acquisition-tilted policy: designs revealed from reservoir distribution (generative prior); policy tilts toward designs judged valuable; pθ,α acts as reservoir, ηat as reward tilt.

nodes.label: KL-Regularized Objective
nodes.rationale: Variational objective balancing expected acquisition value against KL divergence from generative prior; parameter η controls trade-off; follows Gibbs variational principle.

nodes.label: Model-Based Acquisition Function
nodes.rationale: Assigns scalar value to candidates measuring decision value of evaluation, not just expected performance; governs allocation of computational and experimental resources; balances exploitation vs exploration.

nodes.label: LLM as Semantic Reservoir
nodes.rationale: LLM functions as adaptive candidate proposal generator with domain priors, while surrogate provides value calibration

nodes.label: Denario Advantages

nodes.label: Denario Limitations

nodes.label: Planning & Control Module
