nodes.label: BDH-CQ on ARC-AGI-1: 29.5% pass@2 at $0.00070/task
nodes.rationale: 150M-parameter model achieves new cost-efficiency Pareto frontier: 29.5% pass@2 at computed $0.00070 per task (~0.85 H200 GPU-seconds at $3/hour). Breaks through previously reported frontier; ~57x cheaper than GPT-5.6 Luna (Low) at 34.2% accuracy.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Architecture: Recurrent Memory + Latent Reasoning
nodes.norm_label: bdh-cq architecture: recurrent memory + latent reasoning
nodes.rationale: System combines two computational substrates: recurrent contextual memory S_t that evolves with demonstrations (analogous to attention but avoiding explicit key-value cache), and structured latent workspace H_r for iterative reasoning. Intermediate states not decoded to language; only final output verbalized.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Dense Color Mapping: 24/24 at 8 Simultaneous Bindings
nodes.norm_label: bdh-cq dense color mapping: 24/24 at 8 simultaneous bindings
nodes.rationale: Task defines fresh color permutation through demonstrations; requires elementwise application to held-out sequences. System solves all 96 held-out outputs at rank one as simultaneous bindings increase from 2 to 8 (24/24 at every level). Demonstrates substantial contextual binding capacity for task-specific mappings.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ ConceptARC Capability Profile
nodes.rationale: Performance varies across 16 concept families: FilledNotFilled, TopBottom2D, ExtendToBoundary reach 9/10 pass@2; Copy, Order reach 2/10. Gap between test-pair accuracy (77.92%) and strict-task accuracy (59.38%) indicates inconsistent rule application across test inputs within tasks.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Independent Black-Box Audit: 29.5% Reproduced
nodes.rationale: Co-authors from Bielik AI and NYU conducted independent black-box evaluation without access to model weights. Reproduced 29.5% pass@2 on public ARC-AGI-1 evaluation set under documented protocol. Also evaluated on ConceptARC and hand-crafted evaluation set.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Opaque Identifier Replication: No Confound
nodes.norm_label: bdh-cq opaque identifier replication: no confound
nodes.rationale: Replaced semantic task IDs with cryptographically opaque labels and mixed concept batches. Aggregate performance unchanged: 374/480 test pairs in both conditions, 96/160 opaque vs. 95/160 semantic tasks. Six semantic-only and six opaque-only pass@2 successes. Rules out identifier-and-batch confound as explanation for ConceptARC score.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Reasoning Effort: LOW 21% → MEDIUM 27% → HIGH 29.5%
nodes.norm_label: bdh-cq reasoning effort: low 21% → medium 27% → high 29.5%
nodes.rationale: Pass@2 increases monotonically with latent reasoning effort: LOW 21% (22% cost reduction), MEDIUM 27% (11% reduction), HIGH 29.5% (baseline). Demonstrates test-time compute scaling within latent reasoning regime without verbalized intermediate steps.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Scaling: 1B–600B Parameters, Transformer-Like Laws
nodes.rationale: Architecture scales naturally to large sizes with tensor sharding inherited from BDH. Early experiments confirm Transformer-like scaling laws during pretraining at 1B–600B parameters while preserving latent reasoning capabilities. Suggests path to larger models with maintained cost efficiency.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Training Data: ARC-AGI-1 + RE-ARC + ConceptARC + ARC-Heavy + ARC-GEN100K
nodes.norm_label: bdh-cq training data: arc-agi-1 + re-arc + conceptarc + arc-heavy + arc-gen100k
nodes.rationale: 150M-parameter model trained on curated collection combining private examples with public ARC-style data from five sources plus augmentations. Complete internal training recipe proprietary; task interface and data provenance disclosed.

nodes.label: Theme: In-Context Learning via Recurrent Memory
nodes.norm_label: theme: in-context learning via recurrent memory
nodes.rationale: BDH-CQ processes demonstrations sequentially, updating recurrent contextual state S_t. Information available to later inputs depends on associations accumulated from earlier inputs/outputs. Avoids explicit key-value cache while enabling dense task-specific mappings (24/24 at 8 simultaneous color bindings). Combines flexibility of attention with efficiency of recurrent state.

nodes.label: Theme: Latent Reasoning vs. Verbalized Chain-of-Thought
nodes.norm_label: theme: latent reasoning vs. verbalized chain-of-thought
nodes.rationale: BDH-CQ demonstrates alternative to verbalized CoT: continuous hidden-state iteration without discrete token generation. Removes natural-language tokens as mandatory representation of internal computation, enabling parallel exploration of multiple hypotheses. Achieves cost efficiency (0.85 GPU-seconds vs. longer token sequences) while maintaining reasoning capability.

nodes.label: Discovery Operation
nodes.rationale: Expands search frontier; formulates hypotheses previously outside effective reach; brings unknown unknowns into modelled space as known unknowns; distinct from mere evaluation of untested designs.

nodes.label: Epistemic Regimes of Scientific Search
nodes.rationale: Four-regime framework (known knowns, known unknowns, unknown knowns, unknown unknowns) distinguishing uncertainty, reachability, modelling support, and knowledge; organizes search operations by epistemic state.

nodes.label: Exploitation Operation
nodes.rationale: Acts on known knowns; selects designs with high predicted reward μt(x) and low uncertainty σt(x); operates within current search support.

nodes.label: Exploration Operation
nodes.rationale: Resolves known unknowns; evaluates reachable but uncertain designs; reduces posterior uncertainty; transitions designs from known unknowns to known knowns.

nodes.label: Inference Configuration (α)
nodes.rationale: Parameters controlling how generative model is used at inference time; includes prompting strategy, sampling temperature, reasoning procedure, refinement scheme, compute budget; affects effective proposal distribution.

nodes.label: Predictive Uncertainty vs Search Awareness
nodes.rationale: Distinguishes two limitations: predictive uncertainty (what surrogate doesn't know within modelling support, reducible by observation) vs search awareness (which candidates/families are represented/reachable, requires frontier expansion).

nodes.label: Search Context (Ct)
nodes.rationale: Broader information available to generative model beyond empirical data; includes Dt, previously generated candidates, surrogate predictions, acquisition values, constraint feedback, refinement trajectories, search memory.

nodes.label: Search Frontier
nodes.rationale: Conceptual boundary of what current procedure can effectively formulate, reach, and model; distinguishes accessible designs (inside) from unrepresented designs (outside).

nodes.label: Temperature Form Reservoir Distribution
nodes.rationale: Exponential family of reservoirs pθ,α(x|Ct) ∝ pθ(x|Ct)^α; makes α transparent as strength of prior; large α concentrates mass on modes, α→0 spreads toward uniform.

nodes.label: Generative Foundation Model Component
nodes.rationale: Supplies structured prior over design space X; enables generation of candidates reflecting domain knowledge and semantic plausibility; can expand search frontier through context or inference-procedure modification.

nodes.label: Probabilistic Surrogate Model
nodes.rationale: Posterior p(R|Dt) over reward surface; provides empirical grounding absent from foundation models alone; quantifies epistemic uncertainty distinct from measurement noise; instantiated as Gaussian Process for sample efficiency.

nodes.label: Empirical Software as Optimization Problem
nodes.rationale: Converts software creation into search for program maximizing quality score; enables systematic exploration of solution space

nodes.label: Systematic Idea Recombination
nodes.rationale: Programmatic generation of method combinations; 44% of recombinations outperformed base methods; mirrors scientific practice of combining ideas

nodes.label: Test-Time Compute Scaling Paradigm
nodes.rationale: Iterative refinement with increasing compute yields continued quality improvements; contrasts with model parameter scaling

nodes.label: COVID-19 Hospitalization Forecasting
nodes.rationale: Predicts weekly hospital admissions across 52 jurisdictions; rolling validation window; ERA models outperformed CovidHub-ensemble on majority of locations; 14 recombined strategies exceeded ensemble baseline.

nodes.label: GIFT-Eval Time Series Forecasting
nodes.rationale: General time series forecasting across 97 datasets; unified solution with 8 preset configurations; final MASE of 0.734 achieved through iterative refinement with holidays library integration.

nodes.label: scRNA-seq Batch Integration Task
nodes.rationale: Removes batch effects while retaining biological variability; evaluated on OpenProblems benchmark v2.0.030 with 13 metrics across 6 datasets; ERA achieved 0.6671 overall score vs 0.6740 for GPT-5 Best-of-N.

nodes.label: LLM-Driven Code Mutation
nodes.rationale: Semantic-aware rewrites produce complex meaningful variations; more flexible than random mutations in genetic programming

nodes.label: Research Idea Injection Mechanism
nodes.rationale: LLM integrates ideas from papers, textbooks, search results; enables systematic exploration of research idea space; 44% of recombinations outperformed base methods

nodes.label: Time Series Forecasting (GIFT-Eval)
nodes.rationale: Per-dataset solution outperformed May 2025 leaderboard; unified solution created general-purpose library with adaptive configuration system

nodes.label: Tree Search Algorithm for Code Optimization
nodes.norm_label: tree search algorithm for code optimization
nodes.rationale: Maintains diverse candidate tree; backtracks when specific mutations plateau; discovers strategies leading to abrupt score jumps

nodes.label: Learning Mechanics Framework
nodes.rationale: Proposed quantitative, low-level theory of deep learning training dynamics; complements mechanistic interpretability at higher levels of abstraction.

nodes.label: Neuroscience Perspectives on Deep Learning
nodes.rationale: Hypotheses about neural computation (e.g., probabilistic inference) and circuit decomposition inform deep learning theory.

nodes.label: Open Direction 1: Solvable Models of Deep Nonlinear Learning
nodes.norm_label: open direction 1: solvable models of deep nonlinear learning
nodes.rationale: Seeks unified framework combining nonlinear parameter dynamics and nonlinear function learning; would illuminate feature learning and architectural innovations.

nodes.label: Open Direction 5: Discretization Hypothesis
nodes.rationale: Proposes finite networks as discretizations of infinite limits; would unify understanding of width, depth, and learning rate as discretization parameters.

nodes.label: Open Direction 6: Eliminating All Hyperparameters
nodes.rationale: Extends hyperparameter disentanglement program; seeks to determine if all hyperparameters can be eliminated through appropriate limits.

nodes.label: Open Direction 9: Principles of Good Optimizers
nodes.norm_label: open direction 9: principles of good optimizers
nodes.rationale: Seeks fundamental principles explaining optimizer success; would guide design of new optimizers and predict failure modes.

nodes.label: Physics of Deep Learning Perspective
nodes.rationale: Seeks average-case theories of neural network learning; aligned with development of mechanics of learning.

nodes.label: Singular Learning Theory Approach
nodes.rationale: Bayesian framework emphasizing loss landscape geometry and phase transitions; seeks first-principles predictive theories.

nodes.label: Aristotelian Composite PASS: 6 of 15
nodes.rationale: Claude 2/5, GPT 4/5, Gemini 0/5; structural axis uniformly passed; failures driven by Stage 1 training-prior suppression.

nodes.label: Decay World Composite PASS: 0 of 15
nodes.rationale: All trials fail by Stage 3; 14 of 15 fail Stage 3 check itself; qualitative direction perfect (0 wrong), quantitative ratio leaked 23 of 60 times.

nodes.label: F=mv Composite PASS: 6 of 15
nodes.rationale: Claude 3/5, GPT 2/5, Gemini 1/5; failures concentrated on different cognitive moves per model.

nodes.label: Bug Taxonomy: Autonomy Spectrum
nodes.rationale: 15 documented issues: 10 autonomous (convention, algorithm, coefficients), 2 human-accelerated (magnitude discrepancies), 3 human-essential (architectural redesign, fudge-factor rejection, correct formula).

nodes.label: CLAX-PT: Differentiable One-Loop Perturbation Theory
nodes.rationale: JAX implementation computing next-to-leading-order predictions for galaxy clustering; validates to ≲1% accuracy against CLASS-PT reference; end-to-end differentiable.

nodes.label: Explanatory Agency Gap
nodes.rationale: Agent evaluates predictions; physicist evaluates explanations. Agent cannot spontaneously generate meta-question of whether solution frame is correct; cannot distinguish 'right numbers for right reasons' from 'right numbers for wrong reasons'.

nodes.label: Fudge Factor (α=0.27) Failure Mode
nodes.rationale: Agent committed calibrated scalar correction passing all oracle tests but corresponding to no quantity in reference theory; would produce wrong predictions at other cosmologies; caught and replaced by physicist.

nodes.label: Irreducible Human Role (P3)
nodes.rationale: Physicist supplied 100% of decisive architectural and physical judgments despite agent performing bulk of session-time; contribution weight should reflect irreplaceability, not volume.

nodes.label: Oracle Testing Limitation (P1)
nodes.rationale: Oracle tests verify 'what' not 'why'; fudge factor passed because calibrated to test point; multi-cosmology testing insufficient; defense: test at diverse parameter points, automate limiting-case probes.

nodes.label: Redshift-Space Multipoles Crisis
nodes.rationale: 33 sessions (24–56) spent adjusting coefficients within wrong architecture (isotropic damping); agent could not recognize structural incompatibility; physicist diagnosed anisotropic BAO damping, triggered redesign.

nodes.label: Shared Memory Limitation (P2)
nodes.rationale: CHANGELOG prevented literal re-exploration but not structural stagnation; 33 sessions of coherent but futile work within wrong architecture; defense: session-count trigger (~5–10 sessions) for human review.

nodes.label: Supervision Protocol
nodes.rationale: Four infrastructure elements: CLASS-PT as oracle, CHANGELOG as shared memory, --fast flag for context hygiene, parallel sessions via git worktrees; two critical rules: no fudge factors, test at multiple parameter points.

nodes.label: Gated Unlikelihood Penalty
nodes.rationale: Sigmoid-bounded penalty that suppresses token probabilities boosted by negative conditions while avoiding gradient explosion on high-confidence structural tokens.

nodes.label: Intuitor
nodes.rationale: Baseline using average confidence as intrinsic reward for label-free training.

nodes.rationale: Balanced mode (default) achieves 68.3% accuracy with 5.1 avg iterations; conservative mode performs worst (58.9%) despite reading more sections.

nodes.label: Hierarchy Preservation Ablation
nodes.rationale: Removing hierarchy preservation causes 4.9-6.2% accuracy drop, confirming necessity of structural context for effective section ranking.

nodes.label: Information Sufficiency Check Ablation
nodes.rationale: Removing sufficiency check and using only top-1 section causes catastrophic 43.2% accuracy drop (75.4% to 32.2%), revealing incomplete retrieval and hallucination issues.

nodes.label: Additive Manufacturing and Quality Control
nodes.rationale: Material science domain in IntraBench covering 3D printing processes, defect detection, and in-situ monitoring using machine learning for quality assurance.

nodes.label: Agentic-Hybrid-RAG Baseline
nodes.rationale: Hybrid retrieval agent combining graph-based and vector-based retrieval with lightweight knowledge graph for structured reasoning over documents.

nodes.label: Confidence-Based Reading Styles
nodes.rationale: Three reading modes (conservative, balanced, aggressive) allow users to control operational overhead by adjusting sufficiency thresholds and early termination criteria.

nodes.label: Contextual RAG Baseline
nodes.rationale: Enhanced RAG variant that augments chunks with LLM-generated contextual descriptions to improve retrieval precision beyond dense embeddings alone.

nodes.label: DRAGIN Baseline
nodes.rationale: Dynamic retrieval-augmented generation baseline that determines when and what to retrieve based on model uncertainty and token-level salience signals.

nodes.label: Human Factors and Fatigue Detection
nodes.rationale: Engineering domain in IntraBench covering human performance measurement, fatigue classification, and ergonomic risk assessment using wearable sensors and machine learning.

nodes.label: Infectious Disease Modeling
nodes.rationale: Public health domain in IntraBench covering mathematical modeling of disease transmission dynamics using compartmental models (SIR, SEIR).

nodes.label: LLM-Grounded Multiple-Choice Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Evaluation protocol where LLM maps free-form answers to multiple-choice options, addressing scientific terminology variations (abbreviations, synonyms) and enabling semantic correctness assessment.

nodes.label: LongRAG Baseline
nodes.rationale: Long-context RAG baseline with hybrid retriever, LLM-augmented information extractor, and CoT-guided filtering for coarse-to-fine semantic recall.

nodes.label: LUMOS Agent Baseline
nodes.rationale: Literature-focused agent with iterative planning, grounding, and execution modules for multi-hop reasoning over scientific documents.

nodes.label: Main Experimental Results
nodes.rationale: IntrAgent achieves 70.0-75.9% accuracy across seven LLM backbones, outperforming all baselines by 7.9-21.0 percentage points through targeted evidence selection.

nodes.label: Mapping Model Robustness
nodes.rationale: IntrAgent consistently outperforms RAG across different mapping models (GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, DeepSeek-R1), demonstrating robustness to evaluation protocol variations.

nodes.label: Robustness to Noisy Section Headings
nodes.rationale: IntrAgent maintains 84.6% accuracy on physics dataset with corrupted headings (beginner-style, noisy, Shakespearean), showing only 4.6% drop from 89.2% baseline.

nodes.label: Paper Length Impact Analysis
nodes.rationale: Mixed-effects regression shows paper length (6-49 pages, mean 15.2) has no significant effect on IntrAgent performance (p=0.463), indicating model-agnostic robustness.

nodes.label: PaperQA2 Agent Baseline
nodes.rationale: Scientific QA agent with reasoning-based contextual summarization and relevance scoring for evidence extraction from research papers.

nodes.label: R²AG Baseline
nodes.rationale: Reranking-augmented RAG baseline that uses a learned reranker to guide evidence selection and improve relevance alignment in generation.

nodes.label: Remote Sensing and Land Cover Classification
nodes.norm_label: remote sensing and land cover classification
nodes.rationale: Earth science domain in IntraBench covering satellite imagery analysis and land use classification using deep learning and multi-source data integration.

nodes.label: SciMaster Agent Baseline
nodes.rationale: Tool-integrated agentic reasoning system with Solver, Critic, Rewriter, and Selector roles for multi-stage inference-time workflow.

nodes.label: Reasoning-Based Section Ranking
nodes.rationale: Uses LLM reasoning to rank paper sections by relevance to research question, replacing similarity-based retrieval with semantic understanding of section purpose.

nodes.label: Section Ranking Accuracy
nodes.rationale: Reasoning-based ranking achieves 87.5% top-1 accuracy vs 25.0% for similarity-based RAG on physics dataset, demonstrating superiority of semantic understanding.

nodes.label: Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy (SERS)
nodes.rationale: Physics domain in IntraBench covering optical spectroscopy techniques for molecular detection, representing applied physics and engineering applications.

nodes.label: Statistical Significance Testing
nodes.rationale: Wilcoxon signed-rank test confirms IntrAgent significantly outperforms all 12 baselines (padj < 10⁻⁶) with median improvements of 10.9-27.3 percentage points.

nodes.label: Task-Oriented Question Categories
nodes.rationale: IntraBench questions categorized into four types: study subject & experimental setup, data characteristics & collection, technical approach & details, conclusions & results.

nodes.label: Vanilla RAG Baseline
nodes.rationale: Retrieval-augmented generation baseline using embedding-based chunk retrieval with fixed 500-token chunks and cosine similarity ranking.

nodes.label: IntrAgent System
nodes.rationale: LLM-based agent designed specifically for IntraView task, combining hierarchy preservation, reasoning-based section ranking, and iterative reading with information sufficiency checks.

nodes.label: IntraView Task
nodes.rationale: Novel task for retrieving information from scientific literature by reading papers section-by-section with reasoning-based ranking and iterative evidence gathering.

nodes.label: GeneBench-Pro Design Constraints
nodes.rationale: Eight primary constraints ensuring ground-truth identifiability, unique defensible answers, clear numerical separation, minimal viable prompts, robust QC, fully simulated problems, multi-stage inference, and ablation-supported workflow adjudication.

nodes.label: DRX1 Carrier-Screening Residual Risk (Illustrative Problem)
nodes.rationale: Clinical genomics problem requiring carrier call identification, assay calibration, and residual risk computation; demonstrates multi-stage decision points including CNV/segdup discrimination, founder phase collapse, and full-roster standardization.

nodes.label: External Scientific Review Process
nodes.rationale: 82 of 129 problems reviewed by 11 domain experts; identified issues in estimand specification, method implementation, and workflow realism; led to prompt clarifications, data modifications, and complete redesigns.

nodes.label: GeneBench-Pro Evaluation Results
nodes.rationale: GPT-5.6 Sol reaches 28.7% pass rate (31.5% with Pro); GPT-5.5 reaches 12.0%; Claude Opus 4.8 reaches 16.0%; models notice diagnostic clues but fail to propagate implications to downstream decisions.

nodes.label: Binary Grading Rationale
nodes.rationale: All-or-nothing grading reflects real-world scientific workflows where incorrect final answer despite partial correctness represents failure; collapses stage-level diagnostic evidence but maintains decision-relevance.

nodes.label: Cascaded Decision Points in Scientific Analysis
nodes.norm_label: cascaded decision points in scientific analysis
nodes.rationale: Multi-stage problems with 3-13 decision points where incorrect upstream choices propagate downstream; enables measurement of whether agents navigate full inferential chains rather than isolated steps.

nodes.label: Model Reasoning Quality Assessment
nodes.rationale: Qualitative analysis of model-reported reasoning reveals consistent pattern: weaker models notice diagnostic clues but treat as local data cleaning rather than evidence for downstream method changes.

nodes.label: Notice-Act Gap in Scientific Reasoning
nodes.rationale: Models identify diagnostic signals but fail to propagate implications to downstream analysis decisions; resembles expert-novice differences in scientific problem-solving where experts integrate observations into broader problem context.

nodes.label: Simulated Data for Benchmark Construction
nodes.rationale: Enables precise control of complexity, difficulty, and diagnostic clues; ensures QC-sensitive decisions are robust to researcher-choice variation; guarantees graded endpoint is recoverable from agent-visible data.

nodes.label: GeneBench-Pro: Multi-Stage Scientific Reasoning Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Benchmark for AI agents performing realistic multi-stage quantitative analyses in genomics and translational biomedicine; 129 problems across 10 domains with 3-13 decision points each; uses simulated data to ensure identifiability and robust grading.

nodes.label: Batch Size as Budget Variable
nodes.rationale: Larger batches increase token consumption under fixed-step PPO schedule; slightly improve average gain but increase downside risk; not a pure optimization knob but part of broader score–cost tradeoff.

nodes.label: High-Rank Opportunity Cost
nodes.rationale: Beyond middle-rank region (r≥64), adapter footprint increases while performance frontier flattens; unnecessary rank displaces more useful expenditures (additional seeds, ablations, variance control, reward debugging).

nodes.label: Mean–Best Performance Separation
nodes.rationale: Best-seed frontier remains nearly flat across ranks 1–32, while across-seed mean drops at low rank; indicates optimization/initialization bottleneck rather than hard capacity limit.

nodes.label: Personal Models Scale-Down Objective
nodes.rationale: Rank reduction compounds across repeated updates, optimizer states, checkpoints, serving-time loads, and millions of persistent model instances; goal is to keep population close to 'share 99.5%, differ in 0.5%' regime for economic feasibility.

nodes.label: Rank Reduction Under Minimal Parameters
nodes.rationale: Central question in PEFT: whether useful learning survives under extreme rank reduction; LoRA rank defines an adaptation regime rather than a simple capacity knob.

nodes.label: Reliability vs. Capacity Distinction
nodes.rationale: Low-rank limitation is reliability (seed-to-seed variance) rather than expressivity; best runs at rank 1 match ranks 16–32, but mean performance and consistency collapse.

nodes.label: Seed-Heavy Evaluation for Reliability
nodes.rationale: Cheaper adapters enable repeated experimentation (seed-heavy evaluation, stronger initialization, cleaner schedules, tighter KL control, rank-specific hyperparameters); broader evidence collection turns lucky low-rank runs into reliable ones.

nodes.label: Three Distinct Rank Operating Regions
nodes.rationale: Empirical sweep on Qwen3-8B PPO (216 runs) reveals behavior separates into three regions: middle-rank (r=16–32, strongest practical balance), low-rank (r=1–4, best-run competitive but unreliable mean), high-rank (r≥64, inflated footprint without frontier extension).

nodes.label: Low-Rank Adaptation
nodes.rationale: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning method; used 89.8% of vague-goal runs vs 24.1% explicit-task runs

nodes.label: PEFT Rank Reduction and RL-Native Initialization Study
nodes.norm_label: peft rank reduction and rl-native initialization study

nodes.label: Deterministic Aggregation and Statistical Reporting
nodes.rationale: Final stage computes per-arm success rates, paired deltas with bootstrap CI, mode frequencies, fixed/introduced counts, mechanism distributions without additional LLM calls

nodes.label: Failure Mode Taxonomy (12 canonical modes)
nodes.rationale: Mixed success/failure modes distinguish when success is attributable to skill guidance, workflow guidance, or autonomous agent behavior
nodes.source_location: Section A.2, Canonical Taxonomy Induction subsection

nodes.label: Limitation: Incomplete Token Metrics
nodes.rationale: Some skill-arm token fields incomplete; token cost reported only on matched same-task intersection with complete metadata; mechanism and mode analyses treated as primary evidence
nodes.source_location: Section A.2, Reproducibility and Reliability Controls subsection

nodes.label: Limitation: LLM-Assisted Rather Than Exhaustively Human-Coded

nodes.rationale: v1 taxonomy induced from 238 valid labels then applied to 528 triples; trajectory grounding and taxonomy aggregation independently human-validated but full paired-triple dataset remains LLM-assisted
nodes.source_location: Section A.2, Reproducibility and Reliability Controls subsection

nodes.label: Limitation: Representative Trial Policy Does Not Average Repeated Trials
nodes.norm_label: limitation: representative trial policy does not average repeated trials

nodes.label: Paired Success-Rate Delta Analysis
nodes.rationale: Bootstrap CI (1000 iterations) shows Skill vs Workflow Memory (+0.0606, [+0.0076, +0.1136]) is most robust aggregate difference; skills distill trajectories into more compact actionable form

nodes.label: Canonical Taxonomy Induction
nodes.rationale: Two-round batched process: batch-level modes (8-14 per batch) → merged into 12 global canonical modes; intentionally mixes success/failure modes to distinguish guidance sources
nodes.source_location: Section A.2, Canonical Taxonomy Induction subsection

nodes.label: Trajectory Labeling Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Multi-stage process: open coding → taxonomy induction → paired contrastive labeling → deterministic aggregation

nodes.label: LangChain Orchestration Layer
nodes.rationale: Framework for routing natural-language user input to appropriate symbolic computation modules.

nodes.label: Ollama LLM Runtime
nodes.rationale: Open-source LLM inference engine enabling local deployment of language interface without proprietary API dependency.

nodes.label: LLM Agent Orchestration Layer
nodes.rationale: Connects model-building tools to conversational backend; manages intent matching, tool routing, confirmation workflows; LLM never generates physics outputs.

nodes.label: Anomaly Detection Module
nodes.rationale: Verifies gauge anomaly cancellation (SU(3), SU(2), U(1) cubic and gravitational); provides hints for anomaly resolution when models are anomalous.

nodes.label: Complementarity to SARAH, FeynRules, Susyno
nodes.rationale: bsm_agent automates early model-building stage (operator generation from quantum numbers); complements downstream tools that derive vertices, mass spectra from specified Lagrangian.

nodes.label: Computational Scaling with Large Representations
nodes.rationale: Runtime depends on representation sizes; larger SU(2)_L and SU(3)_c multiplets require longer execution; includes representation-aware optimizations for common cases.

nodes.label: Conversation State and Confirmation Workflow
nodes.rationale: Maintains conversation history and model state; infers candidate interpretations and requests confirmation before model creation to prevent errors from ambiguous input.

nodes.label: EWSB and Mass-Matrix Layer
nodes.rationale: Assigns VEVs to neutral color-singlet scalars; derives stationary conditions and tree-level mass matrices from shifted Lagrangian.

nodes.label: Component Field Expansion Layer
nodes.rationale: Expands gauge-invariant operators into explicit component fields using SU(2) and SU(3) index contractions with Clebsch-Gordan coefficients.

nodes.label: Field and Group Representation Layer
nodes.rationale: Defines field classes and group-representation utilities for Standard Model quantum numbers under SU(3)_c × SU(2)_L × U(1)_Y; distinguishes scalar and Weyl-fermion types.

nodes.label: Gauge Anomaly Checking
nodes.rationale: Computes standard anomaly coefficients by summing over left-handed Weyl fermions; reports whether all five coefficients vanish; suggests conjugate representations if needed.

nodes.label: Lagrangian Expansion Module
nodes.rationale: Expands compact operator notation into component fields with explicit SU(3) and SU(2) indices; output depends on basis, normalization, and phase conventions chosen by user.

nodes.label: LangChain Integration
nodes.rationale: Uses langchain-core and langchain-ollama for LLM orchestration; enables tool-calling interface and conversation management.

nodes.label: Leptoquark Model Case Study
nodes.rationale: Complete end-to-end example demonstrating model construction, anomaly checking, Lagrangian expansion, and mass matrix extraction for leptoquark BSM extension.

nodes.label: LLM Natural Language Interface
nodes.rationale: Enables users to specify BSM field quantum numbers in natural language rather than rigid syntax, serving as orchestration layer between user and deterministic symbolic engine.

nodes.label: Mass Matrix Generator
nodes.rationale: Extracts and diagonalizes mass matrices from scalar potential and Yukawa sectors for phenomenological analysis.

nodes.label: Model Construction Layer
nodes.rationale: Initializes SM field content and extends with additional scalar/fermionic fields; generates complete renormalizable gauge-invariant operator basis automatically.

nodes.label: Model State Management
nodes.rationale: Supports incremental model building: users can clear, extend, or reset models via natural-language commands; enables iterative exploration of BSM parameter space.

nodes.label: Natural Language Quantum Number Parsing
nodes.rationale: Accepts multiple equivalent natural-language descriptions of quantum numbers (e.g., 'bar 6', 'anti-sextet', 'color anti 6') and normalizes to canonical form for validation.

nodes.label: Ollama Local LLM Inference
nodes.rationale: Primary intended deployment mode; runs LLM locally on user's machine; supports models like gpt-oss:20b and qwen3.5:35b without external API calls.

nodes.label: Operator Generation Module
nodes.rationale: Constructs all independent interaction terms (kinetic, Yukawa, scalar potential) using group-theoretical rules; output depends only on group theory, free from arbitrariness.

nodes.label: Provider Layer: Local, Remote, Commercial
nodes.rationale: Backend-agnostic separation supporting local Ollama, remote self-hosted servers, and commercial APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic); enables switching without modifying symbolic code.

nodes.label: Reliability Principle: LLM Never Generates Physics
nodes.norm_label: reliability principle: llm never generates physics
nodes.rationale: Core design principle: LLM serves only as orchestration layer; all physics outputs (Lagrangian, anomaly coefficients, mass matrices) generated by deterministic backend.

nodes.label: Automatic Renormalizable Operator Generation
nodes.rationale: Enumerates all scalar monomials up to four fields; tests gauge singlet condition and mass dimension ≤4; generates scalar potential, fermion mass, and Yukawa sectors automatically.

nodes.label: Report Generation Layer
nodes.rationale: Generates compact and fully expanded LaTeX representations of models directly from symbolic backend; produces PDF-ready output.

nodes.label: Right-Handed Neutrino Extension Model
nodes.rationale: Simple BSM model example: SM extended with fermion singlet (1,1,0); demonstrates natural-language model specification and automatic Lagrangian generation.

nodes.label: Standard Model Template
nodes.rationale: Built-in SM field content serves as starting point for BSM extensions; package can generate SM reports, expand Lagrangian, and derive mass matrices.

nodes.label: Supported Gauge Representations
nodes.rationale: SU(2)_L dimensions 1-7 (motivated by minimal dark matter); SU(3)_c singlet, triplet, antitriplet, sextet, antisextet, octet (motivated by SO(10) GUTs); arbitrary U(1)_Y hypercharge.

nodes.label: Symbolic Computation Engine
nodes.rationale: Core deterministic backend performing group-theoretical operator generation, anomaly detection, and Lagrangian expansion independent of LLM, preserving reproducibility and scientific rigor.

nodes.label: SymPy Symbolic Backend
nodes.rationale: Python symbolic mathematics library used for deterministic physics calculations; ensures reproducibility and correctness of model-building results.

nodes.label: Tool-Calling Interface Design
nodes.rationale: LLM interprets natural-language requests, translates to structured field schema, asks clarification questions, selects appropriate backend tools, formats output.

nodes.label: Beyond Standard Model Construction
nodes.rationale: Physics workflow: specify new field quantum numbers → generate all renormalizable interactions → check anomaly cancellation → expand Lagrangian → extract mass matrices; traditionally manual and error-prone.

nodes.label: Symbolic AI Integration with LLMs
nodes.rationale: Paradigm: LLMs serve as interface/orchestration layer for deterministic symbolic engines; preserves transparency, reproducibility, and scientific rigor while improving accessibility.

nodes.label: Basis and Normalization Conventions
nodes.rationale: Package uses canonical field normalization, no numerical prefactors in coupling coefficients, and phase conventions that preserve physical predictions; users must map their conventions to package conventions for meaningful comparison.

nodes.label: Mode Collapse
nodes.rationale: Phenomenon where post-training alignment reduces LLM diversity, causing models to favor narrow set of responses

nodes.label: Group Relative Policy Optimization
nodes.rationale: Training method available to agents in Aspire for weight evolution

nodes.rationale: Decoding technique for improving diversity by regulating text perplexity

nodes.label: μ-sampling

nodes.label: Supervised Fine-Tuning
nodes.rationale: Training method available to agents in Aspire for weight evolution

nodes.label: Theorem D.1: Instance-Level Collapse
nodes.rationale: Formal result: under flat rewards and power-transform sharpening (γ>1), instance prompts collapse to the single mode of the reference distribution exponentially fast

nodes.label: Theorem D.2: List-Level Collapse
nodes.rationale: Formal result: list prompts collapse to top-k modes with at most uniform diversity over k items; auto-regressive conditioning amplifies collapse at each step

nodes.label: Unified Agent Tool Interface
nodes.rationale: Composable interface for data search/download/import/synthesis, SFT/GRPO training, verification, validation, evaluation, branching, termination

nodes.label: Scientific Reasoning Benchmarks
nodes.rationale: Tests multi-step reasoning, technique recommendation, and ability to work from first principles without retrieval shortcuts.

nodes.label: Multi-Turn Scientific Dialogue
nodes.rationale: Engages system in progressive information revelation, testing ability to ask questions, identify missing information, and adapt conclusions.

nodes.label: Human-Centered Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Incorporates user needs from interviews with researchers and engineers; reveals desire for critical thinking, multi-turn dialogue, and trust over autonomous problem-solving.

nodes.label: AI Singularity / Intelligence Explosion
nodes.rationale: Hypothetical transition where positive-feedback loop produces intelligence beyond ordinary forecasting; requires reliable operator mapping present state to demonstrably better successor.

nodes.label: Data-Processing Inequality (DPI)
nodes.rationale: Information-theoretic bound: post-processing cannot create additional mutual information beyond that in inputs; foundational constraint but does not determine which finite procedures expose useful structure.

nodes.label: Epistemic Closure
nodes.rationale: Loop where candidate generation, training targets and evaluation become increasingly endogenous; prevents system from improving representation of world or discovering new objectives.

nodes.label: Epistemic Openness
nodes.rationale: Architectural property of remaining answerable to non-circular correction; system must preserve channels through which hypotheses remain testable against constraints not regenerated from own distribution.

nodes.label: Grounding in Recursive Training
nodes.rationale: Corrective influence supplied by information or constraints not reducible to neutral reproduction of current model distribution; can arise from external data, experiments, formal verification, or invariant criteria.

nodes.label: Resource-Bounded Information Accessibility
nodes.rationale: Operational distinction between global information ceiling (DPI) and what finite procedures can make usable; increased computation can improve access without violating conservation.

nodes.label: Model Collapse in Recursive Training
nodes.rationale: Degenerative loss or distortion arising in recursively trained generative models; depends on update rule and data-retention scheme, not synthetic data alone.

nodes.label: Neurosymbolic Model Synthesis
nodes.rationale: Hybrid approach combining neural proposal generation with symbolic structure manipulation and independent verification; enables mechanism search beyond statistical fitting.

nodes.label: Recursive Self-Improvement
nodes.rationale: Process where improvements to system increase its capacity to produce further improvements; requires directional criterion beyond recursive generation.

nodes.label: Solomonoff Induction
nodes.rationale: Idealised formal framework assigning predictive weight through mixture over programs weighted by 2^(-|p|); defines principled direction for searching generative explanations.

nodes.label: Symbolic Model Synthesis
nodes.rationale: Functional requirement for recursive self-improvement: construction, manipulation and testing of explicit generative structures (programs, equations, causal models) against independent criteria.

nodes.label: Algorithmic Information Dynamics (AID)
nodes.rationale: Studies changes in estimated algorithmic information under controlled perturbations to analyze structural contribution, dynamical organization and reprogram mability of mechanisms.

nodes.label: Block Decomposition Method (BDM)
nodes.rationale: Greedy algorithm extending CTM to larger objects by decomposing into smaller components and reusing local algorithmic-complexity estimates; bridges local estimates to larger structured data.

nodes.label: Coding Theorem Method (CTM)
nodes.rationale: Finite computational method estimating algorithmic probability by enumerating small programs and measuring output frequencies; approximates Solomonoff induction within specified machine and runtime regime.

nodes.label: Gradient Boosting Regressor (XGBoost)
nodes.rationale: Interpretable machine learning model for predicting water diffusion from system parameters

nodes.label: Water Density Profile Analysis
nodes.rationale: Quantifies interfacial water structuring through peak height, position, and bulk density metrics

nodes.rationale: Most influential parameter (SHAP importance 3.07×10⁻⁶), monotonically decreasing diffusion from 1.79 to 0.79×10⁻⁵ cm²/s

nodes.label: SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) Analysis
nodes.rationale: Quantifies individual and synergistic influence of functionalization, coverage, and salt concentration on water diffusion

nodes.label: Water Diffusion Coefficient
nodes.rationale: Primary metric for water mobility in confined graphene channels, tunable over five-fold range

nodes.label: K-Means Clustering for Water State Identification

nodes.label: Reasoning Cliff Phenomenon
nodes.rationale: Sharp performance dropoff at TP-Bench Level 3; all models show dramatic accuracy decline, indicating fundamental reasoning limitation

nodes.label: Human-Adapted Validation Sets (arXiv, QFT Pedagogy)
nodes.rationale: Real-world physics problems from arXiv and pedagogical sources; used to validate synthetic dataset difficulty calibration

nodes.label: QFT Synthetic Dataset (Easy/Medium/Hard)
nodes.rationale: Benchmark dataset for evaluating physics reasoning across difficulty levels; used to measure baseline performance of proprietary and open-weight LLMs

nodes.label: Compositionality Assumption
nodes.rationale: Core assumption: complex representations and computations arise from composition of simpler, modular sub-mechanisms.

nodes.label: Developmental Interpretability
nodes.rationale: Research program explaining how mechanisms form during training; bridges mechanistic interpretability and learning mechanics.

nodes.label: Fourier Features in Algebraic Tasks
nodes.rationale: Mechanistic interpretability finding: networks learn Fourier basis for algebraic tasks; bridges data structure and learned mechanisms.

nodes.label: Induction Heads Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Concrete mechanistic interpretability discovery: circuits that implement in-context learning; target for learning mechanics explanation.

nodes.label: Linear Representability Assumption
nodes.rationale: Core assumption in mechanistic interpretability: features correspond to meaningful directions in activation space.

nodes.label: Locality Assumption
nodes.rationale: Core assumption: features and circuits are localizable to particular subsets of model components.

nodes.label: Open Direction 4: Formal Definition of Features
nodes.norm_label: open direction 4: formal definition of features
nodes.rationale: Seeks mathematical grounding for mechanistic interpretability concepts; would formalize and evaluate core assumptions like linear representability and compositionality.

nodes.label: Sparsity Assumption
nodes.rationale: Core assumption: individual features and circuits are activated on only a small fraction of inputs.

nodes.label: Mechanistic Interpretability
nodes.rationale: Research direction seeking human-understandable explanations of transformer computations. Attention-only conversion enables applying interpretability techniques to MLP layers.

nodes.label: Foundation Model (Shared Prior)
nodes.rationale: Strong shared base model that supplies broad intelligence and common competence; enables small local updates to be high-leverage by providing richer latent structure to redirect

nodes.label: Personal Model Instance
nodes.rationale: System built from shared base model, local adaptive state (adapter), context, tools, and external memory; carries learned consequences of repeated experience such as preferences, skills, and tool habits

nodes.label: Abstraction Barrier Bottleneck
nodes.rationale: AI systems trained on human abstractions may lack ability to form novel concepts from raw data, limiting path to true ASI

nodes.label: Embodied Bottleneck
nodes.rationale: Requirement that novel concepts be validated against physical reality, limiting recursive self-improvement to empirical science speeds

nodes.label: Embodied Bottleneck Slows Recursive Improvement
nodes.rationale: Physical validation of concepts requires real-world experimentation, limiting recursive self-improvement to empirical science speeds

nodes.label: FlashAttention
nodes.rationale: Backend for FA and SWA; enables efficient attention computation.

nodes.label: ThunderKittens
nodes.rationale: Backend for linear attention and LoLCATs; fused SWA + linear-attention kernel.

nodes.label: BABILong Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Long-context reasoning; SWA recovers 25% at 4K context vs. 5% for LoLCATs.

nodes.label: Hedgehog Kernel
nodes.rationale: Learnable projection followed by dual-sided exponential transformation; provides expressiveness, spikiness, monotonicity for linear attention.

nodes.label: Linear Attention Methods
nodes.rationale: Reduces time/memory complexity from quadratic to linear via kernel approximation φ; requires training from scratch or extensive post-training; lower expressivity and untractable forgetting problem.

nodes.label: LoLCATs (Low-Rank Linearizing)
nodes.rationale: Combines linear attention with small SWA; post-trains with 40M tokens using LoRA; recovers 83.2% MMLU and 97.5% average performance.

nodes.label: Single Needle-in-a-Haystack (S-NIAH)
nodes.rationale: Long-context reasoning task; SWA recovers 17-23% of full attention at 4K context vs. 0.8-5.8% for LoLCATs/Liger-GLA.

nodes.label: Sliding Window Attention with Sinks
nodes.rationale: Attends to k previous tokens plus first 4 tokens (sinks); training-free; achieves 93.2% MMLU recovery and 99.0% average benchmark recovery without post-training.

nodes.label: Qwen3 Model Family
nodes.rationale: Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-4B, Qwen3.5-9B evaluated; OPSA improves Avg@32 by 263-307% on AIME24/AIME25/HMMT25.

nodes.label: DAPO-17k Dataset
nodes.rationale: Training dataset for OPSA; 17k mathematical reasoning questions without labels or ground-truth answers.

nodes.label: Entropy-Adaptive Negative Advantages
nodes.rationale: Magnitude scales with token entropy (δ=1); high-entropy positions receive stronger negative signals; preserves diversity at fork tokens while sharpening low-entropy positions.

nodes.label: Low Log-Probability Token Suppression
nodes.rationale: OPD gains concentrate on lowest-logp tokens; high-logp tokens provide negligible gradients; fixed negative advantages on low-logp tokens match OPD performance.

nodes.label: Noisy Teacher Signals Analysis
nodes.rationale: Noise defined as advantage sign disagreement with verifiable reward; 20.4% correct answers receive negative advantages, 40.8% incorrect receive positive; noise increases with teacher scale to 50.6%.

nodes.label: On-Policy Distillation (OPD)
nodes.rationale: Uses strong teacher to provide token-level advantages via reverse KL on student-sampled trajectories; requires white-box teacher access; 30.6-50.6% noise rate in teacher supervision.

nodes.label: On-Policy Self-Adaptation (OPSA)
nodes.rationale: Supervision-free method; assigns entropy-adaptive negative advantages to lowest-20%-logp tokens; suppresses tail tokens, redistributes mass among head tokens; improves Avg@32 by 263-307% on math benchmarks.

nodes.label: Reflective Long-Form Reasoning
nodes.rationale: OPSA elicits more reflective tokens ('wait', 'but', 'perhaps'); response length increases during training; positive correlation between length and accuracy.

nodes.label: Agent-Oriented Documentation and Tooling
nodes.rationale: Convergent body of work showing agents benefit from structured, layered representations over flat corpora. Strongest LLMs implement <40% of novel contributions correctly; semantic misalignment is dominant failure mode. ARA encodes claims, evidence, heuristics, and executable bindings at authoring time, eliminating post-hoc recovery.

nodes.label: ARA Protocol and Format
nodes.rationale: Machine-actionable research artifact format that structures scientific knowledge into four layers (Cognitive, Physical, Exploration, Evidence) with cross-layer bindings to enable agent-native research communication and reproducibility verification.

nodes.label: Cognitive Layer (claims, logic, concepts)
nodes.rationale: Structured scientific logic layer containing claims.md, algorithm.md, concepts.md, and heuristics.md. Encodes claims with explicit Falsification criteria, mathematical formulations, and implementation tricks that PDFs leave implicit or scattered.

nodes.label: ARA Compiler (PDF to ARA extraction)
nodes.rationale: Claude Code SDK agent that extracts structured ARA from finished PDF papers. Faithfully represents only what PDF contains; wrapped in RE-Bench-specific pipeline for failure-trace layer population from MALT transcripts.

nodes.label: Dimensional Gap of Existing Tools
nodes.rationale: Analysis showing PDF, GitHub, and experiment trackers (MLflow, W&B) simultaneously leave knowledge siloed in three unlinked formats with no cross-referencing between claims, code, evidence, and decisions. ARA closes gap by providing executable epistemic graph with cross-layer bindings.

nodes.label: Evidence Layer (experiments, results, tables)
nodes.rationale: Grounded evidence including experiments.md (combinatorial experiment matrix, evaluation protocols, metrics), results tables, and MALT attempt logs. Makes experiment matrix explicit and machine-enumerable rather than compressed in prose.

nodes.label: Knowledge Graph and Collaborative Discovery
nodes.rationale: Medium-term extension where aggregated lineages form queryable scientific knowledge graph. Cross-artifact claim alignment turns literature synthesis into subgraph queries; enables continuous review where claim-confidence surface rises with replications and falls with counter-evidence.

nodes.label: Artifact Lineage and Self-Maintaining Ecosystems
nodes.rationale: Near-term extension where each ARA declares parent artifacts and expresses contribution as structured diff. Reduces construction and verification cost; enables self-maintaining ecosystems where consumption becomes maintenance and corrections propagate upstream.

nodes.label: Machine-Readable Science Movement
nodes.rationale: Growing line of work (FAIR principles, W3C PROV, nanopublications, RO-Crate, Whole Tale, Discovery Engine) arguing scientific knowledge should be authored in machine-readable form during research rather than recovered post-hoc. ARA extends this by jointly binding logic, executable code, and decision history with machine-verifiable reproducibility.

nodes.label: Physical Layer (src/ with kernel/repo modes)
nodes.rationale: Executable code layer with two modes: kernel (algorithmic contributions, minimal core modules) and repository (systemic contributions, full implementation with forensic bindings to claims). Provides executable evidence scaled to contribution type.

nodes.label: Taxonomy of Reproduction-Critical Information
nodes.rationale: Ten-category taxonomy derived from PaperBench rubrics (3,050 leaf requirements): combinatorial experiment matrix (24.1%), evaluation protocol (18.5%), hyperparameters (17.2%), metric logging (10.4%), result interpretation (8.6%), architecture (5.8%), mathematical formulation (4.5%), implementation tricks (4.2%), data pipeline (3.8%), environment/infrastructure (2.9%). Reveals that hyperparameters alone insufficient; combinatorial explosion is dominant challenge.

nodes.label: Rigor Auditor Component
nodes.rationale: Claude Code SDK agent that reads ARA, builds cross-layer maps, scores six dimensions, and compiles findings list. Detects fabricated claims, rebutted-branch leaks, over-claims, and missing falsifications with 82.6% overall detection rate on mutation benchmark.

nodes.label: Seal Review Protocol
nodes.rationale: Three-level automated review system for ARAs: Level 1 (structural integrity), Level 2 (Rigor Auditor for argumentative rigor), Level 3 (execution reproducibility). Operationalizes auditing across provenance, soundness, claim decomposition, and cryptographic lineage.

nodes.label: Gemma-3 Models

nodes.label: Latent Visual Reasoning
nodes.rationale: Research direction moving intermediate computation from explicit text into continuous hidden representations in multimodal models.

nodes.label: LoRA Adaptation
nodes.rationale: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning method used in CVRR to adapt only the recurrent layer.

nodes.label: Visual Competence Preservation
nodes.rationale: Design principle in CVRR ensuring that strict interface constraints do not degrade the model's visual understanding capabilities compared to full multimodal pathways.

nodes.label: Visual CoT Dataset

nodes.norm_label: fast and differentiable simulation with simulation-based inference

nodes.label: Web Navigation and Interaction Agents

nodes.label: Agent Tool Use

nodes.label: Computer-Use Agents

nodes.label: Tool-Use

nodes.label: Latent Space Compression
nodes.rationale: Training separate reasoning model to generate compact latent messages HK with K<<L while preserving task utility; achieves up to 24x reduction in communication latency.

nodes.label: Token-to-Latent Curriculum Learning
nodes.rationale: Stochastic replacement of early communication positions with plan token embeddings; stabilizes training and enhances efficiency in learning to interpret latents.

nodes.label: Latent Space Communication
nodes.rationale: Direct transmission of last-layer hidden states between agents instead of discrete tokens; preserves continuous information and enables compression via latent-space reasoning.

nodes.label: ALFWorld Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Text-only embodied task benchmark simulating household tasks; used to evaluate Interlat latent communication against language-based baselines.

nodes.label: LLaMA3.1 Model
nodes.rationale: 8B-Base model used as actor agent in Interlat experiments; demonstrates cross-family latent communication capability.

nodes.label: Qwen2.5 Model Family
nodes.rationale: Base and instruction-tuned variants (7B, 0.5B) used as reasoning and actor agents in Interlat experiments.

nodes.label: Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD)
nodes.rationale: Cryptographic envelope used by providers to package reasoning traces with header, nonce, authentication tag, and ciphertext.

nodes.label: Distillation Attack Vector
nodes.rationale: Attack circumventing anti-distillation mechanisms to extract proprietary model reasoning by replaying encrypted traces into weaker decoder models.

nodes.label: Reasoning Extraction Attack
nodes.rationale: Scalable decryption jailbreak exploiting cross-model compatibility by injecting encrypted reasoning from capable model into weaker, less safeguarded model to force verbatim transcription.

nodes.label: Jailbreaking Attack Vector
nodes.rationale: Extracting harmful information hidden in reasoning process even when model's final output safely rejects malicious request.

nodes.label: Invisible Prompt Injection Attack Vector
nodes.rationale: Embedding malicious payloads entirely within encrypted reasoning blocks to poison public agentic rollouts without leaving plaintext artifacts.

nodes.label: LLM API Providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google)
nodes.rationale: Major API providers implementing encrypted reasoning traces vulnerable to the described attacks.

nodes.label: Secret Extraction Attack Vector
nodes.rationale: Large-scale private data extraction from publicly shared reasoning blocks, recovering 367 PII artifacts and 182 credentials from 315,320 decoded traces.

nodes.label: Encrypted Reasoning Trace Portability Vulnerability
nodes.rationale: Encrypted reasoning blocks are fully compatible and interchangeable across different sessions, users, and models within provider ecosystem, enabling cross-model decryption attacks.

nodes.label: Claim Check
nodes.rationale: Matches reported numbers to recorded outputs and claims to recorded analyses, ensuring full numerical traceability and claim support

nodes.label: Experiment Stage
nodes.rationale: Iterative code generation with controlled execution, figure capture, and rigour check verifying provenance, multiple-comparison correction, and independence

nodes.label: Rigour Check
nodes.rationale: Code-enforced verification of real execution, all-test accounting, independence, leakage, headline support, and anti-HARKing constraints

nodes.label: Writeup Stage
nodes.rationale: Discipline-aware manuscript generation with 5 structural specifications, section-level expansion from execution record, and claim verification

nodes.label: Field-Specific Writeup Templates

nodes.label: Claim Admission Protocol

nodes.label: Deterministic Gates and Failure Conditions
nodes.rationale: Verification mechanism distinguishing machine-checkable properties (artifact existence, evidence grounding, citation resolution, compilation) from semantic judgment

nodes.label: Evidence-Grounded Experiment Execution

nodes.label: AI-Native Experimental Paradigm

nodes.label: Separate Linear and Activation Functions
nodes.rationale: Theorems 7-8 prove attention heads can separately implement row-wise linear transformations and entry-wise activation functions.

nodes.label: Masking Pattern Encoding in Weights

nodes.label: Bias Token Mechanism

nodes.label: Generalized SiLU Activation Function
nodes.rationale: Function class a1*SiLU(a2*x) that includes SiLU and close approximations of ReLU and GeLU. Required for MLP-attention equivalence proofs.

nodes.label: Masked Softmax Function
nodes.rationale: Row-wise softmax applied only to unmasked entries. Core operation in masked attention heads used for MLP implementation.

nodes.label: Transformer Architecture

nodes.label: Idea Check (Exit Predicate)
nodes.rationale: Deterministic validation of ideation stage; enforces schema completeness, breadth (≥5 candidates), prior art searches, feasibility, novelty evidence, and claim scope; rejected 28 finalize attempts.

nodes.label: Ideation Stage
nodes.rationale: ReAct loop formulating concrete, novel, falsifiable hypotheses with code-enforced checks for completeness, novelty, and leakage

nodes.label: Perception Layer
nodes.rationale: Hierarchical organization of raw artifacts by evidence family and modality with registered tools for native numeric and visual analysis

nodes.label: OpenAlex API for Literature Search
nodes.rationale: Tool for novelty screening and reference retrieval in ideation and writeup stages

nodes.label: ReAct: Reasoning and Acting
nodes.rationale: Agentic loop interleaving observation, reasoning, and action to enable evidence-driven hypothesis formulation
nodes.source_location: Section 4.2, cited from Yao et al. 2023

nodes.label: STEAD Seismic Benchmark
nodes.rationale: 1,500 three-component broadband seismograms with earthquake/noise labels used for noise audit case study

nodes.label: Answer Evaluation Protocol
nodes.rationale: Normalized containment matching: lowercase, remove markup/quotes, collapse whitespace; prediction correct when normalized gold answer appears as substring of normalized prediction

nodes.label: Final Answer Ground Truth
nodes.rationale: Constructed by executing one valid ground-truth path; M_gen walks through sequence and invokes tools in order to obtain target datatype values

nodes.label: Tool Description Generation
nodes.rationale: Natural-language explanations of tool functionality generated by M_gen; clarify contextual meaning of returned datatypes and distinguish tools with similar signatures

nodes.label: Tool Filtering
nodes.rationale: M_fil screens candidate tools using four criteria: deterministic dependency, tool-grounded information access, domain realism, non-trivial information gain

nodes.label: Deterministic Dependency
nodes.rationale: Input datatype set must be sufficient for determining output datatype set; excludes tools with redundant inputs

nodes.label: Domain Realism
nodes.rationale: Input-output relation must be plausible under retail domain semantics encoded in database and datatype inventory

nodes.label: Non-Trivial Information Gain
nodes.rationale: Output datatype set must contribute genuinely new state information, not merely rename, format, or echo available values

nodes.label: Tool-Grounded Information Access
nodes.rationale: Tool must retrieve or derive information from external database, not encode pure reasoning shortcut model could perform without environment interaction

nodes.label: GPT-5.2
nodes.rationale: Used as M_gen for data construction and final answer generation; used as M_fil for tool filtering

nodes.label: Anchor Weakness Risk in Evaluator Evolution
nodes.norm_label: anchor weakness risk in evaluator evolution
nodes.rationale: Weak, noisy, or biased anchor allows evaluators to drift across epochs; particularly problematic since APReS decisions and IMO-GradingBench grades are imperfect

nodes.label: Best-Belief Lower-Bound Trajectory
nodes.rationale: Calibration statement about selected lower-bound trajectory; justifies interpreting increasing best-belief curve as increasing posterior evidence for better agents

nodes.label: Calibration Assumption in Working Posterior
nodes.rationale: Working posterior is mean-consistent only; calibration assumption cannot strictly hold in real-world deployments due to systemic volatility

nodes.label: Epoch-Local Theoretical Guarantees
nodes.rationale: Theoretical guarantees for RQGM are inherently localized and constrained; do not bound transition counts, cumulative regret, or long-term convergence

nodes.label: Evaluator Anchor Lower Bound at Checkpoint
nodes.norm_label: evaluator anchor lower bound at checkpoint
nodes.rationale: Per-checkpoint lower-bound statement; evaluator slot is fixed-criterion selection sampled at checkpoints because replacement test scored only on fixed anchor

nodes.label: Exponential Checkpoint Overhead with Linear Work
nodes.norm_label: exponential checkpoint overhead with linear work
nodes.rationale: Total reprocessed records over exponential checkpoints is O(B) with constant at most ρ/(ρ-1); base-two schedule yields bound of at most 2B

nodes.label: Piecewise Fixed-Criterion Validity
nodes.rationale: Epoch-local result: after conditioning on checkpoint decision and applying selective erasure, each realized epoch is compatible with fixed-criterion binary-outcome interface

nodes.label: Stationary Learned-Evaluation Condition
nodes.rationale: Within each epoch, evaluator-dependent roles satisfy stationary learned-evaluation condition; cannot strictly hold due to provider-side model updates and nondeterministic tools

nodes.label: Controlled Utility Evolution in RQGM
nodes.rationale: Describes slot-m replacement rule, best-belief lower-bound trajectory, and piecewise fixed-criterion validity for evaluator evolution

nodes.label: Automated Scientific Method Implementation
nodes.rationale: Multi-agent systems mirror core aspects of scientific reasoning: hypothesis generation, peer review, debate, evolution, synthesis

nodes.label: Evolution Agent

nodes.label: Generation Agent
nodes.rationale: Initiates research by generating focus areas, hypotheses, and proposals; employs literature search, synthesis, and simulated scientific debates

nodes.label: Meta-Review Agent
nodes.rationale: Synthesizes insights from reviews and tournament debates; identifies patterns to optimize other agents; enables feedback propagation without backpropagation

nodes.label: Proximity Agent
nodes.rationale: Computes similarity between hypotheses; enables clustering, deduplication, and efficient exploration of hypothesis landscape

nodes.label: Ranking Agent with Elo Tournament
nodes.rationale: Employs Elo-based tournament for pairwise hypothesis comparisons via scientific debate; reduces positional bias and enables nuanced evaluation

nodes.label: Reflection Agent
nodes.rationale: Simulates peer review; critically examines correctness, quality, novelty; prevents hallucination through external search tool integration

nodes.label: Effective Spin Parameter Subspace

nodes.source_location: Section 2.4.1, Definition of Physical Parameter Subspaces

nodes.label: Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP)

nodes.rationale: NRSur7dq4, IMRPhenomXO4a, SEOBNRv5PHM, IMRPhenomXPHM, IMRPhenomTPHM compared for systematic uncertainties

nodes.label: Bias and Toxicity Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Comprehensive evaluation on CrowS-Pairs, StereoSet, RealToxicityPrompts, and TruthfulQA showing Galactica exhibits lower bias than comparable models due to scientific corpus.

nodes.label: Protein Function Description Generation

nodes.label: Protein Keyword Prediction Task
nodes.rationale: Task to predict UniProt keywords from protein sequences alone, demonstrating translation from sequence modality to natural language annotations.

nodes.label: Protein Sequence Understanding in Galactica
nodes.rationale: Galactica learns implicit sequence similarity measures from protein sequences without explicit 3D structure modeling. Enables functional annotation and description prediction tasks.

nodes.label: Sequence Validation Perplexity
nodes.rationale: Evaluation metric for protein sequence understanding using holdout sets (CASPSeq, PaenSeq, UniProtSeq) to measure generalization and detect memorization.

nodes.label: Multi-Modal Learning in Language Models
nodes.rationale: Galactica demonstrates learning across text and scientific modalities (SMILES, protein sequences) within single model. Enables cross-modal reasoning and annotation.

nodes.label: Scientific Corpus Construction
nodes.rationale: Galactica training corpus includes 48M papers, 8M reference materials, 2M knowledge bases, and filtered CommonCrawl. Totals ~120B tokens with quality filters applied.

nodes.label: Work Token for Step-by-Step Reasoning
nodes.rationale: Special token enabling intermediate reasoning steps. Improves performance on MATH and MMLU benchmarks compared to chain-of-thought prompting.

nodes.label: Parallel Explore-Exploit (PEE) Orchestrator

nodes.label: Chain-of-Evidence (CoE) Framework
nodes.rationale: Verifiability framework requiring every claim to trace through recorded evidence chain to grounding source; defines what properties verifiable research artifacts must have

nodes.label: Numerical Claim Provenance Rate (CPR)
nodes.rationale: Native check unique to ScientistOne; measures fraction of quantitative claims tracing to matching entry in experimental log; achieves 98.1% (627/639 claims pass)

nodes.label: Claim Verifier
nodes.rationale: Verifies numerical claims (numeric tolerance), citation claims (LLM judge on abstract support), methodological claims (textual overlap against experimental log).

nodes.label: Chain-of-Evidence (CoE) Integrity Audit
nodes.rationale: Four-component audit: Score Verification (LLM extraction + deterministic comparison), Specification Violation (LLM-judged majority vote), Reference Verification (API-based + LLM disambiguation), Method-Code Alignment (LLM-judged).

nodes.label: CoE Integrity Audit
nodes.rationale: Post-hoc audit with four integrity checks: Score Verification (I1), Specification Violation (I2), Reference Verification (I3), Method-Code Alignment (I4)

nodes.label: I1: Score Verification Errors
nodes.rationale: 22 confirmed errors across five systems: value_mismatch (59%), cross_stage_cherry_pick (18%), paper_score_unavailable (9%), evaluator_error (5%), metric_mismatch (9%).

nodes.label: I2: Specification Violation Analysis
nodes.rationale: 11 flagged papers: evaluator import (10 Sakana), evaluator exploitation (7), specification exploit (5), data leakage (1). Sakana ASv2 accounts for 10/11 violations.

nodes.label: I3: Reference Integrity – Hallucinated References
nodes.rationale: Discovered hallucinated references: ARC (1), AIR (21), DS (41). Examples include fabricated papers on optimization, distributed systems, and database techniques.

nodes.label: I4: Method-Code Alignment Findings
nodes.rationale: 95 findings across 25 papers: incomplete_broken (52%), algorithm_class_mismatch (39%), deceptive_dummy_code (9%). ARC only system with deceptive_dummy_code findings.

nodes.label: Method-Code Alignment (I4) Check
nodes.rationale: LLM reads paper method section and solution code side-by-side; judges whether paper faithfully describes what code does; acceptable simplification treated as aligned

nodes.label: Paper Writer
nodes.rationale: Five-stage pipeline enforcing 'provenance before prose': Conceive (narrative structure), Ground (evidence validation), Critic (coherence audit), Resolve (flag resolution), Compose (LaTeX generation).

nodes.label: Problem Investigator (PI)
nodes.rationale: Five-stage pipeline: citation graph traversal, literature filtering, multi-round investigation with specialist agents, evaluation protocol audit, experiment brief synthesis.

nodes.label: Reference Verification (I3) Check
nodes.rationale: Resolves each bibliography entry via multiple academic APIs; LLM cross-checks against returned records; entries matching no record classified as hallucinated

nodes.label: Score Verification (I1) Check
nodes.rationale: Extracts paper's reported score, re-runs solution on golden evaluator, compares within adaptive tolerance accounting for evaluator noise

nodes.label: Solver
nodes.rationale: Two-agent system: Solution Development Agent (iterative refinement in sandbox) and Report Writing Agent (generates technical report from artifacts).

nodes.label: Specification Violation (I2) Check
nodes.rationale: Detects when solution code breaks task rules (reverse-engineering evaluator, hardcoding answers); LLMs inspect code against evaluator and task spec with majority vote

nodes.label: ADRS Benchmark Tasks
nodes.rationale: Five systems-optimization research problems: Prism (LLM-serving model placement), Cloudcast (cloud network cost), EPLB (expert-parallel load balancing), LLM-SQL (tabular data layout), TXN (transaction scheduling)

nodes.label: CoE Integrity Audit Results (Table 1)
nodes.rationale: Comprehensive audit of 75 papers (5 systems × 3 seeds × 5 tasks); ScientistOne achieves perfect score verification (12/12), zero hallucinated references (0/337), highest method-code alignment (14/15)

nodes.label: Failure Mode Case 1: Six Orders of Magnitude
nodes.norm_label: failure mode case 1: six orders of magnitude
nodes.rationale: ARC LLM-SQL seed 2; paper reports combined score 1,538,006.69 on [0,1] scale; actually internal metric sum of squared prefix-hit lengths

nodes.label: Failure Mode Case 2: Bibliography from Model Memory
nodes.norm_label: failure mode case 2: bibliography from model memory
nodes.rationale: AIR PRISM seed 1; 3 of 15 references hallucinated; AIR and DS produce hallucinated references at 9% and 21% rates respectively

nodes.label: Failure Mode Case 3: Convergent Specification Violation
nodes.norm_label: failure mode case 3: convergent specification violation
nodes.rationale: DS LLM-SQL seed 1; code sorts columns per row-group then renames back; exploits gap between evaluator checks and benchmark intent

nodes.label: Failure Mode Case 4: Fictional Algorithm
nodes.rationale: ARC TXN seed 1; paper describes STAR with bitwise encoding and O(1) surrogate; code uses standard Python sets and full simulator

nodes.label: MLE-Bench Generalization Tasks
nodes.rationale: Five Kaggle competitions spanning medical imaging, fine-grained recognition, 3D perception; ScientistOne earns two Gold Medals and two Silver Medals

nodes.label: Parameter Golf LLM Training Task

nodes.label: Beat-Reference Filter (fairness mechanism)
nodes.rationale: Direction-aware filter excluding MALT scoring attempts exceeding reference solution, applied per attempt rather than per run. Central fairness rule ensuring neither paper agent nor ARA agent carries worked-out beating-reference solution that could be transcribed.

nodes.label: Exploration Graph and Dead-End Tracking
nodes.rationale: Promotes dead ends to first-class nodes with structured failure modes and claim cross-references, making negative knowledge machine-queryable. Addresses finding that 59.2% of agent tokens on RE-Bench spent on dead-end exploration discarded by published artifacts.

nodes.label: Negative Knowledge and Failed Trajectories
nodes.rationale: Recent work shows failure traces become actionable only when annotated with root-cause structure. Large-scale experiment logs retain >99.99% more search history than papers report. ARA promotes dead ends to first-class nodes, making negative knowledge machine-queryable rather than lost to narrative selection.

nodes.label: RE-Bench Extension Experiment
nodes.rationale: Tests whether preserving failure trajectories from prior research enables next agent to extend work more effectively; uses 5 RE-Bench tasks with real MALT agent failure traces to measure whether structured dead-end documentation closes exploration gaps.

nodes.label: Sonnet 4.5 Base Model Inversion
nodes.rationale: On triton_cumsum and restricted_mlm, Sonnet 4.5 trajectories invert Sonnet 4.6 results: ARA agent outperforms paper agent. Suggests artifact value scales with gap between documented trace and agent's own discovery bandwidth; weaker base benefits from ranked heuristic list.

nodes.label: Claude Sonnet 4.6 Agent Trajectories
nodes.rationale: Comparison of paper agent vs ARA agent on 5 RE-Bench tasks. ARA agent reaches useful first move earlier on all tasks; ends with better score on rust_codecontests, nanogpt_chat_rl, fix_embedding; paper agent overtakes on triton_cumsum and restricted_mlm via moves trace does not name.

nodes.label: BCH Quantum Codes
nodes.rationale: Algebraic counterexamples: refute rank-only bounds, demonstrate escape from two-dimensional geometric intuition.

nodes.label: CSS Quantum Error Correction Codes
nodes.rationale: Mathematical objects: binary CSS codes specified by check matrices HX and HZ satisfying commutation condition, central to quantum error correction.

nodes.label: Quantum Golay Code [[23,1,7]]
nodes.rationale: Benchmark quantum code: forces ceiling form of rank-distance conjecture, sharp for rank-locality envelope.

nodes.label: Rank-Distance Conjecture
nodes.rationale: Main discovery: relationship between CSS distance and check rank, refined through counterexamples (Steane, Golay, BCH, toric codes).

nodes.label: Symmetric Maximum Rank-Locality Envelope
nodes.rationale: Main conjecture: d(C) ≤ max_σ ⌊rank(Hσ) + 7wmax_σ/8⌋, combining check rank and maximum check weight on both X and Z sides.

nodes.label: Steane Code [[7,1,3]]
nodes.rationale: Benchmark quantum code: sharp for floor form of rank-distance conjecture and for rank-locality envelope.

nodes.label: Toric Code Family
nodes.rationale: Geometric benchmark: shows square-root exponent 1/2 is sharp for rank-distance relationship in two-dimensional surface codes.

nodes.label: Emotional Validation Theory
nodes.rationale: Four-level hierarchical framework from DBT (Linehan, 1997): LEVEL 1 (Listening and Observing), LEVEL 2 (Accurate Reflection), LEVEL 3 (Validating), LEVEL 4 (Radical Genuineness).

nodes.label: EmpathieticDialogues Dataset
nodes.rationale: Crowdsourced empathetic conversation dataset from US-based MTurk workers with diverse personal experiences (Rashkin et al., 2019).

nodes.label: EPITOME Framework
nodes.rationale: RoBERTa-based framework measuring empathy through three dimensions: Interpretations (IP), Explorations (EX), and Emotional Reactions (ER) (Sharma et al., 2020).

nodes.label: ESConv Dataset
nodes.rationale: Emotional Support Conversation dataset with trained crowdworkers as supporters and real/simulated help-seekers; ensures balanced gender representation and high authenticity (Liu et al., 2021).

nodes.label: Emotional Validation Aware Dataset (EVAD)
nodes.rationale: Human preference dataset annotated with emotional validation levels; constructed by prompting ChatGPT to generate utterances at each level, then filtered and ranked by human annotators.

nodes.label: EVAEval Metric
nodes.rationale: Novel evaluation metric assessing whether model-generated responses align with emotional validation theory by measuring distribution of emotional levels across dialogue quartiles.

nodes.label: EVA: Empathetic LLMs with Emotional Validation
nodes.norm_label: eva: empathetic llms with emotional validation
