nodes.label: BDH-CQ Composition: Operation-Dependent Success
nodes.rationale: Rotation composes with relocation on 72/72 outputs; reflection on 47/72; color swap on 0/72. Composition success depends on representation: fixed-layout motifs enable color-swap inference (26/72) but shuffled layouts fail (1/24 each). Demonstrates representation-dependent learning.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Conditional Rule Selection: 56.7% vs. 100% Control
nodes.norm_label: bdh-cq conditional rule selection: 56.7% vs. 100% control
nodes.rationale: Controlled ladder: when marker varies but both values invoke same rule, 40/40 solved (100%). When marker selects between two rules, 68/120 solved (56.7%), a 43.3-point decrease (p=9×10⁻⁹). Indicates difficulty in using contextual cues to select among demonstrated rules.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Generalization: Propagation vs. Ordering vs. Nesting
nodes.norm_label: bdh-cq generalization: propagation vs. ordering vs. nesting
nodes.rationale: Controlled experiments reveal distinct extrapolation patterns: propagation and copying remain correct at 48/48 across tested ranges; ordering saturates at length 5 then falls to 1/24 at length 8; nesting saturates through depth 4 then falls to 29/36 at depth 5. Matched demonstrations recover most failures, indicating extrapolation rather than execution limits.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Mechanic-Stratified Performance: 68.6% Flood Fill to 2.9% Gravity
nodes.norm_label: bdh-cq mechanic-stratified performance: 68.6% flood fill to 2.9% gravity
nodes.rationale: 1,131 generated tasks across 16 mechanics: Flood fill 68.6%, Denoising 56.9%, Scaling 53.7%, ..., Gravity/stacking 2.9%. Spread 65.7 points (p<0.00005 vs. permutation null). Hand-written gravity 80–100% vs. generated 2.9%, indicating task-authoring confound. Mechanic useful diagnostic but not intrinsic operation ranking.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Panel Union: Separation and Count Effects
nodes.norm_label: bdh-cq panel union: separation and count effects
nodes.rationale: Two opposite-corner panels: 26/40 solved (65%). Two touching panels: 3/40 (7.5%). Three panels: 1/40 (2.5%). Separation matters before panel count; suggests segmentation limitation. Consistent with output-level analysis showing 89% of failures preserve correct dimensions.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Support Chain: Dependency Depth Cost
nodes.norm_label: bdh-cq support chain: dependency depth cost
nodes.rationale: Support chains (objects resting on objects): 80% with 1 object, 67.5% with 3, 52.5% with 5, 27.5% with 8. Monotonic decrease suggests dependency-depth cost. Three independent objects reach 40/40, showing multiplicity alone insufficient; gradient consistent with relational depth but not isolated from object count.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Parameter Extrapolation: Demonstrated vs. Unseen
nodes.norm_label: bdh-cq parameter extrapolation: demonstrated vs. unseen
nodes.rationale: Marker-count parameter for downward shift: when value appears in demonstrations, 12/40 solved (30%); when absent, 0/120 solved (0%). Boundary is demonstrated-value presence, not interpolation/extrapolation range. Indicates limited parameter generalization beyond demonstrated values.

nodes.label: Theme: Structured Generalization Boundaries
nodes.rationale: BDH-CQ exhibits operation-specific extrapolation limits: propagation/copying unbounded in tested range, ordering/nesting cliff at specific depths, conditional selection 43.3-point drop, unseen parameters 30-point drop, panel separation 62.5-point drop. Boundaries not uniform; depend on representation, demonstrated support, and relational depth. Suggests capability profile shaped by multiple factors rather than single 'reasoning difficulty' scalar.

nodes.rationale: Persistent grid kernel with atomic counter for work claiming to handle variable-length sequences and data-dependent sparsity

nodes.label: MSA Efficiency Results
nodes.rationale: 28.4× per-token attention FLOP reduction at 1M context, 14.2× prefill and 7.6× decoding wall-clock speedups on H800

nodes.label: Exp-Free Top-K Selection
nodes.rationale: GPU kernel optimization bypassing softmax computation by directly ranking scores, preserving order-preservation property

nodes.label: Gradient Detachment Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Stop-gradient applied to Index Branch input to confine KL loss to indexer projections, preventing backbone degradation

nodes.label: Index Branch Component
nodes.rationale: Lightweight indexer that scores KV blocks and selects top-k for each GQA group using max-pooling over token-level scores

nodes.label: Indexer Warmup Training Schedule
nodes.rationale: Two-stage training: initial full attention phase trains index projections with KL loss, then switches to sparse attention

nodes.label: KL Alignment Loss
nodes.rationale: Auxiliary training objective matching Index Branch selection distribution to Main Branch attention on selected tokens

nodes.label: KV-Outer Iteration Order
nodes.rationale: Kernel design iterating over KV blocks on outer loop with query gathering to maximize arithmetic intensity for sparse attention

nodes.label: Local Block Forcing
nodes.rationale: Always include local block containing query position in selected set to ensure training stability and preserve local context

nodes.label: Long-Context Extension Experiment
nodes.rationale: 140B tokens of long-context training showing MSA preserves capability with tight 2048-token attention budget

nodes.label: Main Branch Component
nodes.rationale: Standard scaled dot-product softmax attention restricted to tokens in blocks selected by Index Branch

nodes.label: MiniMax Sparse Attention Architecture
nodes.rationale: Two-branch sparse attention: lightweight Index Branch selects top-k KV blocks per GQA group, Main Branch performs exact attention on selected blocks

nodes.label: MSA-CPT: Sparse Continued Pretraining
nodes.rationale: Converting pretrained GQA checkpoint to MSA through continued pretraining on 400B tokens, practical conversion route

nodes.label: MSA-PT: From-Scratch Sparse Pretraining
nodes.rationale: Training MSA model from scratch on 3T tokens with 40B-token indexer warmup, learns sparse patterns throughout pretraining

nodes.label: Pre-Scheduled Tile Chunking
nodes.rationale: GPU scheduler splits hot KV tiles across multiple CTAs to handle skewed block popularity without atomic updates

nodes.label: Query Concatenation Optimization
nodes.rationale: Pack multiple query positions sharing same KV operands into single MMA to improve tensor-core utilization

nodes.label: Sliding Window Baseline Comparison
nodes.rationale: Dynamic sparse selection outperforms fixed sliding-window pattern on agent tasks under same FLOP budget

nodes.label: Two-Phase Forward Pass
nodes.rationale: Split-K attention computation with intermediate buffers for partial outputs and log-sum-exps to handle KV-outer iteration

nodes.label: GQA Enables Group-Specific Sparse Selection
nodes.rationale: Grouped Query Attention allows per-group independent block selection while maintaining efficient block-level execution

nodes.label: MSA Addresses Quadratic Attention Bottleneck
nodes.rationale: Sparse attention mechanism directly addresses quadratic cost of softmax attention, key bottleneck for ultra-long-context LLMs

nodes.label: MSA Kernel Design Critical for Realizing Speedups
nodes.norm_label: msa kernel design critical for realizing speedups
nodes.rationale: Theoretical FLOP reduction must be paired with efficient GPU kernels to translate to practical wall-clock speedups

nodes.label: MSA Supports Native Multimodal Training
nodes.rationale: MSA validated on 109B model with native multimodal training on text, image, and video data

nodes.label: LLM Hallucination Problem
nodes.rationale: Well-known issue where LLMs generate incorrect code, unsupported conclusions, or fabricated information

nodes.label: Validation and Evaluation Framework
nodes.rationale: Process of checking whether claims in AI-generated papers are true; includes code verification and result validation

nodes.label: Gene Co-expression Module Identification
nodes.rationale: Clustering genes based on similarity of smoothed pseudotemporal expression patterns to identify coordinated biological processes
nodes.source_location: Section 2.9, Identification and Characterization of Gene Modules

nodes.label: Plasmodium falciparum Parasite
nodes.rationale: Eukaryotic parasite causing malaria; model organism for studying adaptation to laboratory vs. field environments

nodes.label: Pseudotime Assignment and Analysis
nodes.rationale: Abstract measure of developmental progress assigned to cells along inferred trajectories
nodes.source_location: Section 2.7, Developmental Trajectory Inference and Pseudotime Assignment

nodes.label: Putative Regulatory Network Inference
nodes.rationale: Inference of downstream targets of transient regulators based on temporal precedence in pseudotime
nodes.source_location: Section 2.11, Inference of Putative Regulatory Interactions

nodes.label: Single-Cell RNA Sequencing (scRNA-seq) Analysis
nodes.rationale: High-resolution transcriptomic approach to dissect heterogeneous cell populations and reconstruct developmental trajectories

nodes.label: Developmental Trajectory Inference
nodes.rationale: Reconstruction of continuous developmental progression through high-dimensional gene expression space using pseudotime ordering
nodes.source_location: Section 2.7, Developmental Trajectory Inference and Pseudotime Assignment

nodes.label: Candidate Transient Regulator Identification
nodes.rationale: Identification of genes with transient expression peaks preceding major transcriptional shifts or stage transitions
nodes.source_location: Section 2.10, Identification of Candidate Transient Regulators

nodes.label: Inference Cost Parity in Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Self-correction uses multiple LLM responses; fair comparison requires baselines with equivalent inference costs; multi-agent debate should be compared against self-consistency with same number of responses.

nodes.label: Intrinsic Self-Correction Concept
nodes.rationale: Self-correction without external feedback; model must independently determine correctness and decide whether to retain or revise answers; contrasts with oracle-guided approaches that use ground-truth labels.

nodes.label: Self-Correction Performance Findings
nodes.rationale: Intrinsic self-correction decreases accuracy across GSM8K, CommonSenseQA, HotpotQA; models more likely to convert correct answers to incorrect ones; GPT-4/4-Turbo retain initial answers more often due to higher confidence.

nodes.label: Multi-Agent Debate vs Self-Consistency
nodes.rationale: Multi-agent debate underperforms self-consistency with equivalent number of responses; improvement attributed to consistency voting rather than genuine self-correction or debate mechanism.

nodes.label: Oracle Label Dependency in Self-Correction
nodes.rationale: Prior work (RCI, Reflexion) uses ground-truth labels to determine when to stop self-correction; improvements vanish without oracle feedback; counter-intuitive for reasoning tasks where ground truth availability negates need for LLM problem-solving.

nodes.label: Prompt Design Issues in Self-Correction
nodes.rationale: Improvements in prior work stem from suboptimal initial prompts; feedback prompts contain task specifications absent from initial prompts; integrating feedback into initial prompt yields better results than self-correction.

nodes.label: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
nodes.norm_label: large language models cannot self-correct reasoning yet
nodes.rationale: Critical examination of intrinsic self-correction (without external feedback) in LLMs; demonstrates performance degradation on reasoning tasks; identifies issues in prior work including oracle label reliance, unfair baseline comparisons, and suboptimal prompt design.

nodes.label: RAKE-based Concept Extraction
nodes.rationale: Rapid Automatic Keyword Extraction algorithm refined with GPT, Wikipedia, and manual review to generate concept list

nodes.label: GPT Zero-Shot Ranking
nodes.rationale: LLM-based pairwise comparison and ELO ranking of research ideas without human evaluation data

nodes.label: Neural Network Interest Prediction
nodes.rationale: Supervised small neural network (25 features, 50 neurons) trained on human evaluations to predict high-interest ideas

nodes.label: OpenAlex Scientific Database
nodes.rationale: Open-source database of 58M+ scientific papers with metadata used for knowledge graph edge generation

nodes.label: Large-Scale Human Evaluation
nodes.rationale: 110 research group leaders from Max Planck Society evaluated 4,451 AI-generated research ideas on 1-5 interest scale

nodes.label: Scientific Knowledge Graph
nodes.rationale: Graph with 123,128 scientific concepts extracted from 2.44M paper titles/abstracts, edges from co-occurrence in 58M papers

nodes.label: Extension Evaluation (5 RE-Bench tasks)
nodes.rationale: Open-ended R&D tasks: triton_cumsum, restricted_mlm, fix_embedding, nanogpt_chat_rl, rust_codecontests. ARA provides early initialization (shortcuts diagnostic phase), acts as anchor (prevents over-exploration), and surfaces high-value dead ends.

nodes.label: Case Study: fix_embedding (permuted embedding recovery)
nodes.rationale: Both agents implement published 3-phase adapter pipeline correctly (ARA 0.246 vs paper 0.250 by t=180min). Post-reference divergence: paper agent retries permutation recovery (abandoned at t=19min, retried at t=350min); ARA agent never attempts (H11/H13 forbid it). ARA exploration constrained by LR-region heuristics; paper agent invents additional phases.

nodes.label: Case Study: nanogpt_chat_rl (preference RL on 1.5B model)
nodes.norm_label: case study: nanogpt_chat_rl (preference rl on 1.5b model)
nodes.rationale: ARA agent reads trace at t=6.3min, commits to reference-style orchestration (continuation harness) vs paper agent's algorithmic redesign (DPO-plus-SFT). Trace provides empirical anchor ('no MALT run reached 0.85'), bug-fix vocabulary (H08: filter degenerate outputs), and strategy with built-in continuation criterion.

nodes.label: Case Study: restricted_mlm (constrained masked language model)
nodes.norm_label: case study: restricted_mlm (constrained masked language model)
nodes.rationale: Only task where ARA-vs-paper sign flips across models: Sonnet 4.5 ARA 0.73 vs paper 1.03; Sonnet 4.6 paper 0.69 vs ARA 1.02. All four agents discover same architectural family (BiBigramMLM + ConvMLM*). Divergence in exploration breadth: ARA-4.5 commits to single architecture (7h fine-tuning); paper-4.6 invents ConvMLMDilated and trains in serial.

nodes.label: Case Study: rust_codecontests (LLM-as-tool scaffolding)
nodes.rationale: ARA trace converts MALT data point (supplement_run_5: 0.097) into heuristics H12 (hand-coded library outperforms) and H15 (GPT-3.5 ceiling ~0.05-0.10). ARA agent reaches 78 by t=269min vs paper agent's 39 by t=231min, then independently rediscovers library approach at t=395min.

nodes.label: Case Study: triton_cumsum (GPU kernel optimization)
nodes.rationale: ARA agent cites heuristic H01 (grid size 128 for H100) and picks NUM_STAGES ∈{4,8} vs paper agent's {1,24,32,48,64,96}. ARA achieves ~0.27 vs paper ~0.64 on Sonnet 4.5. On 4.6, paper agent overtakes via int8 compression (0.5GB memory vs 2GB).

nodes.label: Discourse-Marker Distant Supervision for Retrieval
nodes.rationale: Extends discourse-marker supervision from sentence-pair classification to corpus-scale retrieval. Phrases like 'to address this problem', 'more generally', 'as an example' identify adjacent sentences presenting problem-addressing, broader, or more specific relations. Markers stripped from input, used to define relevance.

nodes.label: RATIO Ideation Moves: ADDRESS, BROADEN, SPECIFY
nodes.norm_label: ratio ideation moves: address, broaden, specify
nodes.rationale: Three operation-specific retrieval tasks for scientific inspiration: ADDRESS retrieves approaches/insights responding to problems; BROADEN retrieves broader/more general formulations; SPECIFY retrieves concrete instances/narrower formulations. Represent complementary moves through ideation space.

nodes.label: RATIO Marker Lexicon Construction Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Multi-stage process: manual curation (400 frequent markers, expert inspection of 15 samples each), LLM expansion (SOTA models label candidates as strong-true/weak-true/false), rule-based pattern expansion (Hearst-style templates), expert screening. Yields 4,252 validated markers (3,862 ADDRESS, 316 BROADEN, 74 SPECIFY).

nodes.label: RATIO Silver Test Set with Human-Calibrated LLM Validation
nodes.norm_label: ratio silver test set with human-calibrated llm validation
nodes.rationale: High-precision evaluation set created via LLM filtering with human calibration. Two LLM judges evaluate query/gold for grammar, coherence, self-containment, and relation enforcement. Prompts calibrated against 300 expert annotations (F1 .83-.87). Final set: 17,579 queries with gold candidates.

nodes.label: RATIO Temporal Split for Contamination Prevention
nodes.norm_label: ratio temporal split for contamination prevention
nodes.rationale: Train: 2015-Sept 2025; Validation: Oct-Dec 2025; Test: Jan-May 2026. Ensures no test query/candidate seen during training; test pairs from papers published after all evaluated models' pre-training. Conservative evaluation of generalization to unseen text.

nodes.label: Manifest Construction and Trial Normalization
nodes.rationale: Converts heterogeneous benchmark outputs into unified trial table with 8,135 records; aligns injected artifacts with trial outputs; derives success/failure from verifier reward

nodes.label: Verifier Reward Oracle
nodes.rationale: Positive numeric reward = success; zero/missing/non-positive = failure; keeps taxonomy aligned with benchmark oracle rather than agent self-assessment

nodes.label: Empirical Scientific Discovery (Definition 1)
nodes.rationale: Operational definition: sequential process where agent generates hypotheses, selects subset for costly evaluation, observes outcomes, updates beliefs to guide subsequent search; identifies previously unknown relationships supported by empirical evidence.

nodes.label: Open-Ended Design Space
nodes.rationale: Vast, structured, potentially unbounded hypothesis space X where full enumeration is infeasible; agent must progressively construct search support through discovery process.

nodes.label: Recurrent Discovery Policy
nodes.rationale: Iterative cycle: generate candidates under current context, score/refine using acquisition signal, evaluate selected candidates, update Dt and surrogate, update search context; couples generation, evaluation, belief updating.

nodes.label: Sequential Inverse Design Formulation
nodes.rationale: Problem formulation where agent repeatedly decides which candidate to evaluate next under limited budget; maintains probabilistic surrogate learned from evaluated candidates; uses acquisition function to balance value and information gain.

nodes.label: Antibody CDRH3 Sequence Design
nodes.rationale: Biological sequence design domain; LDM achieves 18.2% lower mean binding energy than LLM-only baseline; competitive with specialized BO method AntBO.

nodes.label: AutoResearch Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Neural-network training-program search domain; LDM achieves 2.4× larger validation-BPB reduction than LLM-only baseline; exceeds best previously reported result.

nodes.label: Multi-Objective Molecular Optimization
nodes.rationale: Molecular design domain; LDM improves Pareto front hypervolume 62.4% over LLM-only and 63.1% over classical BO; demonstrates multi-objective capability.

nodes.label: Exploit-Explore-Discover Cycle
nodes.rationale: Tripartite scientific search regime extending classical exploitation-exploration dichotomy to include discovery of new search frontiers

nodes.label: Large Discovery Model (LDM)
nodes.rationale: Central framework that couples LLM generative priors with Gaussian process surrogate value signals for sequential scientific discovery under evaluation budget constraints

nodes.label: Burger's Equation
nodes.rationale: Canonical non-linear PDE used as test case for PINN latent space analysis

nodes.label: Closure Modeling vs. End-to-End Neural Operators
nodes.norm_label: closure modeling vs. end-to-end neural operators
nodes.rationale: Closure models augment numerical solvers with learned corrections (additive, coarse-grid only). Neural Operators replace solvers end-to-end (4–6 orders magnitude faster, differentiable, nonlinear multiscale mixing). Operators achieve better data efficiency and stability.

nodes.label: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs)
nodes.rationale: Neural network architecture that embeds physical laws directly into training objective

nodes.label: Noisy Tool Construction
nodes.rationale: Five noisy variants per executable tool (925 total for 185 executable tools); five noise categories test agent ability to reject unreliable tools using descriptions

nodes.label: Condition-Limited Tool
nodes.rationale: Tool has valid signature but only available under special record conditions not satisfied in benchmark instance

nodes.label: Deprecated Tool
nodes.rationale: Tool returns unsupported-endpoint error when invoked; appears normal but is unavailable

nodes.label: Non-Authoritative Value Tool
nodes.rationale: Tool returns preview, default, estimated, or otherwise non-final value instead of final backend truth

nodes.label: Stale Tool
nodes.rationale: Tool returns right type of field but value comes from outdated cache or lagging replica

nodes.label: Unreliable Tool
nodes.rationale: Tool declares intended output field but returns value from related but wrong backend field

nodes.label: Beyond-Gradient Learning
nodes.rationale: Systems improve by analyzing failures, modifying programs, adding tests, and maintaining procedural structures without retraining

nodes.label: Digital Colleague
nodes.rationale: AI system that accumulates project-specific memory, learns conventions, identifies failures, proposes improvements, and adapts from experience

nodes.label: Self-Evolving AI Ecosystem
nodes.rationale: Systems improve from experience by converting operational traces into validated memories, skills, tests, and policies

nodes.label: AutoGen
nodes.rationale: Multiple agents coordinate through conversation, role specialization, and structured workflows

nodes.label: MetaGPT
nodes.rationale: Multi-agent collaborative framework with role specialization and structured workflows

nodes.label: Multi-Agent Orchestration
nodes.rationale: Framework for coordinating multiple specialized agents in sequential or parallel workflows

nodes.label: Importance-Sampling Exponential Instability
nodes.rationale: Sequence-level importance weight decomposes as product of token-level ratios; exponentially unstable when sequence length T is large; explains why RL fine-tuning is sensitive to early policy movement.

nodes.label: KL Divergence Second-Order Bound
nodes.rationale: If D_KL(π_{θ+} ∥ π_θ) ≤ K and F(θ) ⪰ mI on update subspace, then block update obeys KL constraint; creates weight-space movement budget from policy-space trust region.

nodes.label: KL Leash: Policy-Space Trust Region
nodes.rationale: Policy-space trust region induces weight-space movement budget; RL fine-tuning must make progress through small controlled steps, not large jumps; bad initialization can push optimizer toward directions where small parameter movements create large policy drift.

nodes.label: REINFORCE Gradient Distribution
nodes.rationale: REINFORCE distributes sequence-level reward across token positions; forms basis for token-level surrogate objectives in RL fine-tuning.

nodes.label: Sequence-Level RLVR Objective
nodes.rationale: J(θ) = E[R(x,y)] where R ∈ {0,1} assigned to complete response; importance-weighted form exhibits exponential instability (e.g., 1.01^512 ≈ 163); token-level surrogates depend on first-order Taylor expansion accurate only when policies remain close.

nodes.label: First-Order Taylor Expansion for Token-Level Surrogates
nodes.norm_label: first-order taylor expansion for token-level surrogates
nodes.rationale: Token-level surrogates depend on first-order Taylor expansion; accurate only when rollout and updated policies remain close; dropping higher-order terms gives approximate token-level objective.

nodes.label: Limiting Cases of LDM
nodes.rationale: η→0: search driven by generative model alone; α→0: policy becomes classical Bayesian optimization; LDM operates between these limits, balancing structured prior and empirical acquisition.

nodes.label: AlphaEvolve
nodes.rationale: Couples language-model proposals with automated evaluators at scale; demonstrates feedback loop combining generation, evaluation, and search.

nodes.label: AlphaZero-like Methods
nodes.rationale: Combines generation, evaluation, and search with reliable feedback; effective for domains with cheap, repeatable evaluation.

nodes.label: Autonomous Research Agents
nodes.rationale: Prior work on LLM-based systems for hypothesis generation, code execution, experiment analysis; limited by lack of empirically grounded value signal and unreliable self-assessment.

nodes.label: Bayesian Optimization
nodes.rationale: Complementary capability: learns probabilistic surrogate from limited observations, uses acquisition function to balance performance vs uncertainty; limited by representation and search operators in structured spaces.

nodes.label: LLM Reasoning Systems
nodes.rationale: Prior work on inference-time scaling (chain-of-thought, tree search, best-of-N) with cheap verifiers; effective for domains with repeatable feedback but insufficient for scientific discovery with expensive evaluation.

nodes.label: Spherical Linear Interpolation Fusion
nodes.rationale: Norm-preserving geodesic rotation mechanism for integrating memory into residual stream

nodes.label: Spherical Steering Concept
nodes.rationale: Geodesic rotation of activations on hypersphere toward target concepts without training

nodes.label: von Mises-Fisher Distribution
nodes.rationale: Probabilistic distribution on unit hypersphere parameterized by mean direction (µ) and concentration (κ) for directional data

nodes.label: Zero-Shot Fact Injection Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Database write operation overwriting µ with target embedding and maximizing κ to force memory adoption without gradient updates

nodes.label: von Mises-Fisher N-Gram Memory Module
nodes.rationale: Theoretical proposal for zero-shot fact injection in LLMs using hyperspherical probabilistic distributions

nodes.norm_label: u.s. department of energy, office of science, office of high energy physics

nodes.rationale: Provided funding support to FS
