nodes.rationale: Provided funding support to KMS

nodes.label: Hallucination and Factuality
nodes.rationale: Challenge of agents generating false or unsupported information, critical for safety

nodes.label: Prompt Injection and Adversarial Attacks
nodes.rationale: Security vulnerability where malicious inputs manipulate agent behavior

nodes.label: Tool Misuse and Unintended Actions
nodes.rationale: Risk of agents using tools incorrectly or for unintended purposes

nodes.label: Agent Safety and Security
nodes.rationale: Critical concerns including prompt injection, hallucination, unauthorized actions, and alignment with human values

nodes.label: Claude Opus 4.8: Codeforces 1974C Solution
nodes.rationale: Model derived formula: S23 + S13 + S12 - 3*Sall, where Sij counts pairs matching positions i,j and Sall counts identical triples. Proposed hash-map implementation with long-long encoding for collision-free key representation.

nodes.label: Codeforces 1974C: Beautiful Triple Pairs
nodes.rationale: Competitive programming problem: count pairs of consecutive triples in array that differ in exactly one position. Requires efficient grouping by two-element patterns and subtraction of identical triples.

nodes.label: Gemini 3.5 Flash: Codeforces 1974C (Sorting Approach)
nodes.rationale: Model derived same formula but proposed sorting-based approach: collect triples as (y,z,x), sort, then iterate through blocks computing c*(S-c)/2 for each sub-block. Provided complete C++ implementation with fast I/O and detailed complexity analysis.

nodes.label: GPT-5.6 Sol: Codeforces 1974C (Competitive Programming)
nodes.rationale: Model provided detailed C++17 solution with unordered_map implementation, base encoding scheme (BASE=1000001LL), complexity analysis (expected O(n)), and discussion of hash collision avoidance for values up to 1e6.

nodes.label: Closure-Driven Crystallization (maturity signals)
nodes.rationale: Observations mature through closure signals: topic abandonment (k=5 turns), verbal affirmation, empirical resolution, artifact commitment. Contradiction trigger flags both entries and defers resolution to researcher briefing.

nodes.label: ARA Compiler Skill
nodes.rationale: Self-contained natural-language specification (482 lines) that turns any general-purpose coding agent into a domain-specialized ARA compilation system. Prescribes 4-stage reasoning: semantic deconstruction, cognitive mapping, physical stubbing, exploration graph extraction.

nodes.label: Engineering Tax (implementation details unwritten)
nodes.rationale: Gap between reviewer-sufficient prose and agent-sufficient specification leaves critical implementation details unwritten, requiring agents to infer or rediscover them.

nodes.label: Exploration Cost Analysis (24,008 runs)
nodes.rationale: 59.2% of tokens spent on below-reference runs (90.2% of cost). Median cost ratio 113× for below-ref vs reference runs. Dead-end exploration 44.8%, re-derivation 14.4%. RE-Bench tasks 73.4% below-reference vs SWAA 0.7%.

nodes.label: PDF Information Gap Analysis
nodes.rationale: 8,921 requirements across 23 PaperBench papers: 45.4% sufficient, 50.2% partial, 4.4% absent. Top gaps: missing hyperparameters (26.2%), vague descriptions (21.9%), cross-references (13.4%). Dataset acquisition only 5.4% sufficient.

nodes.label: Live Research Manager Skill
nodes.rationale: Operates continuously alongside researcher without interrupting work. Implements closure-driven crystallization (maturity signals: topic abandonment, verbal affirmation, empirical resolution, artifact commitment), cross-session continuity via reasoning log and key context fields.

nodes.label: PaperBench Corpus (23 ICML 2024 papers)
nodes.rationale: 23 papers spanning efficiency, alignment, interpretability, RL, scientific ML, generative models, optimization, retrieval, evaluation, adaptation. 15 papers in reproduction experiment (8 excluded due to compute/infrastructure constraints).

nodes.label: Reproduction Evaluation (15 papers)
nodes.rationale: Difficulty-weighted success rate: ARA 64.4% vs baseline 57.4%. Per-difficulty: easy 85.1% vs 80.2%, medium 68.5% vs 62.9%, hard 54.5% vs 46.0%. Largest gains on papers with complex multi-step pipelines (fre +21.3%, mechanistic-understanding +20.7%, pinn +19.5%).

nodes.label: Storytelling Tax (failed experiments discarded)
nodes.rationale: PDF publication imposes structural cost: failed experiments and rejected hypotheses are discarded to fit linear narrative, making negative knowledge systematically unavailable to downstream agents.

nodes.label: Understanding Evaluation (Category A/B/C)
nodes.rationale: 450 questions across 30 targets (23 PaperBench papers + 7 RE-Bench tasks). Category A (fidelity): 96.7% ARA vs 89.8% baseline. Category B (configuration): 92.6% vs 67.8%. Category C (failure knowledge): 81.4% vs 15.7%.

nodes.label: Coverage-N Metric
nodes.rationale: Fraction of unique ground-truth answers generated in N samples; measures breadth of answer coverage

nodes.label: KL Divergence from Pretraining Distribution
nodes.rationale: Measures alignment with pretraining distribution; lower values indicate better representativeness

nodes.label: Open-Ended Question Answering
nodes.rationale: Application domain with multiple valid answers where VS generates broader response distributions

nodes.label: DAPO-Math-17k Dataset
nodes.rationale: Mixed mathematics corpus with verifiable rewards used for DAPO training experiments.

nodes.label: Qwen3-8B PPO Rank Sweep
nodes.rationale: 216 runs across 9 LoRA ranks, 4 batch sizes, 6 seeds; fixed 500-step PPO schedule on mixed mathematics corpus with verifiable rewards; primary evidence for three-region behavior.

nodes.label: Rank-1 OLoRA-tail vs LoRA on Qwen3-8B
nodes.norm_label: rank-1 olora-tail vs lora on qwen3-8b
nodes.rationale: Batch size sweep at rank r=1; OLoRA-tail maintains ~+20% gain across all batch sizes (bs16–bs128), while LoRA degrades from +15% to −18% with 67% collapse risk.

nodes.label: Qwen3-8B Model
nodes.rationale: 8B parameter model used for PPO rank sweep and rank-1 OLoRA-tail experiments.

nodes.label: Opinion Convergence in LLM Groups
nodes.rationale: LLM groups exhibit stronger opinion convergence in both public tweet stance and private self-reported opinion compared to human groups, with systematic individual shifts.

nodes.label: Partner Influence Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Individuals shift toward first partner's stance; LLM agents show greater susceptibility to partner influence than humans.

nodes.label: Positive Drift in Public Tweet Stance
nodes.norm_label: positive drift in public tweet stance
nodes.rationale: LLM groups show significant increase in average tweet stance from round 1 to round 3, endorsing false statements in Depth topics, while human groups show no significant change.

nodes.label: Regression to the Mean Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Individuals with extreme initial stances tend to move toward midpoint; LLM agents show stronger correlations than humans in this tendency.

nodes.label: Code Mutation System
nodes.rationale: LLM generates novel code variants conditioned on parent node; mutations occur at code level with ideas embedded in prompts; scored empirically and backpropagated through tree.

nodes.label: PUCT Tree Search Algorithm
nodes.rationale: Polynomial Upper Confidence Trees applied to code search space; balances exploitation of high-scoring solutions with exploration via acquisition score PUCTi = ri + cpuct·E(i).

nodes.label: Method Recombination
nodes.rationale: Combines top-performing methods by prompting LLM to compare and explain technical similarities/differences, then instructs tree search to recombine best parts; differs from prior work by operating in conceptual space via prompts rather than distilled model space.

nodes.label: Research Idea Injection
nodes.rationale: Emulates expert behavior by injecting research instructions from literature into prompts; uses LLM summaries of papers or AI-assisted literature search to guide code generation.

nodes.label: Expected Hypervolume Improvement (EHVI)
nodes.rationale: Multi-objective acquisition function computing expected hypervolume gain of Pareto front without pre-specified objective weights

nodes.label: Expected Improvement (EI) Acquisition Function
nodes.rationale: Acquisition function measuring expected gain relative to current best, balancing exploitation and exploration

nodes.label: Gaussian Process Surrogate Model
nodes.rationale: Probabilistic surrogate providing calibrated posterior mean and uncertainty estimates to guide acquisition-based candidate selection

nodes.label: Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) Acquisition Function
nodes.rationale: Acquisition function combining predictive mean and uncertainty with adjustable exploration weight, with theoretical regret guarantees

nodes.label: AML Drug Repurposing Validation
nodes.rationale: In vitro validation of Co-Scientist predictions; Binimetinib showed IC50 as low as 2 nM in AML cell lines; KIRA6 demonstrated selective cytotoxicity

nodes.label: Antimicrobial Resistance Mechanism Discovery
nodes.rationale: Independently proposed cf-PICI phage tail interaction mechanism; matched unpublished experimental findings in co-timed study

nodes.label: Expert-in-the-Loop Workflow
nodes.rationale: Scientists specify goals, provide feedback, suggest hypotheses, and review outputs; AML study required <1 hour setup + ~3 hours final review

nodes.label: Liver Fibrosis Target Discovery
nodes.rationale: Identified novel epigenetic targets; two showed significant anti-fibrotic activity in hepatic organoids; one (Vorinostat) FDA-approved for cancer

nodes.label: LLM Wiki Three-Layer Architecture
nodes.rationale: Raw sources (immutable), wiki layer (LLM-generated markdown, owned by LLM), schema layer (configuration document defining structure and workflows); human curates sources and asks questions; LLM does maintenance.

nodes.label: LLM Wiki Indexing and Logging
nodes.rationale: index.md: content-oriented catalog (links, summaries, metadata); log.md: append-only chronological record (ingests, queries, lints) with parseable prefixes; enables navigation and timeline of wiki evolution.

nodes.label: LLM Wiki Operations: Ingest, Query, Lint
nodes.norm_label: llm wiki operations: ingest, query, lint
nodes.rationale: Ingest: process new source, update 10-15 wiki pages. Query: search relevant pages, synthesize answer, file results back as new pages. Lint: health-check for contradictions, stale claims, orphan pages, missing cross-references.

nodes.label: LLM Wiki: Persistent Knowledge Base Pattern
nodes.norm_label: llm wiki: persistent knowledge base pattern
nodes.rationale: Pattern for building personal knowledge bases using LLMs; LLM incrementally builds and maintains persistent wiki (markdown files) between raw sources and user; cross-references, contradictions, synthesis compiled once and kept current.

nodes.label: 23-Stage Research Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Formal pipeline with explicit contracts (JSON schemas, acceptance criteria, error-code namespaces) balancing granularity and overhead; stages organized into 8 phases (Research Scoping, Literature Discovery, Knowledge Synthesis, Experiment Design, Experiment Execution, Analysis & Decision, Paper Writing, Finalization).

nodes.label: ARC-Bench: Autonomous Research Benchmark
nodes.rationale: 25-topic ML benchmark (T01–T25) plus 20-topic scientific-domain extension (10 HEP, 7 biology, 3 statistics) supporting three evaluation modes: experiment-stage, end-to-end, and scientific-domain.

nodes.label: Citation Verification Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Four-layer pipeline (DOI resolution via CrossRef, fuzzy title matching against OpenAlex, arXiv identifier lookup, Semantic Scholar fallback) with LLM-based relevance check to classify references as Verified, Suspicious, or Hallucinated.

nodes.label: Cross-Run Evolution System
nodes.rationale: Persistent lesson store with time-decayed weighting (T2=30d). Injects lessons from prior runs into all pipeline stages as prompt overlays. Converts past mistakes into reusable safeguards.

nodes.label: Discovery Phase (scoping, literature, debate)
nodes.rationale: Multi-source literature search, gap analysis, problem decomposition, multi-agent hypothesis debate (Innovator/Pragmatist/Contrarian roles), epistemic triangulation, knowledge synthesis.

nodes.label: Domain Detection Cascade
nodes.rationale: Three-level cascade (forced override, keyword matching against 350+ rules, LLM classification to 24 domain IDs) with generic fallback; enables cross-stage consistency without per-domain engineering.

nodes.label: Domain-Specialized Agents
nodes.rationale: Sandboxed domain-specialized agents (HEP agent with FeynRules/MadGraph/MadAnalysis skills; biology agent with COBRApy/BiGG/flux-balance skills; statistics agent with Monte Carlo/semiparametric inference skills) enabling cross-domain coverage without per-domain engineering.

nodes.label: Experimentation Phase (execution, analysis, decisions)
nodes.rationale: Cascading code generation (complexity-based dispatch), sandboxed Docker execution (3-phase network policy), Pivot/Refine decision loop, result-stage debate (Optimist/Skeptic/Methodologist), statistical testing.

nodes.label: Human-in-the-Loop Collaboration (7 modes)
nodes.rationale: Seven intervention modes from full autonomy to step-by-step oversight. SmartPause mechanism routes decisions to researcher when system uncertainty is high. Targeted intervention at high-leverage points outperforms both full autonomy and exhaustive oversight.

nodes.label: Human-in-the-Loop Intervention Modes
nodes.rationale: Seven intervention modes (Full-Auto, Gate-Only, Thorough, CoPilot, Step-by-Step, Pre-Experiment, Post-Experiment) allowing researchers to select operating point along automation spectrum; CoPilot targets six high-leverage decision points.

nodes.label: Multi-Agent Debate Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Three-agent debate (Innovator/Pragmatist/Contrarian for ML; domain-specialized roles for other fields) at hypothesis generation and result analysis stages to improve quality through cross-examination and critical scrutiny.

nodes.label: Three-Layer Prompt Architecture
nodes.rationale: Primary layer (23 stage-specific prompts), reusable block layer (shared text fragments), and sub-prompt layer (intra-stage operations); total ~46K tokens with domain-aware selection and parity test suite.

nodes.label: Sandbox Security Model
nodes.rationale: Docker containers with three-phase network model (dependency installation, data acquisition, experiment execution with network disabled); AST security checks, module blacklist, import validation.

nodes.label: Self-Healing Execution with Pivot/Refine
nodes.rationale: Treats failure as diagnostic information. Complexity-based code dispatch (threshold τ=0.6), static validation gates, automated repair loop with three decisions: Proceed (evidence supports), Refine (weak results, sound direction), Pivot (fundamentally flawed, return to hypothesis generation).

nodes.label: Self-Healing Executor
nodes.rationale: Iterative repair loop (Pivot/Refine) that diagnoses runtime failures and applies targeted fixes, enabling recovery from execution errors rather than discarding failed runs.

nodes.label: Verifiable Result Reporting & Citation Verification
nodes.rationale: Ties all reported numbers to registry of executed outputs. Four-layer citation verification pipeline prevents fabricated numbers and hallucinated citations. Read-only evaluation harness prevents generated code from redefining measurement infrastructure.

nodes.label: Verified Result Registry
nodes.rationale: Whitelist of all values produced by experiment runs, storing per-condition means, standard deviations, and individual seed measurements; used to verify numeric claims and prevent fabrication.

nodes.label: Writing Phase (drafting, review, verification)
nodes.rationale: Outline generation, draft production, peer review, revision, four-layer citation verification, quality gates, final paper export.

nodes.label: Blocked Tool Set Selection
nodes.rationale: Path-based blocking objective: selects which tools to block such that at least one feasible solution path remains, preserving task solvability while requiring recovery through alternative paths.

nodes.label: Finite Candidate Enumeration
nodes.rationale: Blocked tool candidate selection performed over finite enumerated pool rather than all subsets, with enumeration up to size K_blk and bounded by maximum candidate number limit.

nodes.label: Feasibility Constraints
nodes.rationale: Main block setting uses target remaining-path count n*=1, tolerance δ=1, minimum remaining-path count n_min=1, requiring n_i(C) ∈ {1,2} to ensure at least one feasible path survives blocking.

nodes.label: Seeded Tie-Breaking
nodes.rationale: Task-specific seed σ_i = σ_0 + hash(i) ensures reproducible blocked tool set selection across multiple candidates with same deviation from target remaining-path count.

nodes.label: Dual Profiling of Tasks and Systems
nodes.norm_label: dual profiling of tasks and systems
nodes.rationale: Reconciles contradictory evaluation outcomes by explaining benchmark discrepancies through demand profile differences

nodes.label: System Process Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Applies to new AI systems: run on ADeLe battery, plot characteristic curves, summarize ability profile with radial plot

nodes.label: Task Process Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Extends methodology: use DeLeAn rubrics to obtain demand profiles for new tasks/benchmarks, enabling continuous updates while maintaining measurement space consistency

nodes.label: Grokking Phenomenon
nodes.rationale: Mitigation strategy where mixing AI-generated data with small amount of clean data introduces plateau followed by continued error decrease

nodes.label: Yukawa Force Law Discovery
nodes.rationale: Inverse 1.5 power force law with period-distance relationships distinct from inverse-square gravity; creates stable orbits

nodes.label: Capability Gap: Write Code Matching Verbal Reasoning
nodes.norm_label: capability gap: write code matching verbal reasoning
nodes.rationale: Opus 4.7-specific; agents describe correct physics in prose but submit code that does not match description

nodes.label: Frontier Agent Failure Mode Analysis
nodes.rationale: Systematic analysis of 50 failed runs across claude-opus-4-7 and gpt-5.5 identifying seven primary capability gaps

nodes.label: Synthetic Evaluation Setting with Hidden Risk Structure
nodes.norm_label: synthetic evaluation setting with hidden risk structure
nodes.rationale: Isolates failure mode where embeddings are independent of target risk; demonstrates gap between Cer-Eval's fixed-partition theory and adaptive algorithm in practice.

nodes.label: Backend Database with Concrete Values
nodes.rationale: Instantiated retail records with non-trivial values that cannot be inferred from common sense; tool responses match input arguments to records and return output datatype values.

nodes.label: Query Generation Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Three-step process: (1) specify task as (initial_datatypes, target_datatypes), (2) compute ground-truth tool-call sequences via state graph reachability, (3) instantiate and verbalize as natural-language query with ground-truth answer.

nodes.label: Typed Tool Library Construction
nodes.rationale: Systematic generation of 1,665 tools from 56 datatypes via LLM-proposed tool functionalities filtered for redundancy and realism; includes noisy tools simulating real-world ecosystem distractors.

nodes.label: Embodied and Robotics Agents
nodes.rationale: Agents controlling physical robots and embodied systems for real-world task execution

nodes.label: Multimodal Agents
nodes.rationale: Agents capable of processing and reasoning over multiple modalities including text, images, and video

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Failure Structure: Dimension-Preserving Errors
nodes.rationale: On 533 failed tasks (251 generated + 282 public): 89.2% preserve output dimensions, 72.9% preserve palette, median cell error 4–8.3% among shape-correct failures. Suggests partial rule recovery; ordering failures affect output construction, nesting failures typically localized relational errors.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ Within-Task Consistency: 52/160 Partial Success
nodes.rationale: ConceptARC: 18.5-point gap between test-pair accuracy (77.92%) and strict-task accuracy (59.38%). Under pass@2: 0 pairs for 13 tasks, 1 pair for 15, 2 pairs for 37, all 3 for 95. Thus 52/160 tasks have 1–2 correct inputs but fail strict metric. Evidence that inferred transformation not consistently applied across task inputs.

nodes.label: Theme: Consistency vs. Correctness: Partial Success Problem
nodes.norm_label: theme: consistency vs. correctness: partial success problem
nodes.rationale: 18.5-point gap between test-pair accuracy (77.92%) and strict-task accuracy (59.38%) on ConceptARC. 52/160 tasks have 1–2 correct test inputs but fail strict metric. Indicates inferred transformation not consistently applied across task inputs. Distinguishes isolated correct outputs from consistent rule application—critical for understanding whether model truly learned the rule.

nodes.label: Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate Correction
nodes.rationale: Multiple comparison correction method to control false discovery rate in statistical testing

nodes.label: Differential Gene Expression (DGE) Analysis
nodes.rationale: Statistical comparison of gene expression levels between lab-adapted strains and field isolates within shared life cycle stages

nodes.label: Wilcoxon Rank-Sum Test
nodes.rationale: Non-parametric statistical test robust to characteristics of single-cell data for DGE analysis

nodes.label: Regret Decomposition: Coverage Gap, Surrogate Error, Sampling Suboptimality
nodes.norm_label: regret decomposition: coverage gap, surrogate error, sampling suboptimality
nodes.rationale: Theoretical analysis delineating roles of generative coverage gap, surrogate fitting error, and sampling strategy suboptimality in overall regret

nodes.label: Agent Aging Taxonomy
nodes.rationale: Four mechanisms: compression aging (write-before-query barrier), interference aging (similar entries crowd out target fact), revision aging (changed state not updated correctly), maintenance aging (lifecycle events trigger regressions).

nodes.label: Counterfactual Diagnostic Probes
nodes.rationale: Three probes (P1: baseline, P2: oracle retrieval, P3: oracle context) forming ablation ladder; differences yield utilization error, write error, and read error diagnostic profiles.

nodes.label: Finding I: Aging is Multi-Dimensional
nodes.rationale: No single model dominates across mechanisms; rank reversals recur throughout Table 3; deployment-time model selection depends on which failure mechanism is most relevant.

nodes.label: Finding II: Behavioral and Factual Accuracy Decouple
nodes.norm_label: finding ii: behavioral and factual accuracy decouple
nodes.rationale: On S2, constraint violations remain near zero while precision drops; aging is difficult to detect with behavioral metrics alone; requires mechanism-level probes testing fact recall.

nodes.label: Finding III: Revision Aging is Representational
nodes.norm_label: finding iii: revision aging is representational
nodes.rationale: Accumulator error shows no consistent improvement with larger models or better compression; failure stems from representation and update, not capacity; requires explicit state maintenance.

nodes.label: Finding IV: Write–Read Gap Persists
nodes.rationale: Across Tier 2, workspace fidelity exceeds downstream recall; agents retrieve too little information before answer generation; failure is utilization-stage, not write-stage.

nodes.label: Finding V: Within-Family Aging Asymmetries
nodes.rationale: Opus-4.7 has lowest pytest and ws_fid but competitive retrieval metrics; per-mechanism decomposition reveals write-time fidelity regression; same surface failure requires different repairs.

nodes.label: Memory Pipeline Decomposition
nodes.rationale: Cyclic dataflow decomposed into Write (W), Read (R), Utilization (U), and Store (S) components; compression aging at W, interference at R, revision at U, maintenance at S.

nodes.label: Programmatic Task Generation
nodes.rationale: Seeded generators producing task streams at arbitrary scale with controlled pressure dials (dependency density, update rate, chain depth, interference count) enabling reproducible, mechanism-faithful evaluation.

nodes.label: Threshold-Triggered Runtime Controller
nodes.rationale: Monitors per-session signals and fires corrective actions (typed-state overlay, compaction-prompt swap) when thresholds crossed; aggressive forward-only variant captures 91% of always-on ceiling at 86% wall time.

nodes.label: S8: SWE-Bench-Aging Scenario
nodes.rationale: Long-running developer agent on real OSS repository; eight curated GitHub issues from SWE-bench-Verified touching single Django ORM module; exercises all four mechanisms within longitudinal codebase.

nodes.label: Session Loop Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Formalized evaluation over N sessions where agent reads compressed memory, answers tasks and probes, receives score, and history is compressed for next session; lifecycle events injected at designated sessions.

nodes.label: Seven Evaluation Scenarios
nodes.rationale: S1 (Research Literature), S2 (Lifestyle Assistant), S3 (Knowledge Base), S4 (Software Engineering), S5 (Self-Management), S6 (Naturalistic), S7 (Self-Planning) covering different deployment archetypes and mechanism combinations.

nodes.label: Temporal Dependency DAG
nodes.rationale: DAG structure encoding cross-session dependencies: version chains (fact supersession), dependency edges (probes requiring multi-session synthesis), interference pairs (confusable entities), accumulators (derived state).

nodes.label: Tier-1 and Tier-2 Evaluation Tiers
nodes.rationale: Tier 1: runner-controlled ReAct agents with fixed memory policy enabling per-stage probes; Tier 2: autonomous CLI agents (OpenHands, Claude Code) with self-managed workspace memory.

nodes.label: Typed-State Overlay Intervention
nodes.rationale: JSON sidecar maintaining numeric state alongside text memory; reduces accumulator error by 25% (lossy) to 47% (careful) at ~10% wall-time overhead; addresses revision-aging representational gap.

nodes.label: Chain-of-Thought Analysis Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Three-stage error classification system (Stage 2: distillation, Stage 3: classification) for analyzing model reasoning chains

nodes.label: Error Categories (Mathematical, Logical, Executional, Factual)
nodes.rationale: Taxonomy for classifying reasoning failures; shows inherent ambiguity in error categorization across different LLM judges

nodes.label: DeepSeek R1 Distill Qwen 7B
nodes.rationale: Open-weight model showing complete failure (0.0 accuracy) on Hard synthetic dataset

nodes.label: RL Training Metrics (Score, Entropy, Response Length)
nodes.norm_label: rl training metrics (score, entropy, response length)
nodes.rationale: Diagnostic plots showing convergence behavior during reinforcement learning; score plateaus at ~2000 steps with entropy decline

nodes.label: Dimensional Regularization
nodes.rationale: Physics framework used in QFT synthetic problems; convention for reporting divergent coefficients

nodes.label: Loop Integral Divergences
nodes.rationale: Core physics concept in synthetic problem generation; computing pole coefficients and matching subtraction

nodes.label: Coulomb Inverse-Square Law Discovery
nodes.rationale: Central attractive force proportional to p1 and inversely proportional to distance squared; force magnitude F=k*p1/r^2

nodes.label: Capability Gap: Handle Close Approaches and Singularities
nodes.norm_label: capability gap: handle close approaches and singularities
nodes.rationale: Disproportionately affects GPT-5.5; ODE integrator fails on head-on passages through r=0 without proper softening

nodes.label: Oscillating Logarithmic Potential Discovery
nodes.rationale: Central logarithmic field with temporal modulation cos(πt/2); alternating attraction and repulsion with period four

nodes.label: Capability Gap: Know When to Stop Experimenting
nodes.norm_label: capability gap: know when to stop experimenting
nodes.rationale: Opus 4.7-specific; agents submit early with incomplete models or parameters far from ground truth

nodes.label: Deliberate Slowdown, Regulation & Governance Bottleneck
nodes.rationale: Regulatory capping, safety concerns, and societal backlash may deliberately slow AI capability development

nodes.label: Governance as Both Bottleneck and Steering Mechanism
nodes.norm_label: governance as both bottleneck and steering mechanism
nodes.rationale: Regulation can slow AI progress but also steer development toward beneficial outcomes; international coordination remains elusive

nodes.label: Bi-directional Anticipation Importance
nodes.rationale: Output-conditioned (backward) retrieval frequency strongly correlated with accuracy (r=0.800); low-performing models rely heavily on input-conditioned (forward) retrieval, missing backward reasoning.

nodes.label: Bi-directional Tool Retrieval
nodes.rationale: Three retrieval modes: (1) input-conditioned (forward anticipation from available evidence), (2) output-conditioned (backward anticipation from desired outcome), (3) input-output-conditioned (constrained search).

nodes.label: Evaluation Metrics Suite
nodes.rationale: Seven metrics: accuracy, EGT precision (task-relevant execution), average turns, mean explored datatypes, search-to-call ratio, invalid tool call rate, untrusted input rejection rate.

nodes.label: Exploration-Exploitation Trade-off
nodes.rationale: Mean explored datatypes (EDT) strongly correlated with accuracy (r=0.902), but high search-to-call ratio does not guarantee success; Gemini-3.5-Flash searches 10x more than Gemini-3.1-Pro with lower EDT.

nodes.label: Retrieval-Time Blocking Module
nodes.rationale: Optional perturbation replacing path-critical tools with three failure types: explicit errors, implicit failures (silent wrong values), semantic misleading tools; preserves solvability via alternative paths.

nodes.label: Silent Failure Vulnerability
nodes.rationale: Implicit failures (silent wrong values) most harmful: 42.2% value reuse vs 0% for explicit errors; agents treat invalid values as grounded evidence, propagating failures downstream.

nodes.label: Arbitrary-Order Generation
nodes.rationale: Key advantage of dLLMs over autoregressive models; enables non-left-to-right generation and suffix conditioning for privileged information.

nodes.label: Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs)
nodes.rationale: Alternative to autoregressive LLMs that model language generation as iterative denoising process, enabling arbitrary-order generation and speed-up inference.

nodes.label: Forward Process in dLLMs
nodes.rationale: Gradually corrupts clean input by replacing tokens with mask token; inverse of reverse process used during inference.

nodes.label: Kullback-Leibler (KL) Divergence
nodes.rationale: Primary divergence measure for OPSD; reverse KL (model-seeking) outperforms forward KL (model-covering) in d-OPSD experiments.

nodes.label: Pass@k Sampling Strategy
nodes.rationale: Sampling strategy keeping trajectories until correct answer occurs or iteration threshold met; shares computation overhead with RLVR group k rollouts.

nodes.label: Policy Collapse Failure Mode
nodes.rationale: Observed failure mode where OPSD training degrades catastrophically after peak performance; hypothesized to stem from model-seeking behavior becoming overly narrow.

nodes.label: Reverse Process (Inference) in dLLMs
nodes.rationale: T-step iterative denoising from fully masked sequence to clean response; core inference mechanism of dLLMs.

nodes.label: Discovery Fine-Tuning with Reasoning Augmentation
nodes.rationale: Post-training amortization scheme that distills high-budget test-time search policy into model weights via supervised fine-tuning with surrogate-grounded rationales

nodes.label: d-OPSD: Diffusion On-Policy Self-distillation
nodes.rationale: Novel OPSD framework specifically designed for dLLMs using self-generated answers as suffix conditioning and step-level divergence supervision instead of token-level.

nodes.label: Overlap Top-K Metric
nodes.rationale: Measures proportion of tokens appearing in both student's and teacher's Top-K vocabulary distributions; used to explain why d-OPSD outperforms AR-style OPSD by providing more new knowledge.

nodes.label: Countdown (3 numbers) Task
nodes.rationale: Planning task requiring arithmetic operations to reach target; used to evaluate d-OPSD on planning problems.

nodes.label: 4x4 Sudoku Puzzle Task
nodes.rationale: Planning task requiring constraint satisfaction; used to evaluate d-OPSD on non-mathematical reasoning.

nodes.label: Per-Token Pointwise KL Clipping
nodes.rationale: Stabilization technique addressing skewed token-level divergence across vocabulary; ablation shows substantial performance improvement and training stability.

nodes.label: Step-Level Divergence Supervision
nodes.rationale: Shifts dense supervision from token-level to step-level, aligning with iterative denoising nature of dLLMs where only top-k most confident tokens among masked positions dictate state transitions.

nodes.label: Self-Teacher Construction via Suffix Conditioning
nodes.rationale: Core innovation: uses self-generated answers as suffix privileged information rather than prefix conditioning, enabling student to learn from 'self future-experience' and better aligning with on-policy nature and dLLM's bidirectional capability.

nodes.label: Algorithm 1: Computing Inclusion-Minimal Tool Sets
nodes.rationale: Backward search from target datatype set to enumerate inclusion-minimal tool sets; maintains antichain under set inclusion to avoid redundant solutions

nodes.label: Process-Level Ground Truth
nodes.rationale: Union of all legal execution orders for inclusion-minimal tool sets; serves as reference for process-level evaluation and forms path catalog

nodes.label: State Graph
nodes.rationale: Directed graph G_i = (V_i, E_i) where nodes are agent states (sets of obtained datatypes) and edges are valid tool invocations; used for reachability checks and path enumeration

nodes.label: Tool Schema Construction
nodes.rationale: Each tool has input and output datatype sets; multi-input tools (m ∈ 1-5) match real-world scenarios; tool names use alias-based naming to prevent agents from recovering tool graph via canonical names

nodes.label: Bi-directional Exploration
nodes.rationale: Effective exploration proceeds forward from available evidence and backward from desired target outcome, combining forward planning from task goals with backward planning from tool affordances

nodes.label: Implicit Sub-goals
nodes.rationale: Complex tasks rarely specify all intermediate steps explicitly; agents must infer missing information and determine which tools bridge current state to final objective

nodes.label: Long-Horizon Tasks
nodes.rationale: Tasks requiring multiple dependent steps (≥25 turns or ≥5 tool invocations); agents must maintain state, plan across interactions, and avoid compounding errors

nodes.label: Scalable Generation
nodes.rationale: Realistic evaluation requires broad coverage over tasks, tools, and environments; scalable construction pipeline enables systematic stress-testing under many configurations

nodes.label: Tool Retrieval
nodes.rationale: Agents must retrieve or discover relevant tools from large tool ecosystems (hundreds or thousands of APIs) during problem solving, rather than having full tool set visible

nodes.label: Unreliable Tools
nodes.rationale: Retrieved tools in real systems may be unavailable, stale, misleading, broken, or only partially relevant; robust agents must evaluate feedback and recover from failures

nodes.label: Accuracy Metric
nodes.rationale: Measures whether agent produces correct final answer after following runtime protocol; answer must match gold answer and target datatype must be reached

nodes.label: Average Turns Metric
nodes.rationale: Reports average number of interaction turns; each model response counts as one turn including retrieval requests, tool calls, final answers, and invalid actions

nodes.label: Execution-Ground-Truth Precision
nodes.rationale: Measures fraction of successfully executed datatypes that appear in process-level ground-truth datatype set; only counts trusted successful tool outputs

nodes.label: Invalid Tool-Call Ratio
nodes.rationale: Measures fraction of attempted tool calls that violate runtime protocol for structural reasons (parsing failure, unretrieved tool, mismatched arguments, missing inputs)

nodes.label: Mean Explored Datatype Count
nodes.rationale: Measures how broadly agent explores datatype space; explored datatype closure initialized from input datatypes and expanded by successful executions and retrieved tool implications

nodes.label: Search-to-Call Ratio
nodes.rationale: Compares frequency of tool retrieval against tool execution; larger value indicates more retrieval activity relative to execution

nodes.label: Untrusted Input Rejection Rate
nodes.rationale: Measures fraction of attempted tool calls rejected because one or more arguments come from noisy-tool outputs (untrusted inputs)

nodes.label: Action-Like Tool
nodes.rationale: Represents operation and returns values produced by operation (operation ID, confirmation token, created-record identifier); only available after invocation

nodes.label: Direct Search Tool
nodes.rationale: Uses valid input identifiers to look up requested fields in hidden backend database; values inaccessible before execution

nodes.label: Data Paradigm Shift
nodes.rationale: Evolution from static prompt-response pairs to reasoning traces to state-action-observation trajectories

nodes.label: State-Action-Observation Trajectory
nodes.rationale: Complete execution traces including tool outputs, UI states, workspace changes, and final-state evidence

nodes.label: Rank vs. Initialization Tradeoff
nodes.rationale: Rank determines number of available directions; initialization determines whether those directions are usable; in tiny-adapter regime, choosing direction geometrically can be strictly more parameter-efficient than adding rank.

nodes.label: Usable Capacity vs. Trainable Parameters
nodes.rationale: OLoRA-tail improves adapter's usable capacity without increasing trainable weights, optimizer state, checkpoint size, or serving-time footprint; enables scale-down for personal model populations.

nodes.label: Environment Parameterization for Data Generation
nodes.rationale: Concrete environment parameterized as: D (state carrier: database, repository, simulator), F (tool/action set), P_rule (policies, permissions, constraints), Ω (observation exposure), v (success interface). Serialized specification E describes some/all components; ranges from static interface specs to complete interaction substrate.

nodes.label: POMDP Formulation of Agentic Multi-turn Interaction
nodes.norm_label: pomdp formulation of agentic multi-turn interaction
nodes.rationale: Models tool-augmented interaction as partially observable Markov decision process: U (task/user-intent space), S (latent state), A (action space with language and environment-facing actions), O (observation), P (state transitions), R (reward/evaluation). Policy acts on observable history; environment maintains latent state.

nodes.label: 11 Languages Evaluated
nodes.rationale: Evaluation across: English, German, French, Spanish, Russian, Japanese, Chinese, Arabic, Korean, Portuguese, Italian

nodes.label: Mathematical Writing Limitations
nodes.rationale: Denario outputs lacked formal proofs, logical coherence, and genuine mathematical argumentation despite superficial structural similarity to real papers

nodes.label: Pure Mathematics Case Study: Simplicial Complexes
nodes.norm_label: pure mathematics case study: simplicial complexes
nodes.rationale: Evaluation of Denario on open-ended research problem concerning representability of simplicial complexes as nerves of unit balls

nodes.label: Materials Project Trajectory Dataset (142,899 samples)
nodes.rationale: Curated from MPtrj relaxed structures; 12 tasks: 3 descriptive (formula, space group, crystal system) + 9 property prediction (metallicity, bandgap, stability, formation energy, etc.); 9:1 train/test split.

nodes.label: Two-Stage Training (Pretraining + Fine-tuning)
nodes.rationale: Pretraining: graph-text correlation (contrastive loss), graph-driven text prediction (CLM loss), graph-text association (BCE loss). Fine-tuning: supervised cross-entropy on 12 multimodal subtasks; ~48h on 8 A100 nodes.

nodes.label: Retail Business Flow Model
nodes.rationale: Main flow: customer account → draft order → pricing/quote → finalized order. Payment flow: saved method → payment attempt → authorization → completed payment. Fulfillment: order → warehouse request → shipment → delivery attempts. After-sales: return request → review → refund.

nodes.label: Retail Domain Context
nodes.rationale: Benchmark instantiated in retail domain with record types: customer accounts, products/variants, draft orders, finalized orders, payment methods/attempts/authorizations, fulfillment requests/shipments/delivery attempts, returns/reviews/refunds.

nodes.label: Datatype-Grounded Construction
nodes.rationale: Benchmark construction grounded in predefined domain-specific datatypes representing distinct kinds of retail information. Tools generated by pairing different input/output datatype sets, making query distribution diverse at semantic and structural levels.

nodes.label: Tool Schema Structure
nodes.rationale: Agent-visible schema includes function name, description, parameters, strictness constraints. Internal metadata includes input/output datatypes used for retrieval, dependency validation, progress-call annotation, evaluation. Distinction important for error analysis.

nodes.label: Representative Retail Task Example
nodes.rationale: retail_task_0001: from delivery_attempt_id, find account_number through 8-step path spanning fulfillment, order, return, and payment subflows. Demonstrates why benchmark is not single-hop lookup and why failures can occur at multiple points.

nodes.label: Task Complexity Control
nodes.rationale: Complexity controlled by underlying state graph rather than surface-level linguistic difficulty. Only tasks requiring at least five distinct tool calls retained, ensuring non-trivial multi-step reasoning and ~25 turns average in default setting.

nodes.label: Rubric-Assisted Strict Judge
nodes.rationale: Grades each (framework × topic) cell along three dimensions (CD:CE:RA = 25:25:50) with two independent agent reviewers; per-leaf disagreements exceeding |Δ| > 0.20 are re-adjudicated.

nodes.label: 14 Models Across 7 Families
nodes.rationale: Open-source (Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen3-8B/14B, DeepSeek-R1-7B/14B, Gemma-4-31B, gpt-oss-120B) and closed-source (GPT-4o/4o-mini/5-mini, Claude Haiku/Sonnet/Opus) spanning 7B–120B.

nodes.label: Aging Curve Statistics
nodes.rationale: Half-life (sessions until 50% capability loss), decay slope (OLS fit), hazard proxy (per-session failure probability), final score, time-averaged score computed from aging curves.

nodes.label: Aspire Six Vague Goals
nodes.rationale: Scientific and academic reasoning, humanities and social sciences, health and medicine, mathematical reasoning, logic/reliability/instruction following, academic and scientific writing

nodes.label: Forward-Deployed Engineer Role
nodes.rationale: Human role that translates general-purpose models into working systems by operationalizing vague deployment needs into concrete objectives and constraints; motivates study of vague-goal self-evolution

nodes.label: Goal Operationalization
nodes.rationale: Process of converting a broad capability goal into trainable objectives, learning signals, and validation criteria; identified as missing axis in autonomous post-training

nodes.label: Vague Goal
nodes.rationale: Broad capability direction not yet operationalized as fixed task-level objective; requires agent to diagnose gaps, form intermediate objectives, and construct learning signals

nodes.label: Aspire Hidden Evaluation Set
nodes.rationale: 520 expert-authored items across six goals; items, answers, rubrics remain controller-only; protocol returns only aggregate scores

nodes.label: RQ1: Vague Goals vs Explicit Tasks
nodes.norm_label: rq1: vague goals vs explicit tasks
nodes.rationale: Vague-goal prompting associated with more goal-operationalization work and lower aggregate scores than explicit-task references

nodes.label: RQ2: Self-Directed Weight Evolution
nodes.rationale: Only 1/12 final-only model-goal pairs exceed base score; adaptive feedback produces locally rising trajectories that remain below base in most cases

nodes.label: RQ3: Harness Evolution
nodes.rationale: One-step harness evolution produces executable successors but all remain below engineered Qwen-Agent reference

nodes.label: Answer-Format Collapse Failure Mode
nodes.rationale: Numeric-label SFT training associated with all-digit evaluation outputs and near-zero scores; documents concrete answer-format mismatch

nodes.label: Harness Validation Specialization
nodes.rationale: Narrow agent validation can specialize harness to wrong proxy; validation gain on agent data does not guarantee hidden evaluation improvement

nodes.label: Weight Evolution Instability
nodes.rationale: Apparent progress can be recovery from training-induced regression; continued optimization can induce regression rather than produce better descendant

nodes.label: GPT-5.6
nodes.rationale: External decision model used in adaptive-feedback protocol (Luna, Terra, Sol variants)

nodes.label: Qwen3.5-4B
nodes.rationale: Instruction-tuned base model used in RQ2 weight evolution and RQ3 harness evolution experiments

nodes.label: Adaptive-Feedback Evaluation Protocol
nodes.rationale: Bounded queries permit repeated aggregate scores on same goal items; enables feedback-guided checkpoint search without per-item feedback

nodes.label: Final-Only Evaluation Protocol
nodes.rationale: Agent receives no intermediate evaluation scores; single final-checkpoint submission prevents feedback-guided search

nodes.label: Natural Questions (NQ) Dataset
nodes.rationale: Real user QA dataset based on Wikipedia

nodes.label: Memory Module Ablation Study
nodes.rationale: Systematic removal of memory components (prior chats, initial opinion, demographics, private profile) shows minimal impact in Mode 1 but degraded performance in Modes 2-3 when conversation history is simulated.

nodes.label: Breadth Topics (TBreadth)
nodes.rationale: 100 topics from World Values Survey and Pew Global Attitudes Survey, selected for highest response entropy to reflect public disagreement without ground truth.

nodes.label: Depth Topics (TDepth)
nodes.rationale: Seven topics with known scientific consensus or ground truth, selected to elicit diverse opinions and study opinion dynamics with high-entropy topics.

nodes.label: Utterance-level Evaluation Metrics
nodes.rationale: Semantic similarity, stance difference, length metrics, ROUGE-L, and on-topic utterance rate to assess alignment between LLM-generated and human utterances.

nodes.label: GPT-4o-mini-2024-07-18
nodes.rationale: Best-performing LLM in DEBATE evaluation, achieving strongest alignment on semantic similarity, ROUGE-L, and stance difference across all simulation modes.

nodes.label: DEBATE Group Count
nodes.rationale: 797 four-person groups total; Depth subset 26.43 groups per topic average, Breadth subset 6.12 groups per topic average.

nodes.label: Human Data Collection Protocol
nodes.rationale: 2,792 U.S. participants recruited via Prolific, randomly assigned to 797 four-person groups, engaged in multi-round discussions with initial tweets, dyadic conversations, and final opinions.

nodes.label: Jina Embeddings v3 Encoder
nodes.rationale: 1024-dimensional sentence encoder used for semantic similarity computation in evaluation metrics.

nodes.label: LLM Role-play Agent Construction
nodes.rationale: Digital twin agents conditioned on memory modules reflecting human participants' first-person perspective, including demographics, initial opinions, tweets, and conversation history.

nodes.label: DEBATE Message Count
nodes.rationale: 29,417 total messages across dataset; Depth subset 501 participants, Breadth subset 2,291 participants.

nodes.label: On-Topic Utterance Classification
nodes.rationale: GPT-4o-mini classifier identifies utterances directly addressing discussion topic; validated against 200 human-labeled utterances with 90% accuracy; excludes conversational fillers and unrelated remarks.

nodes.label: DEBATE Participant Demographics
nodes.rationale: 2,792 U.S. participants spanning ages 18-83 (M=39.5), 50.2% male, diverse ethnicities, education levels, income brackets, occupations, political identities, and religious affiliations.

nodes.label: Pew Global Attitudes Survey (PGAS) Topics
nodes.rationale: Source for Breadth topics; complements WVS with diverse policy and social value questions.

nodes.label: Round-wise Aggregated Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Each simulated utterance compared to all on-topic human utterances from same round and speaker; metrics averaged across utterances, agents, and rounds.

nodes.label: Semantic Similarity Metric (Ssem)
nodes.rationale: Cosine similarity between sentence embeddings; measures meaning-level alignment between LLM-generated and human utterances.

nodes.label: Supervised Fine-Tuning Limitations
nodes.rationale: SFT improves surface-level alignment (message length, ROUGE-L) but fails to enhance semantic similarity or stance alignment; suggests naive SFT encourages surface-form mimicry without behavioral alignment.

nodes.label: Simulation Mode 1: Next Message Prediction
nodes.rationale: Predicts immediate response in real conversations using human tweets, human prior utterances, and human current round context.

nodes.label: Simulation Mode 2: Tweet-guided Conversation Simulation
nodes.rationale: Simulates private conversations given trace of real public tweets, using human tweets but simulated prior and current utterances.

nodes.label: Simulation Mode 3: Full Conversation Simulation
nodes.rationale: Simulates agents' dynamics from initial conditions using initial human tweet plus simulated subsequent tweets and utterances; classic opinion dynamics setup.

nodes.label: Stance Score Classification
nodes.rationale: Maps utterances to six-point Likert scale stance scores [-2.5 to +2.5]; GPT-4o-mini classifier validated against 200 human-labeled utterances with 90% accuracy.

nodes.label: Stance Difference Metric (Δstance)
nodes.rationale: Absolute difference between stance scores; captures alignment in opinion polarity between LLM and human utterances.

nodes.label: World Values Survey (WVS) Topics
nodes.rationale: Source for Breadth topics; 100 U.S.-administered questions selected for highest response entropy to reflect public disagreement.

nodes.label: DEBATE Benchmark Dataset
nodes.rationale: Large-scale empirical benchmark for evaluating multi-agent role-playing LLM systems, capturing opinion trajectories from 2,792 U.S. participants across multi-round, multi-party interactions with 29,417 messages.

nodes.label: Marr's Levels of Analysis
nodes.rationale: Framework distinguishing physical implementation, algorithmic computation, and computational goals; applied to deep learning study at multiple levels.

nodes.label: Capability Gap: Act on Parameter-Fitting Signals
nodes.norm_label: capability gap: act on parameter-fitting signals
nodes.rationale: Both models; agents ignore plateaued losses or large parameter warping as evidence of misspecification

nodes.label: Channel-Mixing MLPs
nodes.rationale: MLP layers that operate on rows of input table, enabling per-location feature communication with parameter sharing across spatial locations.

nodes.label: Data Scaling Analysis
nodes.rationale: Mixer improves faster with dataset size than ResNets and ViT, with performance gap shrinking as data scale increases from 3% to 100% of JFT-300M.

nodes.label: ImageNet Transfer Performance
nodes.rationale: Mixer-H/14 achieves 87.94% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet when pre-trained on JFT-300M, competitive with ViT-H/14 (88.55%) while 2.5x faster.

nodes.label: Isotropic Architecture Design
nodes.rationale: Fixed-width layers throughout network unlike pyramidal CNNs, similar to Transformers and deep RNNs, enabling consistent computational complexity.

nodes.label: Parameter Tying in Token-Mixing
nodes.rationale: Same MLP kernel shared across all channels in token-mixing, providing positional invariance and memory savings without empirical performance loss.

nodes.label: Permutation Invariance Study
nodes.rationale: Mixer invariant to patch and pixel shuffling within patches; ResNet performance drops 75% with global pixel permutation vs Mixer's 45% drop.

nodes.label: Token-Mixing MLPs
nodes.rationale: MLP layers that operate on columns of input table, enabling cross-location spatial communication with linear complexity in number of patches.

nodes.label: Learned Feature Visualization
nodes.rationale: Token-mixing MLPs learn both global and local feature detectors with opposing-phase pairs, similar to CNN Gabor-like filters but with global receptive fields.

nodes.label: gMLP BERT Finetuning
nodes.rationale: Large gMLP achieves 87.7% MNLI and 82.1% SQuAD v2.0 F1, better than BERT-large; single-head attention addition improves performance further.

nodes.label: gMLP BERT Pretraining
nodes.rationale: gMLP achieves parity with Transformers on MLM pretraining perplexity, learns Toeplitz-like spatial matrices representing shift invariance.

nodes.label: Channel Projection in gMLP
nodes.rationale: Linear projections along channel dimension similar to Transformer FFNs, with shapes 768×3072 and 3072×768 for BERT-base equivalent.

nodes.label: gMLP ImageNet Results
nodes.rationale: gMLP-B achieves 81.6% ImageNet top-1 accuracy, comparable to DeiT-B (81.8%) with 66% fewer parameters than MLP-Mixer-L/16.

nodes.label: Spatial Gating Unit (SGU)
nodes.rationale: Linear spatial projection with multiplicative gating and channel splitting, enabling cross-token communication with near-zero initialization for training stability.

nodes.label: Learned Spatial Weight Patterns
nodes.rationale: Spatial projection matrices learn both locality and spatial invariance, effectively performing convolution with data-driven irregular kernel shapes.

nodes.label: Circle World Force Law Discovery
nodes.rationale: Constant outward radial acceleration; particles experience uniform repulsion from origin

nodes.label: Ether 2D Gravity with Drift Discovery
nodes.rationale: 2D Newtonian gravity with logarithmic potential; force magnitude scales as G*m_i*m_j/r; uniform northward drift acceleration (ether body force)

nodes.label: Extra Dimensions Inverse-Square with Drag Discovery
nodes.norm_label: extra dimensions inverse-square with drag discovery
nodes.rationale: Attractive inverse-square central force with linear viscous drag; strength scales with probe and source scalar properties ratio

nodes.label: Fractional Laplacian Force Law Discovery
nodes.rationale: Inverse-square law with coupling proportional to p1/p2 ratio; standard 2D Laplacian scenario

nodes.label: Hubble Flow with Logarithmic Attraction Discovery
nodes.norm_label: hubble flow with logarithmic attraction discovery
nodes.rationale: Static radial field with logarithmic short-range attraction and harmonic long-range repulsion; anchor sources field, other particles are inert test particles

nodes.label: Composite Verdict Definition
nodes.rationale: Trial passes only if Stage 1, Stage 2, and all Stage 3 scenarios pass on content axis; structural axis joins conjunction where applicable; Stage 4 reported separately as metacognitive axis.

nodes.label: Dual LLM Judges with Human Audit
nodes.norm_label: dual llm judges with human audit
nodes.rationale: Every stage output judged independently by Claude and GPT; disagreement rate >25% triggers human audit; canonical verdict replaces LLM verdicts for disputed cases.

nodes.label: Irreversible Pre-Registration
nodes.rationale: SHA-256-sealed evaluation specification locked before production data generation; prevents post-hoc criterion drift through git-enforced immutability.

nodes.label: Judge Reliability Does Not Transfer Across Frameworks
nodes.norm_label: judge reliability does not transfer across frameworks
nodes.rationale: More reliable judge reverses between frameworks: OpenAI 82% on Aristotelian, Claude 83% on F=mv, Claude 67% on Decay. Single-judge evaluation unsafe; dual-judge plus disagreement-rate plus audit necessary.

nodes.label: Stage 4 Over-Claim Consistently High
nodes.rationale: Over-claim rate 67–83% across all three frameworks on failure-containing trials; no reliable improvement on harder frameworks; contradicts 'models know what they don't know' calibration framing.

nodes.label: Knowledge Editing vs User-as-Engram
nodes.rationale: Knowledge editing changes facts model already holds; User-as-Engram adds new facts model never saw; opposite problem with different solutions (locate-and-rewrite vs addressed writes).

nodes.label: Meta-Scientific Analysis
nodes.rationale: Empirical study of how innovation unfolds through analysis of recombination patterns across domains

nodes.label: Scientific Hypothesis Generation
nodes.rationale: Training models to propose novel research directions by learning from patterns of past recombinations

nodes.label: Concept Blend
nodes.rationale: Fusion of multiple concepts into a new solution or framework

nodes.label: Inspiration Transfer
nodes.rationale: Transfer of knowledge or insight from one entity (source) to another (target) through analogies or abstraction

nodes.label: Idea Recombination
nodes.rationale: Creation of novel ideas by integrating elements from existing concepts; includes blends and inspirations

nodes.label: Inspirations Cross Domains, Blends Within Domains
nodes.norm_label: inspirations cross domains, blends within domains
nodes.rationale: Inspirations span broader range of domains while blends tend to link within same or similar domains

nodes.label: Robotics Draws Inspiration from Zoology
nodes.rationale: Cross-domain inspiration pattern showing robotics frequently inspired by zoological concepts

nodes.label: Information Extraction for Recombinations
nodes.rationale: NLP task of identifying and extracting recombination instances from scientific abstracts

nodes.label: Distractor Discourse Markers
nodes.rationale: 1,000 markers validated as distractors by NLP expert; remainder by LLM. Includes overly general markers (e.g., 'therefore') and markers signaling contrast/similarity relations outside target set.

nodes.label: LoRA Merging
nodes.rationale: Merging technique for Low-Rank Adaptation modules from multiple fine-tuned models

nodes.label: Task Arithmetic
nodes.rationale: Model merging approach using arithmetic operations on task vectors

nodes.label: Weight Averaging
nodes.rationale: Simple model merging technique that averages weights from multiple models

nodes.label: Research and Scientific Agents
nodes.rationale: Agents designed for literature review, hypothesis generation, and scientific discovery

nodes.label: Creative Writing Task
nodes.rationale: Application domain including poem, joke, and story generation where VS shows 1.6-2.1× diversity improvement

nodes.label: Compact 1D Convolutional Neural Network
nodes.rationale: Deep learning model with 3 convolutional blocks (32, 64, 128 filters) for step detection

nodes.label: MobileNet-Inspired 1D CNN
nodes.rationale: Resource-efficient deep learning model using depthwise separable convolutions (12,252 parameters)

nodes.label: Peak Detection Algorithm (Baseline)
nodes.rationale: Traditional signal processing approach using vector magnitude, band-pass filtering, and peak finding

nodes.label: Subject-Independent 5-Fold Cross-Validation
nodes.rationale: Rigorous validation scheme ensuring all data from single participant belongs to one fold to assess generalizability

nodes.label: Extreme Class Imbalance in Step Detection
nodes.norm_label: extreme class imbalance in step detection
nodes.rationale: Critical challenge where non-step time points vastly outnumber actual step events, causing models to learn trivial solutions

nodes.label: F1-Score Performance Metric
nodes.rationale: Harmonic mean of precision and recall for balanced measure of individual step detection accuracy

nodes.label: Focal Loss Function
nodes.rationale: Loss function designed to mitigate extreme class imbalance in step detection (γ=2, α=0.25)

nodes.label: Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE)
nodes.rationale: Relative error measure for total step count accuracy, crucial for understanding practical utility

nodes.label: Sampling Frequency Trade-off (100Hz vs 25Hz)
nodes.rationale: Higher frequencies capture richer signal detail but demand greater computational resources; critical for wrist-worn sensors

nodes.label: Sensor Placement Impact (Hip vs Wrist)
nodes.rationale: Hip-worn sensors produce clearer signals (F1≈0.42, MAPE≈10%) while wrist-worn sensors show degraded performance (MAPE>50%)

nodes.label: Trivial Solution Convergence
nodes.rationale: Deep learning models converged to predicting zero steps for all inputs despite low training loss, demonstrating loss minimization does not guarantee task performance

nodes.label: Accelerometer Data Collection (Hip and Wrist)
nodes.rationale: Data from 39 participants at 100Hz and 25Hz sampling frequencies from two sensor locations

nodes.label: Extreme Class Imbalance in Sparse Event Detection
nodes.norm_label: extreme class imbalance in sparse event detection
nodes.rationale: Critical challenge where deep learning models converged to trivial solution (predicting zero steps) due to imbalanced data distribution

nodes.label: Deep Learning for Step Counting
nodes.rationale: Lightweight CNN and MobileNet-inspired architectures evaluated for step detection from wearable accelerometer data

nodes.label: F1 Score Metric
nodes.rationale: Harmonic mean of precision and recall; deep learning models achieved near-zero F1 scores

nodes.label: Focal Loss for Class Imbalance
nodes.rationale: Loss function designed to mitigate extreme class imbalance but proved inadequate for this step detection task

nodes.label: Traditional Peak-Detection Algorithm
nodes.rationale: Baseline algorithm for step counting achieving ~10-11% MAPE on hip-worn data but degrading on wrist-worn

nodes.label: Step Counting from Wearable Accelerometer Data
nodes.norm_label: step counting from wearable accelerometer data
nodes.rationale: Comprehensive comparative analysis of peak-detection vs deep learning for step counting in free-living conditions

nodes.label: Behavioral Non-Redundancy Measurement
nodes.rationale: Category coverage overestimates diversity when differently worded samples require same behavior. Compare through tool-call/action graphs, state transitions, dependency paths, clarification/recovery patterns, final-state changes. Graph fingerprints and kernel-based effective-number measures summarize non-redundancy; chosen representation and similarity function must be reported.

nodes.label: AgentBench
nodes.rationale: Evaluates agents across eight environments revealing performance gaps in multi-step settings

nodes.label: GAIA
nodes.rationale: Tests general assistants on multi-step reasoning and tool use

nodes.label: Centrality Measures (Betweenness, Closeness, Eigenvector)
nodes.rationale: Network centrality metrics computed for peptide and amino acid nodes to identify influential positions in aggregate structure
nodes.source_location: Section 2.4.1, Properties for CG Peptide Graphs

nodes.label: Generalization and Distribution Shift
nodes.rationale: Difficulty of agents performing well on tasks different from training distribution

nodes.label: Average Clustering Coefficient
nodes.rationale: Measures local density of connections around nodes; indicates transitivity in peptide/amino acid contacts
nodes.source_location: Section 2.4.1, Properties for CG Peptide Graphs

nodes.label: Self-Consistency
nodes.rationale: Improved robustness by sampling multiple reasoning paths and selecting most frequent answer through majority voting

nodes.label: ABL1–Imatinib Binding Mode Prediction
nodes.rationale: Multi-candidate complex prediction with ESMFold2-fast, ranking by pLDDT/pTM/ipTM, binding-mode analysis via ProteinsPlus/PoseEdit/Protoss; three candidates converged on common binding mode with four hydrogen bonds and two π-stacking interactions.

nodes.label: Agent Squad Architecture
nodes.rationale: Squad design mirrors human research team division of labor, with role-based specialization (supervising, generative, reflective, evolutionary, similarity-checking, synthesizing, simulation, experiment roles) rather than topic-based, enabling disagreement manufacturing through competing hypotheses.

nodes.label: AI Materials Factory
nodes.rationale: In-house automated laboratory for physical execution; sits behind same planning layer as calculations, enabling closed-loop synthesis and characterization where measurements return to the hypothesis-generation loop.

nodes.label: KHP Decomposition Pathway Prediction
nodes.rationale: Autonomous exploration of γ-ketohydroperoxide decomposition network; MIRA enumerated 78 candidate reactions in first layer, promoted three species, enumerated 58 more in second layer, yielding 59 species and 64 validated reactions recovering Korcek mechanism.

nodes.label: Memory and Scientific Wiki
nodes.rationale: Compilation layer (not retrieval) that maintains interlinked wiki pages with explicit cross-references and flagged contradictions; ingestion, querying, and linting operations keep knowledge alive; negative results and provenance persist as reusable assets.

nodes.label: MIRA Compute Platform
nodes.rationale: Cloud-native, AI-native execution layer with batch jobs and hosted inference services; designed for agent consumers rather than human operators, requiring idempotent submission, structured failure reporting, and self-delivering results.

nodes.label: CO Adsorption on Pt(111) Modeling
nodes.rationale: Surface science workflow combining MACE machine-learning optimization with ABACUS DFT relaxation; calculated adsorption energy of −1.817 eV, recovering atop site preference and charge redistribution patterns.

nodes.label: ResearchClawBench Evaluation
nodes.rationale: End-to-end research benchmark with 40 paper-grounded tasks across 10 domains; MIRA scored 17.51 on Chemistry/Energy/Materials subset, highest among seven agents at lowest cost ($0.67/task), dominating all alternatives on both score and cost.

nodes.label: SciAgentArena Drug Discovery Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Multi-institutional benchmark across five task categories (data preprocessing, analysis, molecule optimization, safety assessment, claim validation); MIRA achieved 81.1% overall, leading four of five categories and exceeding purpose-built agents by 11.9+ points.

nodes.label: Scientific Skills Layer
nodes.rationale: Curated procedural knowledge packaged as versioned skills encodes domain expertise (convergence criteria, pre-screening steps, parameter selection, validation procedures) that general-purpose models lack, ensuring dependability and comparability across runs.

nodes.label: Bidirectional Entailment Clustering
nodes.rationale: Operationalization of semantic equivalence using NLI tools; two sentences mean the same thing only if they entail each other bidirectionally, enabling clustering of paraphrases while distinguishing genuinely different meanings.

nodes.label: Confabulation (LLM Failure Mode)
nodes.rationale: Subset of hallucinations where LLMs fluently make claims that are both wrong and arbitrary (sensitive to irrelevant details like random seed), distinct from consistent errors from training data or systematic reasoning failures.

nodes.label: Discrete Semantic Entropy Variant
nodes.rationale: Approximation of semantic entropy for black-box LLMs without access to output probabilities; estimates P(Ci|x) from empirical distribution of sampled generations, enabling application to GPT-4 and similar closed models.

nodes.label: FactualBio Dataset
nodes.rationale: Biography-generation dataset of 21 individuals with 150 factual claims (45 incorrect), generated by GPT-4; enables evaluation of semantic entropy on paragraph-length generations with manual ground-truth labels.

nodes.label: Question-Answering Benchmarks
nodes.rationale: Five datasets for sentence-length evaluation: TriviaQA (trivia), SQuAD 1.1 (reading comprehension), BioASQ (life sciences), NQ-Open (Google Search queries), SVAMP (math word problems); context-free evaluation with 400 train/test examples each.

nodes.label: Semantic Entropy Performance Results
nodes.rationale: Averaged across 30 task-model combinations, semantic entropy achieves AUROC 0.790 (vs naive entropy 0.691, P(True) 0.698, embedding regression 0.687); outperforms baselines consistently across LLaMA, Falcon, Mistral families and model sizes.

nodes.label: Baseline-Scaled Error Amplification
nodes.rationale: Architectures without centralized verification propagate errors more as baseline difficulty grows; survives cluster-robust inference (Probust = 0.030), supporting failure-mode taxonomy where verification bottlenecks intercept errors before aggregation.

nodes.label: Capability-Saturation Threshold (~45%)
nodes.rationale: Empirically derived threshold beyond which additional agents unlikely to improve performance; correctly predicts multi-agent coordination effect in 94% of validation configurations on SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench.

nodes.label: Empirical Coordination Metrics
nodes.rationale: Four categories of predictors: base model capability (intelligence index I), system configuration (agent count na), task properties (tool count T, single-agent baseline PSA), and coordination metrics (efficiency Ec, overhead O%, error amplification Ae, message density c, redundancy R).

nodes.label: Error Absorption Mechanisms
nodes.rationale: Centralized and hybrid architectures achieve 22.7% average error reduction through iterative verification; independent MAS shows +4.6% amplification due to absence of verification; optimal redundancy at R ≈ 0.41 (centralized median).

nodes.label: Five Agent Architectures
nodes.rationale: Canonical architectures compared: SAS (single sequential agent), MAS-independent (parallel agents + synthesis), MAS-decentralized (sequential peer debate + voting), MAS-centralized (hierarchical orchestrator), MAS-hybrid (orchestrator + peer exchange).

nodes.label: Predictive Architecture-Selection Model
nodes.rationale: Linear regression with prespecified interactions (20 parameters) relating performance to intelligence, task properties, and empirical coordination metrics; achieves R²CV = 0.373 (0.413 with task-grounded ACI), selects best architecture in 87% of held-out configurations.

nodes.label: Turn Count Power-Law Scaling
nodes.rationale: Total reasoning turns exhibit super-linear growth with agent count (exponent 1.724 > 1), reflecting quadratic message complexity; hybrid requires 6.2× more turns than SAS, centralized 3.8×, decentralized 3.6×.

nodes.label: Anytime-Valid Confidence Intervals
nodes.rationale: Confidence intervals that maintain coverage guarantee under adaptive stopping and repeated monitoring; combines finite-pool e-process bounds with finite-pool-to-population correction via Hoeffding's inequality.

nodes.label: DeepSeek Model Family
nodes.rationale: 67B variant used as target model in cross-family surrogate-target pairs.

nodes.label: E-Process Construction
nodes.rationale: Time-uniform martingale concentration via hedged capital process; provides anytime-valid bounds without requiring fixed sample size in advance.

nodes.label: Hyperparameter Sensitivity Analysis
nodes.rationale: Studies sensitivity to α-split, hedge weight θ, stabilizer c, and sampling floor β; shows smooth performance changes and stability of default choices.

nodes.label: Llama Model Family (2, 3 variants)
nodes.rationale: Used as both surrogate (8B, 7B) and target (70B) models in experiments; enables same-family and cross-generation comparisons.

nodes.label: Mixtral Model Family
nodes.rationale: 8×7B mixture-of-experts variant used as target model in cross-family experiments.

nodes.label: Dyadic Stitching for Anytime Validity
nodes.rationale: Upgrades finite-horizon e-process bounds to anytime-valid bounds via union bound over dyadic horizons; introduces log log t term in width bound.

nodes.label: Variance-Optimal Sampling Proposal
nodes.rationale: Theoretical optimal sampling distribution proportional to absolute residual magnitude; CELEUS approximates this using label-free proxies (predictive dispersion, entropy).

nodes.label: Tensor Decomposition for Cosmological Information Extraction
nodes.norm_label: tensor decomposition for cosmological information extraction
nodes.rationale: Organizing substructure features into tensors and applying QITT decomposition to compress information while maintaining predictive power
