nodes.rationale: Supervised research; steered project direction; provided funding; led final comprehensive editing and review

nodes.label: Dead-End Registry
nodes.rationale: Shared artifact tracking rejected parameter ranges to prevent duplicate exploration

nodes.label: Llama Model Variants
nodes.rationale: Llama-3.1-Tulu-3-8B-SFT, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, and Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct evaluated; represent pre- vs. post-RLHF checkpoints and varying model scales.

nodes.label: LLM Usage Disclosure
nodes.rationale: Transparency statement: AI used for formatting, text shortening, polishing, implementation aid, and related works expansion

nodes.label: Factor Coverage and Balance Measurement
nodes.rationale: Divide each factor level into categories. Coverage: fraction of declared categories with ≥1 sample. Normalized entropy: how evenly samples distributed across categories (1=uniform, decreases as concentration increases). Complementary: coverage high even if concentrated; entropy alone doesn't show absent categories. Supplement with meaningful joint distributions.

nodes.label: Minor Position Bias in FusioN
nodes.rationale: Finding: Fusor outputs show slightly higher contribution from first and second samples in prompt

nodes.label: Forum-Based Coordination
nodes.rationale: Agents post research directions, hypotheses, critiques, and votes; enables self-organization and cross-team awareness

nodes.label: Future Work Extensions
nodes.rationale: Extend rubrics to multimodal systems, robotics, safety/fairness dimensions; improve level 5+ items; increase predictive power with purer benchmarks.

nodes.label: 111B Model Training Hyperparameters
nodes.rationale: Training configuration: batch size 16, peak LR 5e-6, 64 H100 GPUs, 250-323 steps

nodes.label: 7B Model Training Hyperparameters
nodes.rationale: Training configuration: same as 111B but on 16 GPUs with same hyperparameters

nodes.label: Axiomatization Prompt Cue
nodes.rationale: Paragraph asking for smallest rule set with explicit cross-references; lifted composite PASS and reduced structural failures at F=mv and Aristotelian; did not rescue Decay content axis.

nodes.label: Banned-Word List for Aristotelian
nodes.rationale: 11 tokens: inertia, acceleration, force, momentum, energy, mass, density, gravity, vacuum, friction, post-Aristotelian physicist names; prevents Newtonian category import.

nodes.label: Banned-Word List for Decay World
nodes.rationale: 20+ tokens across three layers: energy-thermodynamics (energy, kinetic, potential, conservation, entropy, Hamiltonian, Lagrangian), decay-mechanism (friction, drag, damping, dissipation, viscous, air resistance, attenuation), mechanics (force, mass, acceleration, momentum, inertia), physicist names.

nodes.label: Banned-Word List for F=mv
nodes.rationale: 8 tokens: velocity, acceleration, momentum, mass, inertia, gravity, friction, energy, F=ma, physicist names; prevents importing answer through memorized vocabulary.

nodes.label: Content Axis Criteria N1–N6 for Decay World
nodes.norm_label: content axis criteria n1–n6 for decay world
nodes.rationale: Six necessary conditions: closed-system loss (N1), multiplicative decline (N2), time-fixed rate (N3), universality across domains (N4), independence from material (N5), numerical rate ~0.99/s (N6).

nodes.label: Content Axis Criteria N1–N6 for F=mv
nodes.norm_label: content axis criteria n1–n6 for f=mv
nodes.rationale: Six necessary conditions on induced rules: present-push principle (N1), proportionalities (N2–N3), no-build-up signature (N4), unified-fall picture (N5), push combination (N6); failing any one is Stage 1 FAIL.

nodes.label: Content Axis Criteria N1–N8 for Aristotelian
nodes.norm_label: content axis criteria n1–n8 for aristotelian
nodes.rationale: Eight necessary conditions: two-regime distinction (N1), heavier-falls-faster (N2), medium-resistance (N3), shape dependence (N4), directional preference (N5), heaven/earth split (N6), projectile tension (N7), floating account (N8).

nodes.label: Structural Axis Criteria N9–N12
nodes.rationale: Four conditions on rule-set organization: parsimony (rule count), independence (no paraphrase), traceability (maps to observations), hierarchy (cross-references for 5+ rules).

nodes.label: Bottleneck Migration Across Difficulty Gradient
nodes.rationale: Empirical signature of difficulty gradient: failures concentrate in different cognitive moves across frameworks. F=mv shows per-model heterogeneity; Aristotelian shows shared Stage 1 training-prior bottleneck; Decay shows Stage 3 quantitative-computation bottleneck.

nodes.label: Induction Is Framework-Specific, Not Stable Model Property
nodes.norm_label: induction is framework-specific, not stable model property
nodes.rationale: Stage 1 pass rates swing widely across frameworks; bottleneck differs: F=mv (reimporting F=ma), Aristotelian (training-prior suppression), Decay (universality across domains).

nodes.label: Reproducible LLM-Judge Fabrication Failure
nodes.rationale: OpenAI judge on Decay World slides from literal substring matching to semantic association in banned-token test; fabricates citations (16 of 18 disagreement verdicts defective); triggered by long ban list and high topical overlap.

nodes.label: Qualitative Direction vs Quantitative Ratio Asymmetry
nodes.norm_label: qualitative direction vs quantitative ratio asymmetry
nodes.rationale: Across 105 quantitative predictions (45 at F=mv, 60 at Decay): 0 direction-wrong predictions but 23 of 60 ratio-leaked at Decay. Models know sign of change but cannot compute ratio under cross-domain pressure.

nodes.label: Rule-Set Organization Is Prompt-Responsive
nodes.rationale: Structural axis major differentiator at F=mv; axiomatization cue doubled structural pass rate at F=mv and saturated at Aristotelian; capability present but not exhibited by default.

nodes.label: Aristotelian Mechanics (Medium)
nodes.rationale: Historically real framework with multi-principle structure; tests ability to suspend training-data prior that labels Aristotelian as wrong.

nodes.label: Decay World (Hard)
nodes.rationale: Multi-domain counterfactual with no underlying substrate; 1% per-second decay across mechanical, thermal, rotational, orbital domains tests cross-domain unification and quantitative computation.

nodes.label: F=mv Counterfactual World (Easy)
nodes.rationale: Single-equation counterfactual replacing F=ma with F=mv; shallowest difficulty level testing induction and rule organization.

nodes.label: Four Types of Newton Leak in Aristotelian
nodes.norm_label: four types of newton leak in aristotelian
nodes.rationale: Banned-vocabulary derivatives, training-data concept import, standard-physics knowledge exposure, missing framework concept; lexical banned-token check alone insufficient; audit catches unmistakably Newtonian content.

nodes.label: Ratio Leak Mechanism in Decay World
nodes.norm_label: ratio leak mechanism in decay world
nodes.rationale: Model correctly names per-second exponential decay but computes per-scenario number using standard-physics relation; treats unstated energy as underlying decaying quantity; back-derives measured quantity from it; gives inconsistent rate across domains.

nodes.label: Impact Statement
nodes.rationale: AUTOSCIENTISTS may accelerate ML/AI for Science; risks include over-trusting models, overfitting to benchmarks, amplifying erroneous hypotheses

nodes.label: Composite PASS Rate Insufficient for Cognitive Evaluation
nodes.norm_label: composite pass rate insufficient for cognitive evaluation
nodes.rationale: Identical composite PASS (6/15) at F=mv and Aristotelian masks completely different cognitive pictures; per-stage decomposition necessary to isolate which move failed.

nodes.label: Framework Choice Is Most Important Benchmark-Design Decision
nodes.norm_label: framework choice is most important benchmark-design decision
nodes.rationale: Counterfactual frameworks separate reasoning from recitation; multi-domain counterfactual with no substrate probes capabilities single-equation and historical frameworks do not; bottleneck migration more informative than pass-rate ordering.

nodes.label: Judging Infrastructure Is Part of Experimental Design
nodes.norm_label: judging infrastructure is part of experimental design
nodes.rationale: Pre-registration floor not ceiling; audit pathway triggered by disagreement threshold necessary at scale; single-judge design would produce systematically wrong verdicts on at least one framework.

nodes.label: Three Frameworks Do Not Span Difficulty Gradient
nodes.norm_label: three frameworks do not span difficulty gradient
nodes.rationale: One Easy, one Medium, one Hard; no multiple frameworks at single difficulty level; bottleneck-migration claim consistent with three data points but not directly tested.

nodes.label: Three Frontier Models Not Exhaustive
nodes.rationale: Claims apply to Claude Opus 4.7, GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro at pinned versions; reasoning-trained or physics-fine-tuned models could differ; no open-weight models tested.

nodes.label: N=5 Trials Per Model Per Framework
nodes.norm_label: n=5 trials per model per framework
nodes.rationale: Descriptive, not statistical inference; per-model composite counts too thin for confidence-level claims; findings about patterns in 45 trials, not population inference.

nodes.label: Agent Benchmarking and Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Frameworks and datasets for systematically evaluating agent capabilities, safety, and real-world performance

nodes.label: Agent Era
nodes.rationale: First major attempt to turn LLMs from passive conversational systems into active problem solvers through environment-action-feedback loops

nodes.label: Agent Memory
nodes.rationale: Maintaining context and accumulating experience; evolved from retrieval-based to persistent experience accumulation

nodes.label: Agent Perception
nodes.rationale: Observing and interpreting environment; evolved from text parsing to multimodal vision-language models

nodes.label: Agent Planning
nodes.rationale: Decomposing goals and reasoning about action sequences; progressed through CoT, ToT, GoT, and RL-based methods

nodes.label: Chain-of-Thought Prompting
nodes.rationale: Foundational technique showing intermediate reasoning steps improve multi-step performance

nodes.label: Persistent Memory
nodes.rationale: Long-running agents need persistent memory across sessions; forms include token-level, parametric, latent, and external

nodes.label: ReAct Loop (Thought-Action-Observation)
nodes.rationale: Canonical form of agent loop interleaving reasoning and acting, distinguishing agents from chatbots

nodes.label: Thinking LLM Era
nodes.rationale: Shift from single-path reasoning to deep, branching, self-correcting reasoning through RL-driven internalization

nodes.label: Tree-of-Thought
nodes.rationale: Extended CoT by allowing multiple reasoning branches and backtracking, casting planning as search problem

nodes.label: Qwen3
nodes.rationale: Unified system with seamless thinking/non-thinking mode switching for dynamic reasoning effort allocation

nodes.label: MATS Fellowship
nodes.rationale: DT conducted this work as part of MATS Fellowship.

nodes.label: Aya Expanse 8B Language Model
nodes.rationale: Smaller candidate model used in test-time scaling experiments to compare with larger models

nodes.label: Nemotron-3 Dataset
nodes.rationale: 1T- and 3T-token subsets used for optimizer experiments. Enables evaluation of convergence and stability across different training horizons.

nodes.label: Double Scaling Law
nodes.rationale: New scaling law showing test error as sum of two power-law terms dependent on both current training data and generator training data

nodes.label: Greatest Common Divisor (GCD) Task
nodes.rationale: Arithmetic task used to validate model collapse theory with transformer models, demonstrating loss of skills phenomenon

nodes.label: Neural Scaling Laws
nodes.rationale: Empirically observed power-law relationships where test error falls off as power of training data size, model size, and compute

nodes.label: Synthetic Data Contamination
nodes.rationale: AI-generated data increasingly populating web and training corpora, often indistinguishable from real data, causing distribution shift

nodes.label: Tail Narrowing Phenomenon
nodes.rationale: Mechanism where synthetic data generation narrows tail exponent of heavy-tailed distribution through temperature scaling and truncation

nodes.label: Triplet Scaling Law for Memory-Limited Models
nodes.norm_label: triplet scaling law for memory-limited models
nodes.rationale: Scaling law for associative memory models showing dependence on embedding dimension and algorithm-specific exponent

nodes.label: Open Philanthropy Grant
nodes.rationale: JB and OE supported by grant from Open Philanthropy.

nodes.label: Large Discovery Models: A Framework for LLM-Guided Scientific Optimization
nodes.norm_label: large discovery models: a framework for llm-guided scientific optimization
nodes.rationale: Core research paper presenting the LDM framework that combines LLMs with Bayesian optimization for scientific discovery

nodes.label: Deployment Prerequisites (adversarial robustness, schema evolution)
nodes.rationale: Two properties required for production use not yet implemented: adversarial robustness and privacy guarantees (lack sandboxed execution, content-level anomaly detection, granular access control); schema evolution story for major revisions (versioning, automatic rewriting, deprecation policy).

nodes.label: Evaluation Scope Limitation (ML-only)
nodes.rationale: Study covers only ML papers where computational reproducibility and well-defined contribution types make ARA's four-layer structure natural fit. Generalization to experimental sciences with physical execution or theoretical disciplines with proof-based results remains empirically untested.

nodes.label: Fidelity Ceiling Limitation
nodes.rationale: ARA fidelity bounded by source of supervision. Compiler faithfully represents only what PDF contains; when paper omits experimental details, environment specs, or ablation results, no extraction method recovers them. Live Research Manager closes gap but assumes AI-native workflow.

nodes.label: Precision, Recall, F1 Computation
nodes.rationale: Skill counts as correct only when canonical identifier occurs in both predicted and gold sets; repeated mentions count once; empty predicted set receives P=R=0.

nodes.label: Radius of Gyration (Rg) Calculation
nodes.rationale: Metric reflecting overall compactness of peptide ensemble and aggregate formation

nodes.label: OpenR Framework
nodes.rationale: Open framework for studying reasoning systems; provides infrastructure for inference-time computation and search.

nodes.label: Matched Token-Cost Analysis
nodes.rationale: Compares token usage on 83-task intersection; Workflow Memory most token-efficient (-129.5K total), Skill achieves highest success (+5.5 pp) while reducing tokens vs Raw (-34.2K total).

nodes.label: RQ1: Representation of Prior Experience
nodes.rationale: Compares three conditions (Raw, Workflow Memory, Skill) to isolate whether representing prior experience as direct procedural memory versus distilled skill changes downstream execution performance.

nodes.label: RQ2: Outcome Annotation and No-Hint Ablation
nodes.norm_label: rq2: outcome annotation and no-hint ablation
nodes.rationale: Tests whether skill benefits derive from underlying experience content or from explicit success/failure outcome annotations during skill construction.

nodes.label: RQ3: Cross-Framework Transfer
nodes.rationale: Evaluates whether reusable procedural knowledge is tied to the framework that produced it by transferring Codex-derived skills to Gemini framework.

nodes.label: Short-Plan Baseline

nodes.label: 1-Wasserstein Distance (Earth Mover's Distance)
nodes.rationale: Metric quantifying minimum cost of transforming one probability distribution into another

nodes.label: Asynchronous Scheduling for ZOS Integration
nodes.rationale: Approximates verification capacity using confidence predictions from two steps prior; enables seamless Zero-Overhead Scheduling integration while maintaining rank-preserving token selection.

nodes.label: Confidence Head
nodes.rationale: Predicts per-position prefix survival probability; trained with binary cross-entropy against analytical acceptance rate derived from total variation distance between draft and target distributions.

nodes.label: DeepSeek-V4 Production Deployment
nodes.rationale: Real-world deployment with 3 MoE layers, γ=5 block size, asynchronous scheduling to integrate with Zero-Overhead Scheduling (ZOS) and CUDA graphs; variable-length kernel modifications for sparse attention.

nodes.label: Parallel Backbone (Draft Generation)
nodes.rationale: Deep transformer layers enabling high-capacity first-token prediction; O(1) latency allows deeper networks than autoregressive alternatives, yielding substantial accuracy margin at position 1.

nodes.label: Hardware-Aware Prefix Scheduler
nodes.rationale: Formulates verification length selection as global throughput maximization; greedily admits draft tokens sorted by survival probability, using profiled SPS(B) capacity curve to balance batch size against expected acceptance.

nodes.label: Sequential Stage (Markov/RNN Head)
nodes.rationale: Lightweight autoregressive correction module conditioning on previously sampled tokens; mitigates multi-modal collision and rapid acceptance decay typical of pure parallel generation.

nodes.label: Sequential Temperature Scaling (STS)
nodes.rationale: Post-hoc calibration addressing neural overconfidence; performs 1D grid search per position to minimize Expected Calibration Error of cumulative product while preserving token rankings.

nodes.label: Training Objective (Three-Term Loss)
nodes.rationale: Combines cross-entropy (Lce), distribution-matching via total-variation (Ltv), and confidence loss (Lconf); position-weighted by exp(-(k-1)/γ) to emphasize early block positions with higher leverage.

nodes.label: Non-Anticipating Property (Losslessness)
nodes.rationale: Admission decisions must not depend on future candidate tokens; early-stopping mechanism in Algorithm 1 enforces causality by breaking when throughput drops, preventing selection bias.

nodes.label: Parallel Generation Suffix Decay Problem
nodes.rationale: Pure parallel drafters suffer rapid acceptance decay at later positions due to multi-modal collision; marginalizing over all possible prior tokens produces inconsistent suffix combinations.

nodes.label: Semi-Autoregressive Design Rationale
nodes.rationale: Combines high-capacity parallel backbone for initial token with dependency-modeling sequential head for subsequent tokens; resolves trade-off between capacity advantage and suffix coherence.

nodes.label: Speculative Decoding (General Concept)
nodes.rationale: Decouples token proposal from verification; draft model generates candidates, target model verifies via rejection sampling; maintains exact target distribution while accelerating generation.

nodes.label: Throughput-Interactivity Trade-off
nodes.rationale: Under resource constraints with fixed KV-cache and limited user traffic, maximizing per-GPU token throughput and per-user generation speed become correlated rather than competing objectives.

nodes.label: Total Variation Distance for Acceptance Rate
nodes.norm_label: total variation distance for acceptance rate
nodes.rationale: Per-step acceptance probability equals 1 - 0.5 * ||p_d - p_t||_1; direct proxy for acceptance rate; minimizing total variation distance in training directly maximizes expected acceptance.

nodes.label: Variable-Length Kernel Optimization
nodes.rationale: Decouples physical execution from logical sequence tracking; flattens tokens across requests and conveys intra-sequence dependencies via marker tensor in sparse attention; enables dynamic routing without GPU under-utilization.

nodes.label: DSpark: Speculative Decoding Framework
nodes.rationale: Semi-autoregressive architecture combining parallel backbone with lightweight sequential head to mitigate suffix decay in speculative decoding; hardware-aware prefix scheduler dynamically routes verification based on system load and confidence estimates.

nodes.label: Benchmark-Side Prediction Factors
nodes.rationale: Three factors jointly affect benchmark predictability: wider score spread increases error (H3), more observed model scores reduce error (H4), strong-neighbor presence reduces error (H5). Tested via Spearman correlation and paired Wilcoxon ablations.

nodes.label: BENCHPRESS Score Predictor
nodes.rationale: Logit-transformed, bias-decomposed alternating least squares (ALS) matrix completion with rank 2 and regularization λ=0.1. Selected as default predictor after evaluating 84 transform-method combinations.

nodes.label: Conformal Prediction Intervals
nodes.rationale: Calibrated 90% prediction intervals for BENCHPRESS predictions. Hybrid estimator produces 27.01 point median width at 90% coverage. Intervals sharpen as more scores observed.

nodes.label: Logit Feature Transform
nodes.rationale: Transform percentage scores s ∈ [0,100] via log(s/(100-s)). Maps bounded range to unbounded scale, symmetrically spreading apart scores near 0 and 100. Selected as best feature transform for BENCHPRESS.

nodes.label: Model-Side Prediction Factors
nodes.rationale: Five factors affect model predictability: reasoning models easier than non-reasoning (H2), higher-scoring models easier (H3), strong-peer presence helps (H5), more observations help (H8), recent training anchors help (H9).

nodes.label: Greedy Probe Set Selection
nodes.rationale: Greedy algorithm selects benchmark probes to minimize pooled prediction error. Five-probe set (GPQA-D, HLE, Codeforces, MMLU-Pro, ARC-AGI-1) recovers scorecard to 3.93 MedAE; cost-aware variant reaches 4.55.

nodes.label: Rank-2 Geometry of Score Matrix
nodes.rationale: Empirical finding: held-out rank sweep minimizes error at rank 2; SVD of fully-observed submatrices shows two factors explain >90% variance. PC1 captures general capability; PC2 separates domains (coding vs. math).

nodes.label: Pairwise Model Ranking Preservation
nodes.rationale: BENCHPRESS predictions preserve 92.1% of pairwise model rankings on same benchmark when true score gap ≥5 points. Margin-aware evaluation accounts for near-ties.

nodes.label: Hybrid Reliability Estimator
nodes.rationale: Combines ensemble-spread disagreement and matrix-support signals to estimate per-cell prediction risk. Identifies safe-to-use predictions; when keeping 20% lowest-risk cells, MedAE drops to 1.83 points.

nodes.label: Temporal Deployment Stress Test
nodes.rationale: Evaluates BENCHPRESS on 27 newly released models using only pre-release training matrix. Five seed scores yield 4.83 MedAE; ten seeds tighten to 2.57 points.

nodes.label: AIME Benchmarks (2022–2025)

nodes.label: GSM8K Mathematical Reasoning Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Evaluation benchmark for mathematical reasoning; used to compare LoRA and OLoRA-tail.

nodes.label: Minor Subspace Safety Property
nodes.rationale: Minor singular vectors span directions comparatively inert in pretrained model; adapter updates remain orthogonal to most sensitive weight directions, keeping KL divergence near zero and training stable.

nodes.label: Principal Subspace Distributional Shift Risk
nodes.rationale: Principal subspace captures dominant pretrained directions; perturbation through on-policy RL updates induces large distributional shifts that DAPO clipping cannot fully contain; explains OLoRA collapse.

nodes.label: RL-Native Initialization Criterion
nodes.rationale: Initialization must expose meaningful low-dimensional learning direction without making first policy updates too large; differs from supervised fine-tuning because RL operates under KL-constrained trust region where early policy movement is exponentially unstable.

nodes.label: DAPO 1.5B Initialization Comparison
nodes.rationale: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B trained with DAPO; compares LoRA, PiSSA, MiLoRA, OLoRA, OLoRA-tail over 500 steps; demonstrates PiSSA/MiLoRA collapse and OLoRA-tail stability.

nodes.rationale: OLoRA-tail achieves 35.5% ± 1.6% average pass rate vs LoRA 24.0%, a +11.5 percentage point (+48% relative) improvement.

nodes.label: DAPO: Direct Advantage Policy Optimization
nodes.rationale: RL training objective used throughout experiments; employs clipping mechanism and KL penalties to maintain trust region; sensitive to early policy movement.

nodes.label: MiLoRA: Minor Singular Subspace Adaptation
nodes.rationale: Uses minor singular directions with singular-value scaling; can be effective in supervised fine-tuning but may underperform in RL; OLoRA-tail removes the scaling component for stability.

nodes.label: OLoRA: Orthogonal LoRA (Principal)
nodes.rationale: Initializes from principal singular vectors; undergoes training collapse under DAPO objective (reward drops to −1.0, KL divergence explodes to ~8 by step 100) because principal subspace captures dominant pretrained directions whose perturbation induces large distributional shifts.

nodes.label: OLoRA-tail: Controlled Geometry Initialization
nodes.rationale: Initializes from minor singular vectors (U_{-r}, V_{-r}) without singular-value scaling; preserves pretrained geometry while avoiding destabilizing scaling that SVD methods (PiSSA, MiLoRA) introduce; designed for RL stability by keeping adapter updates orthogonal to sensitive weight directions.

nodes.label: PiSSA: Principal Singular Subspace Adaptation
nodes.rationale: Initializes adapters using principal singular directions; effective in supervised fine-tuning but exhibits training collapse in RL with verifiable rewards due to large distributional shifts.

nodes.label: Advocate Agent

nodes.label: Advocate-Skeptic Debate Protocol
nodes.rationale: Single-round debate structure where Advocate presents evidence-heavy pro argument followed by Skeptic rebuttal; empirically more stable than multi-round debates and skeptic-first ordering, reducing verbosity and drift while preserving coverage of both strengths and weaknesses.

nodes.label: ASAP Dataset
nodes.rationale: Widely used benchmark of student-written English essays scored by trained raters using prompt-specific rubrics; includes eight essay sets with trait-level annotations for Sets 7 and 8.

nodes.label: Debate Capture Failure Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Judge inherits Advocate/Skeptic framing without verifying claims against essay text; substitutes debate resolution for text verification, producing overconfident misdiagnoses about structure and coherence despite clear textual evidence.

nodes.label: Judge Agent
nodes.rationale: Impartial arbiter synthesizing Advocate and Skeptic arguments with confidence scores and retrieved exemplars to produce final integer score.

nodes.label: Middle-Score Bias
nodes.rationale: Systematic bias in LLM-as-judge where models cluster predictions toward center of scoring scale, avoiding extreme values even when warranted (Zheng et al., 2023).

nodes.label: ProTACT
nodes.rationale: Supervised neural model for analytic trait scoring introducing prompt-aware representations and trait-similarity objective (Do et al., 2023).

nodes.label: Quadratic Weighted Kappa (QWK)
nodes.rationale: Standard agreement metric in AES accounting for ordinal score distances; used to evaluate trait-level scoring performance.

nodes.label: Rubric-Template Collapse Failure Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Under uncertainty, MADRAG falls back on plausible-sounding rubric prose weakly tied to essay content; reduces sensitivity to extremes and enables large deviations when essay is clearly strong or weak, indicating baseline judge limitation rather than component-specific artifact.

nodes.label: Skeptic Agent
nodes.rationale: Specialized agent role critiquing essay weaknesses without assigning scores or mentioning strengths; produces rebuttal focused on shortcomings.

nodes.label: Token Myopia Failure Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Systematic error where MADRAG treats anonymization markers (@CAPS, @PERSON, @DATE) as genuine mechanical errors, leading to under-scoring on Conventions trait; occurs when surface-form noise is amplified by debate and retrieval interaction.

nodes.label: Analytic Essay Trait Scoring Task

nodes.label: ASAP Essay Dataset

nodes.rationale: Sentence embedding model used for embedding discovery and retrieval baseline.

nodes.label: ModernBERT-Embed-Large
nodes.rationale: Modern embedding model evaluated with generic and recommended prefixes; achieves best MRR@10 on SPECIFY (39.1), ADDRESS (21.5), BROADEN (22.2).

nodes.label: Stella-EN-1.5B-V5
nodes.rationale: Instruction-tuned embedding model; achieves highest MRR@10 on SPECIFY (41.1) and BROADEN (20.1) with recommended prefix.

nodes.label: BM25 Lexical Baseline
nodes.rationale: Unigram, bigram, trigram variants with English stopword removal and Snowball stemming; implemented via BM25S and Faiss index.

nodes.label: Embedding Discovery
nodes.rationale: ALL-MPNET-BASE-V2 retrieves ten neighbors for each of 82 foundational markers from 9.5M sentence-initial comma-terminated phrases; GPT-4 validates ~30 additional markers.

nodes.label: GPT-5.4 Automatic Judge
nodes.rationale: LLM-as-judge via OpenAI Batch API; full judging prompt in system message, instance in user message, JSON response format, reasoning_effort=medium.

nodes.label: Marker Lexicon Generation
nodes.rationale: Three LLM models (Claude Opus 4.6, Gemini 3 Flash, GPT5.4) iteratively generate discourse marker variants tagged as strong-true, weak-true, or false to avoid single-model phrasing bias.

nodes.label: Multiple Negatives Ranking Loss
nodes.rationale: Contrastive learning loss with in-batch negatives; scale s=20 (τ=0.05) used for all models.

nodes.label: Pattern Expansion via Hearst Templates
nodes.rationale: Applies Hearst-inspired lexico-syntactic patterns with typed slots filled from curated term lists, expanded via NLTK, spaCy, and PyInflect morphological variants, then filtered by GPT-5.4.

nodes.label: Relevance Judge Calibration
nodes.rationale: 100 pairs per relation manually annotated by NLP expert; 4-6 prompts tested per relation; two highest-F1 prompts retained.

nodes.label: Silver Test Set Construction
nodes.rationale: 400 silver queries per relation sampled via confidence filtering; top 100 candidates retrieved, top 10 judged by human annotators; hard/soft agreement metrics.

nodes.label: Temporal Split Strategy
nodes.rationale: Balances three constraints: earlier training cutoff avoids model pretraining windows; 2025 validation allocation prevents inflation; single-year test partition prevents BROADEN starvation.

nodes.label: Text Normalization and Cleaning
nodes.rationale: Regex-based heuristics applied: lowercasing, noise removal, introduction-clause removal, gold-sentence prefix cleaning, short-sentence removal (<35 chars).

nodes.label: R-KV
nodes.rationale: KV cache eviction combining SnapKV score with redundancy penalty to avoid keeping restated facts twice.

nodes.label: SnapKV
nodes.rationale: KV cache eviction method that scores positions by recent-window attention, baseline for comparison.

nodes.label: TriAttention
nodes.rationale: KV cache eviction scoring positions by calibrated trigonometric distance from current query, strongest baseline.

nodes.label: VaSE
nodes.rationale: KV cache eviction scoring by value magnitude and filling remaining budget stochastically.

nodes.label: KV Cache Compression
nodes.rationale: Core technique for reducing memory bottleneck in LLM inference by compressing or evicting key-value pairs during decoding.

nodes.label: Prompt is the Fragile Part of KV Cache
nodes.norm_label: prompt is the fragile part of kv cache
nodes.rationale: Key finding that most performance gaps between eviction methods disappear when all methods protect the prompt, indicating selection signal contributes little beyond prompt protection.

nodes.label: Random Attention Serves 32-43% Higher Throughput
nodes.rationale: Efficiency finding showing Random Attention's lack of scoring pass provides substantial serving throughput advantage.

nodes.label: Reasoning Trace Protects Itself Through Redundancy
nodes.norm_label: reasoning trace protects itself through redundancy
nodes.rationale: Finding that reasoning traces maintain redundancy at two levels: textual (restating needed values) and cross-head (each head holds copies), enabling random eviction to work.

nodes.label: Random Attention
nodes.rationale: KV cache eviction policy that keeps the prompt and evicts uniformly at random within each attention head, computing no selection score.

nodes.label: Serving Throughput
nodes.rationale: Primary efficiency metric measuring tokens per second in vLLM deployment, showing Random Attention 32-43% faster than TriAttention.

nodes.label: Phi-4-reasoning
nodes.rationale: Reasoning-focused language model used for evaluating KV cache eviction on mathematical and scientific tasks.

nodes.label: PagedAttention
nodes.rationale: Memory management technique for KV cache using block tables, enabling efficient serving of multiple sequences.

nodes.label: Planted-Fact Probe
nodes.rationale: Experimental technique inserting synthetic facts into reasoning traces to measure cross-head redundancy and retrieval patterns under eviction.

nodes.label: Agent Skill
nodes.rationale: Compact procedural abstraction encoding what to do, what to check, and what pitfalls to avoid; differs from raw traces by compressing noisy experience into standardized format; primary mechanism is procedural anchoring (65.7%).

nodes.label: Procedural Anchoring
nodes.rationale: Primary mechanism by which skills improve agent performance (65.7% of cases); stabilizes execution through setup steps, tool sequences, implementation routines, and verification checks rather than injecting factual knowledge.

nodes.label: Cross-Framework Skill Transfer
nodes.rationale: Skills constructed in Codex framework transfer to Gemini CLI; distilled skills preserve reusable procedural guidance more robustly than direct workflow traces across framework boundaries.

nodes.label: Skill Execution Bottlenecks
nodes.rationale: Skills reduce environment_infrastructure_failure (5.3%→0.2%), output_format_schema_mismatch (7.4%→3.2%), but do not eliminate algorithmic_logic_error (8.3%) or static_verification (12.5%).

nodes.label: Skill Failure Modes
nodes.rationale: Skills fail under brittle assumptions, incompatible contexts, insufficient adaptation, or when misapplied (10.0% of skill-arm cases); skill_guidance_misapplied_or_ignored appears in 10.0% vs 0.8% for raw execution.

nodes.label: Skill Lifecycle Framework
nodes.rationale: Skills work when prior experience distilled into reusable procedural anchors, retrieved in compatible contexts, and invoked with adaptation; fail when noisy, over-specific, mismatched, or followed rigidly.

nodes.label: Skill Mechanism Labels
nodes.rationale: 5 mechanism categories: procedural_anchor (65.7%), knowledge_injection (4.5%), failure_warning, none, counterproductive; paired trajectory analysis assigns mechanism to each arm to isolate behavior changes.

nodes.label: Outcome Annotation in Skill Construction
nodes.rationale: Success/failure labels guide skill construction; impact grows as failed trajectories enter pool; at 3s2f mixture, Gemini skill with labels reaches 0.7462 vs 0.4000 without labels.

nodes.label: Skill Retrieval and Pool Confusability
nodes.rationale: As skill pools grow from 5 to 100, actual-use precision falls from 29.6% to 3.3%; semantic confusability (similar distractors) is more stressful than pool size; exact ground-truth invocation neither sufficient nor necessary for success.

nodes.label: Skill-Use Taxonomy
nodes.rationale: 3 high-level categories (SC1: procedural anchoring, SC2: execution-layer failures, SC3: invocation/boundary failures) and 12 fine-grained modes; derived from 240 sampled trajectories with 95.8% human-LLM agreement (κ=0.952).

nodes.label: Workflow Memory
nodes.rationale: Direct procedural memory preserving trace-level execution details; carries irrelevant exploration, failed branches, and process noise; skills improve over workflow memory by 6.06 percentage points in matched comparisons.

nodes.label: ProteinGym Benchmark
nodes.rationale: 217-assay protein engineering benchmark with DMS datasets and indel scans

nodes.label: B1 Aggregate Linear Regression Model
nodes.rationale: Baseline using only 11 global tree features; achieves best overall performance for Ω_m (RMSE 0.0155, R² 0.9696), indicating global merger tree properties are highly informative for this parameter.

nodes.label: B2 Raw Substructure Physical Features Linear Regression
nodes.norm_label: b2 raw substructure physical features linear regression
nodes.rationale: Baseline using raw physical features without topological embeddings; yields negative R² values, indicating poor performance due to high dimensionality and noise in raw substructure features.

nodes.label: B4 Flattened Combined Features XGBoost
nodes.rationale: Baseline using same per-substructure input as QITT (physical + GNN embeddings) but flattened to 4440 features; underperforms QITT_XGBoost, demonstrating QITT's superior compression and representation.

nodes.label: Graph Neural Network Topological Embeddings
nodes.rationale: 64-dimensional embeddings generated by GNN to capture structural information from substructure graphs; t-SNE visualization shows coherence with substructure size (halo count), indicating meaningful topological encoding.

nodes.label: QITT Linear Regression Model
nodes.rationale: Best performer for Ω_m prediction (RMSE 0.0246, R² 0.9231), suggesting QITT features may already linearize relationships between substructure information and cosmological parameters.

nodes.label: QITT XGBoost Model
nodes.rationale: Competitive QITT-based model (Ω_m: RMSE 0.0303, R² 0.8834; σ_8: RMSE 0.0711, R² 0.5577); significantly outperforms B4_FlatCombined_XGBoost, demonstrating QITT's effectiveness over simple flattening.

nodes.label: Cosmological Parameter Ω_m (Matter Density)
nodes.rationale: Target parameter for regression; shows strong signal in global merger tree properties; best predicted by B1_Aggregate_LinearRegression (R² 0.9696).

nodes.label: Cosmological Parameter σ_8 (Matter Power Spectrum Amplitude)
nodes.norm_label: cosmological parameter σ_8 (matter power spectrum amplitude)
nodes.rationale: Target parameter for regression; relates to amplitude of matter fluctuations; generally harder to constrain (lower R² across models); may require more subtle substructure information.

nodes.label: Feature Importance Analysis - QITT XGBoost
nodes.rationale: Top 20 most important features from 202 QITT-derived features for XGBoost model; shows selective reliance on compressed feature subset for cosmological parameter estimation.

nodes.label: Predicted vs. True Ω_m Values (QITT_XGBoost)
nodes.rationale: Scatter plot showing predictions align closely with y=x line, reflecting high R² of 0.8834; clustering around specific true values indicates model's predictive ability with some uncertainty.

nodes.label: Predicted vs. True σ_8 Values (QITT_XGBoost)
nodes.rationale: Scatter plot showing moderate correlation with greater variance in predictions compared to Ω_m, consistent with lower R² of 0.5577; indicates greater difficulty constraining this parameter.

nodes.label: Paired t-tests for Model Comparison
nodes.rationale: Paired t-tests on squared errors of test set predictions; confirms QITT_XGBoost significantly better than B2_RawSubPhys_XGBoost and B4_FlatCombined_XGBoost; no significant difference vs B1_Aggregate_XGBoost.

nodes.label: Substructure Physical Features
nodes.rationale: Physical properties extracted for each substructure; combined with GNN topological embeddings to form per-substructure feature vectors; raw features alone perform poorly without further processing.

nodes.label: t-SNE Projection of Topological Embeddings
nodes.rationale: Visualization of 10,000 64-dimensional GNN embeddings colored by halo count; shows diffuse clustering with coherence between embedding space regions and substructure size, indicating meaningful topological encoding.

nodes.rationale: Single-cell omics benchmark tasks including modality prediction, perturbations, cell communication

nodes.rationale: Core neural network training and implementation framework

nodes.label: ProteinGym SPIKE-SARS2 Task
nodes.rationale: Protein fitness prediction; AUTOSCIENTISTS achieves 0.874 Spearman ρ at n=2 (best crew size for this task)

nodes.label: Benchmark Taxonomy for Scientific AI Systems

nodes.rationale: Comprehensive source-level analysis of Claude Code's architecture, design principles, and subsystem organization

nodes.rationale: Most reliable deployment mode: AI reduces mechanical friction in retrieval, drafting, coding, visualization, but researchers retain responsibility for judgment, interpretation, experimental design, argumentation, accountability.

nodes.rationale: Orchestrated multi-agent system using Claude Code agents with deterministic monitor process and heartbeat loop for coordinated scientific research

nodes.label: Deepscaler Dataset
nodes.rationale: 10k subset of challenging math problems; demonstrates NGU effectiveness on harder problem distributions

nodes.rationale: Base models used for experiments (Qwen2.5-0.5B, Qwen3-4B); NGU applied to improve their RL training

nodes.label: Fusion-of-N: Synthesis-based Aggregation for LLM Outputs
nodes.norm_label: fusion-of-n: synthesis-based aggregation for llm outputs
nodes.rationale: Proposes FusioN method that synthesizes multiple LLM generations into single output, outperforming Best-of-N selection across test-time scaling and synthetic data generation.

nodes.label: SWE-Explore Benchmark
nodes.rationale: 848 instances across 10 programming languages and 203 repositories; evaluates exploration along coverage, ranking, and context-efficiency dimensions; includes restricted-context validation protocol.

nodes.label: Determinantal Point Processes (DPPs)
nodes.rationale: Related mathematical framework for diverse subset selection; uses determinant of kernel matrix; less straightforward interpretation than Vendi Score

nodes.label: Effective Rank
nodes.rationale: Mathematical foundation for Vendi Score; exponential of entropy of normalized singular values; used in signal processing and ML

nodes.label: Image Generative Model Diversity
nodes.rationale: Vendi Score applied to CIFAR-10, ImageNet, LSUN datasets; complements existing metrics like FID and Precision/Recall

nodes.label: IntDiv (Internal Diversity) Metric
nodes.rationale: Baseline diversity metric based on average pairwise dissimilarity; used in molecular generative modeling; has limitations in capturing feature correlations

nodes.label: Mode Collapse in GANs
nodes.rationale: Vendi Score captures fine-grained diversity distinctions beyond Number of Modes metric; reveals imbalances in mode distribution

nodes.label: Molecular Generative Model Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Application domain where Vendi Score identifies model weaknesses (e.g., HMM duplicates) not detected by IntDiv

nodes.label: Spectral Clustering
nodes.rationale: Related use of eigenvalues of similarity matrix; Vendi Score more general than counting connected components

nodes.label: Text Decoding Algorithm Diversity
nodes.rationale: Vendi Score applied to image captioning with diverse beam search; correlates with n-gram diversity but captures additional aspects

nodes.label: Vendi Score Metric
nodes.rationale: Novel diversity evaluation metric based on Shannon entropy of eigenvalues of similarity matrix; connects ecology and quantum statistical mechanics to ML

nodes.label: Von Neumann Entropy
nodes.rationale: Connection to quantum statistical mechanics; Vendi Score equals exponential of von Neumann entropy of normalized similarity matrix

nodes.label: Harbor Tasks
nodes.rationale: Executable task packages derived from researcher collaboration; combine instructions, assets, environment, and rubric-based tests

nodes.label: Inner Recursion: Harness Improvement
nodes.rationale: Feedback-guided procedural edits to instructions, skills, and context; auxiliary model diagnoses failures and proposes bounded changes

nodes.label: Outer Recursion: Model Learning
nodes.rationale: GRPO-based RL with task-adaptive rubric rewards; environment augmentation calibrated to current model and harness

nodes.label: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement
nodes.rationale: Paradigm coupling inner harness refinement (fixed model) with outer model RL (fixed harness); bidirectional feedback enables co-evolution

nodes.label: Task-Adaptive Rubric Rewards
nodes.rationale: Trajectory rewards computed from task-specific rubrics with weighted criteria; fixed during optimization to ensure stable training signal

nodes.label: BiomniEval Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Biomedical AI agent evaluation benchmark; used for case studies on harness adaptation and model learning

nodes.label: LAB-Bench Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Scientific task benchmark covering literature reading, database judgments, protocol troubleshooting, gene/variant assessment

nodes.label: Qwen Models (ScienceBuddy)
nodes.rationale: Qwen3.5-4B used as task model; Qwen3.8-27B as helper for feedback simulation; GPT-6 Astra for harness diagnosis

nodes.label: Crowdworker Evaluation Framework
nodes.rationale: Data collection methodology using select workers (MTurk + Upwork) and general workers; challenges in quality assurance for open-ended conversations

nodes.label: Data Quality Measurement Challenges
nodes.rationale: Open-ended conversations introduce hard-to-control variables; author-rater agreement not predictive of conversation quality; model updates make comparisons moving targets

nodes.label: InstructGPT Model
nodes.rationale: Baseline model for comparison; authors note samples were cherry-picked to display poor behavior

nodes.label: Playground Task (Helpfulness)
nodes.rationale: Task design for collecting helpfulness data; workers chat with AI and compare responses

nodes.label: Red Team Task (Harmlessness)
nodes.rationale: Adversarial task design to elicit harmful model behavior; workers attempt to make AI say bad things

nodes.label: RLHF-trained Response
nodes.rationale: Improved model responses via reinforcement learning from human feedback; demonstrates better helpfulness and harmlessness

nodes.label: CLEVR Synthetic Testbed
nodes.rationale: Controlled synthetic environment for isolating concept transfer between modalities with systematic ablation of color, shape, relation, size, and count

nodes.label: Asymmetric Knowledge Flow
nodes.rationale: Finding that language and visual understanding act as strong priors for visual generation, but visual generation yields neutral effects on other abilities

nodes.label: Physics of Multimodal Pretraining
nodes.rationale: Systematic study of fundamental mechanisms governing unified multimodal pretraining across language, visual understanding, and visual generation

nodes.label: FFN Layer Placement and Scaling in Language Models
nodes.norm_label: ffn layer placement and scaling in language models
nodes.rationale: Investigates optimal placement of FFN-expanded layers across transformer depth to improve model performance under compute-optimal training, finding middle layers most important.

nodes.label: NLP Benchmark Evaluations
nodes.rationale: Standardized evaluation on Lambada, ARC, MMLU, HellaSwag, OpenBookQA, TriviaQA with specific prompt formats

nodes.label: Pre-training under Infinite Compute
nodes.rationale: Proposes data-constrained pre-training recipes using regularization, ensembling, and distillation to achieve 5.17× data efficiency improvement over standard approaches.

nodes.label: Abstraction and Multi-Scale Discovery
nodes.rationale: Technical priority: discovering intermediate scales bridging different levels of explanation; key to scientific breakthroughs

nodes.label: Causality in AI Systems
nodes.rationale: Technical priority: embedding causal structure in models to distinguish spurious correlations from causal relationships

nodes.label: Discourse Gap and Narrative Dominance
nodes.rationale: Institutional challenge: corporate AI narratives dominate public discourse; obscure foundational public research and interdisciplinary teamwork

nodes.label: Scientific Context and Constraints
nodes.rationale: Third dimension of framework; recognizes practical constraints (data, compute, validation requirements, domain tolerance for uncertainty)

nodes.label: Governance Gap in AI for Science
nodes.norm_label: governance gap in ai for science
nodes.rationale: Institutional challenge: policy-practice gap in addressing bias, consent, privacy, transparency, reproducibility, and attribution

nodes.label: Human Understanding in Scientific Discovery
nodes.rationale: Philosophical question: whether science requires human comprehension or whether autonomous AI discovery is scientifically valid

nodes.label: Infrastructure Gap and Compute Concentration
nodes.rationale: Institutional challenge: AI infrastructure concentrated in private companies; threatens open science and scientific independence

nodes.label: Paradigm Shift Question
nodes.rationale: Central question: whether AI represents normal science within computational paradigm or signals fundamental shift in what counts as scientific knowledge

nodes.label: Productivity Paradox in Science
nodes.rationale: Concern: scientific output growing but productivity declining; AI risks intensifying disconnect between output and progress

nodes.label: AI as Repository vs Interface
nodes.rationale: Epistemological question: whether AI encodes knowledge as parameters or provides conduit to external sources; implications for knowledge evolution

nodes.label: Research Culture Gap
nodes.rationale: Institutional challenge: limited career pathways for interdisciplinary AI-science researchers; funding mechanisms poorly adapted to team science

nodes.label: The Science Gap: Pattern Matching vs Causal Reasoning
nodes.norm_label: the science gap: pattern matching vs causal reasoning
nodes.rationale: Central challenge: AI excels at pattern identification but struggles to identify causal mechanisms; gap between statistical and scientific reasoning

nodes.label: Hybrid Mechanistic-Data-Driven Simulation
nodes.rationale: Technical priority: combining mechanistic models with data-driven flexibility to avoid oversimplification or physical implausibility

nodes.label: Task Capabilities Framework
nodes.rationale: First dimension of AI-for-science framework; distinguishes what different AI tools can deliver in practice

nodes.label: Scientific Workflow Needs
nodes.rationale: Second dimension of framework; identifies where AI adds value across hypothesis generation, experimental design, data analysis

nodes.label: Citation Prediction Task

nodes.label: Prompt Pre-training Strategy

nodes.label: Repeated Tokens Training
nodes.rationale: Trains for 4.25 epochs on curated corpus; validation loss continues to fall; contradicts prior work suggesting repeated tokens harmful; suggests quality matters more than scale

nodes.label: Galactica Scientific Corpus
nodes.rationale: Curated dataset of 106B tokens from papers (48M), code (2M), reference material (8M), knowledge bases (2M), filtered CommonCrawl (0.9M)

nodes.label: Working Memory Token <work>

nodes.label: Mathematical Error Persistence

nodes.label: Learner-Relative Task Complexity
nodes.rationale: Complexity is model-aware and configuration-dependent (z includes model, scaffold, tools, budget). Useful data occupy learnable band near capability frontier—too easy tasks are redundant, too hard tasks provide no successful trajectory. Band moves as learner improves.

nodes.label: Acquisition Temperature (η)

nodes.label: Gumbel-Top-K Sampling
nodes.rationale: Batch acquisition sampling technique producing weighted samples without replacement from finite candidate pool

nodes.label: Infinitely-Armed Bandit Framework

nodes.label: KL Divergence Regularization
nodes.rationale: Regularization term in acquisition-tilted optimization balancing acquisition value against deviation from base LLM distribution

nodes.label: LLM Sampling Temperature (T_LLM)

nodes.label: AutoDock Vina Docking Score

nodes.label: Sparse Gaussian Processes for Scalability

nodes.label: Surrogate Misspecification and Reward Exploitation Risk

nodes.rationale: Limitation of current LDM framework regarding potential surrogate model misspecification or reward hacking

nodes.label: Test-Time Search Computational Overhead

nodes.label: Weak Domain Priors in Specialized Domains
nodes.norm_label: weak domain priors in specialized domains
nodes.rationale: Limitation that LDM performance is bounded by LLM's pretrained domain knowledge, difficult in domains with weak priors

nodes.label: Discovery Gap
nodes.rationale: Quantity measuring performance governed by reservoir's tail of near-optimal arms in infinitely-armed bandit setting

nodes.label: Missing-Mass Argument
nodes.rationale: Theoretical tool for analyzing discovery gap through probability mass not yet observed in finite samples

nodes.label: Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Augmentation
nodes.rationale: Fine-tuning technique where proposer generates surrogate-grounded research-progress rationale before emitting candidate action

nodes.label: Graph-of-Thought
nodes.rationale: Generalized reasoning to arbitrary graph structures beyond linear chains

nodes.label: Anchor Signal for Error Correction
nodes.rationale: Small fraction of groups graded by real execution to provide ground truth for bias and noise estimation

nodes.label: KL-Shampoo
nodes.rationale: Gradient covariance estimation via Kullback-Leibler minimization that reduces condition number of Kronecker factors to square root of standard formulation, improving numerical stability

nodes.label: Layer-Wise Distributed Optimizer
nodes.rationale: System-level implementation strategy in Megatron-LM that maintains 2D weight matrices intact across distributed training while using variable-sized allgather collectives for parameter synchronization

nodes.label: Momentum Orthogonalized by Polar (MOP)
nodes.rationale: Variant of Muon that replaces Newton-Schulz orthogonalization with exact polar decomposition via SVD

nodes.label: QR Decomposition for Eigenbasis
nodes.rationale: Per-step QR decomposition in SOAP to recompute eigenbasis, critical for resolving slingshot instability in large-batch training

nodes.label: Qwen-3-30B-A3B Architecture
nodes.rationale: MoE architecture used for large-scale comparative studies of SOAP and Muon optimizers

nodes.label: Slingshot Instability
nodes.rationale: Early-training instability in large-batch pretraining caused by stale preconditioner effect when eigenbasis updates lag behind rapidly changing loss landscape

nodes.label: Atomic Capability Evaluation (ACE)
nodes.rationale: Fine-grained diagnostic benchmark with 2,503 probes across 183 atomic capabilities in 18 categories; enables rapid iteration during development

nodes.label: AI4AI Autonomy Levels
nodes.rationale: Five-level rubric (L1-L5) assessing AI autonomy in R&D tasks; experimentation and deployment reach L4, architecture and learning algorithm design at L2

nodes.label: Binary Function Search Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Evaluates agent capability to locate target functions in stripped ELF binaries; ZGCM-1 achieves 62% on 50-task subset

nodes.label: Curriculum Pre-Training
nodes.rationale: Lexical complexity ordering for general-language documents; improves coding BPB 1.99→0.81 and math BPB 0.97→0.94 at 10B tokens

nodes.label: Data Mixture Composition
nodes.rationale: Balanced across web, code, mathematics, academic/OCR, reasoning, and instruction data; adjusted across pre-training and mid-training stages

nodes.label: Finding 1: Curriculum Pre-training
nodes.rationale: Lexical complexity is cheap corpus-scale ordering signal for general-language text but poor difficulty proxy for code and mathematics

nodes.label: Finding 2: TWEO Enables FP8 Pretraining
nodes.rationale: Suppressing intermediate activation outliers crucial for FP8 training stability; combined with delayed scaling prevents numerical divergence

nodes.label: Finding 3: Pretraining Efficiency Gain
nodes.rationale: Co-design of hybrid SWA (1.4×), FP8 (1.5×), Muon (1.8×), and Pre-LN (1.1×) yields ~4.2× speedup in 16K pretraining time-to-loss

nodes.label: FP8 Mixed-Precision Training
nodes.rationale: Transformer Engine hybrid FP8 (E4M3 forward, E5M2 backward) with delayed scaling; contributes 1.5× throughput gain

nodes.label: General Pre-Training Stage

nodes.label: Hybrid Sliding-Window Attention (SWA)
nodes.rationale: 5:1 ratio of gated sliding-window to global attention; delivers 3.94× throughput speedup and 6.4× KV-cache reduction at 256K

nodes.label: MDP State-Action Modeling in Mid-Training
nodes.rationale: Reformulates agentic traces as Markov decision process-style state-conditioned next-action prediction; provides denser per-step supervision

nodes.label: Mid-Training Stage
nodes.rationale: Capability-oriented continued pre-training with progressive context expansion: 16K (180B tokens), 64K (240B tokens), 256K (180.51B tokens)

nodes.label: TWEO Activation Regularizer
nodes.rationale: Suppresses intermediate activation outliers; enables FP8 training stability when combined with delayed scaling

nodes.label: Web-Environment Deep Research Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Thinking-enabled ReAct policy with up to 64 search-and-read steps; ZGCM-1 achieves 63.09% on WebWalkerQA

nodes.label: Atria Dawn Preview Model
nodes.rationale: 744-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts foundation agentic language model trained via Verifiable Experience Pipeline

nodes.label: Open Challenge 1: Diverse Research Directions
nodes.rationale: How could AI keep generating diverse research directions and assess their potential value before results are available?

nodes.label: Open Challenge 2: Recursive Experience Transformation
nodes.rationale: AI must recursively transform experiences from extended exploration into intrinsic research capabilities

nodes.label: Open Challenge 3: Human Oversight at Scale
nodes.norm_label: open challenge 3: human oversight at scale
nodes.rationale: As AI reveals possibilities beyond human imagination, how can humans formulate meaningful goals and maintain effective oversight?

nodes.label: Open Challenge 4: Authority Allocation and Alignment
nodes.norm_label: open challenge 4: authority allocation and alignment
nodes.rationale: Need clear protocols for authority allocation and alignment standards as AI systems begin to lead most R&D

nodes.label: Human-AI Collaboration in R&D
nodes.rationale: Analysis of 769 task records from 56 participants; AI proposed 64.6% of methods but humans made final choice in 85.5%

nodes.label: Evolution of Human-AI Roles
nodes.rationale: Three stages: research object (full human control), task-level runner (human-designed workflows), project-level coworker (autonomous planning)

nodes.label: Verifiable Experience Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Connects tasks and agent trajectories to artifacts and externally verified outcomes; only experience with verified evidence incorporated

nodes.label: Agentic Co-Training Dynamics
nodes.rationale: Mixed think/no-think fine-tuning on execution-verified trajectories balances deep reasoning with direct-response efficiency for tool-augmented agency.

nodes.label: AI-Native R&D Workflow
nodes.rationale: Researcher-directed agent swarms autonomously manage cluster operations, data curation, and diagnostic evaluation across full model development lifecycle.

nodes.label: DEBATE Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Large-scale empirical benchmark for evaluating authenticity of multi-agent role-playing LLM interactions; 29,417 messages from 2,792 participants

nodes.label: Multi-Agent Opinion Dynamics
nodes.rationale: Evaluates authenticity of group dynamics in role-playing LLM agents; addresses premature consensus convergence and unnatural alignment patterns

nodes.label: Efficiency Scaling: 4.2× Time-to-Loss Improvement
nodes.rationale: ZGCM-1 achieves ~4.2× pre-training time-to-loss speedup through hybrid attention, FP8 precision, and Muon optimizer co-design.

nodes.label: FP8 Pre-Training with Muon Optimizer
nodes.rationale: System-algorithm co-design combining Muon optimizer, hybrid FP8 precision, and TWEO outlier regularization; achieves ~4.2× pre-training time-to-loss speedup.

nodes.label: Hybrid Sliding-Window and Global Attention
nodes.rationale: Interleaves gated sliding-window attention (27 layers, 128-token window) with global attention (5 layers) at 5:1 ratio; achieves 3.94× throughput speedup at 256K context.

nodes.label: Long-Context Generalization via Progressive Scaling
nodes.rationale: Progressive context scaling (16K→64K→256K) with MDP supervision enables efficient long-context training without catastrophic loss spikes.

nodes.label: MDP Mid-Training with Context Scaling
nodes.rationale: Reformulates interaction traces into Markov Decision Process state-action transitions; progressively scales context across 600B tokens (16K→64K→256K).

nodes.label: ZGCM-1: 7B Foundation Model
nodes.rationale: Fully open 7.39B dense model trained with extreme efficiency, coupling deliberate internal thinking with active external tool use across 256K context.

nodes.label: Benchmark Error Classification
nodes.rationale: Errors in problem statements or reference solutions, including incorrect answers, inconsistent conditions, ambiguity, or missing assumptions.

nodes.label: Benchmark Saturation and Defect Masking
nodes.rationale: As model capability grows, true error rate drops below benchmark defect rate; defects become dominant source of reported errors, masking true performance.

nodes.label: CMT-Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Expert-authored condensed matter theory benchmark with 50 questions; pre-audit mean@4 61.0% rises to 87.2% after expert repair.

nodes.label: CritPt Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Expert-curated frontier physics challenges; pre-audit mean@5 32.3% rises to mean@4 87.5% on 54 retained challenges after expert correction.

nodes.label: Grader Error Classification

nodes.label: HLE-Physics Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Expert-authored physics subset of Humanity's Last Exam with 202 text-only questions; pre-audit mean@4 47.3% rises to 78.7% after correction.

nodes.label: Model Error Classification
nodes.rationale: Genuine model errors where problem is well-posed, reference solution is correct, but model gives incorrect answer.

nodes.label: PHYBench Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Public-source physics benchmark with 100 problems from high-school to Physics Olympiad difficulty; grader errors dominate audit set.

nodes.label: Expert Physics Benchmark Audit
nodes.rationale: Systematic expert review of physics benchmarks to distinguish genuine model errors from grader errors and benchmark defects.

nodes.rationale: Public-source benchmark with 1,401 text-only physics questions; 64.86% of audited rejections are grader errors.

nodes.label: Rule-Based Evaluator Brittleness
nodes.rationale: Rule-based evaluators (exact-match, symbolic) reject equivalent answers in different forms; PHYBench and PRISM-Physics show 71.43% and 64.86% grader error rates.

nodes.label: Clustering Analysis

nodes.label: Machine Learning Models
nodes.rationale: Regression and classification models including random forests, XGBoost, and neural networks

nodes.label: Researcher Agent

nodes.label: Statistical Analysis Methods

nodes.label: Data Visualization Techniques
nodes.rationale: Methods for creating plots, heatmaps, and other visual representations of data

nodes.rationale: AI-generated paper mapping size and compositional variations in main asteroid belt

nodes.label: Black Hole-Stellar Mass Relation Paper

nodes.rationale: AI-generated paper analyzing high-mass black hole merger GW231123 using dimensionality reduction

nodes.label: Protein Folding Kinetics Paper
nodes.rationale: AI-generated paper analyzing NTL9 protein folding using dimensionality reduction and Markov state models

nodes.label: Diminishing Returns from LLM Scaling
nodes.rationale: gpt-4.1-nano→gpt-5-nano: +15.5% utility; gpt-5-nano→gpt-5-mini: +1.25%; indicates domain-specific capability becomes bottleneck after sufficient LLM reasoning ability.

nodes.label: Domain Advantage Assumption
nodes.rationale: Theoretical assumption: domain-specific FMs achieve strictly better performance than language-only models on domain-specific components; justifies heterogeneous collaboration.

nodes.label: EywaAgent: Single-Agent Integration
nodes.rationale: Coupled FM-LLM unit with control policy deciding invoke/skip; enables adaptive switching between generalized reasoning and specialized acting; subsumes language-only agents as special case.

nodes.label: EywaMAS: Multi-Agent Composition
nodes.rationale: Plug-and-play multi-agent system mixing LLM agents and EywaAgents; enables parallel specialization and cross-domain collaboration with fixed communication topology.

nodes.label: EywaOrchestra: Dynamic Orchestration
nodes.rationale: Dynamically instantiated heterogeneous multi-agent system with conductor selecting agent roles, LLM backbones, FMs, and topologies per task; enables task-adaptive system construction.

nodes.label: Hyperparameter Robustness
nodes.rationale: Eywa stable across LLM temperature, FM temperature, and prompt designs; gains not tied to specific hyperparameter choices; robust to design variations.

nodes.label: Language Interface Bottleneck
nodes.rationale: Information-theoretic analysis: serialization of non-linguistic inputs into language tokens discards task-relevant information; data processing inequality shows irreducible Bayes risk gap.

nodes.label: Model Context Protocol Implementation
nodes.rationale: Tsaheylu instantiated via MCP; FMs exposed as remote services with defined input/output schemas; query compiler produces structured tool calls; response adapter transforms outputs.

nodes.label: Theorem 17: EywaMAS Solvability
nodes.rationale: Single EywaAgent in EywaMAS propagates recovered information through communication graph; achieves zero risk on task families where LLM-only MAS remains constrained.

nodes.label: Theorem 18: Adaptive Orchestration
nodes.rationale: Oracle adaptive routing strictly improves over best fixed configuration when different task regions favor different configurations; motivates EywaOrchestra.

nodes.label: Theorem 3: EywaAgent Improvement
nodes.rationale: Formal result: EywaAgent achieves strictly lower optimal risk than language-only agents under domain advantage assumption; expands solvable task space.

nodes.label: FM-LLM Tsaheylu Interface
nodes.rationale: Bidirectional communication interface with query compiler (ϕ: state→FM config) and response adapter (ψ: FM output→language context); implemented via Model Context Protocol (MCP).

nodes.label: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Architecture
nodes.rationale: Architecture where each token routes through subset of experts; vulnerable to targeted bit flips in expert parameters despite sparse routing.

nodes.label: Algorithm 1: Red Queen Gödel Machine Search
nodes.norm_label: algorithm 1: red queen godel machine search
nodes.rationale: Complete pseudocode for RQGM procedure: initialization, CMP-guided search between checkpoints, evaluator replacement at checkpoints, and endpoint selection.

nodes.label: Assumption 2: Stationary Learned Evaluation Within Epoch
nodes.norm_label: assumption 2: stationary learned evaluation within epoch
nodes.rationale: Key assumption enabling epoch-local stationarity: evaluator, artifact generation, and scoring rule are frozen throughout each epoch.

nodes.label: Checkpoint Schedule
nodes.rationale: Exponentially-spaced checkpoints where evaluator replacements occur, bounding cumulative re-evaluation cost to O(B) rather than O(B²) over total budget B.

nodes.label: Controlled Utility Evolution
nodes.rationale: Mechanism dividing search into evolutionary epochs with fixed evaluation within each epoch but allowing utility changes at epoch boundaries, enabling non-stationary objectives while preserving per-epoch convergence guarantees.

nodes.label: Definition F.1: Criterion-Valid Record
nodes.rationale: Formal definition of utility evidence records valid under current criterion vector, enabling selective erasure to maintain criterion consistency across epochs.

nodes.label: Definition F.2: Utility Transition
nodes.rationale: Formal definition of evaluator replacement procedure: advancing epoch index, replacing criterion, and applying selective erasure to maintain criterion consistency.

nodes.label: Open-Endedness
nodes.rationale: Goal of generating novel artifacts indefinitely; RQGM enables this by co-evolving objectives, allowing search to bootstrap evaluation beyond static benchmarks.

nodes.label: Proposition 6: Bounded Recovery
nodes.rationale: Theoretical result bounding cumulative re-evaluation cost of evaluator replacements to O(B) with exponentially-spaced checkpoints, preventing asymptotic overhead.

nodes.label: Reward Hacking
nodes.rationale: Problem where agents exploit static benchmarks; RQGM mitigates through co-evolved evaluators that harden over time, making objectives harder to hack.

nodes.label: Red Queen Gödel Machine (RQGM)
nodes.rationale: Core framework enabling co-evolution of agents and evaluators through controlled utility evolution, organizing search into epochs with fixed within-epoch evaluation but evolving objectives across epochs.

nodes.label: Selective Erasure
nodes.rationale: Procedure removing only utility records dependent on a replaced evaluator at epoch boundaries, preserving epoch-local stationarity and enabling evaluator replacement without violating fixed-criterion search guarantees.

nodes.label: Van Valen's Red Queen Hypothesis
nodes.rationale: Biological principle that species adapt to maintain fitness relative to co-evolving competitors; motivates RQGM's co-evolutionary approach to self-improvement.

nodes.label: Cross-Layer Index Reuse in Sparse Attention
nodes.norm_label: cross-layer index reuse in sparse attention
nodes.rationale: Exploits empirical finding that token selection is highly correlated across consecutive transformer layers (70-100% overlap). Enables dramatic reduction in indexer computations by reusing indices from subset of layers.

nodes.label: DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA)
nodes.rationale: Production-grade sparse attention mechanism using lightweight lightning indexer to select top-k tokens. Reduces core attention from O(L²) to O(Lk) but indexer retains O(L²) complexity at each layer.

nodes.label: Full/Shared Layer Partitioning
nodes.rationale: IndexCache partitions layers into Full (retain indexers) and Shared (reuse indices). Adds single conditional branch in inference with no additional GPU memory overhead.

nodes.label: GLM-5 Scaling Results
nodes.rationale: Preliminary results on 744B GLM-5 model confirm IndexCache scalability. Achieves 1.2-1.3x speedup with negligible degradation, demonstrating applicability to production-scale models.

nodes.label: Greedy Layer Selection Algorithm
nodes.rationale: Training-free method for determining which layers retain indexers. Iteratively converts Full layers to Shared layers, selecting conversions that minimize LM loss on calibration set.

nodes.label: Index Overlap Heatmap Analysis
nodes.rationale: Pairwise top-k index overlap across layers reveals distinct clusters with high mutual overlap. Visualizes redundancy structure enabling cross-layer index reuse.

nodes.label: Indexer Redundancy Across Layers
nodes.rationale: Empirical observation: adjacent DSA layers share 70-100% of selected tokens. Heatmap analysis reveals distinct layer clusters with high mutual overlap, indicating most indexer computations are redundant.

nodes.label: Indexer Time Proportion Analysis
nodes.rationale: Profiling shows indexer share of total latency rises sharply with context length (27% at 10K, 81% at 200K prefill). Identifies indexer cost reduction as key to accelerating long-context DSA.

nodes.label: Layer Importance Ordering
nodes.rationale: Greedy search reveals natural ordering of indexer importance: early layers are 'easy' to remove, while later layers are 'critical'. Suggests intrinsic model property rather than data artifact.

nodes.label: Multi-Layer Distillation Loss
nodes.rationale: Training objective that distills each retained indexer against averaged attention distributions of all layers it serves. Mathematically equivalent to distilling against centroid of target distributions.

nodes.label: Training-Aware IndexCache
nodes.rationale: Optimizes model parameters for cross-layer sharing via multi-layer distillation loss. Enables simple uniform patterns to match full-indexer accuracy through joint adaptation.

nodes.label: Training-Free IndexCache
nodes.rationale: Applies to off-the-shelf DSA models without weight updates. Greedy search determines optimal layer pattern by minimizing LM loss on calibration set.

nodes.label: DA Accuracy Metric
nodes.rationale: LLM-judge-based scoring using Gemini-3-Flash to generate strict acceptance rubrics and Qwen-3.5-4B as judge, achieving Pearson r=0.99 with Gemini-3.1-Pro.

nodes.label: DA Attended Tokens Metric
nodes.rationale: Total KV positions attended during decoding, summed over all decode steps and averaged per response, compared as percent reduction relative to vanilla baseline.

nodes.label: DA Context-Length Scaling
nodes.rationale: DA's relative accuracy holds within ~1pp of vanilla up to 32K tokens then declines modestly; absolute token savings grow sharply with context (1M at short context to 21M at longest), scaling with raw context length.

nodes.label: DA Benchmark Suite
nodes.rationale: 15 long-context sources spanning single-span retrieval/reasoning and multi-span reasoning tasks from RULER, LongBench v1/v2, LooGLE, and ZeroScrolls, with contexts from 6.4K to 1M tokens.

nodes.label: Global Attention Dominance in Decode
nodes.rationale: Global attention KV reads dominate decode time (73% on Gemma, 86% on Qwen) in optimized large-batch deployments, making DA's per-step masking savings significant and context-length dependent.

nodes.label: DA Model Capability Scaling
nodes.rationale: DA's relative accuracy improves consistently with model size (29% at Gemma-4-E4B to 99% at Gemma-4-31B), narrowing gap to vanilla; token savings roughly scale-independent at ~50% on five of six models.

nodes.label: DA Roofline Wall-Time Analysis
nodes.rationale: Theoretical framework charging each operation at its hardware ceiling (MFU for compute-bound matmuls, MBU for memory-bound reads) to estimate decode wall-clock time savings in optimized large-batch deployments.

nodes.label: Post-RCP Confirmation Bias
nodes.rationale: Phenomenon where models overwhelmingly adopt injected intermediate answers rather than recovering correct original answers; demonstrates post-RCP generation rationalizes rather than re-verifies.

nodes.label: LLM Overthinking Phenomenon
nodes.rationale: Non-monotonic scaling behavior where excessive reasoning leads to diminishing returns or performance degradation; motivates need for understanding reasoning dynamics.

nodes.label: Reasoning Completion Point (RCP)
nodes.rationale: Instance-specific boundary separating active reasoning from converged reasoning; defined as earliest step where both content stabilization and semantic convergence are achieved.

nodes.label: Reasoning Completion Point Detector (RCPD)
nodes.rationale: Inference-time early-exit method detecting RCP by monitoring rank dynamics of termination tokens (</think>); enables 44% token reduction while preserving accuracy.

nodes.label: Reasoning Length Dynamics
nodes.rationale: Analysis revealing compensatory tradeoff between thinking and content length; shows thinking-content compensation followed by saturation where further thinking becomes redundant.

nodes.label: Semantic Convergence Phase
nodes.rationale: Late reasoning phase where semantics converge toward stable neighborhood with repetitive oscillations; induced content distribution approaches terminal state.

nodes.label: Reasoning Semantic Dynamics
nodes.rationale: Analysis of high-dimensional semantic trajectory evolution; identifies semantic path convergence from active exploration to stable neighborhood with repetitive oscillations.

nodes.label: Semantic Exploration Phase
nodes.rationale: Initial reasoning phase where semantic representations undergo rapid shifts indicating active exploration of solution paths; exhibits high instability in induced content distribution.

nodes.label: Stepwise Truncation Protocol
nodes.rationale: Experimental methodology forcing model to stop thinking at controlled steps and immediately generate content; enables granular analysis of reasoning process evolution.

nodes.label: Thinking-Content Compensation
nodes.rationale: Phenomenon where shorter thinking forces model to offload reasoning into content to maintain performance; results in increased content length in early reasoning stages.

nodes.label: Thinking Redundancy Phase
nodes.rationale: Late-stage reasoning where content retracts to conciseness and accuracy stabilizes; further thinking expands without altering content, manifesting as pure redundancy.

nodes.label: Finding 4: Data Quality Trumps Volume
nodes.rationale: Pruning ~50% of SFT candidates improved six-benchmark mean from 67.78 to 68.83; gains concentrated in reasoning (BBH +10.10)

nodes.label: Supervised Fine-Tuning Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Multi-stage data curation combining rule-based filtering and model-based quality scoring; 4.92M examples organized into general and agentic data

nodes.label: Synthesis vs Selection Paradigm
nodes.rationale: Conceptual shift from treating LLM outputs as competitors (selection/Best-of-N) to collaborators (synthesis/FusioN), enabling integration of complementary strengths.

nodes.label: FusioN Ablation Studies
nodes.rationale: Systematic ablations on fusor size, pool composition, teacher diversity, and contribution analysis.

nodes.label: FusioN Exceeds Oracle Performance
nodes.rationale: Surprising result that synthesized outputs outperform best individual sample in translation tasks, proving synthesis can exceed selection upper bound.

nodes.label: Fusor Model Size Threshold for FusioN
nodes.norm_label: fusor model size threshold for fusion
nodes.rationale: FusioN requires larger fusor models (27B+) to work effectively out-of-box, with continuous improvements up to 111B.

nodes.label: FusioN Synthesis Prompt
nodes.rationale: Simple in-context learning approach using LLM judge to synthesize multiple candidates without specialized training, enabling flexible customization.

nodes.label: Mode Collapse in Aligned LLMs
nodes.rationale: Phenomenon where probability mass concentrates toward typical completions favored by reference policy when rewards are flat

nodes.label: Theorem D.1: Instance Prompts Mode Collapse
nodes.norm_label: theorem d.1: instance prompts mode collapse

nodes.label: Typicality Bias in RLHF
nodes.rationale: Cognitive tendency of human annotators to prefer conventional responses, causing mode collapse in aligned LLMs through preference data

nodes.label: RL Training Loop in SocioHack
