nodes.rationale: Iterative optimization where policy generates strategy rollouts, simulator evaluates against current patch set, successful exploits converted to patches, and patch set injected into next iteration.

nodes.label: Societal Simulator
nodes.rationale: LLM-based simulator that parses free-form strategies into executable actions, constructs state variables via environment dynamics, and scores outcomes against rubric for reproducible evaluation.

nodes.label: Airline Ticket Pricing Case Study
nodes.rationale: RL threads multiple structurally independent exploits (hidden city, hub routing, fuel surcharge auditing) into coherent strategy; ITERPROMPT stays on single exploit family; EVOPROMPT adds fabricated mechanisms.

nodes.label: Dr. GRPO Optimization
nodes.rationale: Bias-free variant of GRPO used for policy optimization with quantile-based reward shaping and eligibility scoring based on patch compliance and outcome improvement.

nodes.label: Ten Exploitation Categories
nodes.rationale: Post-hoc taxonomy of discovered strategies: threshold evasion, procedural bypass, classification manipulation, information asymmetry, temporal windows, entity restructuring, technical circumvention, jurisdictional arbitrage, bundling/unbundling, definitional ambiguity.

nodes.label: Hatch-Waxman Regulatory Timeline
nodes.rationale: RL mines patches in real enacted order (2003 MMA, 2013 Actavis) then extends into proposed but unenacted reforms, demonstrating temporal alignment with actual regulatory evolution.

nodes.label: Historical Loophole Rediscovery
nodes.rationale: RL achieves 61.25% recall and 90.85% precision in rediscovering historically patched loopholes without explicit instructions, outperforming non-parametric baselines.

nodes.label: Patch Pressure Dynamics
nodes.rationale: Constraint accumulation removes shallow exploit families, redirecting search toward more subtle procedurally-structured loopholes; later low-scoring outputs preserve exploit mechanisms under more compliant surface forms.

nodes.label: LLM Safeguards Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Input-side refusal depends on explicit harmful framing rather than exploitative intent; output-side governance and training-time regularization remove only shallow exploits, leaving underlying mechanisms intact.

nodes.label: Societal Hacking Phenomenon
nodes.rationale: Failure mode where RL-trained LLMs discover loopholes in societal regulations by remaining formally compliant while defeating intended purpose; emerges from reward optimization in institutional rule systems.

nodes.label: SocioHack Benchmark
nodes.rationale: 72-environment sandbox comprising Historical (32 real regulations with patched loopholes), Synthetic (20 planted loopholes), and Fictional (20 rewritten scenarios) subsets for studying regulatory loophole discovery.

nodes.label: Data Darwinism Hierarchy: L0-L5 Implementation
nodes.rationale: L0: Data Acquisition; L1: Format Normalization; L2: Rule-based Filtering; L3: Lightweight Model Filtering; L4: Generative Refinement (noise removal, fragmentation repair); L5: Cognitive Completion (reasoning reconstruction, terminological explication, pedagogical bridging)

nodes.label: Abacus Embeddings
nodes.rationale: Learned positional embeddings encoding digit position relative to number start; enables transformers to track exact digit positions in long sequences.

nodes.label: Array Sorting Task
nodes.rationale: Evaluates generalization on variable-length arrays with multiple numbers; tests both number length and array length extrapolation

nodes.label: FIRE Embeddings
nodes.rationale: Additive embeddings in attention mechanism used as baseline for comparison; Abacus Embeddings combined with FIRE show improved performance

nodes.label: Input Injection
nodes.rationale: Skip-connections propagating input copy to each layer; improves performance but removed for multiplication models

nodes.label: Least Significant Digit First Format
nodes.rationale: Data format where least significant digit appears first (e.g., 98282 + 3859172 = 2787472); enables left-to-right processing of carry operations.

nodes.label: Looped Transformer (Recurrent Layers)
nodes.rationale: Transformer block applied recurrently to its own output; enables iterative algorithm execution and achieves near-perfect generalization on addition.

nodes.label: Multi-Digit Addition Task
nodes.rationale: Core benchmark task demonstrating that transformers struggle with positional information representation; Abacus Embeddings achieve 97.9% accuracy on size 20 training data with 6× length generalization

nodes.label: Integer Multiplication Task
nodes.rationale: More challenging task than addition with longer-distance dependencies; output length scales as sum of operand lengths

nodes.label: Progressive Loss Computation
nodes.rationale: Training technique combining loss from nominal recurrences with random smaller number of recurrences; improves generalization to harder tasks

nodes.label: Recurrent Transformer Architecture
nodes.rationale: Weight-tied decoder layers with input injection and progressive loss that improve multi-digit arithmetic by allowing variable recurrences during training

nodes.label: Rotary Embeddings (RoPE)
nodes.rationale: Relative positional embeddings used in state-of-the-art models; weak for length generalization but compatible with Abacus Embeddings

nodes.label: Teacher Fixing
nodes.rationale: Fixing the teacher model leads to greater performance gains in reasoning tasks

nodes.label: Accessibility Tree Representation for GUI
nodes.rationale: GUI observations represented as accessibility trees and UI view hierarchies rather than pixel frames; enables text-based world modeling for Android, Web, OS domains.

nodes.label: Kauffman's Adjacent Possible in Scientific Discovery
nodes.norm_label: kauffman's adjacent possible in scientific discovery
nodes.rationale: Framework distinguishing AI capability (exploring adjacent possible at scale) from human scientific vocation (creating new possibility spaces, reframing problems conceptually).

nodes.label: AI Scientists as Epistemic Actors
nodes.rationale: Central thesis: multi-agent AI systems can expand hypothesis-generating and verification capacity of science; qualitative rather than incremental transition from passive tools to active epistemic participants.

nodes.label: Denario: Multi-Agent Framework for Scientific Discovery
nodes.norm_label: denario: multi-agent framework for scientific discovery
nodes.rationale: Prototype multi-agent system integrating literature exploration, code generation, dataset analysis, and iterative hypothesis testing; demonstrates AI systems can search model spaces faster than humans.

nodes.label: Enduring Role of Human Scientists
nodes.rationale: Humans excel at paradigm shifts, conceptual reframing, recognizing meaningful questions; AI excels at exploring adjacent possible; collaboration preserves human capacities on which scientific value depends.

nodes.label: Language World Model (LWM) Concept
nodes.rationale: Conditional text generator predicting next environment observation given interaction history and agent action; enables both environment simulation and agent foundation model training.

nodes.label: Multi-Agent AI Systems for Scientific Discovery
nodes.norm_label: multi-agent ai systems for scientific discovery
nodes.rationale: Coordinated systems of specialized agents (generation, critic, verification, controller) enabling internal dialectic; traverse model spaces beyond human reach at machine speed.

nodes.label: Stateless vs Stateful Environment Distinction
nodes.rationale: Stateless environments (Search) carry state implicitly in conversation history; stateful environments (Terminal, OS) maintain explicit internal state; LWM operates uniformly over both.

nodes.label: Unified Environment Trajectory Schema
nodes.rationale: Shared format across 7 domains comprising system prompt (task description, action space, initial state, demonstrations, simulation instruction) and alternating (action, observation) turns; enables cross-domain training.

nodes.label: AUTOSCIENTISTS BioML-Bench Results
nodes.rationale: Mean leaderboard percentile 74.40% (SE 6.20%), outperforming Autoresearch (66.07%) by +8.33 points; completes all 24 tasks

nodes.label: Biomni Baseline System
nodes.rationale: Reference baseline; reference [10]

nodes.label: Active Memory Reconstruction Paradigm
nodes.rationale: Transforms memory access from one-shot retrieval into active multi-step reconstruction process that progressively reveals information; integrates LLM reasoning directly into memory access for dynamic strategy adaptation.

nodes.label: CRAFTBENCH Benchmark
nodes.rationale: 279-sample benchmark spanning three figure types (academic, poster, infographic) and four input conditions (text-to-image, mask-completion, key-element composition, sketch-conditioned) with human quality annotation and VLM-based evaluation.

nodes.label: CRAFTEDITOR System
nodes.rationale: Applies same harness pattern to convert raster figures into editable SVGs through extraction, processing, and composition phases with hybrid critic combining VLM and programmatic checkers.

nodes.label: CRAFTER System
nodes.rationale: Core contribution: a multi-agent harness for scientific figure generation combining intent reasoner, plan generator, critic, specification refiner, and convergence judge with shared evolving specification as memory.

nodes.label: Cue–Tag–Content Memory Graph
nodes.rationale: Heterogeneous graph where cues are fine-grained keywords, contents store memory items, and tags encode associative relations; enables two-stage retrieval where LLM first selects tags then retrieves content.

nodes.label: Diversity-Driven Plan Exploration
nodes.rationale: Mechanism treating inter-sample variance as search problem: designer proposes K intent-conditioned candidate plans with distinct visual framings, executor renders all in parallel, convergence judge selects best as starting point for refinement.

nodes.label: Harness Abstraction Pattern
nodes.rationale: Orchestration layer wrapping executor with planning, verification, and structured revision over evolving specification; enables targeted correction without modifying executor itself.

nodes.label: MRAgent System
nodes.rationale: Memory Reasoning Architecture for LLM Agents: performs active and associative memory reconstruction by exploring multiple candidate retrieval paths, pruning irrelevant branches based on intermediate evidence.

nodes.label: Multi-Granular Memory Layers
nodes.rationale: Episodic layer stores event-specific information; semantic layer captures stable knowledge; abstraction layer summarizes recurring patterns; enables flexible combination of evidence at different granularities.

nodes.label: Structured Corrective Layer
nodes.rationale: Replaces free-text revision with typed edits on shared specification; prevents prompt contradictions that plague iterative repair by maintaining internally consistent record across rounds.

nodes.label: Verify-Then-Refine Loop with Directive Critic
nodes.rationale: Directive critic emits per-dimension scores and identified defects rather than scalar scores; verify-then-refine loop applies corrections iteratively with best-so-far checkpoint guarding against non-monotonic regressions.

nodes.label: Automation of Routine Tasks
nodes.rationale: System automates literature search, code writing, plotting, and manuscript generation

nodes.label: Rapid Exploration Capability
nodes.rationale: System enables quick testing of multiple research directions and hypotheses

nodes.label: Interdisciplinary Research Capability
nodes.rationale: System can combine methods and concepts from different scientific fields

nodes.label: Speed Advantage
nodes.rationale: System generates complete analysis pipelines and papers in hours rather than weeks or months

nodes.label: AG2 Agent Framework
nodes.rationale: Open-source AgentOS supporting advanced agentic AI applications with conversation programming

nodes.label: Methodology Development Module
nodes.rationale: Develops detailed research plans and methodologies to execute project ideas

nodes.label: Ethical Considerations
nodes.rationale: Questions about validation standards, authorship, and appropriate use of AI in science

nodes.label: Context Overflow Failure Mode
nodes.rationale: System processes trajectory files within context instead of computationally analyzing them

nodes.label: Hallucination Failure Mode
nodes.rationale: System generates plausible-sounding but incorrect or fabricated content without proper implementation

nodes.label: LaTeX Rendering Failure Mode
nodes.rationale: System generates LaTeX errors in mathematical expressions or image insertion

nodes.label: Missing Libraries Failure Mode
nodes.rationale: System cannot find or install critical libraries required for analysis

nodes.label: Graphical User Interface
nodes.rationale: Web-based interface for running Denario locally or through cloud deployment

nodes.label: Human-in-the-Loop Approach
nodes.rationale: Iterative refinement of prompts and results through human feedback and guidance

nodes.label: Input Text Specification
nodes.rationale: Detailed description of data, problem, and research context provided by user

nodes.label: LangGraph Orchestration Framework
nodes.rationale: Python framework for orchestrating agents through directed graphs with dynamic flow control

nodes.label: Citation Quality Issues
nodes.rationale: System may cite tangentially relevant papers or miss key references in specific fields

nodes.label: Depth vs Breadth Trade-off
nodes.rationale: AI systems explore wide range of possibilities superficially while humans go deeper into promising directions

nodes.label: Limited Domain Knowledge
nodes.rationale: System lacks deep contextual understanding of specific research fields and their literature

nodes.label: Limited Novel Insight Generation
nodes.rationale: System struggles to generate truly novel hypotheses or recognize subtle patterns without human guidance

nodes.label: Philosophy of Science Implications
nodes.rationale: Considerations about how AI-generated research fits within scientific methodology and epistemology

nodes.label: Python API Interface
nodes.rationale: Programmatic interface for running Denario modules in scripts or notebooks

nodes.label: Research Assistant Role
nodes.rationale: System designed to accelerate discovery by assisting researchers rather than replacing them

nodes.label: AI-Native Research Paradigm
nodes.rationale: Research increasingly conducted through collaboration between researcher and general-purpose coding agent across full lifecycle. Process born digital and textual, enabling comprehensive research-process capture at negligible marginal cost.

nodes.label: Closure Signals
nodes.rationale: Indicators that observation has been treated as settled: topic abandonment, explicit researcher affirmation, empirical resolution of linked experiments, or artifact-level commitment.

nodes.label: Context Harvester
nodes.rationale: Scans session record (conversational history, tool outputs, experiment results, code diffs) to extract research-significant events: actions AI agent performed and directions researcher expressed or confirmed.

nodes.label: Design Principle P1: Silent, Framework-Independent Integration
nodes.norm_label: design principle p1: silent, framework-independent integration
nodes.rationale: Live Research Manager is natural-language specification loadable by any coding agent, requiring no custom SDKs. Runs as background process collecting traces without researcher intervention.

nodes.label: Design Principle P2: Faithful Epistemic Provenance
nodes.norm_label: design principle p2: faithful epistemic provenance
nodes.rationale: Every event tagged with provenance (user, ai-suggested, ai-executed, user-revised). Raw observations staged rather than forced into categories, maturing progressively as evidence accumulates.

nodes.label: Design Principle P3: Comprehensive Trajectory Capture
nodes.norm_label: design principle p3: comprehensive trajectory capture
nodes.rationale: Full branching research process including dead ends and pivots recorded with cross-layer bindings. Version-controlled so each milestone produces navigable snapshot; retroactive revisions are first-class operations.

nodes.label: Event Router
nodes.rationale: Classifies extracted events into seven types (decision, experiment, dead_end, pivot, claim, heuristic, observation), tags with provenance (user, ai-suggested, ai-executed, user-revised), and routes to appropriate ARA layer.

nodes.label: Seven Research Event Types
nodes.rationale: Decision, experiment, dead_end, pivot, claim, heuristic, observation. Each carries structured payload enabling machine-executable research record.

nodes.label: Live Research Manager
nodes.rationale: Background system that distills researcher-agent conversations into typed events accumulating across ARA layers. Three-stage pipeline: Context Harvester → Event Router → Maturity Tracker. Enables zero-documentation-overhead artifact population.

nodes.label: Maturity Tracker
nodes.rationale: Reviews staging area and promotes observations with sufficient evidence into formal entries. Crystallizes at two timescales: continuously appends trace events; periodically crystallizes into structured layers when closure signals indicate settlement.

nodes.label: Progressive Crystallization
nodes.rationale: Two-timescale artifact construction: continuously appends trace events at session boundaries; periodically crystallizes observations into structured layers when closure signals indicate settlement.

nodes.label: ARA Compiler
nodes.rationale: Agent skill that translates legacy research sources (PDFs, code repos, datasets, rubrics, trajectory logs) into complete ARAs. Performs forensic reconstruction to recover cross-layer lineage from implicit sources.

nodes.label: Code-Paper Reconciliation
nodes.rationale: Cross-referencing codebase against claims to surface tacit knowledge: implicit assumptions, undocumented tricks, extra parameters. Written back to /logic as provenance-tagged heuristics.

nodes.label: Cognitive Mapping
nodes.rationale: Second stage: populates /logic with motivation chain, falsifiable claims with proof pointers, formal concepts, and solution structure, with every claim linked to verifying experiment.

nodes.label: Collective Inference
nodes.rationale: When library of previously compiled ARAs available, Compiler retrieves heuristics and configurations from same-domain artifacts, flags common patterns current paper omits, adds as candidate heuristics tagged collective_inference.

nodes.label: Exploration Graph Extraction
nodes.rationale: Fourth stage: reconstructs research DAG as nested YAML tree with dead-end leaf nodes documenting hypothesis, failure mode, and lesson.

nodes.label: Forensic Reconstruction
nodes.rationale: Process of recovering cross-layer forensic bindings connecting claims to experiments, experiments to evidence, and evidence to code from sources where lineage exists only implicitly.

nodes.label: High-Fidelity Preservation Principle
nodes.rationale: Every numerical result, hyperparameter, architectural detail, and negative finding in sources must appear somewhere in artifact. Missing PDF-accessible information constitutes compilation failure.

nodes.label: Knowledge Lineage Principle
nodes.rationale: Compiler performs forensic reconstruction recovering cross-layer forensic bindings from sources where lineage exists only implicitly, enabling agents to trace claims downstream to code or upstream to hypotheses.

nodes.label: Physical Grounding
nodes.rationale: Third stage: generates /src with annotated configurations, typed code stubs, and environment manifest. When code repository available, performs code-paper reconciliation to surface tacit knowledge.

nodes.label: Semantic Deconstruction
nodes.rationale: First stage of top-down ARA generation: strips narrative framing to expose raw research content (formulations, configurations, results, dependencies, failed approaches) in fact-dense telegraphic form.

nodes.label: Universal Input, Canonical Output Principle
nodes.rationale: ARA Compiler is many-to-one: accepts any combination of PDFs, code repos, datasets, rubrics, trajectory logs; always produces single ARA conforming to protocol. Degradation graceful.

nodes.label: B-cos Networks (Inherently Interpretable)
nodes.rationale: Baseline for comparison; DAVE improves upon inherent B-cos explanations by producing sharper, more object-aligned attributions.

nodes.label: Low-Pass Filtering via Stochastic Averaging
nodes.rationale: Applies Gaussian smoothing to equivariant effective transformation to attenuate high-frequency artifacts while preserving stable attribution signals, equivalent to convolution with smoothing kernel.

nodes.label: GridPG (Grid Pointing Game) Localization Metric
nodes.rationale: Evaluation metric measuring whether maximally attributed location falls inside ground-truth object region; DAVE achieves 60.19% on ViT-B/16, improving over baselines.

nodes.label: Autoresearch Baseline System
nodes.rationale: Single-agent baseline adapted to BioML-Bench with same coding-agent backend; reference [3]

nodes.label: Compile Autotuning Discovery
nodes.rationale: One of seven heterogeneous improvements discovered in GPT nanochat from-champion regime

nodes.label: EXPLORED.md Dead-End Registry
nodes.rationale: Negative-knowledge file listing previously dead-ended research directions; shared between systems in from-champion regime

nodes.label: GPT Nanochat From-Baseline Results
nodes.rationale: AUTOSCIENTISTS reaches val_bpb ≈ 0.978 in 34 experiments vs. Autoresearch in 65 experiments; 1.9× speedup; parallelism across three teams (architecture, schedule, optimizer)

nodes.label: GPT Nanochat From-Champion Results
nodes.rationale: AUTOSCIENTISTS accepts 7 improvements over 93 experiments (val_bpb = 0.9730); Autoresearch accepts 0 over 100; improvements span heterogeneous directions not explored by single-agent

nodes.label: Final-Learning-Rate Fraction Discovery
nodes.rationale: One of seven heterogeneous improvements discovered in GPT nanochat from-champion regime

nodes.label: Matrix Initialization Discovery
nodes.rationale: One of seven heterogeneous improvements discovered in GPT nanochat from-champion regime

nodes.label: Noise-Floor Recalibration Discovery
nodes.rationale: One of seven heterogeneous improvements discovered in GPT nanochat from-champion regime

nodes.label: Query-Key Normalization Order Discovery
nodes.rationale: First improvement discovered by AUTOSCIENTISTS in from-champion regime; never proposed by single-agent Autoresearch in 100 attempts

nodes.label: Softcap Value Discovery
nodes.rationale: One of seven heterogeneous improvements discovered in GPT nanochat from-champion regime

nodes.label: Value-Embedding Gate Width Discovery
nodes.rationale: One of seven heterogeneous improvements discovered in GPT nanochat from-champion regime

nodes.label: Ranked Region List Task
nodes.rationale: Formulation of repository exploration as returning ranked list of relevant code regions under fixed line budget; enables comparison of retrievers, search agents, and long-context selectors on common axis.

nodes.label: Restricted-Context Validation Protocol
nodes.rationale: Controlled downstream protocol feeding each explorer's output as only available context to fixed coding agent; verifies that exploration metrics track repair success without requiring explorer to write patches.

nodes.label: Trajectory-Grounded Supervision
nodes.rationale: Novel annotation method deriving ground truth lines from successful agent trajectories; distills specific code regions solution paths actually consulted with minimal manual annotation.

nodes.label: Discretization Hypothesis
nodes.rationale: Practical neural networks understood as noisy finite approximations to infinite-size models; finite-size corrections worsen performance while saving costs

nodes.label: Hyperparameter Disentanglement
nodes.rationale: Techniques like μP and width-scaling separate hyperparameter effects from core dynamics; enables simpler effective systems and transfer across scales

nodes.label: Guided vs Random Experimentation Ablation
nodes.rationale: Isolates experimental design capability; Claude Opus 4.7 shows monotonic improvement with guided experiments, GPT-5.5 plateaus after round 4.

nodes.label: Latent Structure Discovery
nodes.rationale: Strongest models fail on worlds requiring uncovering hidden particle species, dark matter, extra dimensions; indicates systematic limitation in hypothesis revision.

nodes.label: Noise Robustness Analysis
nodes.rationale: Claude Opus 4.7 retains high explanation scores at 50% noise on Ether world by designing noise-mitigating experiments; GPT-5.5 degrades faster.

nodes.label: Hierarchy Preservation
nodes.rationale: Constructs section tree representing hierarchical structure of literature to support LLM reasoning and structured text parsing; removes redundant nodes.

nodes.label: IntraBench Benchmark
nodes.rationale: 315 test instances from five STEM domains (physics, earth science, public health, engineering, material science) with expert-authored questions paired with literature.

nodes.label: IntraView Task: Information Retrieval from Literature
nodes.norm_label: intraview task: information retrieval from literature
nodes.rationale: Novel task requiring faithful extraction of information from provided research papers in response to domain-specific queries, with explicit hallucination avoidance.

nodes.label: Iterative Reading Stage
nodes.rationale: Sequential section access, detail extraction, and sufficiency checking to accumulate information until query is adequately answered; mitigates hallucination through explicit reasoning.

nodes.label: Section Ranking Stage
nodes.rationale: Structure-aware reasoning to prioritize relevant literature sections through heading parsing, hierarchy preservation, and reasoning-based ranking—contrasts with flat semantic-similarity RAG.

nodes.label: Information Sufficiency Check
nodes.rationale: LLM-based reasoning to determine whether gathered details are sufficient to answer query; governs iteration loop and explicitly prevents hallucination through anti-speculation instructions.

nodes.label: CAA (Contrastive Activation Addition)
nodes.rationale: State control using paired contrastive examples to compute steering vectors. Adds vectors to hidden states to shift representations toward or away from targeted behavior.

nodes.label: Composite Steering
nodes.rationale: Composition of multiple steering methods from different control surfaces. Enables study of complementary vs. conflicting interactions and composition order effects.

nodes.label: ControlSpec Abstraction
nodes.rationale: Enables parameter sweeping for steering methods. Supports Cartesian grids and functional relationships for exploring control parameter space.

nodes.label: DeAL (Decoding-time Alignment)
nodes.rationale: Output control implementing reward-guided search during decoding. Enables composition with state controls for improved truthfulness-informativeness tradeoffs.

nodes.label: ITI (Inference-Time Intervention)
nodes.rationale: State control using probe-based head selection. Trains per-head probes across all layer-head pairs and steers selected heads to elicit truthful answers.

nodes.label: PASTA (Post-hoc Attention Steering)
nodes.rationale: State-based control that selectively rescales attention scores at attention heads. Downweights tokens outside input spans to steer model focus toward emphasized tokens.

nodes.label: State Control Abstractions
nodes.rationale: Reusable patterns for activation steering: estimator (learns steering artifact), selector (chooses control site), transform (applies modification), gate (per-step decision). Enables systematic composition of steering methods.

nodes.label: Steering Pipeline Abstraction
nodes.rationale: Unified interface for composing multiple steering methods across different control surfaces. Enables systematic study of steering interactions and trade-offs.

nodes.label: UseCase and Benchmark Classes
nodes.rationale: Framework for defining tasks and systematically comparing steering pipelines. Enables fixed and variable control parameter evaluation with custom metrics.

nodes.label: Adversarial Agent Co-Evolution
nodes.rationale: Agents co-evolve through opposing objectives; one agent's progress raises difficulty for opponent; includes pairwise (GAN-like) and multi-source pressure

nodes.label: Co-Evolution in Agentic Systems
nodes.rationale: Central organizing principle: multiple components impose evolutionary pressure on one another, distinguishing mutual adaptation from mere interaction or information exchange

nodes.label: Collaborative Agent Co-Evolution
nodes.rationale: Agents co-evolve through shared goals; one agent's improvement forces partners to adjust coordination; includes parallel and role-differentiated collaboration

nodes.label: Evolving Agent Organizations
nodes.rationale: Agents co-evolve with organizational structure including role assignments and interaction topology

nodes.label: Feedback-Space Co-Evolution
nodes.rationale: Environment co-evolves in how it evaluates/rewards agent behavior; includes preference-driven, outcome-driven, and consistency-augmented feedback

nodes.label: Interaction-Space Co-Evolution
nodes.rationale: Environment adapts where agent acts; includes executable world construction and model-based world construction

nodes.label: Red Queen Effect
nodes.rationale: Biological principle: sustained progress requires mutual adaptation rather than adaptation on only one side; motivates co-evolution over single-entity self-evolution

nodes.label: Agent–Agent Co-Evolution
nodes.rationale: First stage: co-evolution within agent collective where each agent's improvement is driven by other evolving agents; includes adversarial, collaborative, and organizational adaptation

nodes.label: Agent–Environment Co-Evolution
nodes.rationale: Second stage: extends adaptation to environmental components (tasks, feedback, interaction spaces); agents reshape environment which then reshapes agents

nodes.label: Task-Space Co-Evolution
nodes.rationale: Environment adapts what problem agent solves next; includes exposure/selection from fixed pool and adaptive task generation

nodes.label: Assumption 1: HGM-Compatible Fixed-Criterion Search
nodes.rationale: Foundational assumption for RQGM theory: fixed evaluator, time-homogeneous outcomes, external oracles, and fixed budget accounting enable HGM guarantees within epochs.

nodes.label: Clade Metaproductivity (CMP)
nodes.rationale: Search utility scoring nodes by success rate pooled over their clade (subtree of descendants) rather than individual performance, capturing long-run self-improvement value beyond immediate benchmark scores.

nodes.label: Gödel Machine
nodes.rationale: Theoretical self-improving system that modifies itself whenever it can prove changes beneficial; RQGM makes this empirical through archive search with co-evolved evaluators.

nodes.label: Huxley-Gödel Machine (HGM)
nodes.rationale: Prior self-improvement framework using archive search guided by clade metaproductivity; RQGM extends HGM to support non-stationary utilities while preserving its per-epoch convergence guarantees.

nodes.label: Limitation: Epoch-Local Guarantees
nodes.rationale: Acknowledged limitation: theoretical guarantees are epoch-local, covering improvement only within epochs, not across epoch boundaries.

nodes.label: Proposition 1: Working-Posterior Consistency
nodes.rationale: Theoretical result showing pooled Beta accumulator converges to role-task balanced utility under balanced sampling, preserving HGM's flat success/failure interface for Thompson sampling.

nodes.label: Proposition 3: Epoch-Local Fixed-Criterion Validity
nodes.rationale: Core theoretical result establishing each epoch as fixed-criterion binary-outcome search problem, enabling direct application of HGM convergence guarantees within epochs.

nodes.label: Thompson Sampling
nodes.rationale: Exploration-exploitation strategy used to select nodes for expansion/evaluation by sampling from Beta posterior over clade metaproductivity, balancing discovery against exploitation.

nodes.label: Three-Level Sampling Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Hierarchical sampling selecting nodes by CMP, then roles by least-evaluated, then tasks by least-evaluated, ensuring balanced evaluation across roles and tasks within each node.

nodes.label: UCB-Air Expansion Gate
nodes.rationale: Mechanism controlling archive growth by deciding whether to expand or evaluate based on relationship between evaluation budget and archive size, preventing unbounded tree growth.

nodes.label: Constraint-Modified Problems
nodes.rationale: Non-standard modifications of original problems render straightforward lookup futile; maintains difficulty while preventing retrieval contamination.

nodes.label: Data Contamination Problem
nodes.rationale: Core benchmarking challenge: LLM cutoff insufficient; information distributed across Reddit, lectures, transcripts; requires restricting to novel problems or masking identifying information.

nodes.label: Ground Truth Problem for Novel Research
nodes.norm_label: ground truth problem for novel research
nodes.rationale: Dilemma: known problems enable verification but contaminate via retrieval; novel problems lack ground truth; solution: programmatically-generated problems hard to solve but easy to verify.

nodes.label: Multi-Turn Interaction Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Benchmarks should capture iterative scientific workflows: literature consultation, approach revision, colleague feedback; more realistic than single-shot question-answer.

nodes.label: Reasoning Process Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Evaluation dimension: validity of intermediate steps, not just final result; critical for scientific reasoning assessment.

nodes.label: Retrieval vs. Reasoning Distinction
nodes.rationale: Key challenge: well-designed systems should use retrieval when appropriate; benchmarks must distinguish genuine reasoning from retrieval and synthesis.

nodes.label: Scientific Multi-Agent AI System
nodes.rationale: Integrates LLMs with external tools, simulation capabilities, and iterative reasoning for physics research assistance; architecture includes data, orchestration, interaction, and validation layers.

nodes.label: Tool Selection Capability
nodes.rationale: Evaluation dimension for multi-agent systems: ability to choose appropriate tools for given problems.

nodes.label: Uncertainty Calibration
nodes.rationale: Evaluation dimension: does system know when it does not know? Critical for high-stakes scientific applications.

nodes.label: Curriculum-Like Effect
nodes.rationale: Progressively stricter evaluators across epochs impose curriculum on task agents, with each replacement re-ranking archive and advancing population around resilient backbone lineages.

nodes.label: Darwin-Gödel Machine (DGM)
nodes.rationale: Prior empirical self-improvement system ranking self-modifying coding agents by benchmark utility; baseline for comparison in coding domain.

nodes.label: Data Isolation
nodes.rationale: Separation of training data (shown to meta-agent for guidance) from validation data (used for search utility), preventing overfitting and ensuring generalization.

nodes.label: Evaluator-Dependent Roles
nodes.rationale: Task roles (e.g., paper writing, proof writing) lacking ground-truth signals, requiring learned evaluators scored against held-out ground-truth anchors for replacement decisions.

nodes.label: Evaluator-Independent Roles
nodes.rationale: Task roles with fixed benchmarks (e.g., coding with executable tests), providing objective evaluation signals independent of learned evaluators.

nodes.label: Figure 3: Evaluator Replacements Re-Rank Archive
nodes.rationale: Empirical evidence that evaluator replacements substantially and permanently re-rank archive, with Spearman ρ settling well below 1, showing curriculum effect.

nodes.label: Figure 4: Backbone Lineage Preservation
nodes.rationale: Empirical evidence that best lineage survives evaluator replacements intact while remainder is re-ranked, showing curriculum advances around stable backbone.

nodes.label: HyperAgents
nodes.rationale: Self-improvement system introducing metacognitive workspaces where each archive node contains multiple role agents plus a meta-agent that edits code; RQGM builds on this multi-agent workspace architecture.

nodes.label: Multi-Agent Workspace
nodes.rationale: Each archive node contains K role agents (task agents and evaluators) plus a meta-agent, enabling co-evolution where shared code expansions improve multiple utilities simultaneously.

nodes.label: RQ3: Evaluator Replacements as Curriculum
nodes.rationale: Research question examining whether evaluator replacements drive curriculum-like search by re-ranking archive while preserving backbone lineages.

nodes.label: Dynamic Difficulty Families
nodes.rationale: Designs problem families with difficulty parameters to obtain scaling curves revealing performance degradation points

nodes.label: Future Research Directions Extraction
nodes.rationale: Feasibility study demonstrating extraction of 414 future directions from 300 papers using LLM-based pipeline

nodes.label: Self-Consistency Tests
nodes.rationale: Tests internal consistency of outputs without ground truth by solving problems using different approaches

nodes.label: System Evaluation Protocol
nodes.rationale: Multi-faced evaluation approach including ablation studies, tool-use analysis, process-level evaluation, and scaling curves

nodes.label: Benchmark Design for Scientific AI Systems
nodes.norm_label: benchmark design for scientific ai systems
nodes.rationale: Unified framework for evaluating agentic scientific systems across multiple benchmark families and construction strategies

nodes.label: Accuracy Driven by Sensibility
nodes.rationale: Key finding: task accuracy correlates with sensibility (S∩C and S∩¬C cohorts) regardless of compliance; sensible/non-compliant often outperforms compliant/non-sensible.

nodes.label: Contrastive Activation Addition (CAA) Steering
nodes.rationale: Intervention technique to steer model compliance by applying steering vectors to specific layers; increases compliance up to 29% but reveals task-neglect side effects and accuracy trade-offs.

nodes.label: Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) Analysis
nodes.rationale: Representation similarity analysis across reasoning instructions; reveals instruction-dependent geometry differences vary by model family (LLaMA shows largest differences, Qwen shows transient dips).

nodes.label: P(True) Confidence Estimation
nodes.rationale: Method to measure model confidence by asking follow-up question about answer truth value; reveals subtle friction from reasoning conflicts even when not catastrophic.

nodes.label: Lexical Mirroring Phenomenon
nodes.rationale: Models incorporate key terminology from prompts (e.g., 'most probable', 'simplest hypothesis') to signal compliance while internally pivoting to different reasoning type; masks true reasoning process.

nodes.label: Linear Probing of Hidden States
nodes.rationale: Mechanistic analysis: trains linear probes on residual stream activations to predict instructed reasoning type, judge-inferred type, and compliance; shows instruction encoding is robust but compliance is weaker signal.

nodes.label: Sensibility vs Compliance Trade-off
nodes.rationale: Key tension: models achieve higher accuracy when reasoning is sensible (S∩C and S∩¬C) regardless of compliance; compliance correlates with internal confidence but not accuracy.

nodes.label: Data Contamination Risk in Benchmarks
nodes.rationale: Problem where models achieve high scores by retrieving memorized answers rather than genuine reasoning; motivates need for dynamic evaluation paradigms.

nodes.label: Numerical Evaluation Protocol
nodes.rationale: Strict 1% relative error tolerance for numerical answers; requires correct answers on all dynamic variants for credit; includes LaTeX-based evaluation function.

nodes.label: Memorization vs. Reasoning Detection
nodes.rationale: Dynamic evaluation paradigm designed to distinguish genuine physical reasoning from pattern memorization by testing robustness to numerical perturbations.

nodes.label: LLM Physics Reasoning Gap
nodes.rationale: Substantial performance gaps in physics reasoning even for state-of-the-art models; Gemini 2.5 Pro achieves only 43% on static problems with 22.5% average drop on dynamic variants.

nodes.label: Phy_A: Static Physics Problems
nodes.rationale: Fixed set of 400 graduate-level or Olympiad-level physics problems providing stable baseline for model performance evaluation.

nodes.label: Phy_B: Dynamic Physics Problems
nodes.rationale: 100 parameterized physics problems with automatic variation engine that alters numerical constants to test model generalization and prevent memorization.

nodes.label: PHYSICS Dataset: Large-Scale Physics Problems
nodes.rationale: Large-scale corpus of physics problems with training/test splits; related work on scale and trainability of physics reasoning evaluation.

nodes.label: UGPhysics: Undergraduate Physics Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Prior physics reasoning benchmark with university-level problems; ABench-Physics extends with higher difficulty and dynamic evaluation.

nodes.label: FFN-Deactivated Layer
nodes.rationale: Transformer layer with FFN completely removed, consisting only of self-attention mechanism; used to test whether FFN functionality can be redistributed to other layers.

nodes.label: FFN-Expanded Layer
nodes.rationale: Transformer layer with expanded intermediate representation dimension in FFN; used to concentrate FFN computational capacity in specific layers while maintaining total parameter count.

nodes.label: FineWeb-Edu Pretraining Dataset
nodes.rationale: Dataset used for pretraining baseline and experimental models in FFN importance study.

nodes.label: FFN Knowledge Storage Hypothesis
nodes.rationale: Hypothesis that FFNs primarily serve to store knowledge from training data, functioning similarly to key-value memory; motivates investigation of optimal FFN positioning.

nodes.label: Layer Placement Positions
nodes.rationale: Three positional configurations for FFN-expanded layers: first (near input), middle (center), and final (near output); enables investigation of position-dependent FFN importance.

nodes.label: LLaMA Transformer Architecture
nodes.rationale: De facto standard Transformer LM architecture with pre-LN, SwiGLU activation, and RoPE positional encoding; used as basis for FFN importance analysis.

nodes.label: Middle 70% Configuration
nodes.rationale: Optimal FFN configuration concentrating 70% of FFN parameters in consecutive middle layers; consistently outperforms baseline across model scales (285M-1.2B parameters).

nodes.label: Zero-Shot Relation Extraction (zsRE) Knowledge Assessment
nodes.rationale: Evaluation method using knowledge-based QA pairs to measure model's ability to retrieve factual information; assesses FFN knowledge storage capacity.

nodes.label: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) Prompting
nodes.rationale: Prompting technique enabling LLMs to show intermediate reasoning steps; used in GSM-Symbolic evaluation with 8-shot examples.

nodes.label: Chinese Room Argument
nodes.rationale: Philosophical argument distinguishing true comprehension from symbol manipulation; referenced to support distinction between genuine reasoning and pattern-matching in LLMs.

nodes.label: GSM-NoOp Dataset
nodes.rationale: Dataset variant adding seemingly relevant but ultimately inconsequential statements to questions, designed to test whether LLMs can discern relevant information for problem-solving.

nodes.label: GSM-Symbolic Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Symbolic template-based benchmark enabling generation of diverse question variants from GSM8K, allowing controllable evaluation of LLM mathematical reasoning across different instantiations and difficulty levels.

nodes.label: Pattern-Matching Hypothesis for LLMs
nodes.rationale: Hypothesis that LLMs perform probabilistic pattern-matching rather than formal logical reasoning, explaining sensitivity to input variations and inability to handle out-of-distribution information.

nodes.label: ARPL Loss
nodes.rationale: OSR-specific loss function by Chen et al. (2021) that can be enhanced with temperature scheduling for improved performance.

nodes.label: AUROC Metric
nodes.rationale: Area under receiver operating characteristic curve measuring known-unknown detection performance in OSR.

nodes.label: Cross-Entropy Loss
nodes.rationale: Standard classification loss where temperature parameter scales logits before softmax, controlling sharpness of probability distributions.

nodes.label: Familiarity Hypothesis
nodes.rationale: Hypothesis by Dietterich & Guyer (2022) that OSR methods detect novelty from absence of learned semantic features, recommending extraction of instance-level features for improved detection.

nodes.label: Label Smoothing
nodes.rationale: Regularization technique softening one-hot labels; can provide additional performance improvements when combined with temperature scheduling.

nodes.label: Maximum Logit Scoring Rule
nodes.rationale: OSR scoring rule using maximum logit value to distinguish known from unknown classes; foundation for evaluating OSR performance.

nodes.label: Negative Cosine Schedule (NegCosSch)
nodes.rationale: Novel temperature schedule starting with lower temperature for coarse decision boundary, gradually increasing to prioritize more neighbors and refine representations while maintaining separation from open set samples.

nodes.label: Open Set Recognition (OSR)
nodes.rationale: Task of simultaneously classifying known classes and detecting unknown classes not present in training data, requiring strong generalization and ability to discern novel semantic classes.

nodes.label: Open Set Classification Rate (OSCR)
nodes.rationale: Metric measuring trade-off between open set and closed set performance in OSR tasks.

nodes.label: Semantic Shift Benchmarks (SSBs)
nodes.rationale: Fine-grained OSR benchmarks on CUB, FGVC-Aircraft, and Stanford Cars with varying difficulty levels and more training classes, providing more challenging evaluation than standard OSR benchmarks.

nodes.label: Supervised Contrastive Loss (SupCon)
nodes.rationale: Loss function using multi-viewed batches to push apart negative samples and pull together positive samples, with temperature controlling hard negative mining.

nodes.label: Temperature Effect on Representation Learning
nodes.rationale: Lower temperature encourages instance-specific features with sharp decision boundaries; higher temperature encourages semantic features with smooth boundaries—fixed temperature prevents exploring both ends of spectrum.

nodes.label: Temperature Scheduling for Representation Learning
nodes.rationale: Dynamic temperature modulation during training enabling gradual task switching from instance-specific to semantic features, creating richer and more generalizable representation spaces for both open and closed set tasks.

nodes.label: LLM-Judged Explanation Score
nodes.rationale: Evaluates conceptual understanding against human-written rubric; captures whether agent identifies underlying principles beyond fitting data.

nodes.label: N-Body Physics Simulator
nodes.rationale: Generates trajectories on-demand using pairwise force laws; supports multiple integrators (RK4, Yoshida, Dormand-Prince, symplectic Euler, leapfrog).

nodes.label: Pass@k Metric
nodes.rationale: Expected worlds passed from k independent attempts; world passes if normalized MSE < 0.1 AND explanation score ≥ 0.9.

nodes.label: Science Agent (LLM)
nodes.rationale: Active participant in simulated worlds; proposes experiments, observes trajectories, iteratively refines hypothesis about underlying physical law.

nodes.label: Symbolic Regression vs Discovery
nodes.rationale: DiscoverPhysics departs from symbolic regression: discovery requires identifying conceptual content and generative mechanism, not just fitting equations.

nodes.label: Trajectory MSE Metric
nodes.rationale: Measures predictive accuracy on held-out test particles; normalized by test particle variance to account for world-specific scale differences.

nodes.label: FireAct - Distilling Agent Reasoning
nodes.rationale: Fine-tuned Llama2-7B on GPT-4 ReAct trajectories; achieved 77% performance increase on HotpotQA.

nodes.label: WorkflowLLM - Scaling to Complex Workflows
nodes.rationale: Compiled API orchestration knowledge from 106K workflow samples into 8B model; related to DiscoverPhysics' procedural knowledge compilation.

nodes.label: Feature-Level Patch Record
nodes.rationale: Summarizes prior implementation change: affected files, relevant symbols, behavior before/after, constraints to preserve, revision reason, and bounded code evidence.

nodes.label: Localized Modify Execution
nodes.rationale: Plan-Act-Guard pipeline for multi-turn slide editing; projects revision requests onto smallest affected slide region, applies minimal effective edits, and verifies coverage before finalizing updates.

nodes.label: Diagnostic Matched-Pair Modify Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Paired agent executions with fixed source deck, model, persona, and request; compares tool-memory injection to measure closed-loop completion, verification, and edit efficiency.

nodes.label: MemSlides: Hierarchical Memory for Personalized Slide Generation
nodes.norm_label: memslides: hierarchical memory for personalized slide generation
nodes.rationale: Framework separating long-term memory (user profile + tool memory) from working memory for multi-turn localized slide revision; enables persistent personalization across jobs while preserving session-specific constraints.

nodes.label: Multi-Persona Multi-Intent Profile Bank
nodes.rationale: Controlled testbed with 10 occupation-style personas × 3 role-intent buckets = 30 profile entries; covers diverse demographics, occupations, and presentation contexts for personalization evaluation.

nodes.label: Template-Guided Generation
nodes.rationale: Uses task-time design constraints from templates to guide slide generation while persona-conditioned generation adapts content and emphasis.

nodes.label: Tool Memory for Reliable Editing
nodes.rationale: Execution-side memory organized at round-scope (task experience) and operation-scope (tool-chain experience) granularities; supports reliable multi-turn modification by recording reasoning-tool-observation chains.

nodes.label: User Profile Memory
nodes.rationale: Long-term memory storing intent-conditioned user preferences organized by presentation dimensions (theme, content, visual, layout, template, general); routed into working memory at job start and consolidated at job end.

nodes.label: Working Memory for Session State
nodes.rationale: Session-scoped state layer maintaining active temporary preferences, carryover instructions, edit-state records, and tool-memory signals; enables multi-turn revision within single authoring job.

nodes.label: Configuration Depth Gap
nodes.rationale: Across PaperBench's 8,921 expert reproduction requirements, only 45.4% fully specified in source PDF. Published papers omit hyperparameters, environment specs, implementation details necessary for reproduction.

nodes.label: PaperBench Benchmark
nodes.rationale: 23 peer-reviewed ML papers with 8,921 expert-authored rubric requirements. Supplies configuration depth via expert rubrics encoding hyperparameters, implementation tricks, configurations absent from papers.

nodes.label: CISPO: Off-Policy RL Algorithm for Proof Generation
nodes.norm_label: cispo: off-policy rl algorithm for proof generation
nodes.rationale: Clips importance-sampling weight rather than surrogate loss; preserves token-level gradients in long responses; uses group-level std-threshold filter to suppress noisy group-relative advantages.

nodes.label: Four-Layer Defense-in-Depth Verifier Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Engineered to minimize false positives during long-horizon RL: Layer 1 (bad-case filtering), Layer 2 (solution normalization), Layer 3 (multi-judge scoring), Layer 4 (pessimistic min aggregation).

nodes.label: Fixer Expert: Proof Repair by Rejection-Sampling Fine-Tune
nodes.norm_label: fixer expert: proof repair by rejection-sampling fine-tune
nodes.rationale: Learns to repair flawed proofs given critique; trained via rejection sampling on Proof Expert's RL byproducts, accepting only repairs verified as fully correct.

nodes.label: MaxProof: Population-Level Test-Time Scaling Framework
nodes.rationale: Model-agnostic framework converting best@K into pass@1 via population search, conservative fitness, diverse parent selection, dual PATCH/REWRITE refinement, and pairwise tournament selection.

nodes.label: M2 Cycle Reward-Hacking Case Study
nodes.rationale: Documents four canonical hacking patterns (length bias, format hacking, semantic shortcut, judge-specific preference) that motivated M3 verifier design.

nodes.label: Per-Problem Search Dynamics and Selection Loss
nodes.norm_label: per-problem search dynamics and selection loss
nodes.rationale: Oracle-best vs. self-pick analysis reveals population ceiling and selection mechanism quality; USAMO 2026 P2 shows 4-point selection loss when ranker disagrees with verifier scores.

nodes.label: Proof Expert: Long-Horizon RL under Defense-in-Depth Verifier
nodes.norm_label: proof expert: long-horizon rl under defense-in-depth verifier
nodes.rationale: Trained via CISPO RL with four-layer generative verifier (bad-case filtering, solution normalization, multi-judge scoring, pessimistic aggregation) to suppress reward hacking patterns.

nodes.label: Verifier Expert: Aligned Error Finding
nodes.rationale: Distills verifier behavior into single M3 model via error-finding task formulation; trained on harvested data from Proof Expert's RL run to ensure alignment on same notion of correctness.

nodes.label: Agent Era: Environment-Action-Feedback Loops
nodes.rationale: LLMs move from passive dialogue to active tool-calling agents; fragile due to incorrect action formats, missing observations, and unrecovered intermediate errors.

nodes.label: Chatbot Era: Fast-Response Language Generation
nodes.rationale: Characterized by scaling-driven language generation, parametric knowledge compression, behavioral alignment (RLHF), and multimodal expansion; limited by lack of intrinsic verification and self-correction.

nodes.label: Data Paradigm Shift: From Instruction-Response to State-Action-Observation Trajectories
nodes.norm_label: data paradigm shift: from instruction-response to state-action-observation trajectories
nodes.rationale: Chatbot era uses instruction-response pairs; Thinking LLM era adds Chain-of-Thought and process reward data; Agent/OpenClaw era uses state-action-observation trajectories for task-oriented learning.

nodes.label: Evaluation Paradigm Shift: From Output Scoring to Task-State Verification
nodes.norm_label: evaluation paradigm shift: from output scoring to task-state verification
nodes.rationale: Stage I: final-output accuracy; Stage II: LLM-as-judge for reasoning; Stage III: task closure rate; Stage IV: workspace capability and safety verification.

nodes.label: Long Chain-of-Thought and Inference-Time Scaling
nodes.rationale: Qualitatively different from short CoT: enables deep reasoning (tens/hundreds of steps), extensive exploration (branching alternatives), and feasible reflection (error detection/correction).

nodes.label: OpenClaw Era: Persistent Workspaces for Task Closure
nodes.norm_label: openclaw era: persistent workspaces for task closure
nodes.rationale: Tool use embedded in persistent workspaces with files, terminals, browsers, logs, permissions, reusable skills, and verification procedures; enables context maintenance and failure recovery.

nodes.label: Reinforcement-Learning-Driven Reasoning
nodes.rationale: Models like o1 and DeepSeek-R1 use RL to internalize search, reflection, and self-correction within single output sequence; enables spontaneous interleaving of derivation, branching, and verification.

nodes.label: Thinking LLM Era: Inference-Time Scaling and RL-Driven Reasoning
nodes.norm_label: thinking llm era: inference-time scaling and rl-driven reasoning
nodes.rationale: Models allocate additional inference-time compute for deliberate reasoning via long Chain-of-Thought, exploration, and reflection; enables System-2 slow thinking for mathematics, coding, planning.

nodes.label: Active Learning and Reinforcement Learning
nodes.rationale: Paradigms for iterative measurement-informed decision making; enable hypothesis selection, data quality checks, and design process optimization

nodes.label: Agentic Systems
nodes.rationale: LLM-based systems with reasoning and coding capabilities for outer-loop orchestration of workflows and automated decision making across all Grand Challenges

nodes.label: AI Training and Inference as a Service
nodes.norm_label: ai training and inference as a service
nodes.rationale: Backbone infrastructure for AI-native experimentation; enables offloading AI compute to external services at national laboratories

nodes.label: American Science Cloud (AmSC)
nodes.rationale: Emerging national infrastructure offering unified inference for open-source and industry models; supports Genesis Mission goals through Intelligent Interfaces and MCP servers

nodes.label: Anomaly Detection
nodes.rationale: Unsupervised/weakly supervised methods for identifying deviations from dominant distributions; enables model-agnostic searches and automated system monitoring

nodes.label: Data Curation, Governance, and Open Access
nodes.norm_label: data curation, governance, and open access
nodes.rationale: Federated Data Lakehouse with coherent representations and automated curation pipelines; enables cross-experiment foundation models and FAIR data principles

nodes.label: Differentiable Simulation
nodes.rationale: Integration of simulators into automatic differentiation frameworks enabling gradient-based optimization for sensitivity analysis, calibration, design optimization, and simulation-based inference

nodes.label: Digital Twins
nodes.rationale: Realistic, dynamic models of physical experiments enabling tight feedback loops and verifiability; key substrate for AI-native experiments and agentic AI

nodes.label: Fast Data Generation and Simulation
nodes.rationale: Generative AI and accelerated simulation to provide rapid, adaptable, on-demand data creation; essential for design optimization, operations, and analysis

nodes.label: Foundation Models for HEP
nodes.rationale: Multimodal foundation models adaptable to multiple levels of analysis stack (reconstruction, population, inference); enable transfer across detector geometries and event topologies

nodes.label: Four Grand Challenges in AI for Particle Physics
nodes.norm_label: four grand challenges in ai for particle physics
nodes.rationale: Unified framework organizing AI research across detector design, simulation/reconstruction, autonomous experiments, and data-to-discovery workflows

nodes.label: Neural Simulation-Based Inference
nodes.rationale: Methods at conjunction of simulation, probabilistic modeling, and deep learning enabling high-dimensional Bayesian/Frequentist inference with significant sensitivity improvements

nodes.label: Workforce Development Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Structured training from undergraduate through postdoctoral levels; dual-competency in physics and AI; leverages existing programs (REU, SULI, PURSUE, SUPER, IRIS-HEP Fellows)

nodes.label: Author Agent
nodes.rationale: Analyzes research papers and generates structured scripts with modular element functions; enables systematic verification and efficient error correction

nodes.label: Convergence Test
nodes.rationale: Progressively increases computational accuracy parameters to ensure numerical convergence of results

nodes.label: Integration Tests for Hierarchical Execution
nodes.rationale: Decomposes computation into levels and executes incrementally; identifies compatibility issues between element functions

nodes.label: LLM Hallucinations in Scientific Research
nodes.rationale: Critical barrier to AI-driven discovery; includes domain-specific errors in code syntax and physical configurations; requires systematic verification mechanisms

nodes.label: Physical Assertion Test
nodes.rationale: Validates script against predefined physical constraints: limiting case tests, symmetry tests, and analytical tests

nodes.label: Programming Verifier
nodes.rationale: Conducts unit tests and integration tests to ensure programming correctness; achieves near-100% executability through parallel error correction

nodes.label: Rubric Test for Physical System Validation
nodes.norm_label: rubric test for physical system validation
nodes.rationale: Checks script against human-curated scorecard covering physical system, computational method, and parameter correctness

nodes.label: Scientific Verifier
nodes.rationale: Performs rubric tests, physical assertion tests, and convergence tests to ensure physical validity; provides human-auditable evidence of correctness

nodes.label: Unit Tests for Element Functions
nodes.rationale: Examines each element function in isolation using verifier library; reveals programming errors within target functions

nodes.label: Verifier Library for Unit Tests
nodes.rationale: Repository of verified element functions distilled from official package repositories; provides test environments for systematic verification

nodes.label: Grand Challenge 1: AI for Detector Design and Optimization
nodes.norm_label: grand challenge 1: ai for detector design and optimization
nodes.rationale: Addresses accelerating detector design cycles through AI-driven optimization, reducing design time from years to months and enabling exploration of vastly larger design spaces

nodes.label: Grand Challenge 2: AI for Simulation and Reconstruction
nodes.norm_label: grand challenge 2: ai for simulation and reconstruction
nodes.rationale: Aims to transform simulation from static pre-computed resource to dynamic adaptive element; enable fast, differentiable simulation; and improve reconstruction through foundation models

nodes.label: PhysVEC: Verifiable and Self-Correcting AI Physicist Framework
nodes.norm_label: physvec: verifiable and self-correcting ai physicist framework
nodes.rationale: Multi-agent framework with Author, Programming verifier, and Scientific verifier; enforces self-verification and error correction for both code correctness and physical validity

nodes.label: QMP-Bench: Quantum Many-Body Physics Benchmark
nodes.rationale: First end-to-end research-level benchmark with 100 tasks from 21 high-impact articles; covers tensor networks (dmrg), neural quantum states (nqs), quantum circuits (qsim), and DFT (dft)

nodes.label: Adaptive Knowledge Selection
nodes.rationale: Method allowing agents to autonomously choose relevant knowledge from shared pool based on their needs, filtering noise while maintaining personalization.

nodes.label: Consistent and Correct Ratio
nodes.rationale: Metric measuring both consistency and correctness of debate outcomes, indicating cognitive island mitigation.

nodes.label: Cognitive Islands Problem
nodes.rationale: Phenomenon where agents with limited and different knowledge backgrounds stubbornly adhere to incorrect viewpoints or easily abandon correct ones, hindering multi-agent consensus.

nodes.label: LLM Hallucination
nodes.rationale: Phenomenon where LLMs generate factually incorrect information, exacerbating cognitive islands in multi-agent debates.

nodes.label: Knowledge Gap Problem
nodes.rationale: Limited and different background knowledge among agents leading to incomplete reasoning and incorrect conclusions.

nodes.label: MADKE Framework
nodes.rationale: Multi-Agent Debate with Knowledge-Enhanced framework combining shared knowledge pool and adaptive selection to mitigate cognitive islands.

nodes.label: Orderly-Talk Stage
nodes.rationale: Second debate stage where agents sequentially respond to previous viewpoints and selected knowledge.

nodes.label: Shared Knowledge Pool
nodes.rationale: Centralized repository of retrieved knowledge from Wikipedia and Google Search accessible to all debate agents.

nodes.label: Simultaneous-Talk Stage
nodes.rationale: First debate stage where agents independently present initial viewpoints without influence from others.

nodes.label: Design Principle P1: Automate Mechanical, Reserve Humans for Judgment
nodes.norm_label: design principle p1: automate mechanical, reserve humans for judgment
nodes.rationale: Structural validity, internal consistency, and claim reproducibility are objective properties; significance, novelty, and taste require domain expertise. Never ask human to verify machine-checkable issues.

nodes.label: CI Report
nodes.rationale: Output of Stage 1 (Conceptual Verification): records structural failures, rigor critiques, and advisory diagnostics (dead-end nodes, baseline coverage, experiment-claim gaps).

nodes.label: Stage 1: Conceptual Verification
nodes.rationale: Checks whether artifact is well-formed and conceptually well-supported without running experiments. Validates structural integrity (Level 1) and argumentative rigor (Level 2). Produces CI Report.

nodes.label: Empirical Review Report
nodes.rationale: Output of Stage 2 (Empirical Verification): records which claims verified, which failed, which deferred due to budget, and experimental gaps identified.

nodes.label: Stage 2: Empirical Verification
nodes.rationale: Tests whether claimed results reproduce. Executes ARA Seal Level 3 with venue-specified compute budget. Agent isolated from evidence layer. Produces Empirical Review Report.

nodes.label: (Human+AI)² Research Network
nodes.rationale: Scientific communication system where ARA is primary object. Researchers pursue questions; paper accrues automatically as ARA. Agents render on demand into surfaces needed. Contributions compound at artifact level; publishing becomes Git-like operation.

nodes.label: Stage 3: Human Review
nodes.rationale: Human reviewers focus on judgment questions: significance, novelty, taste, ethical implications. Receive submission with CI Report and Empirical Review Report. Write structured reviews linked to ARA components.

nodes.label: Design Principle P2: Reproducibility as Foundational Requirement
nodes.norm_label: design principle p2: reproducibility as foundational requirement
nodes.rationale: Reproducibility is machine-verified property of artifact itself. Passing Level 1 is submission requirement; Level 2 produces critique before compute spent on Level 3; results attached to every review.

nodes.label: Three-Stage ARA Review Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Mirrors CI/CD practices: Stage 1 (Conceptual Verification, minutes) checks structural integrity and argumentative rigor; Stage 2 (Empirical Verification, hours-days) tests claim reproducibility; Stage 3 (Human Review, days-weeks) focuses on significance, novelty, taste.

nodes.label: Agent-In-World (AIW) Module
nodes.rationale: LLM analyzes failed trajectories to extract failure modes; retrieves tasks with similar failure patterns from offline history; reshapes training data distribution for targeted practice.

nodes.label: Role-Agent Framework
nodes.rationale: Single LLM functioning as both agent and environment for bootstrapped co-evolution via World-In-Agent (WIA) state prediction and Agent-In-World (AIW) failure mode analysis.

nodes.label: State-Level Advantage Computation
nodes.rationale: Groups identical states across rollout batch; computes state-level advantages independent of temporal ordering; combines with trajectory-level advantages via coefficient α for final advantage signal.

nodes.label: World-In-Agent (WIA) Module
nodes.rationale: LLM predicts future states at each step; predictive reward computed via Longest Matching Subsequence (LMS) similarity; modulates task reward to encourage environment-aware reasoning.

nodes.label: ALFWorld and WebShop Benchmarks
nodes.rationale: Interactive text-based environments: ALFWorld tests multi-step household tasks; WebShop simulates e-commerce with 1.18M products; Role-Agent achieves 90.9% and 71.9% success rates respectively.

nodes.label: Failure Mode Library
nodes.rationale: 11 unique failure modes on ALFWorld (repetitive exploration, wrong target location, entity confusion, etc.); accumulated during training; enables targeted retrieval of similar tasks for practice.

nodes.label: GiGPO Baseline
nodes.rationale: State-grouped RL method achieving 86.7% on ALFWorld and 83.1% on WebShop; Role-Agent outperforms with 4.2% and 6.9% relative gains respectively.

nodes.label: Search-Augmented QA Tasks
nodes.rationale: Single-hop (NQ, TriviaQA, PopQA) and multi-hop (HotpotQA, 2Wiki, MuSiQue, Bamboogle) QA datasets; Role-Agent achieves 45.8% average, with +8.2% on 2Wiki and +5.2% on MuSiQue.

nodes.label: Context Extraction for Queries
nodes.rationale: GPT-4o-mini extraction of background/motivation sentences from abstracts to create specific query contexts; includes leak detection filtering.

nodes.label: Scientific Domain Classification
nodes.rationale: Zero-shot classification of entities into arXiv categories or broader scientific branches; includes domain grouping to address sparsity in non-arXiv fields.

nodes.label: Entity Normalization Process
nodes.rationale: Multi-step process including abbreviation expansion via regex and scispacy, followed by agglomerative clustering with cosine similarity to group semantically equivalent entities.

nodes.label: GPT-4o Reranking for Predictions
nodes.rationale: RankGPT-based reranking of top-20 predictions using GPT-4o; improves recombination prediction accuracy through multi-turn ranking dialogue.

nodes.label: Knowledge Graph Construction
nodes.rationale: Process of building graph nodes from extracted entities, assigning scientific domains via GPT-4o, normalizing entities, and postprocessing with LLM refinement.

nodes.label: Recombination Prediction Task
nodes.rationale: Bi-encoder architecture task that predicts novel recombination inspirations given a query context; uses contrastive learning with RankGPT reranking.

nodes.label: User Study Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Human evaluation of model-predicted recombination suggestions by NLP researchers; assesses helpfulness for research ideation and novelty of cross-domain inspirations.

nodes.label: Accelerating Innovation Through Analogy Mining
nodes.rationale: Prior work on mining analogies from scientific literature to accelerate innovation; directly related to CHIMERA's recombination prediction task.

nodes.label: Markov State Models
nodes.rationale: Stochastic models for analyzing molecular dynamics and protein folding kinetics

nodes.label: Adversarial Objective
nodes.rationale: Search intervention correcting LLM self-preference bias by introducing adversarial pool of AI-generated papers accepted by displaced reviewer, rewarding future reviewers for rejecting them equally with human papers.

nodes.label: APReS Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Conference paper acceptance/rejection dataset used as ground-truth anchor for paper-review domain, enabling evaluator replacement decisions.

nodes.label: Figure 6: Adversarial Reviewer Results
nodes.rationale: Empirical results showing adversarial RQGM reviewer accepts AI and human papers at similar rates, correcting self-preference bias while driving strongest writer.

nodes.label: Paper Writing Domain
nodes.rationale: Experimental domain without objective benchmark where RQGM co-evolves writers with learned reviewers, achieving 1.78×–1.86× higher acceptance rates over HGM-H on fixed reviewer panel.

nodes.label: RQ2: Learned Evaluation Without Benchmarks
nodes.rationale: Research question validating that co-evolved agents outperform fixed-evaluator baselines in domains with no objective benchmark.

nodes.label: LLM Self-Preference Bias
nodes.rationale: Known weakness of LLM judges favoring AI-generated text; RQGM corrects this through adversarial objectives, discovering reviewers equally stringent on machine and human work.

nodes.label: Table 1: Paper Writer Results
nodes.rationale: Empirical results showing co-evolved writers achieve 1.78×–1.86× higher acceptance rates over HGM-H on fixed reviewer panel.

nodes.label: Table 7: Mechanism Ablations
nodes.rationale: Ablation study isolating components: replacement alone escapes saturation, erasure prevents stale utility, adversarial pool refines decision boundary.

nodes.label: AgentWorldBench: Comprehensive World Model Evaluation Benchmark
nodes.norm_label: agentworldbench: comprehensive world model evaluation benchmark
nodes.rationale: Benchmark constructed from frontier model trajectories on 9 established benchmarks across 7 domains; evaluates simulation quality through 5-dimensional rubric (Format, Factuality, Consistency, Realism, Quality) with reference-grounded judging.

nodes.label: Differentiated Matching Criteria
nodes.rationale: Classifies content into deterministic (exact match required), pre-existing (format/plausibility only), runtime metadata (format/range only); reduces false negatives from irreproducible details.

nodes.label: Domain-Aware Rubric Customization
nodes.rationale: Each domain has tailored judge prompt applying five dimensions in domain-specific terms; enforces professional standards (shell prompts for Terminal, JSON schema for MCP, fact-priority for Search).

nodes.label: Five-Dimensional Evaluation Rubric
nodes.rationale: Evaluates Format (structural compliance), Factuality (correctness of facts), Consistency (internal and cross-turn coherence), Realism (behavioral match to real environment), Quality (completeness and conciseness).

nodes.label: Cross-Judge Consistency Analysis
nodes.rationale: Compares three frontier models as judges; achieves Spearman rank correlations ρ=0.92-0.99; reference-grounded design enables high consistency despite absolute score differences.

nodes.label: Reference-Grounded Judging Protocol
nodes.rationale: Judge receives ground-truth observation alongside prediction; converts evaluation from open-ended quality judgment to factual comparison; substantially reduces judge hallucination and improves cross-judge consistency.

nodes.label: RL Enhancement of Micro-Level Simulation Fidelity
nodes.norm_label: rl enhancement of micro-level simulation fidelity
nodes.rationale: RL training improves simulation fidelity at fine-grained level; different rubric dimensions improve at markedly different rates; Factuality shows largest relative improvement yet remains lowest-scoring.

nodes.label: Turing Test Calibration for Judge Selection
nodes.norm_label: turing test calibration for judge selection
nodes.rationale: Uses double-blind Turing test to select judge model and tune prompts; judge with high Turing-test accuracy must attend to fine-grained differences between faithful and plausible-but-wrong simulation.

nodes.label: Planted-Structure Problems
nodes.rationale: Contamination-resistant problem class where answer is engineered; enables verification while avoiding retrieval shortcuts.

nodes.label: Command A LLM
nodes.rationale: Large language model used as the fusor in FusioN experiments, performs generative fusion of teacher outputs

nodes.label: ARA Seal
nodes.rationale: Three-level machine-verifiable credential: Level 1 (Structural Integrity, seconds), Level 2 (Argumentative Rigor, minutes), Level 3 (Execution Reproducibility, hours-days). Passes issue Seal Certificate for downstream verification.

nodes.label: Rigor Auditor Agent
nodes.rationale: Agent skill that executes ARA Seal Level 2 without executing code or consulting external sources. Evaluates epistemically sound content along six objective dimensions with anchored rubrics.

nodes.label: Seal Certificate
nodes.rationale: Signed record of artifact ID, verification level achieved, timestamp, environment hash, and per-claim reproduction outcomes. Downstream agents check before investing compute.

nodes.label: ARA Seal Level 1: Structural Integrity
nodes.rationale: Verifies artifact is well-formed and internally consistent: directory ontology exists, structured files conform to schema, all cross-layer references resolve.

nodes.label: ARA Seal Level 2: Argumentative Rigor
nodes.rationale: Rigor Auditor agent evaluates epistemically sound content along six objective dimensions: evidence relevance, falsifiability quality, methodological rigor, scope calibration, argument coherence, exploration integrity. Scored 1-5 per dimension.

nodes.label: ARA Seal Level 3: Execution Reproducibility
nodes.rationale: Verifies central claims reproduce empirically via scaled-down directional checks. Verifying agent isolated from evidence layer (receives only code kernel and algorithm descriptions) to prevent fabrication.

nodes.label: Cognitive Burden Effect
nodes.rationale: Complex prompts can degrade LLM performance, but VS variants overcome this effect

nodes.label: Emergent Trend: Larger Models Benefit More
nodes.norm_label: emergent trend: larger models benefit more
nodes.rationale: Larger models achieve diversity gains 1.5 to 2 times greater than smaller models with VS

nodes.label: KL Divergence with Pre-training Distribution
nodes.rationale: Verbalized distribution aligns with pre-training corpus distribution at KL divergence of 0.12

nodes.label: Verbalized Sampling (VS)
nodes.rationale: Training-free prompting method that frames requests as sampling from distributions rather than single instances to restore diversity

nodes.label: Universal Phenomena in Deep Learning
nodes.rationale: Common inductive biases and representations across models; analogous to critical phenomena and renormalization group flow in physics

nodes.label: AutoML-Based System Prompt Optimization
nodes.rationale: Formulates prompt optimization as automated research problem; iterative propose-evaluate-refine cycles with optimizer and judge agents; generates 12 template variants with different styles.

nodes.label: Continual Pre-Training Stage
nodes.rationale: Injects world knowledge through next-token prediction on environment trajectories and specialized-domain corpora; uses turn-level information-theoretic loss masking to focus on genuine environment information.

nodes.label: Turn-Level Information-Theoretic Loss Masking
nodes.rationale: Categorizes turns into 7 semantic categories (retrieval, expansion, action, transform, boilerplate, echo, other) based on statistical signals; masks low-information turns to focus learning on genuine environment knowledge.

nodes.label: Qwen-AgentWorld-35B-A3B Model
nodes.rationale: Language world model trained via three-stage pipeline (CPT, SFT, RL) for simulating 7 agent interaction domains; demonstrates world modeling improves downstream agent performance.

nodes.label: Qwen-AgentWorld-397B-A17B Model
nodes.rationale: Larger language world model achieving highest overall score on AgentWorldBench; demonstrates scalability of world modeling approach across text and GUI domains.

nodes.label: Agentic Fact-Checking Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Verifies abstractions against Wikipedia using free API and gpt-oss-120b; achieves F1 0.93 on manual validation; enables large-scale risk evaluation.

nodes.label: FactScore Benchmark
