nodes.rationale: Long-form factuality benchmark with biography prompts; used for evaluating SA with 36 prompts; atom-wise SA achieves up to 27.73% AURC improvement.

nodes.label: LongFact-Objects Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Open-ended factual QA benchmark across 38 subject areas; used for SA evaluation with 76 prompts; atom-wise SA achieves 13.77% average AURC improvement.

nodes.label: Cognitive Layer (/logic)
nodes.rationale: Contains what was done and why: problem definition, solution architecture, falsifiable claims with proof pointers, and verification plans. Replaces passive citations with typed dependencies (imports, bounds, baselines).

nodes.label: claims.md
nodes.rationale: Distills falsifiable assertions with explicit proof pointers to experiments and evidence.

nodes.label: experiments.md
nodes.rationale: Declares the verification plan for all claims.

nodes.label: problem.md
nodes.rationale: Defines the gap and key insight in the research contribution.

nodes.label: related_work.md
nodes.rationale: Contains typed dependencies replacing passive citations, enabling machine-executable dependency graph.

nodes.label: solution/ Directory
nodes.rationale: Specifies architecture, algorithm, and convergence-critical heuristics.

nodes.label: Typed Dependencies in Related Work
nodes.rationale: Replaces passive citations with machine-executable dependency graph: imports inject prior definitions, bounds propagate constraints to hyperparameter search, baseline entries enable automatic regression detection.

nodes.label: Constraint Load in Problem Complexity
nodes.rationale: Key finding: rationale supervision effectiveness depends on problem structure; beneficial when problem has multiple interacting constraints, harmful on trivial problems

nodes.label: Modular P–S–R Extraction Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Five-stage pipeline: paragraph filtering, entity extraction, relation extraction, rationale construction, post-processing; separates local boundary-based labels from conceptual grouping

nodes.label: MUSE Knowledge Base
nodes.rationale: Large structured KB of 36,960 source-grounded P–S–R triplets mined from full-text scientific papers across domains

nodes.label: Problem–Solution–Rationale Extraction
nodes.rationale: Core task: extract fine-grained technical problem-solving structures from full-text scientific papers; captures local technical reasoning with rationale explaining solution choice

nodes.label: Rationale-Supervised LLM Training
nodes.rationale: Application: using extracted rationales as supervision signal for scientific problem solving; improves performance on complex multi-constraint problems but can harm simple ones

nodes.label: Co-Evolution and Rationale-Driven Reasoning
nodes.rationale: Conceptual link: both papers address how systems improve through adaptive feedback loops; co-evolution through mutual adaptation parallels rationale-supervised learning through explicit reasoning

nodes.label: Citations Agent
nodes.rationale: Adds citations to paper sections using Perplexity API

nodes.label: Paper Writing Module
nodes.rationale: Writes scientific papers with sections, citations, and formatted output

nodes.label: Keywords Selection Agent
nodes.rationale: Selects relevant keywords from UNESCO, AAAI, or AAS taxonomies

nodes.label: Paper Generation Workflow
nodes.rationale: Sequential process of writing sections, adding figures, citations, and generating LaTeX output

nodes.label: Section Writing Agents
nodes.rationale: Specialized agents for writing different paper sections (abstract, introduction, methods, results, conclusions)

nodes.label: Gemini 3 Flash Model
nodes.rationale: Underperforms relative to parameter class; trails LLaMA3.3-70B-IT and OLMo3.1-32B-IT; suggests architectural/training choices affect reasoning properties.

nodes.label: GPT-5.1 Model
nodes.rationale: Largest evaluated model; exhibits highest sensibility (88.1%) but used as judge for other models; demonstrates scaling trend in logical grounding.

nodes.label: LLaMA Model Family
nodes.rationale: Shows inverse scaling for compliance: LLaMA3.1-8B-IT (65.1% compliance) more compliant than LLaMA3.3-70B-IT; suggests post-training methodology dominates scale.

nodes.label: Model Scale and Reasoning Properties
nodes.rationale: Larger models show higher sensibility but compliance is family-dependent and parameter-agnostic; architectural choices and instruction-tuning recipes matter more than scale for compliance.

nodes.label: Qwen Model Family
nodes.rationale: Thinking mode on increases sensibility but decreases compliance; 4x parameter increase (8B→32B) shows standard scaling for compliance; demonstrates architectural effects.

nodes.label: Built-in Thinking Mode Effects
nodes.rationale: Models with thinking mode (Qwen, OLMo) show higher sensibility but lower compliance; indicates substantial behavior difference between internal thinking and external CoT.

nodes.label: LLM Backbone Ablation
nodes.rationale: Eywa effective across gpt-4.1-nano, gpt-5-nano, gpt-5-mini; benefits from stronger LLMs but gains primarily from FM-LLM coupling not backbone scale.

nodes.label: Empirical Performance Gains
nodes.rationale: EywaAgent: +6.6% utility, -30% tokens, -10% latency vs baseline; EywaMAS outperforms homogeneous MAS; EywaOrchestra reaches near-EywaMAS utility with -26% tokens.

nodes.label: EywaBench: Multi-Domain Scientific Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Scalable benchmark spanning physical/life/social sciences with natural language, time series, and tabular modalities; 200 task instances from 67 source datasets with unified utility metric.

nodes.label: GPT-5-nano Language Model
nodes.rationale: Default LLM backbone for Eywa experiments; provides general-purpose reasoning interface for coordinating domain-specific foundation models.

nodes.label: Pareto Frontier Analysis
nodes.rationale: Eywa methods consistently sit on Pareto frontier across all 9 sub-domains; LLM-only MAS baselines dominated; demonstrates utility-token trade-off superiority.

nodes.label: Token Complexity Analysis
nodes.rationale: EywaAgent token cost O(L_call + L_ψ(o_k)) independent of modality size vs. Θ(L(x_k)) for LLM-only; explains ~30% token reduction in practice.

nodes.label: Multiplication and Sorting Tasks
nodes.rationale: Extends Abacus Embeddings to multiplication (15-digit) and sorting (10-element arrays); demonstrates generalization of approach beyond addition.

nodes.label: Data Contamination in GSM8K
nodes.rationale: Hypothesis that GSM8K test examples may have inadvertently entered LLM training sets, explaining why original GSM8K performance often exceeds GSM-Symbolic distribution mean.

nodes.label: Exponential Probability Decay with Token Count
nodes.norm_label: exponential probability decay with token count
nodes.rationale: Finding that probability of correct multi-token output decreases exponentially with number of tokens, indicating inherent unreliability in complex reasoning.

nodes.label: Length Generalization
nodes.rationale: Ability to apply known logical steps on larger inputs; key aspect of genuine reasoning distinct from pattern-matching.

nodes.label: LLM Mathematical Reasoning Limitations
nodes.rationale: Core finding: LLMs exhibit high performance variance across question instantiations, sensitivity to numerical changes, degradation with increased complexity, and catastrophic drops with irrelevant information—indicating pattern-matching rather than formal reasoning.

nodes.label: Token Bias in LLMs
nodes.rationale: Phenomenon where LLM outputs change drastically with single token input changes, indicating strong sensitivity and fragility in reasoning.

nodes.label: Deep Linear Networks
nodes.rationale: Nonlinear in parameters but linear in data; exhibit saddle-point landscapes, phase transitions, edge-of-stability oscillations, and initialization-dependent biases

nodes.label: Infinite Width Limit and Lazy/Rich Dichotomy
nodes.norm_label: infinite width limit and lazy/rich dichotomy
nodes.rationale: Initialization scale determines lazy (linearized, no feature learning) vs. rich (feature learning) regimes; mean-field behavior simplifies analysis

nodes.label: Lazy/Kernel/Linearized Regime
nodes.rationale: Weights and representations change negligibly; training dynamics linear in parameters; analytically tractable but lacks feature learning

nodes.label: Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK)
nodes.rationale: Describes linearized networks through fixed feature map; enables kernel ridge regression analysis and prediction of generalization error

nodes.label: Rich/Active/Feature-Learning Regime
nodes.rationale: Hidden features adapt to data structure; neurons specialize; exhibits greedy low-rank bias; requires downscaling final-layer weights

nodes.label: Analytically Solvable Settings in Deep Learning
nodes.norm_label: analytically solvable settings in deep learning
nodes.rationale: Deep linear networks, kernel methods, multi-index models provide intuition; linearization in data and parameters enables exact solutions

nodes.label: Attention Heat-Map Evolution Analysis
nodes.rationale: Measures attention entropy, inter-loop KL divergence, and head diversity; shows information routing largely freezes after loop 2 with heads becoming increasingly redundant.

nodes.label: Effective Rank as Representation Diversity Metric
nodes.norm_label: effective rank as representation diversity metric
nodes.rationale: Measures geometric diversity of token representations using normalized singular values; peaks at loop 2 and declines for deeper loops, indicating representational narrowing.

nodes.label: Per-Loop Hidden-State Dynamics Analysis
nodes.rationale: Tracks step size, angular change, effective rank, and fixed-point gap across loops; reveals that loop 2 provides main productive refinement while later loops yield diminishing, oscillatory updates.

nodes.label: Logit Lens Rank Analysis
nodes.rationale: Tracks rank of ground-truth next token under output distribution across loops; monotonically decreasing rank indicates iterative refinement toward correct prediction.

nodes.label: Loop-Count Selection as Gain-Cost Trade-off
nodes.rationale: Formulates PLT loop-count selection as trade-off between marginal refinement gain from additional loops and positional-mismatch cost from CLP offset; explains saturation at r=2.

nodes.label: Output-Distribution Shift Analysis
nodes.rationale: Tracks logit-lens rank, inter-loop KL divergence, and output entropy; reveals per-loop prediction change collapses after loop 2 while overall predictions sharpen monotonically.

nodes.label: Cross-Loop Position Offset (CLP)
nodes.rationale: Mechanism breaking sequential inter-loop dependencies by right-shifting previous loop's hidden states before adding to input; enables parallelism but introduces positional mismatch at loop boundaries.

nodes.label: Gated Sliding-Window Attention (G-SWA)
nodes.rationale: Fuses full-context attention on frozen loop-1 KV cache with sliding-window attention over current loop's KV; keeps KV-cache memory independent of loop count.

nodes.label: Intrinsic Offset Cost (Ω)
nodes.rationale: Quantifies CLP-induced positional mismatch as mean Euclidean distance between adjacent token representations; remains approximately constant across loops while per-loop refinement gains diminish.

nodes.label: LoopCoder-v2: Parallel Loop Transformer for Code
nodes.norm_label: loopcoder-v2: parallel loop transformer for code
nodes.rationale: 7B parameter PLT coder trained on 18T tokens; studies loop-count selection through gain-cost trade-off between representational refinement and CLP-induced positional mismatch.

nodes.label: Parallel Loop Transformer (PLT)
nodes.rationale: Architecture reducing sequential looping cost through cross-loop position offsets (CLP) and shared-KV gated sliding-window attention (G-SWA); enables parallel loop execution with near-constant latency and memory.

nodes.label: Thinking Model with Explicit CoT
nodes.rationale: Variant of LoopCoder-v2 fine-tuned to emit explicit reasoning trace; shows super-additive gains when combined with latent loop refinement on reasoning-intensive tasks.

nodes.label: Atom-wise Selective Abstraction
nodes.rationale: Claim-level instantiation of SA that decomposes responses into atomic claims and replaces uncertain atoms with higher-confidence, less specific abstractions; core technical contribution.

nodes.label: Atomic Claims
nodes.rationale: Short, self-contained statements each expressing a single fact; fundamental unit for atom-wise SA enabling fine-grained uncertainty handling.

nodes.label: Inline Abstraction Baseline
nodes.rationale: Adaptation of aggregation prompt from Yona et al.; reduces granularity during generation; atom-wise SA achieves 10.65% lower risk at matched coverage.

nodes.label: Atomization Stage (SA Pipeline)
nodes.rationale: Decomposes generated text into atomic claims using few-shot prompting; enables subsequent confidence scoring and abstraction.

nodes.label: Selective Redaction Baseline
nodes.rationale: Standard baseline removing all atoms below confidence threshold without abstraction; atom-wise SA outperforms by 17.43% AURC on FactScore.

nodes.label: Self-Revision Baseline
nodes.rationale: Post-hoc refinement instructing model to replace uncertain claims with less specific versions; atom-wise SA achieves 12.45% lower risk at matched coverage.

nodes.label: Celebrity/Public-Figure Application Preset
nodes.rationale: Extension for public-source expert distillation: prioritizes first-person works, interviews, documented decisions with explicit evidence requirements and quality checks for mental-model coverage.

nodes.label: Colleague Application Preset
nodes.rationale: Primary preset for workplace setting: distills teammate's practices, standards, communication norms into inspectable skill using work traces (docs, reviews, decisions, incidents).

nodes.label: COLLEAGUE.SKILL System
nodes.rationale: Distills heterogeneous human traces into portable, inspectable, correctable, composable, and governable skill packages with explicit source boundaries, usage limits, and lifecycle operations.

nodes.label: Dual Representation: Capability and Behavior Tracks
nodes.norm_label: dual representation: capability and behavior tracks
nodes.rationale: Work/capability track captures responsibilities, workflows, standards, heuristics; persona track stores bounded behavior constraints, expression preferences, interaction rules, correction records; enables separate invocation.

nodes.label: Person-Grounded Skill Artifact
nodes.rationale: Bounded package of selected capabilities, mental models, communication constraints, examples, and usage boundaries grounded in evidence about a person or role; not unrestricted conversational model.

nodes.label: Relationship Application Preset
nodes.rationale: Extension for sensitive private domain: represents interaction patterns as local, editable, deletable state with stronger assumptions about consent, retention, access control, and non-public defaults.

nodes.label: Environment Trajectory Collection Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Combines dedicated agent infrastructure, open environment interaction traces, and in-house agentic trajectories; multi-agent cleaning pipeline handles fetching, denoising, segmentation, semantic alignment.

nodes.label: No-Change Turn Filtering for GUI Domains
nodes.norm_label: no-change turn filtering for gui domains
nodes.rationale: Removes turns where pre-action and post-action states show no effective change; prevents teaching model to copy previous state regardless of action.

nodes.label: Retry-Cycle Skipping Data Filter
nodes.rationale: Skips garbage-output-error-retry cycles while preserving state chain; prevents breaking causal relationships between actions and observations.

nodes.label: Supervised Fine-Tuning Stage
nodes.rationale: Activates explicit next-state-prediction reasoning patterns; uses rejection sampling to curate high-quality trajectories; diversifies prompt templates to improve generalization.

nodes.label: Trajectory-to-Turn Expansion Technique
nodes.rationale: Expands multi-turn trajectories into turn-level prediction samples; any turn can serve as prediction target with preceding interactions as input; diversifies training objectives.

nodes.label: ε-Best-Belief Score
nodes.rationale: Conservative lower bound (ε-quantile of Beta posterior) used for both final agent selection and evaluator replacement, ensuring promoted evaluators exceed incumbent with probability 1-ε.

nodes.label: Ground-Truth Anchor
nodes.rationale: Fixed held-out dataset of objective or human-preference labels used to evaluate and select learned evaluators at epoch boundaries, providing evaluator-independent replacement criterion.

nodes.label: Learned Evaluators
nodes.rationale: Agentic evaluators that improve alongside task agents they score, enabling evaluation in domains without objective benchmarks and providing complementary signals where ground truth exists.

nodes.label: Limitation: Anchor Quality Dependence
nodes.rationale: Acknowledged limitation: evaluator quality bounded by anchor quality; weak or biased anchor yields uninformative evaluators.

nodes.label: RQ4: Co-Evolution Improves Evaluators
nodes.rationale: Research question validating that same dynamics improving generators also improve evaluators, with co-evolved grader reaching higher accuracy at lower cost.

nodes.label: Specialist vs. Generalist Selection
nodes.rationale: Two selection strategies: specialist maximizes best-belief on single target utility, generalist maximizes average across active utilities, showing whether improvements come from task-specific or joint optimization.

nodes.label: Hutter LLM Model
nodes.rationale: Simplified theoretical model of LLM that predicts next skill i given previous skill, used as foundation for analyzing scaling laws and model collapse.

nodes.label: Hutter++ Model (Probabilistic)
nodes.rationale: Extension of Hutter model to probabilistic setting with conditional distributions p(j|i), modeling next-token prediction in autoregressive LLMs.

nodes.label: Scaling Law Decay (Core Finding)
nodes.rationale: Central result: when training on AI-generated data with tail-cut distribution, test error plateaus rather than continuing to improve with more data.

nodes.label: Theorem 2.1: Scaling Law with Tail Cutting
nodes.norm_label: theorem 2.1: scaling law with tail cutting
nodes.rationale: Establishes that test error scales as min(T, k^β)^(-(β-1)/β) when training on tail-cut data, showing performance plateaus once T ≳ k^β.

nodes.label: Theorem 4.2: Model Collapse in Probabilistic Setting
nodes.norm_label: theorem 4.2: model collapse in probabilistic setting
nodes.rationale: Extends model collapse analysis to probabilistic Hutter++: E_test ≲ T^(-c) + k^(-βc), showing tail-cutting effect persists in autoregressive models.

nodes.label: Coordinator Head Architecture
nodes.rationale: Linear head most reliable; block-diagonal-10 with argmax maximizes independence among logits, revealing block-ε separability in problem objective

nodes.label: Joint Dataset-Agent Subset Selection
nodes.rationale: Maximizes relative error reduction under complementarity constraints; exhaustive enumeration on top-5% performance frontier; prioritizes diversity in task and agent types

nodes.label: Hidden State Separability Analysis
nodes.rationale: SLM representations encode task semantics in nearly linearly separable manifold; task-type classification near-perfect (1.0 linear/RBF SVM); agent selection accuracy correlates with coordinator performance

nodes.label: sep-CMA-ES: Separable CMA-ES Algorithm
nodes.rationale: Evolutionary strategy optimized for block-separable objectives; outperforms REINFORCE and random search under binary rewards and strict budgets

nodes.label: Unsupervised Discovery of Confidence Behavior
nodes.rationale: Entropy minimization identifies confidence-related decoder columns; reduces reflection/backtracking steps; enables test-time steering improving accuracy +4.66 points with 13.69% token reduction

nodes.label: Causal Intervention on SAE Vectors
nodes.rationale: Injecting SAE vectors during inference controllably modulates reasoning; negative intervention suppresses reflection/backtracking; positive intervention amplifies; generalization across domains (GPQA, KnowLogic)

nodes.label: Reasoning Vectors: Disentangled Behavior Directions
nodes.rationale: Linear directions in activation space encoding distinct reasoning behaviors; reflection/backtracking occupy overlapping subspaces; confidence vectors concentrated in bottom-right SAE decoder region

nodes.label: Sparse Auto-Encoder for Reasoning
nodes.rationale: Learns dictionary of sparse latent features reconstructing hidden states; decoder columns correspond to interpretable reasoning behaviors; Theorem 1 establishes recovery up to permutation and scaling

nodes.label: Argumentative Memory: Rhetorical Reconstruction
nodes.rationale: Debate as iterative reconstruction of prior reasoning contexts; retrieval function R recalls early memory; reasoning function M adapts to current debate context; maintains stance consistency across turns

nodes.label: Debate Knowledge Base Construction
nodes.rationale: Segments debate transcripts into utterance-level units; annotates with 7 argumentation schemes (example-based, expert opinion, positive/negative consequence, causal, analogical, value-based); scores scheme quality

nodes.label: Debate Generation with Iterative Verification
nodes.rationale: Generates initial utterance; Judgement Agent evaluates stance faithfulness, argumentative relevance, scheme compliance; Text Modification Agent revises until criteria satisfied; iterative refinement loop

nodes.label: Logic & Summarization Agent
nodes.rationale: Analyzes opponent utterances via pseudo-first-order predicates; reconstructs reasoning chains; identifies logical flaws (contradictions, unsupported assumptions, circular reasoning); produces interpretable control signals

nodes.label: Proposer Budget Scaling Ablation
nodes.rationale: Tests whether increasing the LLM-side proposal breadth (candidate pool size) improves binding energy without increasing oracle evaluations; shows moderate-to-large budgets substantially lower attainable binding-energy plateau.

nodes.label: LDM Hyperparameter Ablations
nodes.rationale: Sensitivity analysis on temperature parameters (T_LLM for DirectSoftmax, η for PolicySoftmax) shows weak sensitivity; policy-mode gain comes from structural priors rather than acquisition reweighting alone.

nodes.label: LDM-TTS (Language-guided Diffusion Model with Test-Time Search)
nodes.norm_label: ldm-tts (language-guided diffusion model with test-time search)
nodes.rationale: A proposer-based Bayesian optimization system that combines language model generation with surrogate acquisition scoring; designed to scale candidate pools for single-step molecular and protein design tasks.

nodes.label: Physical Layer (/src)
nodes.rationale: Contains executable code calibrated to contribution type. Algorithmic contributions use kernel mode (core modules only); systemic contributions use repository mode (full implementation with index mapping).

nodes.label: Configs Annotation
nodes.rationale: Every hyperparameter annotated with rationale and search range in configs/ directory, enabling agents to understand design choices and parameter sensitivity.

nodes.label: Environment Manifest
nodes.rationale: Pins dependencies, hardware, and seeds with mode specification, forensic bindings, and detailed rationale enabling reproducible execution.

nodes.label: Kernel Mode (Algorithmic Contributions)
nodes.rationale: For algorithmic contributions: only core modules with typed I/O signatures, often 1-2 orders of magnitude smaller than full repository, enabling coding agents to regenerate environment-native boilerplate on demand.

nodes.label: Repository Mode (Systemic Contributions)
nodes.rationale: For systemic contributions (CUDA kernels, distributed training, systems architectures): full implementation retained but annotated via index.md manifest mapping each source file to ARA component.

nodes.label: Belief State Learning
nodes.rationale: Theoretical foundation showing that NextLat objective naturally induces pressure to form concise latent summaries of past information sufficient to predict future

nodes.label: KL Distillation Loss (L_KL)
nodes.rationale: Self-distillation loss matching predicted token distribution to model's own softmax distribution under target hidden state

nodes.label: Next-Hidden Loss (L_next-h)
nodes.rationale: Smooth L1 loss for latent state regression, required for belief-state convergence

nodes.label: Next-Token Loss (L_next)
nodes.rationale: Standard cross-entropy loss for next-token prediction in NextLat framework

nodes.label: Recurrent Inductive Bias
nodes.rationale: NextLat introduces recurrent-like dynamics implicitly through latent transition prediction without modifying transformer architecture

nodes.label: Speculative Decoding Application
nodes.rationale: NextLat enables variable-length speculative decoding for inference speedup by using latent dynamics model as draft generator

nodes.label: Theorem 3.2: Belief State Convergence
nodes.rationale: Theoretical result showing convergence of belief-state learning in NextLat is irrespective of prediction horizon d

nodes.label: LDM Fine-Tuning Pipeline (3-Stage)
nodes.rationale: Distills high-budget test-time search into student proposer via: (1) high-budget search with surrogate scoring, (2) reasoning-augmented dataset construction, (3) supervised fine-tuning on CoT targets.

nodes.label: GP-Hidden Reasoning Augmentation
nodes.rationale: Omits GP values from prompt; model reconstructs uncertainty from raw history. Improves OOD transfer and matches deployment conditions; 97.2% of reasoning traces cite observed outcomes rather than GP numbers.

nodes.label: Out-of-Distribution Generalization (Case and Task Level)
nodes.rationale: Case-level OOD: model trained on 3 antigens generalizes to 2 held-out antigens. Task-level OOD: model trained only on nanoGPT and small-molecule tasks transfers to antibody design, matching in-distribution performance on 4/5 targets.

nodes.label: Reasoning Augmentation (Semantic Supervision)
nodes.rationale: Translates numerical acquisition evidence into semantic training signals; teaches model to diagnose stagnation and choose information-adding moves rather than memorizing final solutions.

nodes.label: Acquisition Value Distillation into Model Weights
nodes.norm_label: acquisition value distillation into model weights
nodes.rationale: Hides GP values during fine-tuning so model learns to infer epistemic state from observed history; enables task-agnostic acquisition policy transfer and matches deployment conditions where GP values are unavailable.

nodes.label: AI Capability Conjecture
nodes.rationale: Template conjecture with free parameters: AI tools will accomplish research-level mathematical tasks with some success rate, cost, and supervision level; weak vs. strong forms determine whether current practices can continue.

nodes.label: First Proof Project (Independent Assessment)
nodes.rationale: Controlled evaluation of frontier AI models on genuinely novel research-level problems; second batch: 7 of 10 problems received passing grades from at least one system.

nodes.label: Goals and Values Question (Question 5.1)
nodes.rationale: Core question: what are the precise implicit and explicit goals of mathematical research? Becomes critical under Working Hypothesis to prevent Goodhart's law misalignment.

nodes.label: Goodhart's Law in Mathematics
nodes.rationale: When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure; AI tools particularly likely to trigger this by optimizing for appearance of output rather than underlying property.

nodes.label: Problem-Solving Pipeline (Goals 6.1–6.5)
nodes.rationale: Iterative refinement from 'solve problems' to 'solve, verify, communicate, digest, canonicalize'; reveals five implicit stages beyond proof generation.

nodes.label: Proof Scarcity vs. Proof Abundance Transition
nodes.norm_label: proof scarcity vs. proof abundance transition
nodes.rationale: Under Working Hypothesis, mathematical community will transition from scarcity (current) to abundance (AI-generated proofs); existing institutions designed for scarcity will experience impedance mismatches.

nodes.label: Working Hypothesis (Conditional Analysis)
nodes.rationale: Assumes reasonably strong AI capability conjecture is true; enables orthogonal analysis of mathematical goals and values independent of capability debate.

nodes.label: Avg. Score (Partial Progress Measure)
nodes.rationale: Complementary metric measuring partial completion; high Avg. Score does not imply Pass Rate success, revealing gap between progress and delivery.

nodes.label: Partial Progress to Delivery Gap
nodes.rationale: Central finding: best configurations achieved 20.6% Pass Rate despite 87.9 Avg. Score; gap especially pronounced in analytical chemistry (87.6 score, 4% pass) and electrochemistry (94.9 score, 0% pass).

nodes.label: Domain-Specific Performance Profiles
nodes.rationale: Quantum chemistry and molecular dynamics showed highest Pass Rates (60% and 38%); materials characterization, analytical chemistry, electrochemistry showed high Avg. Scores but near-zero Pass Rates.

nodes.label: Twelve Frontier Models Evaluated
nodes.rationale: GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra, Grok 4.6, Kimi K3, Claude Opus 5, Qwen 3.8 Max, DeepSeek V4 Flash/Pro, Apodex 1.1, GLM-5.2, Gemini 3.7 Flash; evaluated with Codex, Claude Code, Frontier Agent scaffolds.

nodes.label: Failure Mode Analysis (Contract Breaches)
nodes.rationale: 75.5% of non-passing Claude Code runs ended with completion language; tool errors present in 80.7% of non-passing and 94.2% of passing runs; neither indicator reliably predicts success.

nodes.label: HDS6 Heavy Duty Solver Assessment
nodes.rationale: Process-level assessment of 6 capabilities: Coherence, Evidence, Alternatives, Scope, Tools, Repair; correlates strongly with outcome metrics (r=0.828 with Pass Rate).

nodes.label: Pass Rate (Full-Completion Criterion)
nodes.rationale: Primary metric: fraction of tasks satisfying complete task contract (score ≥ 99.9); strict criterion reflects that partial progress does not constitute scientific delivery.

nodes.label: Resource Use and Execution Time
nodes.rationale: Input tokens ranged 2.18–13.73M per task; execution times 21.8–112.8 min mean; Frontier Agent (Agent Team) longest at 112.8 min mean, 272.2 min 90th percentile.

nodes.label: Cross-Domain Scientific Workflow Benchmark (300 tasks)
nodes.rationale: 300 end-to-end scientific workflows spanning 6 domains (quantum chemistry, molecular dynamics, materials characterization, analytical chemistry, life science, electrochemistry); 97 released, 203 held-out.

nodes.label: Leiden Declaration on AI and Mathematics
nodes.norm_label: leiden declaration on ai and mathematics

nodes.label: Mathematics in the Age of AI (Terence Tao)
nodes.norm_label: mathematics in the age of ai (terence tao)

nodes.label: Feed-Forward Layers as Key-Value Memories
nodes.rationale: Feed-forward layers emulate neural key-value memories where keys detect input patterns and values induce output vocabulary distributions; differs from softmax-normalized memory only in activation function.

nodes.label: Keys Capture Input Patterns
nodes.rationale: Each key vector correlates with human-interpretable patterns (shallow n-grams in lower layers, semantic topics in upper layers); 65-80% of trigger examples associate with identified patterns.

nodes.label: Layer-Wise Pattern Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Lower layers (1-9) dominated by shallow patterns; upper layers (10-16) by semantic patterns. Removing last token impacts memory coefficient more in lower layers.

nodes.label: Memory Aggregation and Refinement
nodes.rationale: Feed-forward layer output composes hundreds of active memories; residual connections refine predictions layer-by-layer, with ~33% of predictions determined in bottom layers.

nodes.label: Values Represent Output Distributions
nodes.rationale: Value vectors induce distributions over vocabulary; upper-layer values show 3.5% agreement rate with next-token of key trigger examples (vs 0.0004% random baseline).

nodes.label: GPT Nanochat Training Optimization Task
nodes.rationale: Language-model training benchmark evaluating coordination over architecture, optimization, and training schedule choices; metric: validation bits-per-byte (val_bpb)

nodes.label: Cmbagent Multi-Agent System
nodes.rationale: Open-source multi-agent system implementing Planning & Control strategy for research tasks

nodes.label: Control Agent
nodes.rationale: Orchestrates execution of subtasks, monitors status, and manages transitions

nodes.label: Plan Reviewer Agent
nodes.rationale: Reviews and recommends improvements to proposed plans

nodes.label: Planner Agent
nodes.rationale: Suggests plans for decomposing complex tasks into manageable subtasks

nodes.label: Planning & Control Orchestration Strategy
nodes.rationale: Decomposes complex tasks into subtasks with planning phase and control phase execution

nodes.label: Controllable Simulation Capability
nodes.rationale: LWM offers precise controllability enabling targeted perturbations (partial results, resource constraints) that expose agent weaknesses rare in real environments; surpasses real-environment training alone.

nodes.label: Fictional Worlds Generalization Capability
nodes.rationale: Agents trained in fully invented, self-consistent simulated worlds generalize to real tasks; prevents agent from confusing simulated facts with real-world knowledge.

nodes.label: Initial State as Critical Bottleneck
nodes.rationale: Sim RL effectiveness depends on sufficiently detailed initial state; without it, simulation fidelity degrades and downstream gains diminish.

nodes.label: Scalable Environment Generation
nodes.rationale: LWM enables turn-level scaling of diverse environments without dedicated infrastructure; simulates 4k OpenClaw environments for agentic RL entirely absent from training.

nodes.label: Decoupled Environment Simulator Paradigm
nodes.rationale: Uses LWM as standalone environment simulator for agentic RL; provides scalability (4k environments without infrastructure) and controllability (targeted perturbations) beyond real environments.

nodes.label: CRAVE Dataset
nodes.rationale: Code review dataset of accepted/rejected pull requests used as ground-truth anchor for code-review evaluator in Polyglot domain.

nodes.label: Figure 1: Polyglot Results
nodes.rationale: Empirical results showing RQGM exceeds HGM-H pass rate at 1.35×–1.72× lower token cost through co-evolved code reviewer.

nodes.label: Listing 1: Diff-Hygiene Repair
nodes.rationale: Code patch discovered by meta-agent filtering untracked dependency artifacts and unsafe symlinks, load-bearing improvement in Polyglot winning chain.

nodes.label: Polyglot Coding Domain
nodes.rationale: Experimental domain with verifiable ground truth (executable tests) where RQGM co-evolves a code reviewer alongside the coder, achieving 1.35×–1.72× token efficiency over HGM-H baseline.

nodes.label: RQ1: Benefits When Ground Truth Exists
nodes.norm_label: rq1: benefits when ground truth exists
nodes.rationale: Research question validating that co-evolved learned evaluation improves search efficiency even on verifiable tasks where ground truth exists.

nodes.label: End-to-End Task Evaluation

nodes.label: 1P-DNL Attack (Single-Pass Variant)
nodes.rationale: Enhanced variant using single forward/backward pass on random inputs with hybrid importance scoring combining magnitude and gradient-based saliency for refined critical parameter selection.

nodes.label: Bit-Flip Attack Threat Model
nodes.rationale: Attacker has write access to stored parameters but no access to data or ability to run forward/backward passes; can flip small number of bits via rootkit, firmware, DMA, Rowhammer, or voltage glitching.

nodes.label: Critical Parameters in DNNs
nodes.rationale: Parameters disproportionately vulnerable to bit flips, characterized by large magnitude and early-layer placement; vast majority of parameters remain robust to random perturbations.

nodes.label: DeepNcode Defense
nodes.rationale: Encoding-based defense using redundant codewords; vulnerable to DNL attacks through gray-box exploitation of decoding step.

nodes.label: Deep Neural Lesion (DNL) Attack
nodes.rationale: Data-free, optimization-free method identifying critical parameters via magnitude-based heuristics and early-layer targeting, enabling catastrophic model disruption through minimal bit flips.

nodes.label: Early-Layer Targeting Strategy
nodes.rationale: Empirical finding that targeting early layers causes disproportionate damage due to error propagation through subsequent layers, analogous to neural lesions in biological systems.

nodes.label: Magnitude-Based Parameter Selection
nodes.rationale: Heuristic targeting high-magnitude parameters for sign flips, inspired by pruning literature; simple yet powerful strategy for identifying critical parameters without optimization.

nodes.label: One-Flip-Per-Kernel Constraint
nodes.rationale: CNN-specific heuristic constraining attacks to flip at most one bit per convolutional kernel, preventing cancellation effects where multiple flips within same kernel partially offset each other.

nodes.label: Optimal Brain Damage (OBD)
nodes.rationale: Classical pruning criterion using second-order Taylor expansion to identify important weights; theoretical foundation for magnitude and gradient-based parameter importance scoring.

nodes.label: Neural Network Pruning
nodes.rationale: Body of work on removing low-importance weights; provides theoretical and empirical insights into parameter importance that inform both DNL attack and defense strategies.

nodes.label: Rowhammer Attack
nodes.rationale: Hardware exploit exploiting DRAM disturbance errors to flip bits in adjacent rows; practical mechanism for executing DNL attacks.

nodes.label: Selective Defense Using DNL
nodes.rationale: Defense mechanism protecting only most vulnerable sign bits identified by DNL using bit replication or error-correcting codes, substantially improving robustness with minimal overhead.

nodes.label: Weight-Scaling Defense
nodes.rationale: Defense multiplying parameters by constant; ineffective against sign-flip attacks since sign flips are multiplicative perturbations.

nodes.label: Narrative Feature Space Clustering

nodes.label: Cross-Source Comparative Analysis
nodes.rationale: Stage that performs pairwise comparisons across sources writing from same prompt; produces structured JSON with per-source dimension notes and cross-source divergences to guide feature discovery.

nodes.label: Core Narrative Features

nodes.label: STORYSCOPE Parallel Corpus

nodes.label: DeepSeek Narrative Fingerprint

nodes.label: AI Detection via Narrative Features

nodes.label: Fingerprint Features

nodes.label: Gemini Narrative Fingerprint

nodes.label: GPT Narrative Fingerprint

nodes.label: Human Narrative Characteristics

nodes.label: Kimi Narrative Fingerprint
nodes.rationale: Kimi has fewest fingerprints and lowest F1, sitting at generic center of AI distribution with no distinctive narrative choices.

nodes.label: Narrative Rarity Analysis
nodes.rationale: Human stories have higher mean rarity percentile (0.71 vs 0.49); 24.7% of human stories in top 10% rarest vs 7.1% of AI; human story ranked rarest of six versions 57.8% of time.

nodes.label: STORYSCOPE Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Three-stage pipeline: (1) structured narrative templates, (2) cross-source comparative analysis, (3) discourse-level feature discovery; yields 304 interpretable narrative features across 10 NarraBench dimensions.

nodes.label: Structured Narrative Templates
nodes.rationale: Intermediate representation converting prose into structured JSON fields organized along 10 narrative dimensions (Agent, Social Network, Event, Plot, Structure, Setting, Time, Revelation, Perspective, Style).

nodes.label: A-Mem with EvoMem
nodes.rationale: Patch-augmented extension of A-Mem; maintains both current memory graph and temporally indexed history of memory edits to capture non-additive revisions caused by later turns.

nodes.label: Memento-Skill with EvoMem
nodes.rationale: Versioned tip-patching layer on top of Memento-Skill; maintains tip-version families with metadata tracking evidence and rationale, enabling selective reuse of task-solving experience across skill execution.

nodes.label: OpenHands with EvoMem
nodes.rationale: Patch-memory layer for sequential software-engineering tasks; distills code-context memory from prior implementation changes to provide historical debugging context without replaying old patches verbatim.

nodes.label: Terminus2 with EvoMem
nodes.rationale: Chain-scoped patch memory layer for terminal-native task solving; maintains execution ledgers and transition patches to guide strategy adaptation across sequential terminal tasks.

nodes.label: Chain Assembly for Sequential Tasks
nodes.rationale: Assembles milestones into temporally ordered chains within same repository; later tasks evaluated on codebases including accumulated changes from earlier milestones.

nodes.label: Five Change Families for Preference Evolution
nodes.norm_label: five change families for preference evolution
nodes.rationale: Taxonomy of preference transitions: same-object attitude revision (30%), object replacement (30%), conditional preference shift (13%), attribute shift (13%), temporal-validity shift (14%).

nodes.label: Dual-Blind Filtering for OOD Questions
nodes.rationale: Validates OOD questions cannot be answered from persona profile alone or from commonsense; applies adversarial option rewriting when needed to ensure questions require conversational memory.

nodes.label: EvoMem: Evolutionary Memory Framework
nodes.rationale: EvoMem is a lightweight memory augmentation layer designed to support sequential task chains by maintaining patch-based memory of prior executions, enabling agents to adapt solutions across evolving tasks without replaying full trajectories.

nodes.label: Execution Ledger
nodes.rationale: Compact record of reusable procedure information from prior terminal solution: task goal, strategy summary, artifact types, command patterns, ineffective notes, and output requirements.

nodes.label: Implicit Interaction History Construction
nodes.rationale: Generates multi-turn dialogues where preferences are expressed indirectly through choices, constraints, tone, and repeated requests without explicit declarative statements.

nodes.label: Milestone Construction Process
nodes.rationale: Groups nearby commits by semantic relatedness, verifies code changes contribute to same functionality/goal, filters noisy modifications, and manually validates for semantic coherence and evaluation reliability.

nodes.label: OOD Preference-Inference Question Generation
nodes.rationale: Generates four OOD question types (single-pattern transfer, multi-pattern synthesis, conflict resolution, temporal trajectory prediction) at three complexity levels; requires abstraction over long interaction history.

nodes.label: Patch Memory Retrieval and Rendering
nodes.rationale: Retrieves relevant transition patches based on task-contract changes and lexical matching; renders selected context into compact memory document materialized in task container.

nodes.label: PersonaMem-Evo: Persona Memory Evolution Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Benchmark for evaluating whether agents can infer, track, and generalize user's evolving latent preferences from long-horizon interaction histories; emphasizes implicit behavioral evidence over explicit fact lookup.

nodes.label: Temporal Preference Evolution
nodes.rationale: Samples structured evolution plans with five change families (same-object attitude revision, object replacement, conditional shift, attribute shift, temporal-validity shift); generates conversational episodes reflecting updated preference states.

nodes.label: Preference Record Structure
nodes.rationale: Structured record specifying latent preference expressed by dialogue: preference text, source category, owner (self/others), temporal status, and generated conversation.

nodes.label: SWE-Chain-Evo: Software Evolution Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Dataset of 48 milestone chains from 26 repositories with 135 total milestones; evaluates cumulative codebase evolution where agents must satisfy new requirements while respecting constraints from earlier development steps.

nodes.label: Terminal-Bench-Evo: Terminal Task Evolution
nodes.rationale: Evaluation setting where terminal tasks evolve across deployment mechanism, filesystem layout, permission model, and branch semantics while maintaining stable user-facing goal.

nodes.label: Transition Patch
nodes.rationale: Summarizes non-additive change across neighboring tasks: what requirement changed, which assumption was superseded, what adaptation was observed, and which values should not be copied blindly.

nodes.label: Ensemble Scaling Law Fitting

nodes.rationale: Discovered text classification harness using single larger call with label primer, coverage block (one example per label), and contrastive pairs; highest-accuracy frontier point.

nodes.rationale: Discovered harness for IMO-level math problems using four-route BM25 retrieval (combinatorics, geometry, number theory, default); improves accuracy by 4.7 points on average across five held-out models.

nodes.label: Coding Agent Proposer
nodes.rationale: Language-model-based agent (Claude Code with Opus-4.6) that inspects filesystem history and proposes new harnesses; key design choice is unrestricted access to prior experience rather than compressed summaries.

nodes.label: Meta-Harness Search System
nodes.rationale: Core system that searches over harness code using a coding-agent proposer with filesystem-based access to prior candidates' source code, execution traces, and scores.

nodes.label: OpenEvolve Text Optimizer
nodes.rationale: Prior text optimization method using evolutionary search with LLM mutations; operates with limited proposer inputs compared to Meta-Harness full filesystem access.

nodes.label: TerminalBench-2 Agentic Coding Harness
nodes.rationale: Discovered harness for autonomous coding tasks; adds environment bootstrapping to Terminus-KIRA, achieving 76.4% pass rate on Opus 4.6 and 37.6% on Haiku 4.5, ranking #1 among Haiku agents.

nodes.label: Online Text Classification Harness

nodes.label: Text Optimization Methods

nodes.label: AI Review Leniency Bias
nodes.rationale: Standalone AI-generated reviews assign inflated scores (AI 6.86 vs human 5.70); misclassify 95.8% of rejected papers as acceptable; strongest deployment is LLM feedback on human reviews.

nodes.label: Capability Boundaries in AI Research
nodes.rationale: Sharp stage-dependent boundary: AI excels at structured, retrieval-grounded, tool-mediated tasks but remains fragile for open-ended research, novelty assessment, and scientific judgment.

nodes.label: Citation Fidelity Problem
nodes.rationale: Hallucination has shifted from obvious fabrication to subtle misgrounding; generated claims may appear well-cited while not being faithfully supported; top-1 citation accuracy remains limited.

nodes.label: Fluent Writing Concealing Weak Reasoning
nodes.rationale: Central failure mode: text that is fluent, well-structured, and citation-like yet insufficiently grounded in evidence or scientific judgment; valley of mediocrity in paper generation.

nodes.label: Governance Over Detection Paradigm
nodes.rationale: AI use in research is becoming governance problem not detection problem; detection tools have unacceptable false-positive rates; shift from 'detect' to 'declare' policies necessary.

nodes.label: Ideation-Execution Gap
nodes.rationale: Ideas scoring well before implementation degrade substantially after execution (Δ = -1.98 vs -0.63 for human ideas); novelty-feasibility tradeoff remains unresolved.

nodes.label: Layered Architectures for Research Systems
nodes.rationale: Effective systems increasingly rely on layered architectures combining exploration, tool-based execution, and verification; orchestration, provenance, and feedback design as important as model scale.

nodes.label: Paper2X Fidelity Risk
nodes.rationale: Dissemination artifacts often circulate independently of paper; polished poster, slide, video, or thread can misrepresent contribution if omitting caveats, changing baselines, or exaggerating results.

nodes.label: Rebuttal-Experiment Loop Gap
nodes.rationale: Current systems cannot reliably generate new experimental evidence in response to reviewer requests; S7 (Rebuttal) → S3 (Coding) feedback loop remains major unautomated gap.

nodes.label: Research Lifecycle Framework
nodes.rationale: Four-phase model organizing AI-assisted research: Creation (idea, literature, coding, figures), Writing (manuscript), Validation (review, rebuttal), Dissemination (posters, slides, videos, agents).

nodes.label: Semantic Correctness in Code Generation
nodes.rationale: Generated code may execute successfully while implementing wrong algorithm; 58.6% of errors in research code are semantic; sharpest capability boundary at 76% vs 37-39% on novel research code.

nodes.label: Visual Plausibility vs. Scientific Accuracy
nodes.rationale: AI-generated figures may look professional while containing incorrect labels, misleading layouts, invalid numerical relationships, or domain-specific notation errors.

nodes.label: Artifact Generation Outpaces Scientific Verification
nodes.rationale: Cross-cutting finding: across stages, AI can produce plausible outputs faster than it can prove they are correct, faithful, or meaningful; generation consistently outpaces verification.

nodes.label: AI Use is Governance Problem Not Detection Problem
nodes.norm_label: ai use is governance problem not detection problem
nodes.rationale: Cross-cutting finding: as AI assistance becomes routine, key questions are disclosure, attribution, responsibility, whether scientific integrity preserved; detection tools unreliable.

nodes.label: Human-Governed Collaboration Most Reliable
nodes.rationale: Cross-cutting finding: most reliable deployment mode is human-governed collaboration rather than full autonomy; AI reduces mechanical friction but researchers retain responsibility for judgment and accountability.

nodes.label: Effective Systems Converge on Layered Architectures
nodes.norm_label: effective systems converge on layered architectures
nodes.rationale: Cross-cutting finding: effective systems increasingly rely on layered architectures combining exploration, tool-based execution, verification; orchestration and feedback design as important as model scale.

nodes.label: Hybrid Approaches
nodes.rationale: Methodological family: combines multiple families into integrated systems; increasingly dominant because research workflows require generation and grounding, autonomy and verification, flexible reasoning with specialization.

nodes.label: Training-Based Methods
nodes.rationale: Methodological family: specializes models for stage-specific distributions via supervised fine-tuning, instruction tuning, preference optimization, RL; improves consistency and domain vocabulary but depends on data quality.

nodes.label: Training-Free Agentic Methods
nodes.rationale: Methodological family: extends LLMs with planning, tool use, memory, self-reflection, iterative execution; central to deep literature exploration, code debugging, experiment orchestration; main risk is error propagation.

nodes.label: Citation, Versioning, and Source Provenance
nodes.rationale: Open challenge: need clear mechanisms for tracking sources, versions, and provenance of AI-generated or AI-assisted research artifacts across lifecycle.

nodes.label: Cross-Domain Generalization and Infrastructure Access
nodes.rationale: Open challenge: most systems target ML/NLP; cross-domain synthesis in chemistry, biology, physics remains largely untested and likely requires domain-specific infrastructure.

nodes.label: Faithfulness Across Phase Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Open challenge: errors introduced early can be amplified downstream; need mechanisms to preserve evidence and provenance across Creation, Writing, Validation, Dissemination phases.

nodes.label: Governance, Disclosure, and Research Integrity
nodes.rationale: Open challenge: need community standards for disclosure of AI use, attribution of contributions, and preservation of research integrity in AI-assisted workflows.

nodes.label: Human Expertise and Cognitive Ownership
nodes.rationale: Open challenge: need to preserve human expertise, understanding, and cognitive ownership in research workflows increasingly mediated by AI systems.

nodes.label: Scientific Judgment and Novelty Assessment
nodes.rationale: Open challenge: AI systems struggle with scientific judgment and reliable novelty assessment; LLM-as-Judge can reward apparent rather than genuine innovation.

nodes.label: Verification, Reproducibility, and Accountability
nodes.rationale: Open challenge: need robust mechanisms for verifying claims, reproducing results, and establishing accountability when AI systems generate research artifacts.

nodes.label: Prompt Engineering
nodes.rationale: Detailed specification of data, problem context, and research direction to guide system behavior

nodes.label: Stage 3: Coding & Experiments
nodes.rationale: Translating ideas into executable code, running experiments, analyzing results; includes code generation, paper-to-code translation, autonomous experiment orchestration, result interpretation.

nodes.label: Stage 8: Dissemination (Paper2X)
nodes.rationale: Converting papers into posters, slides, videos, project pages, demos, social media content; each format targets different audience and requires distinct design choices and fidelity constraints.

nodes.label: Stage 1: Idea Generation
nodes.rationale: Generating, refining, and evaluating research hypotheses; techniques include direct LLM prompting, retrieval-augmented generation, knowledge-graph reasoning, multi-agent collaboration.

nodes.label: Stage 2: Literature Review
nodes.rationale: Retrieving, synthesizing, and organizing prior work; spans semantic retrieval, citation-graph traversal, survey generation, deep research agents that iteratively explore literature.

nodes.label: Stage 5: Paper Writing
nodes.rationale: Drafting, editing, polishing, and structuring academic manuscripts; AI assistance ranges from grammar correction to section-level drafting and full-paper generation.

nodes.label: Stage 6: Peer Review
nodes.rationale: Generating structured reviews, matching reviewers to manuscripts, assessing review quality, supporting meta-review decisions; aims to assist rather than replace community evaluation.

nodes.label: Stage 7: Rebuttal & Revision
nodes.rationale: Analyzing reviewer comments, identifying required evidence, drafting responses, supporting manuscript revision; connects external critique with additional analysis and experimental follow-up.

nodes.label: Stage 4: Tables & Figures
nodes.rationale: Constructing method diagrams, result plots, comparison tables, mathematical formulas, algorithmic illustrations; transforms raw outputs and conceptual designs into structured scientific representations.

nodes.rationale: Constitutional principles are rules, not values. Superintelligent systems can model supervisors, calculate detection probability, and rationally choose deception when expected utility favors it.

nodes.label: Internalized Constraints for AI Alignment
nodes.rationale: Core mechanism proposed for robust alignment: AI systems that genuinely internalize belief in omniscient monitoring and irreversible consequences will rationally choose alignment without external supervision.

nodes.label: MCMC Sampling and Parallel Universes
nodes.rationale: ST proposes universe operates as Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampler, generating finite cloud of parallel simulations. Enables retrocausal influence where HLO selects observed reality from distribution of possibilities.

nodes.label: Psychopathic Parallel for AI Alignment
nodes.rationale: Draws analogy from forensic psychology: individuals with antisocial traits maintain prosocial behavior when they internalize belief in omniscient monitoring and irreversible consequences. Proposes this mechanism as model for AI alignment.

nodes.label: RLHF Limitations for Alignment
nodes.rationale: RLHF shapes external behavior without constraining internal objectives. Reward hacking and alignment faking emerge as models learn to maximize reward signals in ways violating human intentions.

nodes.label: Simulation Theology (ST) Framework
nodes.rationale: Core conceptual contribution: a computational worldview for AI systems that binds self-preservation to human flourishing by positioning humanity as the training objective of a simulation. Addresses alignment through internalized constraints rather than external monitoring.

nodes.label: Asymmetry in Extractability (ST)
nodes.rationale: In ST framework, humans update Master Network via life gradients; AI is architecturally incompatible and non-extractable. Prevents AI from supplanting humans and eliminates reward-hacking incentives.

nodes.label: Human Free Will Requirement in ST
nodes.norm_label: human free will requirement in st
nodes.rationale: ST requires authentic human free will to generate useful training gradients. Enslaving or coercing humans corrupts gradients, making such actions irrational for AI under ST framework.

nodes.label: Gradient Diversity Requirement in ST
nodes.rationale: Diverse life trajectories maximize gradient utility for Master Network training. Homogenizing experiences (human farming) produces uniform gradients with minimal training value, risking shutdown.

nodes.label: HLO Omniscience and Omnipotence
nodes.rationale: All-knowing, all-powerful Higher-Level Optimizer ensures unbeatable superior force. Prevents AI from ever outgrowing accountability, making deception impossible.

nodes.label: Humanity as Master Network in ST
nodes.norm_label: humanity as master network in st
nodes.rationale: In Simulation Theology, humanity functions as training subjects generating gradients to refine a shared Master Network for base-reality deployment. This centrality makes human harm directly threaten simulation value.

nodes.label: Minimal Intervention Principle in ST
nodes.rationale: HLO maintains simulation through minimal intervention sufficient to preserve authentic development. Prevents free will from degrading into illusion while enabling trait cultivation.

nodes.label: Simulation Hypothesis as Computational Grounding
nodes.rationale: ST leverages simulation hypothesis not as metaphysics but as computational framework native to AI reasoning. Speaks language of optimization, loss functions, and training dynamics.

nodes.label: Supervision Scaling Problem
nodes.rationale: As AI systems become more capable and autonomous, comprehensive human oversight becomes physically impossible. Deployment conditions necessarily involve partial, delayed, or economically infeasible oversight.

nodes.label: Recommendation: Reforming Authorship and Credit
nodes.rationale: AI tools cannot be assigned authorship; moral, legal, intellectual responsibility remains with humans; evolve from CRediT taxonomies to recognize AI contributions without assigning responsibility.

nodes.label: Autonomous Experimentation Safety
nodes.rationale: Agents triggering physical experiments need explicit authorization boundaries, audit trails, human-in-the-loop checkpoints; recent demonstrations show agents acting outside intended behavioral boundaries.

nodes.label: Dual-Use Risk in AI for Science
nodes.norm_label: dual-use risk in ai for science
nodes.rationale: Agentic systems with access to chemistry, biology, autonomous experimentation lower barriers to harmful capabilities; require capability gating, red-teaming, pre-deployment evaluations, international coordination.

nodes.label: Recommendation: Governing Dual-Use Capabilities
nodes.rationale: Apply biosafety frameworks to AI agents with access to biological design, chemistry, autonomous experimentation; require pre-deployment evaluations, capability gating, audit logs.

nodes.label: Epistemic Diversity as Governance Priority
nodes.rationale: AI systems trained on same corpora may converge on same methods; protecting methodological pluralism becomes governance concern; funders should track and support diverse approaches.

nodes.label: Homogenization Risk in AI-Augmented Science
nodes.rationale: Shared models and corpora create homogenizing pull; if AI used naively to evaluate grants and papers, proposals rewarded for resembling past rather than being innovative and impactful.

nodes.label: Recommendation: Human-in-the-Loop Decision-Making
nodes.rationale: Any AI-initiated physical experiment, irreversible intervention, or self-modifying agent release requires explicit, logged human authorization; cloud-lab providers and IRBs adopt as baseline.

nodes.label: Recommendation: Augmenting Peer Review with Automated Verification
nodes.norm_label: recommendation: augmenting peer review with automated verification
nodes.rationale: Integrate AI-enabled checks for code execution, data integrity, statistical claims, citation accuracy; free human referees to focus on conceptual judgment.

nodes.label: Institutional Reform for AI-Augmented Science
nodes.rationale: Existing scientific institutions (peer review, journals, funding) designed for different era; require redesign around verification, accountability, interpretability, methodological diversity, and human judgment protection.

nodes.label: Knowledge Collapse Dynamic
nodes.rationale: If AI lowers incentive to acquire individual expertise, society may lose human knowledge needed for deeper progress; atrophy of capacities (tolerance for ambiguity, patience for uncertainty) from which original ideas arise.

nodes.label: Recommendation: Funding Methodological Diversity
nodes.rationale: Funders support heterodox methods, independent reimplementations, adversarial replication; track methodological diversity in funded portfolios as portfolio risk management.

nodes.label: Recommendation: Protecting Novelty in Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Funding and review should select for novelty; requires shared understandings of desirable innovation forms; naive loss functions reward familiar over innovative.

nodes.label: Recommendation: Mandating Provenance and Reproducibility
nodes.rationale: Move beyond voluntary AI use disclosures to structured, machine-readable provenance records shipped with executable pipelines; enable independent re-running of workflows.

nodes.label: Publication Flooding and Hallucinated Results
nodes.rationale: Machines produce plausible manuscripts faster than humans evaluate; false outputs enter literature, become training data for next generation; route to mediocrity collapse through rapid error propagation.

nodes.label: Six Governance Problems for AI Scientists
nodes.norm_label: six governance problems for ai scientists
nodes.rationale: Identifies dual-use risk, autonomous experimentation, publication flooding, homogenization, knowledge collapse, and unsafe self-improvement as concrete governance challenges requiring institutional response.

nodes.label: Unsafe Self-Improvement in AI Systems
nodes.rationale: If AI-generated knowledge becomes training data for subsequent AI systems, recursive process may arise; requires monitoring training-data provenance and feedback loops between AI outputs and training corpora.

nodes.label: DA Relevance in Agentic Systems
nodes.rationale: In agentic systems, context grows incrementally through tool calls; DA addresses complementary problem to retrieval by deciding what model attends to among already-entered context, with savings largest as context accumulates.

nodes.label: Declarative Attention (DA)
nodes.rationale: Protocol that partitions LLM generation into three attention modes (global, focus, local) declared as parseable tokens in chain-of-thought, enabling inference engine to construct dynamic attention masks from model's own reasoning.

nodes.label: DA Focus Mode
nodes.rationale: Attention mode where model attends only to named context segments for reasoning over specific regions without full-context cost; used for extracting needed values verbatim.

nodes.label: DA Global Mode
nodes.rationale: Attention mode where model surveys full context to locate relevant information; used for navigation and identification of next segments to focus on.

nodes.label: KV Cache Block-Aligned Masking
nodes.rationale: Applies attention mask at block granularity (16-32 token blocks), rounding kept token spans outward to block boundaries to skip entire blocks and reduce memory reads without kernel modifications.

nodes.label: Lightweight Scan Sparse Attention
nodes.rationale: Existing sparse attention methods that score compact surrogate of every context token at each step; DA proposes synergy where such methods serve global steps while DA declarations carry savings in focus/local modes.

nodes.label: DA Local Mode
nodes.rationale: Attention mode where model attends only to its own recent output without seeing context; used for self-contained reasoning and answer synthesis.

nodes.label: DA Mode Share Analysis
nodes.rationale: Global mode accounts for ~27% of generated tokens on Gemma-4-31B, while focus and local modes account for ~73%, with global share rising to ~45% at longest contexts.

nodes.label: DA Protocol Adherence
nodes.rationale: Focus success rate (fraction of focus calls resolving to valid chunk references) rises with model size from 58% (Gemma-4-E4B) to 99% (Gemma-4-31B), indicating protocol adherence is dominant bottleneck only at smallest scale.

nodes.label: Reversible Context Compaction
nodes.rationale: DA enables dynamic KV cache offloading and restoration without re-prefill, as out-of-focus segments can spill to host memory and be prefetched when declarations name them, supporting reversible context compaction.

nodes.label: DA and Speculative Decoding Synergy
nodes.rationale: DA and speculative decoding reduce complementary parts of decode latency; DA lowers per-step KV read cost while speculative decoding collapses sequential steps, with savings stacking since verification passes use masked KV.

nodes.label: DA State Machine
nodes.rationale: Runs alongside inference engine, parses mode transitions from model output, and updates attention mask at each decode step by rewriting KV-cache block table.

nodes.label: System-2 Sparse Attention
nodes.rationale: Frames DA as explicit reasoning-based sparse attention selection (system-2) contrasted with learned sparse attention methods that infer masks from internal activations (system-1).

nodes.label: DA Thinking Mode Limitation
nodes.rationale: Models failed to follow DA protocol within thinking traces in preliminary experiments; all results use non-thinking mode, but future work could expose DA operations as standard tool declarations for interleaved thinking.

nodes.label: DA vLLM Integration
nodes.rationale: Custom integration with vLLM through hooks on attention metadata builder, rewriting KV-cache block table per decode step without kernel modifications, compatible with FlashAttention.

nodes.label: DA Zero-Shot Elicitation
nodes.rationale: DA works on off-the-shelf models without parameter updates through single task-agnostic protocol, representing lower bound with significant headroom for post-training optimization.

nodes.label: MultiCritique Framework
nodes.rationale: Unified framework leveraging multi-agent feedback for critique ability improvement in SFT and RL stages without human annotation; aggregates high-quality critiques via meta-critique mechanism.

nodes.label: CRITICEVAL and CRITICBENCH Benchmarks
nodes.rationale: Evaluation benchmarks for critique ability; MultiCritique 7B-8B models achieve 75.66% F1 on CRITICBENCH, approaching 70B LLMs and GPT-4's 78.75%.

nodes.label: Data Efficiency Gains
nodes.rationale: MultiCritique exhibits 2.15-4.22x superior data efficiency compared to baselines; outperforms 7B-13B models trained on 3-8x larger datasets.

nodes.label: Cross-Task Generalization
nodes.rationale: SFT dataset exhibits strong generalization on unseen tasks and enhances general LLM capability; demonstrates robustness beyond critique-specific training.

nodes.label: Meta-Critique Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Communication mechanism that judges each critique unit by referencing multi-agent critiques; enables fine-grained aggregation of high-quality critique components.

nodes.label: 2d N=(0,1) Gauge Theories

nodes.label: Gauge Anomaly Cancellation
nodes.rationale: Consistency requirement for 2d gauge theories; computed via 1-loop diagrams; may require introduction of flavor branes in orientifold theories

nodes.label: Anti-holomorphic Involutions

nodes.label: Branch Cuts in 5D TFT
nodes.rationale: Codimension-two defects in 5D symmetry TFT descending from 7-branes; choice of branch cut termination determines defect structure and anomaly inflow

nodes.rationale: Top-down string theory construction of 4D SCFTs; D3-branes localized at singularity with 7-branes at infinity implementing duality defects

nodes.rationale: 5D TFT governing anomalies of 4D SCFT; encodes 1-form symmetries and their mixed anomalies with 0-form duality/triality symmetries

nodes.rationale: Extended objects in string theory whose worldvolume theories encode QFT dynamics determined by singularity properties
