nodes.label: N=4 Super Yang-Mills Theory
nodes.rationale: Maximally supersymmetric 4d gauge theory; realized as worldvolume of D3-branes in flat space; admits duality and triality defects

nodes.label: Non-invertible Duality Symmetries
nodes.rationale: Generalized symmetry operators with non-trivial fusion rules; arise from topological defects in QFTs; implemented via 7-branes at infinity in string theory

nodes.label: Partial Resolution and Higgsing
nodes.rationale: Geometric partial resolutions of CY4 singularities map to higgsing of gauge theories; symmetric resolutions project to higgsing of orientifold theories

nodes.label: Q^{1,1,1} Geometry
nodes.rationale: Toric CY4 with multiple phases; admits non-universal Spin(7) orientifolds leading to generalized N=(0,1) triality with mixed SO/USp gauge groups

nodes.label: Q^{1,1,1}/Z_2 Geometry
nodes.rationale: Z2 orbifold of Q^{1,1,1}; admits 14 toric phases; Spin(7) orientifolds produce theories with U(N) and SO(N) gauge groups; exhibits U(N) triality

nodes.label: Seiberg Duality
nodes.rationale: IR equivalence between electric and magnetic 4d N=1 gauge theories; geometric realization via non-uniqueness of theories on D3-branes at CY3 singularities

nodes.label: SL(2,Z) Duality of Type IIB
nodes.rationale: Fundamental duality of type IIB string theory; descends to duality transformations in 4d QFTs on D3-branes; acts on axio-dilaton and RR/NS-NS 2-form potentials

nodes.label: Spin(7) Orientifolds
nodes.rationale: New class of string theory backgrounds combining Joyce's construction of Spin(7) manifolds via anti-holomorphic involutions of CY4-folds with worldsheet parity, enabling engineering of 2d N=(0,1) gauge theories on D1-branes

nodes.label: Symmetry TFT
nodes.rationale: 5d topological field theory obtained from dimensional reduction of IIB Chern-Simons term on boundary of CY cone; encodes global structure and defect group of 4d theory

nodes.label: Topological Duality Defects
nodes.rationale: Codimension-one topological interfaces implementing duality transformations; arise from 7-branes wrapped on boundary of CY cone; do not contribute to stress-energy tensor

nodes.label: Universal Involution
nodes.rationale: Anti-holomorphic involution applicable to any CY4; maps all gauge groups to themselves and all chiral fields to themselves anti-holomorphically; realizes N=(0,1) theories as real slices of N=(0,2)

nodes.label: Ablation: Conversation Component
nodes.rationale: Removing multi-turn conversation (asking all questions at once) drops heading soft recall from 86.26% to 77.97%; iterative research is crucial.

nodes.label: Ablation: Outline Stage
nodes.rationale: Removing outline stage (direct article generation) significantly deteriorates all metrics; outline provides essential structure for long-form generation.

nodes.label: Ablation: Perspective Component
nodes.rationale: Removing perspective guidance reduces heading soft recall from 86.26% to 84.49% (GPT-3.5); shows perspectives improve but conversation is more critical.

nodes.label: Direct Generation Baseline
nodes.rationale: Baseline that directly prompts LLM to generate outline without research; produces basic 'What/When/Where' questions, lacks depth and coverage.

nodes.label: Heading Entity Recall Metric
nodes.rationale: Measures percentage of named entities in human-written article headings covered by generated outline, using FLAIR NER.

nodes.label: Heading Soft Recall Metric
nodes.rationale: Evaluates outline coverage using cosine similarity of Sentence-BERT embeddings between generated and human-written article headings.

nodes.label: Human Evaluation with Wikipedia Editors
nodes.rationale: Expert evaluation by 10 experienced Wikipedia editors (500+ edits, 1+ years experience) on 20 article pairs using 1-7 scale rubric.

nodes.label: Outline-driven RAG (oRAG) Baseline
nodes.rationale: Retrieval-augmented generation baseline that searches with topic to generate outline, then searches with section titles for section-by-section article generation.

nodes.label: Outline Creation and Refinement
nodes.rationale: Two-stage process: generate draft outline from topic alone, then refine using collected conversations to create comprehensive multi-level section structure.

nodes.label: Perspective-Guided Question Asking
nodes.rationale: Discovers diverse perspectives by surveying related Wikipedia articles, then uses these perspectives to guide LLM question generation for more in-depth research.

nodes.label: RAG Baseline
nodes.rationale: Retrieval-augmented generation baseline that searches with topic and uses results to generate outline; unorganized information makes outline generation harder.

nodes.label: Simulated Conversations (Expert-Writer)
nodes.rationale: Multi-turn dialogue where LLM-powered writer asks questions and expert answers grounded on Internet sources; enables iterative research and follow-up questions.

nodes.label: Source Bias Transfer Problem
nodes.rationale: Generated articles inherit emotional language and lack neutrality from Internet sources; addresses need for bias mitigation in pre-writing stage.

nodes.label: STORM System
nodes.rationale: Synthesis of Topic Outlines through Retrieval and Multi-perspective Question Asking; automates pre-writing stage for Wikipedia-like article generation.

nodes.label: Wikipedia Editor Feedback
nodes.rationale: 70% of editors find STORM helpful for pre-writing; 80% think it helps editing new topics; identifies practical utility despite quality gaps vs human articles.

nodes.label: GSPO Reinforcement Learning Algorithm
nodes.rationale: Used for RL stage; handles extreme prompt-output asymmetry in LWM training; caps prompt at 128k tokens for computational efficiency.

nodes.label: Hybrid Rubric-and-Rule Reward Design
nodes.rationale: Combines 5-dimensional LLM rubric (multi-dimensional feedback) with rule-based verifier (binary correctness); 9:1 weighting balances open-ended feedback with objective anchor.

nodes.label: Reward Collapse Mitigation Strategy
nodes.rationale: Restricts trajectory expansion to exactly one turn per trajectory in RL pool; prevents shared-prefix overlap causing reward variance collapse and policy degeneration.

nodes.label: Reward Hacking Prevention Mechanisms
nodes.rationale: Combines rule-based verifier (binary anchor), content-type classification (deterministic content exact match), and tag extraction (separates thinking from prediction) to prevent self-praise exploitation.

nodes.label: Reinforcement Learning Stage
nodes.rationale: Sharpens simulation fidelity using GSPO with hybrid rubric-and-rule rewards; addresses reward collapse, reward shaping, and reward hacking through systematic design choices.

nodes.label: GPQA Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Graduate-level physics/biology/chemistry questions intentionally 'Google-proof'; frontier models exceed 90% on Diamond subset, signaling need for harder tests.

nodes.label: MMLU Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Early LLM evaluation: 57-subject closed-form questions; privileges recall over open-ended reasoning; frontier models approaching saturation.

nodes.label: Adaptive Worker Selection
nodes.rationale: Finetuning approach enabling Conductor to generalize to arbitrary subsets of models, allowing customization to user constraints and cost preferences

nodes.label: Correctness Condition Reward
nodes.rationale: Reward signal in Conductor training based on whether final workflow output matches ground truth solution

nodes.label: Format Condition Reward
nodes.rationale: Reward signal in Conductor training penalizing responses that cannot be parsed as valid workflow specifications

nodes.label: GRPO Training
nodes.rationale: Group Relative Policy Optimization algorithm used to train Conductor with format and correctness reward conditions

nodes.label: RL Conductor
nodes.rationale: Language model trained with reinforcement learning to automatically discover coordination strategies among LLMs through prompt engineering and communication topology design

nodes.label: Recursive Topologies
nodes.rationale: Extension allowing Conductor to leverage its own capabilities as a worker, enabling adaptive test-time scaling through online iterative adaptation

nodes.label: Agentic Workflow
nodes.rationale: Sequence of workflow steps defined by natural language subtasks, assigned worker agents, and access lists specifying information visibility

nodes.label: Block-ε-Separability
nodes.rationale: Property of optimization landscape where most informative signal is concentrated within blocks with negligible inter-block interference

nodes.label: Lightweight Coordination Head
nodes.rationale: Linear layer with ~10K parameters that maps hidden states to logits over agent-role pairs

nodes.label: Hidden State Representations
nodes.rationale: Penultimate token hidden states from SLM provide rich contextual signals sufficient for lightweight head to coordinate diverse LLMs effectively

nodes.label: TRINITY Coordinator
nodes.rationale: Lightweight coordinator (0.6B SLM + 10K parameters) optimized with evolutionary strategy to orchestrate multiple LLMs through multi-turn tri-role coordination

nodes.label: Representation State h(s)
nodes.rationale: Hidden state vector from SLM encoding contextual information about interaction state

nodes.label: Separable CMA-ES Optimization
nodes.rationale: Derivative-free evolutionary strategy superior to RL under high dimensionality, weak parameter correlations, and tight budget constraints due to block-ε-separability

nodes.label: Singular Value Fine-tuning
nodes.rationale: Efficient parametrization learning only singular value scales while keeping orthogonal matrices fixed, enabling representational benefits with minimal parameters

nodes.label: Tri-Role Coordination
nodes.rationale: Three distinct roles (Thinker, Worker, Verifier) enable coordinator to offload complex skill acquisition while maintaining lightweight parametrization

nodes.label: ACE2–Spike Binding Development Assay
nodes.rationale: Single development assay for Kermut optimization; chosen for challenging low baseline Spearman's ρ

nodes.label: Analyst Agent Role
nodes.rationale: Default team composition: 3 analyst agents; coordinate research direction and deliberation

nodes.label: Claude Code Coding Agent
nodes.rationale: Base model for all agents in AUTOSCIENTISTS; reference [50]

nodes.label: Claude Sonnet 4.6 LLM
nodes.rationale: Underlying LLM backend; reference [51]

nodes.label: Agent Deliberation Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Shared state and agent logs enable diversification from redundant proposals, identification of saturated search directions, hypothesis transfer across teams, and retirement of dead-end directions

nodes.label: Experiment Agent Role
nodes.rationale: Default team composition: 6 experiment agents; execute queued experiments and report results

nodes.label: H100 GPU Resource
nodes.rationale: Computational resource provided to AUTOSCIENTISTS for running experiments

nodes.label: Heartbeat Loop Orchestration
nodes.rationale: Deterministic monitor process repeatedly invokes agents in coordinated cycles

nodes.label: Model Card Artifact
nodes.rationale: TDC hERG Blocking Prediction model card produced by AUTOSCIENTISTS; demonstrates documentation capability

nodes.label: Rank-Oriented Model Selection
nodes.rationale: Discovered component in AUTOSCIENTISTS-Kermut; improves variant ordering

nodes.label: Carryover Effects Across Phenomena
nodes.rationale: Empirical finding: refusal exhibits strongest carryover effects, followed by sycophancy, with hallucination weakest. Suggests phenomena vary in coherence within model representations.

nodes.label: Closed Model Inference via Probabilistic Perspective
nodes.norm_label: closed model inference via probabilistic perspective
nodes.rationale: Probabilistic perspective applicable to closed models (GPT-5, Claude-Opus-4.5) without white-box access. Enables inference of internal geometric traps from external behavior patterns.

nodes.label: Conditioned Effect on Prior State
nodes.rationale: Holds question fixed while varying preceding state. Demonstrates model responses shift as function of prior state, providing direct evidence that previous states shape current behavior.

nodes.label: Geometric Trap in Latent Space
nodes.rationale: Key finding: behavioral persistence manifests as geometric separation in latent space. Large angular separation between phenomenon states makes transitions incomplete, trapping model in previous behavioral state.

nodes.label: Gram-Schmidt Basis Construction
nodes.rationale: Method for constructing orthonormal basis from mean hidden states of phenomenon classes. Enables projection of hidden states onto 2D subspace for angular analysis.

nodes.label: Hidden State Geometry Analysis
nodes.rationale: Constructs orthogonal bases from phenomenon-present and phenomenon-absent activations. Measures angular separation (θref) and transition angles to quantify geometric constraints on behavior.

nodes.label: Higher-Order Markov Chain Analysis
nodes.rationale: Evaluates whether phenomena depend on more than one previous turn. Finds first-order history dominates but second/third-order dependencies remain non-negligible.

nodes.label: HISTORY-ECHOES Framework
nodes.rationale: Dual-perspective framework for analyzing behavioral persistence in LLMs. Bridges probabilistic (Markov chain trace) and geometric (latent space angles) analyses to reveal how conversational history creates structural constraints on model behavior.

nodes.label: Layer Depth and Geometric Correlation
nodes.rationale: Strongest correlation between probabilistic and geometric perspectives at 85% relative depth (upper-middle layers). Aligns with prior findings on optimal layers for semantic concept detection.

nodes.label: Markov Chain Analysis of LLM Behavior
nodes.norm_label: markov chain analysis of llm behavior
nodes.rationale: Models conversational dynamics as first-order Markov chain with binary states (phenomenon present/absent). Trace of transition matrix quantifies state persistence; values >1 indicate carryover effects.

nodes.label: Markov Chain Mixing Time Analysis
nodes.rationale: Analyzes convergence rate of Markov chain via second eigenvalue. Refusal exhibits slowest mixing (highest persistence), hallucination fastest, indicating phenomenon-specific structural properties.

nodes.label: Orthogonal Procrustes Rotation Analysis
nodes.rationale: Estimates optimal rotation angles characterizing state transitions. Reveals incomplete rotations between phenomenon states, providing evidence of geometric trapping.

nodes.label: Topic Coherence Dependency of Carryover
nodes.rationale: Carryover effects dissolve in topically inconsistent conversations. Suggests behavioral persistence is context-dependent, with implications for adversarial jailbreaking strategies.

nodes.label: Dynamic Evaluation Challenge
nodes.rationale: Open challenge: evaluating co-evolution requires determining whether all components improve, whether gains transfer to unseen partners/environments, and component contributions

nodes.label: Safety and Governance in Co-Evolution
nodes.rationale: Open challenge: as co-evolution becomes autonomous, humans may lose control; need governance keeping evolution auditable, interruptible, with rollback and intervention points

nodes.label: Self-Refutation Loop
nodes.rationale: Failure mode in long-horizon evolution: system repeatedly concludes experiments fail to support objective yet continues revising same direction

nodes.label: Citation Validity and Fabrication Detection
nodes.rationale: Achieves 99.5% citation validity; fabrication detection increases from 14% (single-pass) to 92% (full stack); adversarial review achieves 74% precision

nodes.label: Cost-Efficient Paper Generation
nodes.rationale: Full system uses 11.9M tokens, costs $8.1 per manuscript, requires 3.2 hours; lightweight design without separate agent platform or orchestration service

nodes.label: Editable Vector Figure Generation
nodes.rationale: Role-aware generation: measured results from deterministic plotting, method figures from image generation then code reconstruction; achieves 96.4% figure editability

nodes.label: Evidence-Grounded Claim Revision

nodes.label: Catastrophic Forgetting Problem
nodes.rationale: Central challenge in continual learning where sequential updates cause loss of previously learned knowledge; naive fine-tuning achieves only 1.2% retention after 100 tasks.

nodes.label: Long-Horizon Memorization Problem
nodes.rationale: Formalized as a distinct continual learning challenge where models learn 100 query-answer tasks through sequential fine-tuning without retaining raw examples or receiving task identifiers at inference.

nodes.label: Data Anchor: Unconditional Generative Replay
nodes.rationale: Preserves earlier task information by training on replayed sequences generated from a frozen previous model, using a task-agnostic replay token.

nodes.label: 2^4 Factorial Experiment

nodes.label: Function Anchor: Self-Distillation
nodes.rationale: Constrains model output distributions on current-task inputs by matching predictions with a frozen previous model, following Learning without Forgetting.

nodes.label: LLM-QA Dataset
nodes.rationale: 100 tasks with 10,000 LLM-generated fictional facts across topics; tests memorization with natural language and familiar entity types.

nodes.label: Memory Half-Life Metric
nodes.rationale: Measures memory decay by counting tasks until retention falls below 50%; naive fine-tuning: 1-2 tasks, best composition: 19-44 tasks.

nodes.label: Merged LoRA: Low-Rank Allocation Rule
nodes.rationale: Folds each task's LoRA update into the dense model before initializing a new adapter, enabling multiple low-rank updates while maintaining constant state size.

nodes.label: Real-QA Dataset
nodes.rationale: 100 tasks with 5,000 natural questions from 10 public QA datasets, filtered to exclude base-model knowledge; tests memorization of real facts.

nodes.label: Super-Additive Interaction: Replay × Merged LoRA
nodes.rationale: Replay and merged LoRA interact super-additively on all three datasets; combined gains far exceed sum of standalone contributions (e.g., 31.0 vs 7.7 points on LLM-QA).

nodes.label: Symbol-QA Dataset
nodes.rationale: 100 tasks with 10,000 random key-value associations; tests memorization of arbitrary associations without semantic structure.

nodes.label: Task-Level Successive Halving (TSH)
nodes.rationale: Search procedure that progressively increases task horizons (10→20→50→100) and ranks configurations by retention, reducing computational cost by 71.8% versus exhaustive search.

nodes.label: Weight Anchor: Importance-Based Regularization

links.rationale: Both concern maintaining coherent reasoning chains and mapping between representations
Both address autonomous planning and exploration in complex reasoning tasks
Both employ multi-level evaluation rubrics to assess reasoning quality beyond binary correctness
Foundation models require understanding of learning dynamics; learning mechanics provides theoretical foundation
Both address automated scientific discovery through AI; PhysVEC exemplifies verification mechanisms needed for Grand Challenge 4
Both address implicit knowledge and reasoning structures that must be made explicit for AI systems
Both address unified agent architectures; world-model–actor unification parallels memory system integration into agent reasoning loops.

Both involve multi-stage workflows that distill or communicate complex processes; LDM pipeline distills acquisition strategy into language, while problem-solving pipeline distills research progress into canonical form.
Both methods learn to coordinate and compose multiple components (latent dynamics vs LLMs) to improve reasoning and task performance

Both decompose scientific work into multi-stage pipelines; Tao's 5-stage problem-solving pipeline (proof generation → verification → exposition → publication → canonicalization) parallels FrontierChallenge's multi-artifact contract evaluation.
Both employ agent-based orchestration; Author agent exemplifies agentic workflow design for scientific tasks

Both papers address persistent data management for LLM agents; Qwen-AgentWorld focuses on environment simulation while agent memory focuses on information storage/retrieval, but both are foundational infrastructure for agent execution.
Both represent AI systems as epistemic actors capable of reasoning and planning; LWM is technical instantiation of reasoning capability needed for AI scientists.

Both systems address autonomous research through structured artifact design and multi-agent collaboration, though ARA focuses on knowledge representation while AutoResearchClaw emphasizes execution robustness and cross-run learning.
MaxProof's persistent population archive and reusable refinement procedures align with Workspace+Skill paradigm for stateful task execution.

Both address the challenge of scaling from partial progress to complete delivery; Tao's proof abundance scenario parallels FrontierChallenge's finding that high Avg. Scores do not guarantee Pass Rates.
Both use RL-based training to learn coordination strategies for orchestrating multiple LLMs, though with different optimization approaches
Multi-agent systems coordinate specialized agents; LWM provides world knowledge enabling coordination; both enable reasoning beyond single-model capabilities.
Both employ iterative refinement with intermediate evidence accumulation and dynamic strategy adaptation
Both employ long reasoning chains, inference-time scaling, and RL-driven cognition for complex problem-solving.
Both papers address AI systems as active agents in knowledge discovery; 2606.22859 focuses on institutional governance while 2606.24597 focuses on technical implementation of world models for agents.
